scientific_name: Tomato yellow leaf curl Thailand betasatellite
potential_eco_desc: The disease symptoms were widespread throughout the potato growing districts with an incidence of 5 to 10%.
description: In April 2011, during a field survey, a severe leaf curl disease was observed on potato (Solanum tuberosum) in potato-growing areas of Punjab, Pakistan (approximate coordinates 30.3551°N, 72.5321°E). Based on molecular diagnostics confirmed that potato leaf curl disease was caused by Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus (ToLCNDV) and a Tomato yellow leaf curl Thailand betasatellite (TYLCTHB). This is the first report of a bipartite begomovirus, ToLCNDV, with leaf curl disease of potato in Pakistan. In addition, this is the first report of the association of ToLCNDV and TYLCTHB infecting potato in Pakistan.
reference_name: First Report of Tomato leaf curl New Delhi virus and a Tomato yellow leaf curl Thailand betasatellite Causing Severe Leaf Curl Disease of Potato in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: Disease incidence in the fields was in the range of 70 to 80%.
description: In November 2015, Citrullus lanatus plants exhibiting leaf curl as well yellowing and crumpling of leaves were observed at the Agricultural Experimental Station at Sultan Qaboos University Oman. Due to the presence of large numbers of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci, the vector of begomoviruses) on the plants, a begomovirus (genus Begomovirus, familyGeminiviridae) was suspected to be the causal agent. The samples were collected, based on electron microscopy and molecular diagnostics showed the causal agent was virus, and they are Chilli leaf curl virus(ChiLCV) and Tomato leaf curl betasatellite(ToLCB). To our knowledge, this is the first report of a monopartite begomovirus associated with betasatellite infecting C. lanatus in Oman. ChiLCV has been reported to infect several important horticulture crops in South Asia and Oman.  The presence of large numbers of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci, the vector of begomoviruses) on the Citrullus lanatus plants infected by viruses.
reference_name: First Report of Chilli leaf curl virus and Tomato leaf curl betasatellite Infecting Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) in Oman
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: The incidence was 50%.
description: In October 2014, chilli plants exhibiting geminivirus-like symptoms, including leaf curling and stunting were observed at the National Agriculture Research Centre (Islamabad, Pakistan), with an incidence of 50%. Leaf samples were collected from ten diseased chilli plants. Based on TAS-ELISA and PCR assay indicated the presence of Tomato leaf curl virus (ToLCV) and Croton yellow vein mosaic betasatellite (CroYVMB). This is the first report of the association of ToLCV and CroYVMB with chilli plants exhibiting leaf curl symptoms in Pakistan.
reference_name: First report of Tomato leaf curl virus and Croton yellow vein mosaic betasatellite infecting chilli plants in Pakistan

host_range: 斑翅果蝇寄主广泛，涉及18个科 60 余种植物，包括蓝莓、黑莓、红树莓、樱桃、草莓、李子、桃子、葡萄、无花果、猕猴桃、梨等。

potential_eco_desc: 斑翅果蝇成虫产卵于果皮下。卵孵化后在果实内蛀食危害，果实变褐软化，影响果实品质，并且还可吸引黑腹果蝇以及造成病原菌侵染，引发严重的经济损失，相比于绿色的果实或者过于成熟的果实，斑翅果蝇更偏好在刚开始成熟变色的水果上产卵，这是因为斑翅果蝇产卵管为较硬的锯齿状，并且对新鲜水果中丰富的糖类、维生素和其他碳水化合物具有更强烈的趋性。
management_info: 研究表明，甲维盐和多杀霉素对斑翅果蝇成虫及幼虫均有高效毒杀作用，实际应用时可以在果蝇危害发生初期喷施这2种杀虫剂，成虫1 h 后死亡率达85%以上，并且这2种杀虫剂对果蝇的持效期较长，为5～14 d; 葡萄收获以后可再次施用该杀虫剂以降低翌年发生基数。氟啶脲、联苯菊酯、啶虫脒和除虫菊酯对果蝇有较高的毒杀作用，在实际应用中几种杀虫剂可以混合交替使用。但不宜长期循环使用化学杀虫剂，以免导致农药残留、果蝇抗药性倍增和对环境、人畜、天敌等产生不良影响。采用植物性杀虫剂0.6%苦内酯水剂进行防治，防治效果达到92.8%以上;生姜精油对果蝇成虫有较强的急性毒性;藜芦碱在葡萄果蝇防治中具有较好的应用前景。

potential_eco_desc: MSV is a serious constraint to maize production throughout sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt and islands in the Indian Ocean (Mauritius, Reunion, Madagascar, Sao Tome and Principe) but also affects other cereals such as oats, wheat, sorghum, millet, finger millet and sugarcane (Thottappilly et al., 1993; Bosque-Perez, 2000). Across the African tropics maize is grown predominantly as a subsistence crop and consequently no estimates have been made of the financial losses due to streak disease. With the increasing importance of maize to agriculture in this region more detailed information on the economic impact of MSV is likely to become available. ^p^pLike many virus induced diseases, maize streak disease is naturally erratic, varying from insignificant in some years to epidemic proportions in others (Efron et al., 1989). Outbreaks of the disease are often associated with drought conditions or irregular rains such as those in west Africa in 1983 and 1984 (Rossel and Thottappilly, 1985). In addition, yield losses vary with the time of infection and varietal resistance (Guthrie, 1978; van Rensburg, 1981; Bosque-Perez et al., 1998). In Mauritius yield losses of 24 to 48% were reported in the mid-1970s with the greatest reduction of grain yield occurring in plants that were infected at an early stage. Field trials relying on natural infection in east Africa detected yield losses of between 33 and 56% (Guthrie, 1977), whereas losses of 100% were reported in many countries in west Africa (Fajemisin and Shoyinka, 1976). Trials conducted between 1983 and 1985, presented by Fajemisin et al. (1986), reported a yield reduction of 71 to 93% in maize due to MSV. Under conditions of natural infection yield losses ranged from 24 to 76%. ^p^pA study conducted by Vogel et al. (1993), looking at the interaction of planting date, streak resistance, application of fertiliser and the maize stalk borer (Busseola fusca) on maize yield in Zaire, showed that losses were highest for late plantings of the susceptible (local) maize variety without fertiliser (94% compared with 66% for the resistant variety). Use of fertiliser reduced these losses to 82 and 45%, respectively. For the early planting dates unfertilised losses were 25% for the local variety and 9% for the resistant variety (27 and 5%, respectively, for the fertilized trial). Overall the yield decreased from 1360 to 270 kg/ha for the local variety when planting was delayed, while the yield of the resistant variety decreased from 1710 to 420 kg/ha in unfertilised fields. For the fertilised fields yield decreased from 3080 to 800 kg/ha and from 3840 to 1580 kg/ha with delayed planting for local and resistant varieties, respectively. This demonstrates the significant increase in maize crop yield that can be gained from improved cultural practices and the use of MSV-resistant planting material.

management_info: Cultural Control^p^pCertain cultural control methods can reduce the incidence of MSV in crops. Often, high rainfall during the wet season (autumn) correlates with a large migration of infected vectors as the dry season (spring) approaches.^p^pPlanting downwind of covered crops should be avoided, and close attention should be given to management and rotation practices in irrigated areas. A 10-m barrier of paved ground has been shown to reduce the number of immigrant vectors, and removing the remnants of previous crops is advised (Rose, 1978). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pChemical insecticides can be effective and should be chosen for moderate persistence in order to cover the peak period of immigration when emerging crops are at greatest risk.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pBreeding programmes have been ongoing for several years to obtain MSV-resistant cultivars. The inheritance of resistance appears to be simple (Storey and Howland, 1967; Kim et al., 1989). Breeders at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture have developed lines showing reduced symptom severity (possibly either tolerance or resistance). Durable resistance has now been back-crossed into germplasm adapted to many diverse African environments, and these varieties are still being disseminated (Anon., 1983; Efron et al., 1989).^p^pOn the basis of preliminary data, genetically engineered resistance to MSV seems to be an achievable goal before 2005 (DN Shepherd, University of Cape Town, South Africa, personal communication, 2002).

像很多病毒造成病害一样，玉米线条病毒是必然不规则的，由一些年份中不重要的一而变为在其它中的流行的部分(Efron et al., 1989)。病害的暴发常常与干旱条件或无规律的雨季有关像那些1983和1984年在非洲西部的(Rossel and Thottappilly, 1985)。除此之外，产量损失随着侵染的时间和可变的抗性改变(Guthrie, 1978; van Rensburg, 1981; Bosque-Perez et al., 1998)。在毛里求斯24到48%的产量损失被报道于20世纪70年代中期随着发生于在早期阶段被侵染的植株中的谷粒产量的最大的降低。依赖于自然侵染的田间试验在东非中发现33和56%之间的产量损失(Guthrie, 1977)，而100%的损失被报道于西非很多国家里(Fajemisin and Shoyinka, 1976)。试验操纵于1983和1985年之间，由Fajemisin et al. (1986)引见，报道归因于MSV的玉米中71到93%的产量降低。在自然侵染的条件下产量损失范围为24到76%。 MSV is a serious constraint to maize production throughout sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt and islands in the Indian Ocean (Mauritius, Reunion, Madagascar, Sao Tome and Principe) but also affects other cereals such as oats, wheat, sorghum, millet, finger millet and sugarcane (Thottappilly et al., 1993; Bosque-Perez, 2000). Across the African tropics maize is grown predominantly as a subsistence crop and consequently no estimates have been made of the financial losses due to streak disease. With the increasing importance of maize to agriculture in this region more detailed information on the economic impact of MSV is likely to become available. 
Like many virus induced diseases, maize streak disease is naturally erratic, varying from insignificant in some years to epidemic proportions in others (Efron et al., 1989). Outbreaks of the disease are often associated with drought conditions or irregular rains such as those in west Africa in 1983 and 1984 (Rossel and Thottappilly, 1985). In addition, yield losses vary with the time of infection and varietal resistance (Guthrie, 1978; van Rensburg, 1981; Bosque-Perez et al., 1998). In Mauritius yield losses of 24 to 48% were reported in the mid-1970s with the greatest reduction of grain yield occurring in plants that were infected at an early stage. Field trials relying on natural infection in east Africa detected yield losses of between 33 and 56% (Guthrie, 1977), whereas losses of 100% were reported in many countries in west Africa (Fajemisin and Shoyinka, 1976). Trials conducted between 1983 and 1985, presented by Fajemisin et al. (1986), reported a yield reduction of 71 to 93% in maize due to MSV. Under conditions of natural infection yield losses ranged from 24 to 76%. 由Vogel et al. (1993)指导的研究，检查种植日期的相互影响，线条抗性，肥料的运用和玉米茎穿孔者(Busseola fusca)在玉米产量上在Zaire，显示损失是最高的对易受影响的（地区的）玉米品种没有的晚期种植而言（94%与66%比较就抗病品种而言）。肥料的使用降低这些损失到82和45%，各自地。就早期种植的日期而言不施肥的损失为25%就地区的品种而就抗病品种而言为9%（27和5%，各自地，就施肥的试验而言）。总的产量从1369 kg/ha减少到270 kg/ha就当地的品种而言当种植被推迟时，而抗病品种的产量从1710 kg/ha减少到420 kg/ha在不施肥的田间里。对施肥的田间而言产量从3080 kg/ha减少到800 kg/ha而随着推迟种植从3840 kg/ha减少到1580 kg/ha就当地的和抗病的品种而言，各自地。这表明了能从改善的栽培操作和MSV抗病的种植材料的使用中获得的玉米作物产量的重大的增加。 A study conducted by Vogel et al. (1993), looking at the interaction of planting date, streak resistance, application of fertiliser and the maize stalk borer (Busseola fusca) on maize yield in Zaire, showed that losses were highest for late plantings of the susceptible (local) maize variety without fertiliser (94% compared with 66% for the resistant variety). Use of fertiliser reduced these losses to 82 and 45%, respectively. For the early planting dates unfertilised losses were 25% for the local variety and 9% for the resistant variety (27 and 5%, respectively, for the fertilized trial). Overall the yield decreased from 1360 to 270 kg/ha for the local variety when planting was delayed, while the yield of the resistant variety decreased from 1710 to 420 kg/ha in unfertilised fields. For the fertilised fields yield decreased from 3080 to 800 kg/ha and from 3840 to 1580 kg/ha with delayed planting for local and resistant varieties, respectively. This demonstrates the significant increase in maize crop yield that can be gained from improved cultural practices and the use of MSV-resistant planting material.

management_info:
化学的杀虫剂是有效的且应该被选择中持续性的以便覆盖迁移的高峰期当萌芽的作物在最大的风险时。 Chemical insecticides can be effective and should be chosen for moderate persistence in order to cover the peak period of immigration when emerging crops are at greatest risk. 繁殖计划已正在进行几年为了获得MSV抗性的栽培种。抗性的遗传显然是简单的(Storey and Howland, 1967; Kim et al., 1989)。在热带农业的国际机构的繁殖者已发展显示降低症状严重性的种（可能既耐性又抗性）。持久的抗性现在已被回交到适应很多不同的非洲的环境的种质中，且这些品种还正在被广为传播(Anon., 1983; Efron et al., 1989)。
在初步的数据的基础上，MSV的基因工程的抗性似乎是可完成的目标在2005年之前(DN Shepherd, University of Cape Town, South Africa, personal communication, 2002)。 Breeding programmes have been ongoing for several years to obtain MSV-resistant cultivars. The inheritance of resistance appears to be simple (Storey and Howland, 1967; Kim et al., 1989). Breeders at the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture have developed lines showing reduced symptom severity (possibly either tolerance or resistance). Durable resistance has now been back-crossed into germplasm adapted to many diverse African environments, and these varieties are still being disseminated (Anon., 1983; Efron et al., 1989).
On the basis of preliminary data, genetically engineered resistance to MSV seems to be an achievable goal before 2005 (DN Shepherd, University of Cape Town, South Africa, personal communication, 2002). 某些栽培防治方法能降低作物里MSV的发病率。通常，潮湿的季节（秋天）期间高的降雨量与具侵染性的媒介昆虫的大量迁移有关像干旱的季节（春天）接近。
大量作物的下风向的种植应该被避免，且紧密的注意灌溉区中的管理和轮换操作。铺平的地面的10米的屏障已显示降低迁移的媒介昆虫的数量，且移除先前的作物的残渣被建议(Rose, 1978)。 Certain cultural control methods can reduce the incidence of MSV in crops. Often, high rainfall during the wet season (autumn) correlates with a large migration of infected vectors as the dry season (spring) approaches.
Planting downwind of covered crops should be avoided, and close attention should be given to management and rotation practices in irrigated areas. A 10-m barrier of paved ground has been shown to reduce the number of immigrant vectors, and removing the remnants of previous crops is advised (Rose, 1978).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
一些叶蝉种类已经被鉴定为MSV的媒介昆虫在自然界中(Brunt et al., 1990) 包括: 玉米叶蝉（Cicadulina mbila）， 花生二点叶蝉（C. arachidis）,二点叶蝉（C. bipunctella）, C. triangula, C. bimaculata,花生灰绿叶蝉（C. similis）, C. latens, C. ghaurii 和 C. parazeae。 Nesoclutha declivata是马唐线条病毒的媒介昆虫在印度里。一些种类的种群，包括最重要的媒介昆虫，C. mbila，能被分成“有效的”和“无效的”媒介昆虫，例如，那些能够或不能够传播。无能传播能被克服通过试验性地刺穿肠壁或通过注射病毒到“无效的”个体的腹部里。有能力传播被遗传为一种简单的最重要的，性结合的基因，有效的那些允许MSV病毒粒体通过肠壁而进入血淋巴，从那里它们到达唾腺而后能被传播当昆虫下一次取食时。症状大概发展于接种后2周。
MSV不通过花粉或通过种子被机械地传播。 Several leafhopper species have been identified as vectors of MSV in nature (Brunt et al., 1990) including: Cicadulina mbila, C. arachidis, C. bipunctella, C. triangula, C. bimaculata, C. similis, C. latens, C. ghaurii and C. parazeae. Nesoclutha declivata is the vector of Digitaria streak virus in India. Populations of several of the species, including the most important vector, C. mbila, can be divided into “active” and “inactive”vectors, i.e. those able or unable to transmit. The inability to transmit can be overcome by experimentally puncturing the gut wall or by injecting virus into the abdomen of “inactive” individuals. The ability to transmit is inherited as a simple dominant, sex-linked gene, the effect of which is to allow the MSV virions to pass through the gut wall and into the haemolymph, from which they reach the salivary glands and can then be transmitted when the insect next feeds. Symptoms develop approximately 2 weeks after inoculation.
MSV is not transmitted mechanically, by pollen or via seed.
author: zhangjianjun

host_range: Chlorotic streak has been observed on sugarcane and other cultivated and uncultivated members of the Gramineae (Bruehl, 1953; Egan, 1989). These include Pennisetum purpureum, Panicum maximum, Paspalum paniculatum, Erianthus arudinaceus and Arundo donax. R
potential_eco_desc: The disease is not of major importance in any country, though losses in some industries in Australia (Queensland), Hawaii, Mauritius, Puerto Rico and Guyana have been significant (Abbott et al., 1961). Sugarcane (Saccharum hybrid) is the main crop affected, but the disease has also caused yield losses in some pasture species (e.g., Pennisetum purpureum) in Puerto Rico (Bruehl and Boneta-Garcia, 1955).  Yield losses tend to be restricted to flood-prone or poorly drained portions of affected crops; the range of average losses in diseased areas is 5-20%. Losses are occasionally higher, especially in older ratoons where stool death has occurred. Research in the Herbert River district of Queensland, Australia suggested that a 0.24% yield loss was associated with every 1% of diseased stalks (Nielsen et al., 1986).
author: CPC2006

remark: The wide distribution of chlorotic streak disease through most sugarcane-producing countries has decreased the emphasis on excluding the disease. However, normal screening procedures for germplasm exchange and prophylactic treatments ensure that future introductions are not made.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pFew, if any, industries emphasize the breeding of resistant cultivars because the disease can be adequately controlled using other means. Resistance is available in Saccharum germplasm, and this could be used if the disease proves difficult to control (Egan, 1989).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pImproving the drainage of cropping areas significantly reduces the transmission and level of disease caused by chlorotic streak. The disease is not spread mechanically (Bell, 1934; Hughes, 1940). Avoiding harvesting crops under excessively moist soil conditions may minimize disease levels.^p^pDisease levels can be reduced by using disease-free planting material. Dipping vegetative material (whole stalks or setts) in water at 50°C for 30 minutes, or at 52°C for 20 minutes eliminates the disease Bell, 1932, 1938, 1940). In several countries, dipping planting material in water at 50°C for 3 hours is routine practice to control ratoon stunting disease (Clavibacter xyli xyli) and it also controls chlorotic streak.

potential_eco_desc: 病害不是主要的重要性在任何国家里，尽管在澳大利亚（昆士兰），夏威夷，毛里求斯，波多黎各和圭亚那的一些工业中损失已经很重大(Abbott et al., 1961)。甘蔗(Saccharum hybrid)是主要的受影响的作物，但是病害也已经造成产量损失在一些牧草种类中（例如象草）在波多黎各里(Bruehl and Boneta-Garcia, 1955)。产量损失趋于受感病作物的易泛洪水或不良排水段限制；感病地区中平均损失的范围为5-20%。损失偶然会更高，尤其在分蘖死亡已经发生的较老的截根苗中。在澳大利亚昆士兰的赫伯特河地区中的研究显示0.24%的产量损失与每1％的病害蔓延有关(Nielsen et al., 1986)。 The disease is not of major importance in any country, though losses in some industries in Australia (Queensland), Hawaii, Mauritius, Puerto Rico and Guyana have been significant (Abbott et al., 1961). Sugarcane (Saccharum hybrid) is the main crop affected, but the disease has also caused yield losses in some pasture species (e.g., Pennisetum purpureum) in Puerto Rico (Bruehl and Boneta-Garcia, 1955).  Yield losses tend to be restricted to flood-prone or poorly drained portions of affected crops; the range of average losses in diseased areas is 5-20%. Losses are occasionally higher, especially in older ratoons where stool death has occurred. Research in the Herbert River district of Queensland, Australia suggested that a 0.24% yield loss was associated with every 1% of diseased stalks (Nielsen et al., 1986).
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
很少，如果有，工业强调抗病品种的繁殖因为病害能被适当地控制运用其它的方式。抗性是可以获得的在甘蔗种质里且这能被使用如果病害证明难以防治(Egan, 1989)。 Few, if any, industries emphasize the breeding of resistant cultivars because the disease can be adequately controlled using other means. Resistance is available in Saccharum germplasm, and this could be used if the disease proves difficult to control (Egan, 1989). 收获地区的排水的改进大大地减少由褪绿线条引起的病害的传播和水平。病害不通过机械传播(Bell, 1934; Hughes, 1940)。避免在过湿的土壤条件下收获作物可能减至最低的病害水平。
病害水平能被减小通过运用抗病害种植材料。在50℃的水中浸泡植物的材料（全肉茎或嫩果实）30分钟，或在52℃浸泡20分钟消灭病害(Bell, 1932, 1938, 1940)。在一些国家中，在50℃的水中浸泡种植材料3小时是防治截根苗矮缩病害的常规的操作(Clavibacter xyli xyli)且它也防治褪绿线条。 Improving the drainage of cropping areas significantly reduces the transmission and level of disease caused by chlorotic streak. The disease is not spread mechanically (Bell, 1934; Hughes, 1940). Avoiding harvesting crops under excessively moist soil conditions may minimize disease levels.
Disease levels can be reduced by using disease-free planting material. Dipping vegetative material (whole stalks or setts) in water at 50℃ for 30 minutes, or at 52℃ for 20 minutes eliminates the disease (Bell, 1932, 1938, 1940). In several countries, dipping planting material in water at 50℃ for 3 hours is routine practice to control ratoon stunting disease (Clavibacter xyli xyli) and it also controls chlorotic streak.
author: zhangjianjun

description:
褪绿线条的病原体是通过洪水或排水(Steindl, 1955)和植物的种植材料的转移传播的。没有知道的昆虫媒介。运用水培栽培系统的研究已经显示与感病根系相关的水变得具侵染性。对于接触到病害的根而言最小的侵染期是短于1h而最短的接种期是2天。30℃的根温度有助于症状的发展(Sturgess, 1962)。如果根在截根苗的3天内被接种病害那么传播比例很高。侵染能被保持至少150天在不存在的寄主植物中的砾石水培培养基中。然而，干燥砾石5天消灭侵染原(Egan, 1961, 1963a,b, 1966; Sturgess, 1964, Hughes et al., 1967, 1968)。侵染性土壤能保持侵染高达9个月。
排水不良和在湿的条件下收获有助于病害。感病种植材料的使用已经导致病害的更广分布和更高的病害水平在作物中。 The causal agent of chlorotic streak is spread by flood or drainage waters (Steindl, 1955) and by the transfer of vegetative planting material. There are no known insect vectors. Research using hydroponic culture systems has shown that water in contact with diseased root systems becomes infective. The minimum infection period for roots exposed to the disease is less than 1 hour and the minimum incubation period is 12 days. A root temperature of 30℃favours the development of symptoms (Sturgess, 1962). The transmission rate is high if the root is inoculated with the disease within 3 days of ratooning. Infection can be maintained for at least 150 days in gravel hydroponic culture in the absence of host plants. However, drying the gravel for 5 days eliminates the infectious agent (Egan, 1961, 1963a,b, 1966; Sturgess, 1964, Hughes et al., 1967, 1968). Infested soil can remain infectious for up to 9 months.
Poor drainage and harvesting under wet conditions favour the disease. The use of diseased planting material has led to wider distribution of the disease and higher disease levels in crops.
author: zhangjianjun

description: 通过媒介昆虫可自然传播，受感染的寄主植物和媒介昆虫在国际贸易中可作远距离传播。
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: 危害性一般。

description: In sweet potato symptomless virus 1 (SPSMV-1) study, a survey of sweet potato fields was conducted in Pelotas, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, to determine the presence and incidence of SPSMV-1. A total of 303 asymptomatic leaf samples of sweet potato local varieties were randomly collected from different producing regions in Pelotas rural zone (districts 3, 6, and 9) between February and May of each year (2013 and 2014). Based on molecular diagnostics, SPSMV-1 virus was detected in the local variety ‘Pé de galinha’, which has as the following morphological characteristics: leaves with five lobes and slightly yellowish peel and pulp. This is the first report of SPSMV-1 infecting sweet potato in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
reference_name: First Report on Sweet Potato Symptomless Virus 1 in Ipomoea batatas in State of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: WDV has been reported to cause severe yield losses of cereals in certain years.
description: Wheat and barley fields were monitored for WDV symptoms in Slovenia from 2014 to present. Plants exhibiting yellowing, reddening, and/or browning symptoms. The samples were collected and one sample out of the two taken in a wheat field in Rogoza near Maribor, northeast Slovenia tested positive by DAS-ELISA. The presence of Wheat dwarf virus (WDV) was confirmed by (RT)-PCR and sequences analysis. This is the first finding of WDV in Slovenia and estimating WDV incidence was limited.  Psammotettix alienus is the vector of WDV.
reference_name: First Report of the Occurrence of Wheat dwarf virus Infecting Wheat in Slovenia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: 一般。

description: During 2015 watermelon(Citrullus lanatus) plants with fruits showing cracking, yellowing and brown areas in the flesh were observed in some areas in Morocco. During 2017, similar symptoms were again observed in the regions of Marrakech, Tifelt and Zagoura. The symptoms observed were similar to those caused by Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV) which was recently reported affecting watermelon in Tunisia inducing "hard fruit syndrome". The samples were collected for investigation, CpCDV presence was confirmed by dot-blotting and PCR. These results constitute the first record of CpCDV infecting watermelon in Morocco and indicate that the virus has been present in the country since at least 2015.
reference_name: First report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus in watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) in Morocco
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: Affected fields were very frequent and more than 90% of the papaya plants presented severe symptoms.
description: During extensive field surveys carried out in seven states (Kebby, Zamfara, Kaduna, Jigawa, Taraba, Gombe, and Borno) of northern Nigeria in April and May 2016, papaya (Carica papaya) plants showing virus-like symptoms were observed. Leaf samples were collected from seven symptomatic plants (cultivars Dogowar gwadda, Gajeruwar gwadda, and Arziki), each from a local government area of each state (Aliero, KE; Tsafe, ZA; Sabon Gari, KD; Ringim, JI; Gassol, TA; Nafada, GO; and Kwaya Kusar, BO). Based on molecular diagnostics confirming a novel strain of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV) was presence in the simples, we propose the name CpCDV-S. To our knowledge, this is the first record of CpCDV in Nigeria.
reference_name: A Novel Strain of the Mastrevirus Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Papaya in Nigeria
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: CpCDV strain C has been most frequently isolated from chickpea, but most recently it has been isolated from tomato and cucumber in Pakistan.
potential_eco_desc: Approximately 15% of okra plants were exhibiting leaf curling, yellowing, and vein thickening symptoms, in two locations of the city.
description: In June 2012, during a field survey in okra cultivations in the Vehari district of Punjab, Pakistan, approximately 15% of okra plants were exhibiting leaf curling, yellowing, and vein thickening symptoms, in two locations of the city. Total DNA was extracted from leaves collected from five symptomatic plants, the pathogen was identified as Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV) by sequences analysis. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV associated with symptomatic okra plants in Pakistan.  CpCDV is a member of the genus Mastrevirus. Mastreviruses are leafhopper-transmitted.
reference_name: First Report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Okra in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: CpCDV has also been reported infecting tomato plants in Pakistan. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV infecting cucumber worldwide. This finding supports the hypothesis that the host range of CpCDV is increasing in the Punjab region in Pakistan.
potential_eco_desc: Disease incidence ranged between 20 to 30%.
description: Field surveys were conducted during 2012 to 2013 to determine the incidence of cucurbit-infecting viruses in Punjab Province, Pakistan. Virus-like symptoms were observed in cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) plants in commercial fields in the Vehari district of Pakistan. Leaf samples were collected, based on molecular diagnostics showed cucumber was infected by Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV infecting cucumber worldwide.  Both whiteflies and leafhoppers were observed to colonize cucumber plants.
reference_name: First Report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Cucumber in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: CpCDV infecting several species has been reported from many tropical and subtropical countries and was recently found in Tunisia on chickpea. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV infecting watermelon.
potential_eco_desc: In recent years, hard fruit syndrome of watermelon was reported the incidence ranged between 10 and 40% in Tunisia.
description: Hard fruit syndrome of watermelon was reported in Tunisia since 1994, when up to 70% incidence was reported in some areas; in recent years, the incidence ranged between 10 and 40%, leading growers to switch to alternative crops. Between 2005 and 2015, watermelon fields were surveyed in different areas of Tunisia (Kairouan, Zaghouan, Gabes, Gafsa, and Beja). Samples were collected from unmarketable fruits exhibiting chlorotic mottling on rind and white hard portions inside the flesh. Based on molecular diagnostics, the causal agent was identified as Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV). CpCDV infecting several species has been reported from many tropical and subtropical countries and was recently found in Tunisia on chickpea. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV infecting watermelon.
reference_name: First Report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus in Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) in Tunisia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus has been reported to infect food legumes in many countries.
potential_eco_desc: Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus incidence levels reported here are expected to increase if environmental conditions are favourable for the multiplication and spread of the leafhopper vector population.
description: Of the 1133 field chickpea samples (displaying yellowing and/or stunting symptoms) collected from 43 fields covering three regions (Cap Bon, Bizerte and Mateur) of Tunisia during May-June 2014, four of the samples were found to be TBIA positive for Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV). These genomes were cloned and Sanger sequenced. The genomes of the two CpCDV isolates from the Tunisian chickpea plants share 99% pairwise identity. This is the first report of CpCDV naturally infecting chickpea in Tunisia.
reference_name: First report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus naturally infecting chickpea in Tunisia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: CpCDV has been reported infecting pepper crops in India and Oman, corroborating other solanaceous species as hosts. The apparently broader-than-expected host range of CpCDV, which now includes legume and solanaceous species, has economic implications to Asia and the Arabian Peninsula. The discovery suggests that the host range of CpCDV is broader than expected. This is the first report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus infecting tomato crops in Pakistan.
potential_eco_desc: 70% incidence。
description: During 2012, severe leaf curl symptoms reminiscent of geminivirus infection were observed in commercial tomato (Lycopersicon esculentum Mill.) plantings (70% incidence) in Vehari, Pakistan. The test demonstrated that the causal agent was Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV) strain C, a member of the genus Mastrevirus, previously identified in Pakistan infecting lentil plants. Based on the criteria for Mastrevirus species and strain demarcation, the cloned virus genome represents the first isolate of the C strain of CpCDV from tomato. CpCDV has been reported infecting pepper crops in India and Oman, corroborating other solanaceous species as hosts. The apparently broader-than-expected host range of CpCDV, which now includes legume and solanaceous species, has economic implications to Asia and the Arabian Peninsula. The discovery suggests that the host range of CpCDV is broader than expected.
reference_name: First Report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Tomato Crops in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 辣椒Capsicum annuum
description: Hot pepper (Capsicum annuum) cultivated in India has been identified as a host of geminiviruses causing leaf curl disease such as Chilli leaf curl virus and Pepper leaf curl virus, leading to serious crop losses. In June 2013, hot pepper plants growing in Bangalore showed stunting and upward leaf curling. Viral DNA was extracted from a hot pepper, based on molecular detection showed that the causal agent was Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus (CpCDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of CpCDV infecting hot pepper in India. CpCDV was recently reported from pepper plants in Oman, but it shared the lowest sequence identity (85.9%) with CpCDV-Bangalore isolate.
reference_name: First Report of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Hot Pepper in India
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 辣椒Capsicum annuum
potential_eco_desc: Symptoms observed included upward leaf curling leading to cupping and stunting with 15 to 25% disease incidence in surveyed fields.
description: （2011年调查时发现）To our knowledge, this is the first report of a mastrevirus on the Arabian Peninsula and the first record of pepper as host of CpCDV.
reference_name: A Distinct Strain of Chickpea chlorotic dwarf virus Infecting Pepper in Oman
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 重要的自然寄主有可可(Theobroma cacao)、厚皮可乐果(Cola chlamydantha) 、吉贝(Ceiba pentandra)　大可乐果变近无毛变种(Cola gigantean var. glabrescens)和一种苹婆属植物Sterculia tragacantha。人工接种还可侵染木棉科(Bombacaceae)、 椴树科(Tiliaciae)、 梧桐科(Sterculiaceae)、锦葵科( Malvaceae) 等30 种植物,其中猴面包树(Adansnia digitata)和Cola cordifolia 易感病。
potential_eco_desc: 可可树受侵染后的4个月内有15% 树出现症状,6个月开始衰退,在以后的27个月中衰退加剧，在其间有16％的树死亡,其他的也呈濒死状态。果荚和干可可的产量在受侵后的2年内大大降低。3年内降至更低水平。  可可肿枝病毒在加纳危害十分严重,尤其是东部省份的可可种植老区，为害更加显著，有的地区可可种植园几乎毁于此病。1939-1944年在Mangoase附近种植园30-40年树龄的可可树有74％被毁,20-30年树龄的可可树有43％被毁。产量自1926-1929年的每年30吨降至1936-1939年的每年20吨。1945-1946年东部省份的可可产量为70,000吨,而8年前的产量却是116,000吨。1935-1936年加纳可可总产量为285,000吨,到1945-1946年产量降为204,000吨。由于CSSV的危害，到1982年底,加纳已销毁了1.855亿株病树,这相当于123,000公顷面积所种的可可树被毁。在尼日利亚, 可可肿枝病毒最多可引起Amelonado可可产量损失20％，1946- 1948年尼日利亚有525,000株可可树,相当于1050公顷面积上栽培的可可树被毁。
description: 可可肿枝病毒可通过嫁接、机械接种和多种粉蚧传播。粉蚧传播最主要的种有尼兰粉蚧(Planococcoides njalensis )、肯尼亚咖啡粉蚧(Planococcus kenyae)、橘粉蚧(Planococcus citri)和热带弗氏粉蚧(Ferrisia virgata)。若虫和雌成虫是有效的传毒介体,但雄成虫不传播病毒,粉蚧的传毒机制比较接近于半持久性,但尼兰粉蚧若虫在饲毒后蜕皮仍有保毒能力。
remark: 为我国一类进境检疫性有害生物。
reference_name: 中国进境植物检疫性有害生物——病毒卷

potential_eco_desc:
CSSV is a serious constraint to cocoa production in West Africa, particularly in Ghana. Severe strains of this virus can kill sensitive cocoa within 2-3 years. They affect Amelonado cocoa more seriously than Upper Amazon cocoa and hybrids, some of which have been selected and widely used in Ghana for resistance to the virus (Legg, 1977).

The disease was first recognized in 1936 (Steven, 1936) but there is anecdotal evidence that it occurred in West Africa in 1920 (Dale, 1962). Early estimates of annual yield losses due to this virus vary from about 20,000 tonnes (Phillips, 1962) to approximately 120,000 tonnes of cocoa from the Eastern Region of Ghana alone (Hale, 1953). The average annual loss between 1946 and 1974 in Ghana was estimated to be worth over £3,650,000 (Legg, 1977).

Attempts at CSSV control in Ghana have required substantial financial and manpower inputs. The ‘ cutting-out‘  policies in place in Ghana since the mid-1940s which attempted to control the cocoa swollen shoot disease resulted in the removal of over 190 million trees up to 1988 (Ollennu et al., 1989). Over 10 million infected trees which still required ‘ cutting out‘  had been identified in the field by 1990 and this number continues to increase.
reference_name: Cacao swollen shoot virus (cacao swollen shoot)

remark: CSSV is currently confined to West Africa but viruses causing similar symptoms also occur in Sri Lanka and Sumatra (Posnette, 1940; Murray, 1945; Alibert, 1946; Peiris, 1953; Carter, 1956; Blencowe et al., 1963; Turner, 1972; Partiot et al., 1978). However, the devastation which has occurred in West Africa has serious implications for germplasm movement. International attempts at crop improvement are hampered by the need to index cocoa germplasm for this virus, particularly if the germplasm is to be moved to where highly vulnerable varieties are grown. Although seed transmission of this virus is not known to occur (Posnette, 1947), there is often the need to move germplasm as stem cuttings or budwood which must then pass through intermediate quarantine for indexing. Intermediate quarantine facilities routinely use grafts to sensitive Amelonado seedlings. Activities are at present hampered by the lack of rapid indexing methods for the virus but they are being developed.

management_info: Sanitation^p^pThe removal or ‘ cutting out‘  of visibly infected trees together with contact trees has been the control method advocated in Ghana where the disease has been of economic importance since the 1940s (Posnette, 1951). Depending on the size of the outbreak, the number of contact trees which must be removed varies. For outbreaks of less than 10 trees, only the adjacent trees are removed (to a distance of 5 m from the outbreak). However, when the outbreak is greater than 100 trees, the adjacent trees and any other trees to a distance of 15 m from the visibly-infected trees are removed (Ollennu et al., 1989).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pThe use of resistant cocoa is advocated as many of the new hybrids available in West Africa do have some resistance to CSSV (Thresh et al., 1988). The results of traditional resistance breeding programmes in Ghana (Adu-Ampomah et al., 1999) and Nigeria (Badaru et al., 1999) have been well reviewed. Attempts have also been made to obtain virus-resistant plants by irradiation with gamma rays (Abu-Ampomah et al., 1996).  ^p^p^Mild Strain Cross-Protection^p^pMild strain protection is a possibility which is being investigated (Ollennu and Owusu, 1989; Ollennu et al., 1996). Mild strains which appear to confer some protection against the severe strains are available (Hughes and Ollennu, 1993b; Hughes et al., 1995) and are being tested in the field in Ghana. However, the degree of protection afforded so far is not economic and further research is necessary.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^p Infection of new plantings can be decreased by isolation from known infections. There are also advantages in establishing large, compact plantings to decrease the production of plants in the peripheral areas which are most exposed to infection from sources around the margin (Thresh et al., 1988; Ollennu et al., 1989). Moreover, there is the possibility of isolating new cocoa plantings from infected cocoa by using barriers of CSSV-immune crops. These crops would form a barrier to the movement of the vectors (Ollennu et al., 1989). Examples of possible barrier crops include oil palm, coffee, cola and citrus.

management_info:
抗性可可的使用被提倡，如许多在西非被利用的新的对CSSV有些抗性的杂交种(Thresh et al., 1988)。在加纳(Adu-Ampomah et al., 1999) 和尼日利亚 (Badaru et al., 1999)的传统的抗性育种程序已被研究。通过γ-射线的照射得到病毒抗性植物的尝试已被进行(Abu-Ampomah et al., 1996)。
轻微株系保护是有可能的，这正在被调查(Ollennu and Owusu, 1989; Ollennu et al., 1996)。能对严重株系给予一些保护的轻微株系是可利用的(Hughes and Ollennu, 1993b; Hughes et al., 1995)，并正在于加纳的田间被测试。然而，到目前为止能给予的保护的等级是不经济的，需尽心进一步的研究。 The use of resistant cocoa is advocated as many of the new hybrids available in West Africa do have some resistance to CSSV (Thresh et al., 1988). The results of traditional resistance breeding programmes in Ghana (Adu-Ampomah et al., 1999) and Nigeria (Badaru et al., 1999) have been well reviewed. Attempts have also been made to obtain virus-resistant plants by irradiation with gamma rays (Abu-Ampomah et al., 1996). 
Mild strain protection is a possibility which is being investigated (Ollennu and Owusu, 1989; Ollennu et al., 1996). Mild strains which appear to confer some protection against the severe strains are available (Hughes and Ollennu, 1993b; Hughes et al., 1995) and are being tested in the field in Ghana. However, the degree of protection afforded so far is not economic and further research is necessary. 移除或‘切除’明显受感染的树木以及与其接触的树木，自20世纪40年代在该病害有经济重要性的加纳这是被提倡的防治方法(Posnette, 1951)。根据爆发的规模大小、必须移除的接触树木的数量而变化。对于少于10棵树木的爆发，只有邻近的树木需移除（在爆发的5米距离内）。然而，当爆发大于100棵树木时，邻近的树木和离明显受侵染树木15米的任何其他的树木需移除(Ollennu et al., 1989)。
通过使用CSSV免疫作物作屏障来从感染可可中隔离新种植的可可的可能性必须要考虑。这些作物会对媒介的运动形成一个屏障(Ollennu et al., 1989)。可能作物屏障作物的例子包括油棕、咖啡、可乐树和柑桔。 The removal or ‘cutting out’ of visibly infected trees together with contact trees has been the control method advocated in Ghana where the disease has been of economic importance since the 1940s (Posnette, 1951). Depending on the size of the outbreak, the number of contact trees which must be removed varies. For outbreaks of less than 10 trees, only the adjacent trees are removed (to a distance of 5 m from the outbreak). However, when the outbreak is greater than 100 trees, the adjacent trees and any other trees to a distance of 15 m from the visibly-infected trees are removed (Ollennu et al., 1989).
The possibility of isolating new cocoa plantings from infected cocoa by using barriers of CSSV-immune crops must be considered. These crops would form a barrier to the movement of the vectors (Ollennu et al., 1989). Examples of possible barrier crops include oil palm, coffee, cola and citrus.

description:
可可树肿枝病毒能侵染任何植物生长阶段的可可。该病毒被认为在可可内是部分系统性的，在感染树上的一些枝条可以是无症的(Posnette, 1947)。在可可的敏感品种如Amelonado 可可树，树木在受到该病毒的严重株系的侵染后的死亡能在2－3年内发生，超过25％的产量损失在头一年内变得明显(Posnette, 1941, 1950; Dale, 1957; Brunt, 1975)。
这个病毒通过粉蚧媒介以半持久方式传播(Cotterell, 1943; Posnette and Robertson, 1950; Bigger, 1972)。被报道能传播该病毒的粉蚧品种是来自蚧总科中的粉蚧科的，其中包括：尼日兰粉蚧（Planococcoides njalensis）、柑橘粉蚧（Planococcus citri）、Phenacoccus hargreavesi、Pseudococcus concavocerrari、弗氏粉蚧（Ferrisia virgata）、拟长尾粉蚧（Pseudococcus longispinus）、Delococcus tafoensis 和 Paraputo anomalus。
当媒介蜕皮时该病毒仍保持，但它不能在媒介中繁殖或传播到后代。两个性别的蛹和雌性成虫，通过爬行迅速地在邻近的树木之间从感染树木传播病害到健康树木中或被附带的蚂蚁(举腹蚁属（Crematogaster ）和 弓背蚁属（Camponotus spp.）)所携带(Cornwell, 1958)。有时候，当粉蚧被风吹动，之后侵染与侵染的最初位置有一些距离的树木时，‘跳跃传播’会发生(Strickland, 1950; Cornwell, 1960)。
CSSV在可可树上不能通过种子传播(Posnette, 1947)。
该病毒能通过嫁接和机械接种(Brunt and Kenten, 1962)以及通过利用转化的Agrobacterium [Rhizobium] tumefasciens的农业侵染，实验性地传播到敏感的品种中去。 Cacao swollen shoot virus can infect cocoa at any stage of plant growth. The virus is believed to be only partially systemic in cocoa, as some branches on an infected tree may be symptomless (Posnette, 1947). In susceptible varieties of cocoa such as Amelonado cocoa, death of the trees after infection with severe strains of the virus can occur within 2-3 years, with yield losses of up to 25% becoming apparent within the first year (Posnette, 1941, 1950; Dale, 1957; Brunt, 1975).
Natural transmission of this virus is by mealybug vectors in a semi-persistent manner (Cotterell, 1943; Posnette and Robertson, 1950; Bigger, 1972). The mealybug species which have been reported to transmit this virus (Bigger, 1972) are from the Pseudococcidae family-group within the Coccoidae and include: Planococcoides njalensis, Planococcus citri, Phenacoccus hargreavesi, Pseudococcus concavocerrari, Ferrisia virgata, Pseudococcus longispinus, Delococcus tafoensis and Paraputo anomalus.
The virus is retained when the vector moults, but it does not multiply in the vector nor is it transmitted to progeny. Nymphs of both sexes, and adult females, spread the disease radially between adjacent trees by crawling through the canopy from infected to healthy trees or by being carried by attendant ants (Crematogaster and Camponotus spp.) (Cornwell, 1958). Occasionally ‘jump-spread’ may occur when mealybugs are blown by the wind and then infect trees at some distance from the original site of infection (Strickland, 1950; Cornwell, 1960).
CSSV is not transmitted through seed in Theobroma cacao (Posnette, 1947).
The virus is transmitted experimentally to susceptible species by grafting and mechanical inoculation (Brunt and Kenten, 1962) and by agroinfection using transformed Agrobacterium [Rhizobium] tumefasciens (Jacquot et al., 1999; Muller et al., 2001).

Severe strains of this virus can kill susceptible cocoa within 2-3 years. They affect Amelonado cocoa, widely considered to give the best quality cocoa, more seriously than Upper Amazon cocoa and hybrids which have been selected for resistance to the virus (Legg, 1977).
The disease was first recognized in 1936 (Steven, 1936) but almost certainly occurred in West Africa in 1920 (Dale, 1962). Estimates of annual yield losses due to this virus vary from about 20,000 tonnes (Phillips, 1962) to approximately 120,000 tonnes of cocoa from the Eastern Region of Ghana alone (Hale, 1953). The average annual loss between 1946 and 1974 in Ghana was estimated to be worth over ?,650,000 (Legg, 1977).
Attempts at CSSV control in Ghana have required substantial financial and manpower inputs. The ‘cutting-out’ policies in place in Ghana since the early 1940s which attempted to control the cocoa swollen shoot disease resulted in the removal of over 190 million trees up to 1988 (Ollennu et al., 1989). Over 10 million infected trees which still required ‘cutting out’ had been identified in the field by 1990.

description: Surveys of Beet curly top virus (BCTV) strains infecting crops and weeds in the Central Valley of California were conducted. In May 2014, a tomato sample from San Joaquin County with typical curly top symptoms, including stunting and crumpling, curling, and vein purpling of leaves, was collected and tested for BCTV infection. Sequence analysis revealed 98% identity with the sequence of the spinach curly top strain of BCTV (BCTV-SpCT). PCR tests and DNA extracts from 2013 and 2014 pepper and tomato curly top samples revealed BCTV-SpCT infection in four out of 316 tomato samples, including one each from Contra Costa and Solano counties, and two from San Joaquin county; and three out of 22 pepper samples from San Joaquin Co. This is the first report of BCTV-SpCT in California (and outside of Texas) causing curly top of peppers and tomatoes in the field, and revealed that additional genetic diversity in BCTV causing curly top disease.  In a partial host range test performed with beet leafhopper transmission, BCTV-SpCT induced severe curly top symptoms in several hosts. These results established the leafhopper transmissibility of BCTV-SpCT.
reference_name: First Report of Curly Top Disease of Pepper and Tomato in California Caused by the Spinach Curly Top Strain of Beet curly top virus

potential_eco_desc: The disease was first recognized causing important damage in 1888, in Nebraska, USA, and has since caused frequent and often very destructive outbreaks throughout the area to the west of the Rocky Mountains and locally to the east of them. During the last 20 years in the USA, BCTV isolates have increased in severity to the point that isolates considered severe in the 1950s are now considered mild; infection of a resistant cultivar with severe BCTV isolates, even 10 weeks after seeding, can cause losses of over 13% when only 72% of the plants show symptoms. remark: BCTV used to be an EPPO A2 quarantine pest (OEPP/EPPO, 1982), on the basis of the reported problems in North America. However, in view of the probable origin of the virus in the eastern Mediterranean area, its presence in several Mediterranean countries, its failure to spread in the EPPO region, the limited natural distribution of its vectors and its very minor importance in Europe, it was deleted from the EPPO list in 1984. There is a possible danger that severe strains of the virus could spread in Europe in areas where sugarbeet and potatoes are grown. The virus is of quarantine significance for IAPSC and CPPC.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Owing to the epidemiological complexity of the curly top disease, strategies for effective control are quite limited. However, successful control is possible through a combination of measures. Chemical control of the vector should be applied inside the production area as well as outside in order to eliminate the breeding areas of the leafhoppers (Duffus, 1986). Resistant cultivars should also be used, as described by Martin and Thomas (1986) and Lewellen (1989). Since most host crop plants are more readily infected by BCTV in the younger stages, seed treatment with systemic insecticides can provide some protection to susceptible plants. Therefore, the use of specific systemic insecticides when plants are most susceptible to BCTV infection is an effective alternative component in curly top disease control. It will also avoid undesirable effects on nontarget organisms by massive insecticidal spraying (Wang et al., 1999).

Furthermore, current virulent isolates have a serious impact on the sugar content of both susceptible and resistant sugarbeet cultivars (Duffus and Skoyen, 1977). management_info: 成功的防治可能是通过综合的方法。媒介的化学防治应在生产区域的内部和外部使用，来清除育种区域的叶蝉(Duffus, 1986)。抗性品种也应被利用，如Martin和Thomas (1986)以及Lewellen (1989)所描述的那样。因为大多数寄主作物在年幼时期较易受到BCTV的感染，因此在种子上使用系统性杀虫剂能给敏感植株提供一些保护。于是，在植物对BCTV最敏感的时候，特效的系统性杀虫剂的种子处理在曲顶病害防治中是有效的可选择的方法。它也会避免大量的杀虫剂喷雾对非目标生物体的不良的影响。 successful control is possible through a combination of measures. Chemical control of the vector should be applied inside the production area as well as outside in order to eliminate the breeding areas of the leafhoppers (Duffus, 1986). Resistant cultivars should also be used, as described by Martin and Thomas (1986) and Lewellen (1989). Since most host crop plants are more readily infected by BCTV in the younger stages, seed treatment with systemic insecticides can provide some protection to susceptible plants. Therefore, the use of specific systemic insecticides when plants are most susceptible to BCTV infection is an effective alternative component in curly top disease control. It will also avoid undesirable effects on nontarget organisms by massive insecticidal spraying (Wang et al., 1999).
author: zhangjianjun

description: 该病毒不容易通过机械方法传播。主要的媒介是取食韧皮部叶蝉，如北美洲的Neoaliturus tenellus和地中海地区的N. opacipennis。似乎有两种的由昆虫传的病毒传播类型：通过受感染口气的纯粹的机械传播，以及在昆虫能够传播以前有21－24小时延迟的循环的传播。该病毒被认为不能在昆虫媒介中繁殖。叶蝉能够在感染材料上吸取大约几分钟后获得病毒，并保持病毒一个月或更长时间(Duffus, 1986)。 The virus is not easily transmitted by mechanical means.The main vectors are phloem-feeding leafhoppers, such as Neoaliturus tenellus in North America and N. opacipennis in the Mediterranean area. There seem to be two types of transmission of the virus by the insect: a purely mechanical transmission by contaminated mouthparts, and circulative transmission in which there is a delay of 21-24 h before the insect can transmit. It is thought that the virus does not multiply in the insect vector. The leafhoppers can acquire the virus in a matter of minutes during sucking on infested material and retain it for a month or more (Duffus, 1986).

host_range: In July 2014, grapevine(Vitis vinifera) exhibiting foliar symptoms of mottling, yellowing, reddening, and malformation were collected in Suwon and Gyeongsan, Korea. GRBaV was identified by PCR. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of GRBa on grapevine in Korea.

description: Some grapevine viruses, including Blueberry leaf mottle virus, Grapevine fleck virus, Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 1 (GLRaV-1) and GLRaV-3, and Grapevine pinot gris virus, have been identified in Korea, but GRBaV has not yet been reported. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of GRBaV, an increasingly important emerging viral pathogen in the United States, on grapevine (V. vinifera) in Korea.

host_range: 葡萄 Vitis
description: In 2008, a disease characterized by red blotches along leaf margins and red veins under the leaf surfaces was recognized in red grape cultivars in Napa Valley, CA. Symptoms appeared to be associated with a DNA virus named Grapevine red blotch-associated virus (GRBaV) from the family Geminiviridae.  Further studies showed that GRBaV is widely distributed in the United States. In order to assess the novelty of GRBaV, we analyzed historic specimens of California grapevines preserved at the Center for Plant Diversity/Herbarium, University of California, Davis. Tissues were available only from 56 grapevine specimens (23 Vitis vinifera and 33 American hybrids) in the collection from several counties including Napa and Sonoma and tested for GRBaV. Specimens were originally collected between 1937 and 1950. Of the 56 specimens tested, one gave a specific PCR product that shared 97 to 100% nucleotide homology with GRBaV sequences currently available in the GenBank database. This particular sample was V. vinifera cv. Early Burgundy (common syn. Abouriou), collected in Sonoma County in 1940. Results of our study suggest that GRBaV is not a newly emergent virus, but appears to have been present in California vineyards 74 years ago.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine red blotch-associated virus in Archival Grapevine Material From Sonoma County, California

potential_eco_desc: 一种嗜氮植物，与农作物争夺水肥，为农田有害杂草，影响农作物产量，种子会随农产品传播。塞尔维亚报道，假葈耳危害甜菜。匈牙利报道，假葈耳侵占并威胁春播作物，如向日葵、玉米和甜菜等，给向日葵生产带来损害。假葈耳是斯洛伐克多瑙河地区农业生产的重要杂草。假葈耳易形成密集成片的单一优势种群，排挤本地植物，使本地植物失去生存环境。奶牛进食假葈耳叶片产生苦味牛奶，花粉是引起花粉病的过敏源，影响人体健康。
description: 种子小，易随水流、鸟类和牲畜携带传播扩散。而人类活动是促进传播的主要方式，种子可随作物种子调运进行远距离传播，也可随运输工具等进行扩散。原产美国的假葈耳，最早于19世纪传入欧洲，德国最早的纪录是1858年，在位于波茨坦附近的植物园发现。瑞士最早的记录是在1902年的巴塞尔，斯洛伐克为1934年，奥地利为1942年，捷克为1948年，匈牙利南部是1950年，在东亚和新西兰有零散发现。在塞尔维亚发现公路和铁路是假葈耳扩张范围的主要途径，在船舶港口和沿河流（莱茵河和易北河）两岸有发现，表明它主要是通过粮食和油籽从美国传入中欧和东欧的。
management_info:
检验检疫方法：假葈耳是一种极具危险性的恶性杂草，因此许多国家将其列为有害杂草并加以控制，如美国列为有害杂草、澳大利亚列为入侵杂草、俄罗斯列为境内限制传播的检疫杂草、瑞士列为境内高危险性外来入侵植物等。中国口岸检验检疫机构从美国进口大豆和加拿大进口大麦中发现，因此，加强口岸检疫是重要手段之一。
防治方法：
（1）人工措施：小范围发生区可采用人工清除，需注意清除根系，防治从残存根系处长出新枝，定期观察追踪，防止土壤中种子的萌发。
（2）化学方法：塞尔维亚使用氟胺磺隆、甜菜宁、甜菜安和苯嗪草酮对大批滋生假葈耳的甜菜进行了分期施药，防效可达100%。

description: G. sepium was introduced from Mexico to the Philippines before 1815, probably much earlier, and possibly as early as the early 1600s (Wiersum and Dirdjosoemarto, 1987), along with at least 200 other tropical American species, including other woody legumes from the genera Acacia, Leucaena, Pithecellobium, Prosopis and Samanea, aboard one of the annual Spanish government galleons that sailed from Acapulco to Manila during the period from 1521 to 1815 (Merrill, 1912).^p^pAn early introduction to many other countries, principally for use as a shade tree over cacao, coffee or tea plantations, has been documented: to the Caribbean before 1850 (Ford, 1987), and to Sri Lanka in the 1880s based on seed from a single tree from Trinidad (Hughes, 1987). G. sepium has subsequently spread to India, Indonesia in about 1900 (Wiersum and Nitis, 1997), West Africa and Uganda in the early 1900s (Tothill, 1940), and to Kenya from the Caribbean in 1930 (Streets, 1962). These sporadic early introductions have been supplemented by even more widespread distribution of seed to 55 countries for species trials, and later provenance trials (Hughes and Styles, 1984; Hughes, 1987), and G. sepium now has a pantropical distribution.^p^pMore than 1000 plants have established in the foothills and coastal plain areas of Puerto Rico but because of the relatively slow spread recorded in this country, Francis and Liogier (1991) predicted that they would are likely to remain localized or infrequent. It is one of a number of plants considered common or weedy on American Samoa (Space and Flynn, 2000a) and Niue (Space and Flynn, 2000b). Holm et al. (1979) list it as a weed of unspecified importance in Jamaica. Due to the climatic similarity between the northern coast of Australian and the native range of this species, it is considered a potential environmental weed in Australia, perhaps capable of establishing over large areas (Anon., 1998). However in other areas such as Malaysia and Sri Lanka, G. sepium tends not to spread, limited by the fact that it is unusual for it to set seeds (Hughes and Styles, 1989).
author: CPC2006

description: G. sepium pods open explosively, and can catapult seed up to 40 m from standing trees (Simons, 1996a), and wind and water flow also influences the direction in which seeds are dispersed (WAC, 2005). Long distance dispersal is by man, who has planted this species widely in agroforestry, particularly as a shade tree, and widescale repeated introduction to exotic ranges has led to a pantropical distribution.
author: CPC2006

remark: G. sepium is already widely distributed, now being one of the most widely planted agroforestry trees. Risks are therefore more likely to be associated with existing plants in cultivation becoming weedy than to be linked with new introductions. The extent to which it is considered a problem weed varies among authors, as in some countries spread is prevented due to the inability of G. sepium to set seed, though the monitoring of sites where it is already cultivated for signs of invasiveness may be prudent.
author: CPC2006

management_info: G. sepium withstands fire well by quickly resprouting after damage. No precise information on the control of G. sepium is available, but because of its popularity as an agroforestry tree, biological control methods could conflict with the interests of commercial plantings, and would therefore have to focus on limiting the potential of the plant to set seed.

host_range: A. psilostachya is an aggressive and competitive weed of agriculture and pastures. The plants of perennial ragweed inhibit germination and early seedling growth of different crops, notably rye, wheat, oat, tomato and alfalfa (Dalrymple and Rogers, 1983).
potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pAmbrosia spp. (incl. A. psilostachya) are weeds harmful to various crops in North America (Piper, 1978), Poland (Karnkowski, 2001), Russia and in other countries (Moskalenko, 2001). They cause severe drying of plants, impoverishment of the soil and yield reduction (Karnkowski, 2001), even though A. psilostachya does not appear to reduce the growth of standing prairie grasses in its native range (Vermeire and Gillen, 2000). Potential sesquiterpenoid allelochemicals were found in A. psilostachya, which have been shown to be active as phytoalexins or allelopathic agents (Elakovich et al., 1987). Leaf and rhizome extracts of A. psilostachya inhibited germination and early seedling growth in a range of Poaceae including wheat, oats and rye, reducing germination by an average of 19.5% and shoot and root growth by an average of 56.8%. Combined effects of reduced germination and growth resulted in test plants giving only 34.8% of the production of control plants grown in distilled water (Dalrymple and Rogers, 1983). ^p^p^p^Social impact^pA. psilostachya sheds large quantities of air-borne pollen that causes hay fever symptoms (Wodehouse, 1971; Culver et al., 1988; Karnkowski, 2001), with the allergen 'amb pV' (A1 variant) isolated from A. psilostachya pollen (Ghosh et al., 1994). However, the more localized occurrence of plants and their smaller size lessens the importance of A. psilostachya as a cause of hay fever. Global warming could aggravate allergic hazards and thereby jeopardize public health in years to come because warming resulted in a 105% increase in A. psilostachya aboveground biomass (Wan et al., 2002).^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>environment; crop production; livestock production; human health; native flora; animal / plant products; trade / international relations; tourism^p^p(dayuhao)i>Positive impact on: (dayuhao)/i>native fauna
description: A. psilostachya was introduced into British Columbia, Canada probably as early as 1885. It then migrated from the south-west into eastern Canada (Bassett and Terasmae, 1962). The first record of A. psilostachya in Russia was from Krasnodar region, Southern Russia in 1945 (Anon., 1970) and by 1960 was found in 6 regions of Russia: Krasnodar, Stavropol, Samara, Volgograd, Bashkortostan and Kalmikiya. In 1969, A. psilostachya infested 1761 ha in Russia and was found for the first time in Orenburg region. Quarantine measures limited weed distribution, and now the area occupied by A. psilostachya is about 1160 ha (Moskalenko, 2001). In Kazakhstan, A. psilostachya was found for the first time in 1970 and by 1975 was classed as invasive (Buyankin, 1975).
author: CPC2006

description: Natural Dispersal (Non-Biotic)^p^pA. psilostachya spreads primarily by rootstocks and secondary by seeds. Seeds of A. psilostachya are spread by wind and water from mother plants. In spring they transfer by water in ditches, canals and rivers (Moskalenko, 2001).^p^pVector Transmission (Biotic)^p^pSeeds of A. psilostachya are eaten by bobwhite quail (Colinus virginianus) and whole plants and eaten by deer (Odocoileus hemionus) and white-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus) (Soltero-Gardea, 1991; Soltero-Gardea et al., 1994; Vermeire and Gillen, 2000). It is assumed that these seeds retain viability though this is not proven.^p^pAgricultural Practices^p^pTillage may be the cause of movement because A. psilostachya can grow from rhizomes (Miziniak and Praczyk, 2002).^p^pAccidental Introduction ^p^pThe fruits of A psilostachya were found by Russian quarantine observations on imported wheat grain from Canada (Moskalenko, 2001), and this is possibly the greatest threat for further long-distance introduction. ^p^pIntentional introduction ^p^pIt is unlikely to have been intentionally introduced.Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Fruits (inc. Pods): Seeds.^p - Growing Medium Accompanying Plants: Roots.^p - Flowers/Inflorescences/Cones/Calyx: Seeds.^p - True Seeds (inc. Grain): Seeds.Plant parts not known to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bark^p - Bulbs/Tubers/Corms/Rhizomes^p - Leaves^p - Seedlings/Micropropagated Plants^p - Roots^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches^p - Wood.Transport pathways for long distance movement - Conveyances (transport Vehicles): Railway Freight, Dock Cargo, Agricultural Vehicles (Moskalenko 2001)^p - Soil, Gravel, Water, Etc.: Soil, Sand (Moskalenko 2001)
author: CPC2006

remark: A. psilostachya was listed in the noxious weed act of Manitoba, Ontario and Saskatchewan (Bassett and Crompton, 1975), listed as a noxious weed by three states of the USA (USDA-NRCS, 2002), and is declared a class C noxious weed in the Northern Territory, Australia (Crothers, 1993). Ambrosia spp. seem to possess the highest potential phytosanitary risk in Poland (Karnkowski, 2001) and in Russia, A. psilostachya is listed as a quarantine weed. Quarantine phytosanitary measures limited weed distribution (Moskalenko, 2001), but there remains a high risk that this species will be further introduced as a seed contaminant of cereal grain.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Mechanical Control ^p^pMechanical damage of rhizome buds slightly influenced the regrowth of ragweed (Miziniak and Praczyk, 2002). ^p^p^Chemical Control ^p^pFor chemical control of A. psilostachya, aerially applied 2,4-D was as effective and more consistent than 2,4,5-T, fenoprop and dichlorprop, with late April and early May the optimum time for spraying (Elwell and McMurphy, 1973). Picloram, dicamba and 2,4-D provided effective control of A. psilostachya in pastures when applied for 2 successive years (Hoffman, 1972; McCarty and Scifres, 1972). Dahl et al. (1989) found that triclopyr and dicamba + 2,4-D were ineffective, but picloram + 2,4-D and dicamba gave adequate control of A. psilostachya. Picloram is recommended for control of A. psilostachya in Mauritius (McIntyre, 1985). Atrazine applied in April also reduced the density of A. psilostachya (Baker, 1979; Rice and Stritzke, 1985; 1986; 1989; Gillen et al., 1987).^p^p^Biological Control ^p^pZygogramma suturalis (F.) (Coleoptera, Chrysomelidae) was introduced from North America for the biological control of Ambrosia spp. and released in several countries, including Russia in 1978 (Reznik et al., 1994), Yugoslavia in 1984 (Igrc, 1987), Croatia in 1985 (Igrc et al., 1995) and China in 1997 and 1998 (Wan and Wang, 1989; 1990). The larvae and adults of the Z. suturalis were able to feed and develop on A. artemisiifolia and A. psilostachya in the natural environment (Kovalev et al., 1983; Kovalev and Vecherin, 1986; Reznik and Kovalev, 1989). However, 10 years after it was introduced into Russia, Z. suturalis was only moderately successful as a biological control agent due to low population establishment (Reznik et al., 1994) and poor movement (Reznik et al., 1990). The second natural enemy of Ambrosia spp., Zigogramma disrupta (Rogers) was introduced into the former USSR from Texas, USA in 1981 for the biological control of A. artemisiifolia and A. psilostachya (Kovalev et al., 1983), with the adults and larvae feeding on the uppermost foliage of the plant (Piper, 1978). The western biotype of Tarachidia candefacta (Hb.) (Lepidoptera, Noctuidae) was introduced from California, USA into the former USSR in 1967 for the biological control of Ambrosia spp. (Nayanov, 1973; Gilstrap and Goeden, 1974; Kovalev, 1989) and was found to have acclimatized in Krasnodar region, Southern Russia (Shurov, 1998).

host_range: P. nemorensis is confined to coniferous trees and has a very wide host range which includes the widespread species in Canada and northern USA Pinus banksiana, Picea glauca and Picea mariana, the more local south-eastern species Pinus echinata, Pinus ellio
potential_eco_desc: P. nemorensis is of little importance in natural pine stands, due to the lack of suitable breeding materials. However, in Christmas tree plantations, the numerous stumps are ideal for the beetle. As re-afforestation increases, the importance of the weevil is expected to increase. Nursery plants are often badly damaged as adults feed on the bark of seedlings. Besides the direct damage it causes, P. nemorensis acts as a vector of Leptographium procerum, causing procerum root disease, the most serious problem of growers producing Pinus strobus as Christmas trees in Virginia, USA Nevill and Alexander, 1992a, b. P. nemorensis has also been found to be contaminated with Gibberella circinata (the cause of pitch canker of pine) in south-eastern USA, and considered as a possible vector of the disease on P. radiata if introducted into California (McCain et al., 1987).^p^pIn South Africa (Wingfield and Swart, 1994; Zwolinski et al., 1995), P. nemorensis particularly damages trees affected by Sphaeropsis sapinea dieback.

remark: P. nemorensis is regulated by the European Union (EU, 2000) and other EPPO countries (Turkey). It presents a risk of further spread in southern Africa, and potentially to temperate conifer forests throughout the world. In its natural range, P. nemorensis is a serious pest especially in conifer nurseries and in Christmas tree plantations. It includes among its hosts the very important European species Pinus sylvestris, and also several North American species which are more or less widely planted in other parts of the world (Picea glauca, P. pungens, Pinus contorta, P. radiata). The conditions of eastern North America are broadly similar to those of Europe, northern Asia and parts of Australasia, and one could certainly expect P. nemorensis to establish there. In North America, P. nemorensis seems to attack the locally dominant conifers fairly indiscriminately, and to move onto introduced species. P. nemorensis has already been introduced into South Africa, where it is damaging, and probably into the Far East of Russia, where it has not apparently attracted much attention. Introduction of P. nemorensis could have severe economic impacts in many parts of the world.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Control^p^pIntensive sanitation over wide areas is effective in maintaining low weevil populations. For chemical control, carbofuran has been reported to be efficient in Christmas tree plantations (Appleby et al., 1988). Ethanol-turpentine baited flight traps can be used to monitor populations (Rieske and Raffa, 1993; Rieske, 2000). For more information, see Finnegan and Godwin (1967). In South Africa, Wingfield and Swart (1994) recommend an integrated approach, in controlling Sphaeropsis sapinea dieback, which predisposes Pinus radiata to attack by the weevil.^p^pPhytosanitary Measures^p^pTo prevent the introduction of life stages of P. nemorensis, EPPO recommends that the importation of plants for planting and cut branches of host species of Picea and Pinus from North America should be prohibited (OEPP/EPPO, 1990). There is also a risk that P. nemorensis should enter on conifer wood, which is effectively covered by the measures recommended for Scolytidae (kiln drying or fumigation).

description: In July 2017, eight samples of passionflower vines (Passiflora edulis, cultivar Flora Brasil-200), from Mossoró County, state of Rio Grande do Norte, exhibiting severe mosaic accompanied by yellow spots, leaf deformation, and blisters were received in the laboratory of Plant Virology (Escola Superior de Agricultura “Luiz de Queiroz”/Universidade de S?o Paulo) for diagnosis. The symptoms resembled those associated with begomovirus infection previously reported for passionflower. The passion fruit plants were heavily infested by whitefly. Nucleotide sequences for three amplicons revealed the whitefly as being Bemisia tabaci Middle East-Asia Minor 1 (formerly biotype B). Based on molecular diagnostics confirming the member of begomovirus was Sida Mottle Alagoas Virus (SiMAV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of SiMAV naturally infecting passionflower in Brazil.  The passion fruit plants were heavily infested by whitefly. Nucleotide sequences for amplicons revealed the whitefly as being Bemisia tabaci Middle East-Asia Minor 1 (formerly biotype B).

host_range: N. trichotoma replaces both native and introduced (pasture) grasses, especially in the Tableland grasslands of Australia and the South African veld (Wells and de Beer, 1987; Campbell and Vere, 1995; Cronk and Fuller, 1995).
potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pN. trichotoma causes more reductions in carrying-capacity than any other pasture weed in Australia (Parsons and Cuthbertson, 1992; Campbell, 1998). Similarly, in New Zealand, N. trichotoma can reduce the carry-capacity by up to 90%, leading to the abandonment of sheep farming (Healy, 1945). If forced to eat N. trichotoma, both sheep and cattle may die, due to the rumen becoming blocked by undigested leaves (Campbell, 1998). The annual benefits from control of N. trichotoma in New South Wales, Australia alone, have been put at over AU$40 million (Jones and Vere, 1998), mainly due to losses incurred by the wool and lamb industries.^p^p^Environmental impact^pIn South Africa, it has been known for many years that N. trichotoma invades and competes with natural vegetation, especially in the upland grasslands (Veld) and Fynbos (Wells, 1978). Only recently, however, has this environmental impact been appreciated in Australia, and techniques are being developed for the selective removal of N. trichotoma from native grasses swards and their replacement with native grasses (Hocking, 1998). It is also invading and impacting on conservation areas, including dry coastal vegetation, grassy woodland, dry sclerophyll forest and rocky outcrop vegetation in New South Wales and Victoria (McLaren et al., 1998), and Goninon (1998) has identified the threat posed to sensitive native grasslands in Tasmania.^p^p^Social impact^pIn worst case scenarios in New South Wales (Australia), farmers cannot sell infested properties and have to seek alternative employment (Campbell, 1998). In an economic assessment, Jones et al. (2000) concluded that on low rainfall and low soil fertility sites, the socially optimal control option for N. trichotoma is to retire the land from agriculture and plant trees. Similar social impacts have been experienced in New Zealand (Healy, 1945). Gardener and Sindell (1998) considered that its impact on conservation lands resulted in a decrease in their aesthetic value.^p^p^Impact on biodiversity^pAnecdotal evidence quoted by Gardener and Sindel (1998) indicates that there is a drop in biodiversity in grasslands invaded by N. trichotoma because the litter from the tussocks excludes shade-tolerant native herbs, and also eliminates mosses and lichens which typically colonize bare soil or rocky ground. McLaren et al. (1998) listed a number of native Eucalyptus spp. as well as understorey shrubs, in grassy woodland and dry sclerophyll forest in New South Wales (Australia), which are being threatened by invasion of N. trichotoma; although infestation into high-grade conservation areas, especially those dominated by native tussock grasses, appears to be slow (Hocking, 1998).^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>biodiversity; environment; livestock production; native fauna; native flora; animal / plant products; trade / international relations
description: The history of introduction of N. trichotoma is well documented, although the actual taxonomic status of the new alien was often not firmly established until many years after its critical arrival. For example, in New Zealand it was claimed to have been introduced from South America in the 1860s, either accidentally as a contaminant of packing materials, wool, ballast or pasture seed, or even deliberately to stabilize sand-dunes (Healy, 1945). However, it was not formally identified in New Zealand until the 1930s (Allen, 1935). Wells (1978) reports in detail on the likely means, as well as entry points, of its introduction into South Africa, postulating that the seeds arrived in hay, exported from Argentina for horse fodder by the British Army during the Boer War (1899-1902), through the ports of East London and Port Elizabeth. Once again, it was not until much later (1952) that it was correctly identified (Wells, 1977). Its manner of introduction into Australia is less precise. Anecdotal evidence from landholders put it in the late 1890s to early 1900s, although it was not identified until 1935, when it was known as Yass River tussock (Cross, 1937; Campbell, 1982). Its subsequent history of spread would suggest that this is a 'sleeper' species whose populations have a prolonged lag phase before increasing rapidly and dramatically (McLaren et al., 1998). Thus, from a minor infestation at Yass River in 1935, N. trichotoma had spread over 680,000 ha of New South Wales by 1975 (Campbell, 1982), and 20 years later this had increased to more than 870,000 ha (McLaren et al., 1998). In Victoria, N. trichotoma was not detected until 1954, but by 1979 it had increased to ca 130,000 ha (McLaren et al., 1998). The latter authors estimate that 32 million ha of southern Australia are at risk. N. trichotoma was introduced into Tasmania, probably in pea seeds imported from New Zealand during the 1920s (Goninon, 1998), although it was not identified until the mid-1950s (Fricke, 1956). Its minor incursions into Europe have been linked with wool imports (Campbell, 1982).
author: CPC2006

description: Natural dispersal^p^pPropagation is entirely by seeds which are produced in enormous numbers on windblown panicles, which can be dispersed up to 16 km, according to Healy (1945), or >8 km per day (Taylor, 1987), and this has recently been revised upwards of 20 km per day (Jones and Vere, 1998).^p^pVector transmission^p^pDispersal by grazing animals, both externally and internally, has been well documented (Wells, 1978; Campbell, 1998; Cook, 1998), with sheep passing large quantities of seed up to 4 days after ingestion (Campbell, 1962). New guidelines on transport of stock are now being considered in Australia, including quarantine, shearing before sale and restricting sale of unshorn stock in the flowering period (Cook, 1998). Seed is also spread by machinery and man (Campbell, 1998).^p^pAgricultural practices^p^pLinked to vector transmission.^p^pAccidental introduction^p^pThere are numerous examples of intercontinental movement of seed as contaminants of trade goods, especially in: hay or fodder to South Africa (Wells, 1978); seed of Medicago sativa to New Zealand (Healy, 1945); pea seed to Tasmania (Goninon, 1998); Festuca seed in the USA (Westbrooks, 1991); and wool in Europe (Campbell, 1982).^p^pIntentional introduction^p^pExotic Nassella species, particularly those with drooping tussocks, are sold in nurseries in Australia as ornamentals. N. tenuissima (Mexican feather grass) is causing concern because it is taxonomically close to N. trichotoma (Jacobs et al., 1998). The latter authors detail attempts to apply pressures to the nursery industry to prevent the importation and sale of such South American grasses. Potentially, N. trichotoma could be sold alongside, or confused with, N. tenuissima in plant nurseries.Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Leaves: Seeds.^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches: Seeds.^p - True Seeds (inc. Pods)^p - Flowers/Inflorescences/Cones/Calyx^p - Seedlings/Micropropagated Plants^p - Roots^p - Wood.Transport pathways for long distance movement - Conveyances (transport Vehicles) (Campbell & Vere 1995)^p - Non-host Plant Material: Crop Seeds; Fodder. (Wells 1978; Westbrooks 1991; Goninon 1998)^p - Containers And Packing: Wool Packing. (Healy 1945; Campbell & Vere 1995)^p - Soil, Gravel, Water, Etc. (Campbell & Vere 1995)
