management_info: According to Coulibaly (1995) and Hamadoun and Traore (1996) management practices have been advocated for rice farmers in Mali. These pratices include discontinuation and substitution of susceptible varieties with resistant/tolerant ones, burning of rice straws after harvest, change of nursery sites, early planting, rouging and destruction of infected plants in the field. Other practices include reduction of fertilizer (e.g. urea) application on infected plots, flooding of tilled plots, careful use of insecticides against the beetle vectors and timely weeding. The use of natural host-plant resistance is an appropriate way to control RYMV (Fomba, 1988; Thottappilly and Rossel, 1993). Exotic varieties of rice are generally highly susceptible to RYMV whereas traditionally grown, African upland varieties are usually moderately resistant or tolerant to the virus (IITA, 1979; Raymundo et al., 1979; Raymundo and Konteh, 1980; Rossel and Thottappilly, 1985; Fomba, 1988; Taylor, 1989; Awoderu, 1991b, Thottappilly and Rossel, 1993). Among indigenous African Oryza species like O. glaberrima and O. barthii, several accessions were identified as highly resistant (Attere and Fatokun, 1983; Thottappilly and Rossel, 1993). Breeding for resistance to RYMV was initiated in many countries (Masajo et al., 1988; Paul, 1992; Masajo and Rasoafalimanana, 1995; Paul et al., 1995a, b; Vales et al., 1995; John et al., 1985, 1986b; Ahmadi and Cisse, 1995a, b; Singh, 1995; Fomba et al., 1995a; Alluri et al., 1995; Bouet et al., 1995). Reckhaus和Andriamasintseheno (1995, 1997)在马达加斯加提倡IPM策略防治RYMV。这个策略包括作物剩余物的毁灭，延迟种植时间那里灌溉设备可以利用，忍受力品种的使用，和媒介昆虫的化学防治。在马里，根据Coulibaly (1995)和Hamadoun 和 Traore (1996)治理实践已经为水稻农民提倡。这些实践包括有抗病性或忍受性易受影响的品种的终止和代替，收成后水稻稻秆的烧毁，苗圃大小的改变，早期种植，田里侵染植株的搽和毁灭。其它实践包括受侵染的土地上肥料运用的减少，耕地的洪灾，对抗甲虫媒介昆虫的杀虫剂的小心使用和适时的除草。 Reckhaus and Andriamasintseheno (1995, 1997) advocate an IPM strategy for control of RYMV in Madagascar. This strategy includes the destruction of crop residues, delaying planting time where irrigation facilities are available, the use of tolerant varieties, and chemical control of vectors.According to Coulibaly (1995) and Hamadoun and Traore (1996) management practices have been advocated for rice farmers in Mali. Other practices include reduction of fertilizer (e.g. urea) application on infected plots, flooding of tilled plots, careful use of insecticides against the beetle vectors and timely weeding.

description: Poor or no regrowth of a sorghum-Sudangrass hybrid (Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench ×Sorghum bicolor var. sudanense) grown for hay in nine fields (approximately 45 ha total) in Williamson Co., TX, was observed in September and October 2014. description: An extensive survey was done in five high-yielding alfalfa(Medicago sativa) regions in Saudi Arabia, namely Riyadh, Qassim, Hail, Tabuk, and Jouf during 2012 to 2014. Several fields in 135 farms were surveyed in these regions and 1481 symptomatic samples were collected. Symptoms were mostly mosaic, mottling, interveinal chlorosis, crinkling, and small leaves. To our knowledge, this is the first report of LTSV in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as well as in Asia.

description: During the fall of 2013, endive (Cichorium endivia L.) and escarole (C. endivia ssp. latifolia) fields in New Jersey were found with severe disease symptoms. The cores of the heads were necrotic and rotted, while outer leaves were yellow with more pronounced yellowing of veins and occasional veinal necrosis. The disease occurred in plants grown in sandy loam soils, and developed following a period of extended soil moisture; most escarole and endive in the ground at that time developed symptoms. Similar symptoms have been observed for 15 to 20 years in the area and are commonly referred to as yellows. The samples were collected and identified, the causal agent was Moroccan pepper virus (MPV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of MPV in escarole anywhere in the world, and the first report of MPV in a United States field crop outside of California and Arizona. MPV and TBSV are known to cause the disease, lettuce dieback, in the western United States. Like yellows on escarole, lettuce dieback is associated with saturated soils and other stress factors (Wintermantel, unpublished). Further studies will be needed to determine if MPV is the sole cause of yellows in escarole and endive or if it is part of a disease complex; however, the identification of MPV in this important leafy greens production region and its association with yellowing and core rot symptoms in escarole warrant further study of the association of MPV and potentially other tombusviruses with yellows of escarole.
reference_name: First Report of Moroccan pepper virus in Association with Yellows on Escarole in the United States and the World

host_range: TBSV can be transmitted mechanically to a wide range of plant species in 18 different botanical families ( Schmelzer, 1958 ). Systemic infections, characterized by stunting, mottling and malformation of the leaves, are induced in N. clevelandii and N. benthamiana. AMCV, like other tombusviruses, persists in the soil where it is likely to be acquired by healthy plants without the intervention of a vector. Highly infectious AMCV was recovered in large quantity from the soil of an artichoke field, at a site of a severe AMCV outbreak (Martelli et al., 1981). Sources of virus entry in the environment are likely to be crop debris and living roots from which infective virus is released in the soil. Local spread of AMCV can take place through vegetatively propagating artichoke (Martelli, 1981).
AMCV is not known to be seed transmitted.

host_range: More than 50 leguminous and a few non-leguminous species are susceptible to SbDV (Tamada, 1973; Ashby et al., 1979; Damsteegt et al., 1990). SbDV strains differ in host range and symptomatology. In general, SDV-Y causes more severe symptoms than SDV-D. Th
potential_eco_desc: SbDV causes a serious loss of soyabeans in Japan. Yield losses in soyabeans vary from mild to almost total loss depending on cultivar, virus strain, aphid density, plant age when infected, and environmental conditions. Inoculation tests showed that SDV-Y causes much more severe losses in major soyabean cultivars and lines than SDV-D (Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976). In naturally infected fields, for example, a 50% level of field infection results in a 40% reduction in yield, mostly through a reduction in the number of pods/plant (Tamada, 1975).^p^pIt is unknown whether SbDV is important for soyabean production in other countries. Damsteegt et al. (1990) reported that SbDV does not appear to pose an economic threat to soyabean production in the USA.^p^pIn Japan, SDV-Y causes a serious damage in common beans (Tamada, 1975; Mizukoshi et al., 1992). In Australia and New Zealand, SDV-SCRLV causes severe or mild yield loss in legume pastures such as subterranean clover and in grain legumes such as broad beans, lupins and peas (Wilson and Close, 1973; Johnstone, 1978; Ashby et al., 1979).
author: CPC2006

remark: There are no known quarantine restrictions on SbDV.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pWhite (Ladino) and red clover plants in perennial pastures provide the major sources of inocula, but it is difficult to remove such clover plants from a field. If soyabean plants can be grown in regions where no or few clover plants occur, the soyabeans may escape virus infection. ^p^pAltering the planting date may enable the crop to avoid the aphid vector. For example, soyabeans planted later usually suffer less from SbDV than those planted early in the season, because the migration of winged aphids is less later in the season (Tamada, 1975). Similar results have been obtained in the case of infection of SDV-SCRLV on broad beans (Johnstone and Rapley, 1979).^p^pMulching with silver polyethylene film reduced infection of kidney beans by SbDV in Hokkaido (Mizukoshi et al., 1992), so this measure may be applicable to soyabean fields.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pThe spread of SbDV is considerably inhibited by application of insecticides to the soil at planting time (Tamada, 1975). Insecticides may not always prevent infection by migration of infective alate aphids, because these insects can infect before they die; however, they can to a considerable extent prevent the secondary spread of virus within a field (Tamada, 1975). Thus, the success of chemical control measures depends on the relative importance of primary and secondary infection by SbDV.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pThe use of resistant or tolerant cultivars is an important way of controlling SbDV. There are considerable differences among soyabean varieties regarding the percentage of infection and the severity of symptoms, although no immunity to natural virus infection in fields was found in more than 2300 soyabean cultivars and lines (Tanimura et al., 1982). In general, cultivars and lines showing a high percentage of infection tend to develop more severe symptoms, which are closely correlated with the degree of yield loss. Soyabean varieties and lines Ohoujyu, Adams, Peking, Bavender SP-4, Bavender SP-7 and PI-90763 are relatively resistant to SbDV. They show only mild symptoms and rather small loss in yield (Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976). Cultivars with moderate resistance to SbDV, such as Tsurukogane (Tanimura and Banba, 1987), have been developed in a breeding programme by the Hokkaido Central Agricultural Experiment Station. These cultivars should be planted in areas such as Hokkaido, where the risk of infection by SbDV is high.

management_info:
SbDV的传播是很受抑制的通过杀虫剂对土壤的使用在种植时期(Tamada, 1975)。杀虫剂不可能总是防止侵染通过侵染性有翅蚜虫的迁移，因为这些昆虫可以在它们死之前侵染；然而，它们能到相当大的范围防止病毒的次要传播在田间内(Tamada, 1975)。这样，化学防治措施的成功取决于通过SbDV的主要和次要侵染的相对重要性。 The spread of SbDV is considerably inhibited by application of insecticides to the soil at planting time (Tamada, 1975). Insecticides may not always prevent infection by migration of infective alate aphids, because these insects can infect before they die; however, they can to a considerable extent prevent the secondary spread of virus within a field (Tamada, 1975). Thus, the success of chemical control measures depends on the relative importance of primary and econdary infection by SbDV. 抗病或耐抗栽培种的使用是控制SbDV的重要方法。虽然对于侵染的比例和症状的严重性在大豆品种之间有相当大的不同，但是对在田间的自然病毒侵染没有免疫性被发现于多于2300种大豆栽培种和系中(Tanimura et al., 1982)。一般地，显示高侵染比例的栽培种和系趋向发展更严重的症状，那些与产量损失的等级密切相关。大豆品种和系Ohoujyu， Adams， Peking，Bavender SP-4，Bavender SP-7和PI-90763 对SbDV有相对地抗性。它们仅呈现轻度症状和相当小的产量损失(Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976)。具对SbDV中抗性的栽培种，例如Tsurukogane (Tanimura and Banba, 1987)，已经发展于繁殖工程通过北海道中心农业试验所。这些栽培种应该被种植于像北海道这样的地区，在那里SbDV侵染的风险很高。 The use of resistant or tolerant cultivars is an important way of controlling SbDV. There are considerable differences among soyabean varieties regarding the percentage of infection and the severity of symptoms, although no immunity to natural virus infection in fields was found in more than 2300 soyabean cultivars and lines (Tanimura et al., 1982). In general, cultivars and lines showing a high percentage of infection tend to develop more severe symptoms, which are closely correlated with the degree of yield loss. Soyabean varieties and lines Ohoujyu, Adams, Peking, Bavender SP-4, Bavender SP-7 and PI-90763 are relatively resistant to SbDV. They show only mild symptoms and rather small loss in yield (Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976). Cultivars with moderate resistance to SbDV, such as Tsurukogane (Tanimura and Banba, 1987), have been developed in a breeding programme by the Hokkaido Central Agricultural Experiment Station. These cultivars should be planted in areas such as Hokkaido, where the risk of infection by SbDV is high. 白(Ladino)和红三叶在多年生植物草原里提供主要的接种原，但从田间移除这些三叶草植株是很困难的。如果大豆植株可以种植于没有或少数三叶草植株发生的地区，那么大豆可能逃出病毒侵染。
改变种植时间可能能够使作物避免蚜虫媒介。例如，种植于后期的大豆通常比那些种植于早期的遭受更少SbDV在季节里，因为有翅蚜虫的迁移在季节后期是比较少的(Tamada, 1975)。同样的结果已经获得于SDV-SCRLV侵染的实例中在豌豆上(Johnstone and Rapley, 1979)。
用聚乙烯薄膜护根减少菜豆被SbDV的侵染在北海道(Mizukoshi et al., 1992)，所以这种措施可能对大豆田间是有运用性的。 White (Ladino) and red clover plants in perennial pastures provide the major sources of inocula, but it is difficult to remove such clover plants from a field. If soyabean plants can be grown in regions where no or few clover plants occur, the soyabeans may escape virus infection.
Altering the planting date may enable the crop to avoid the aphid vector. For example, soyabeans planted later usually suffer less from SbDV than those planted early in the season, because the migration of winged aphids is less later in the season (Tamada, 1975). Similar results have been obtained in the case of infection of SDV-SCRLV on broad beans (Johnstone and Rapley, 1979).
Mulching with silver polyethylene film reduced infection of kidney beans by SbDV in Hokkaido (Mizukoshi et al., 1992), so this measure may be applicable to soyabean fields.
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc:
由SbDV引起的病害的发生率取决于病毒株系和地理分布。在日本，SDV-D在大豆仅引起矮缩，而SDV-Y在大豆引起矮缩和黄化。SDV-Y在法国菜豆里也引起黄化，而在蚕豆和豌豆引起轻度黄化(Tamada, 1973, 1975)。
在新西兰和澳大利亚，SDV-SCRLV引起地三叶草的叶变红(Kellock, 1971; Wilson and Close, 1973; Ashby et al., 1979)，豌豆的顶端黄化 (Johnstone, 1978)，矮缩菜豆的矮化和黄化，蚕豆的叶卷曲 (Ashby et al., 1979; Johnstone, 1978)和糖萝卜的黄化(Johnstone and Munro, 1980)。 The incidence of disease caused by SbDV depends both on the virus strain and geographical distribution. In Japan, SDV-D causes only dwarfing in soyabeans, whereas SDV-Y causes dwarfing and yellowing in soyabeans. SDV-Y also causes yellowing in French beans, and mild yellowing in broad beans and peas (Tamada, 1973, 1975).
In New Zealand and Australia, SDV-SCRLV causes leaf-reddening of subterranean clover (Kellock, 1971; Wilson and Close, 1973; Ashby et al., 1979), top-yellowing of peas (Johnstone, 1978), stunting and yellowing of dwarf beans, leaf rolling of broad beans (Ashby et al., 1979; Johnstone, 1978) and yellows of sugarbeet (Johnstone and Munro, 1980). SbDV造成大豆的严重损失在日本。在大豆里的产量损失由轻度的到几乎全部损失变化取决于栽培，病毒株系，蚜虫密度，侵染时的植株龄期，和环境条件。接种试验显示SDV-Y造成更加严重的损失在主要的大豆栽培种和系比SDV-D (Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976)。在自然受侵染的田间，例如，田间侵染的50%水平导致产量40%的减少，大多数通过荚/植株数量的减少(Tamada, 1975)。
SbDV在其他国家里对大豆生产是否重要是不知道的。Damsteegt et al. (1990) 报道SbDV没有明显地对大豆生产造成经济威胁在美国。
在日本，SDV-Y 在普通菜豆里造成严重损害(Tamada, 1975; Mizukoshi et al., 1992)。在澳大利亚和新西兰，SDV-SCRLV造成严重的或轻度的产量损失在豆科植物牧场里例如地三叶草和在谷粒豆科植物例如蚕豆，羽扇豆和豌豆(Wilson and Close, 1973; Johnstone, 1978; Ashby et al., 1979) SbDV causes a serious loss of soyabeans in Japan. Yield losses in soyabeans vary from mild to almost total loss depending on cultivar, virus strain, aphid density, plant age when infected, and environmental conditions. Inoculation tests showed that SDV-Y causes much more severe losses in major soyabean cultivars and lines than SDV-D (Tamada, 1975; Tanimura and Tamada, 1976). In naturally infected fields, for example, a 50% level of field infection results in a 40% reduction in yield, mostly through a reduction in the number of pods/plant (Tamada, 1975).
It is unknown whether SbDV is important for soyabean production in other countries. Damsteegt et al. (1990) reported that SbDV does not appear to pose an economic threat to soyabean production in the USA.
In Japan, SDV-Y causes a serious damage in common beans (Tamada, 1975; Mizukoshi et al., 1992). In Australia and New Zealand, SDV-SCRLV causes severe or mild yield loss in legume pastures such as subterranean clover and in grain legumes such as broad beans, lupins and peas (Wilson and Close, 1973; Johnstone, 1978; Ashby et al., 1979).

description:
SbDV通过蚜虫茄钩无网蚜以持续（循环）方式最有效地传播。环球无网蚜（Aulacorthum circumflexum）也是一种病毒的有效媒介昆虫但不可能是重要的在自然界(Helms et al., 1983)。而且，SbDV的一个或更多的株系被报道是通过豌豆蚜有效传播在澳大利亚(Johnstone and Guy, 1986)，美国(Johnstone et al., 1984)，日本 (Mikoshiba et al., 1996) 和叙利亚 (Makkouk et al., 1997)。这些豌豆蚜特定的株系通过茄钩无网蚜（Aulacorthum solani）低效地或无效地传播。这样，就有SbDV的媒介固定的株系。
SbDV被发现不通过其它试验的蚜虫种类传播，大豆蚜，苜蓿蚜， 棉蚜，桃蚜， 苜蓿无网蚜（Acyrthosiphon kondoi），大戟长管蚜和苜蓿彩斑蚜（Therioaphis trifolii f. maculata ）(Tamada, 1970, 1975; Kellock, 1971; Johnstone and Patten, 1981; Helms et al., 1983)。
SbDV的有效传播不同由于茄钩无网蚜的种群的地理的多样性(Damsteegt and Hewings, 1986)。SbDV的两种株系通过美国和新西兰种群比通过日本种群的更低效传播。 SbDV is most efficiently transmitted by the aphid Aulacorthum solani in the persistent (circulative) manner. Aulacorthum circumflexum is also an efficient vector of the virus but is unlikely to be important in nature (Helms et al., 1983). Furthermore, one or more strains of SbDV were reported to be efficiently transmitted by Acyrthosiphon pisum in Australia (Johnstone and Guy, 1986), the USA (Johnstone et al., 1984), Japan (Mikoshiba et al., 1996) and Syria (Makkouk et al., 1997). Such Acyrthosiphon pisum-specific strains are less or not efficiently transmitted by Aulacorthum solani. Thus, there are vector-specific strains of SbDV.
SbDV was found not to be transmitted by other aphid species tested, Aphis glycines, Aphis craccivora, Aphis gossypii, Myzus persicae, Acyrthosiphon kondoi, Macrosiphum euphorbiae and Therioaphis trifolii f. maculata (Tamada, 1970, 1975; Kellock, 1971; Johnstone and Patten, 1981; Helms et al., 1983).
The transmission efficiency of SbDV differs because of the geographical diversity of populations of Aulacorthum solani (Damsteegt and Hewings, 1986). Two strains of SbDV are transmitted less efficiently by the USA and New Zealand populations than the Japanese population.

management_info: As with most other virus diseases, control is best achieved by the propagation and planting of virus-tested material. ElLV is reported to be readily eradicated from infected elderberry by taking stem cuttings from the tops of plants kept at 38°C for several months (Ellis et al., 1992) and from pelargonium by thermotherapy for 3 weeks at 35°C followed by apical meristem tip culture (OM Stone, Glasshouse Crops Research Institute, Littlehampton, UK, unpublished data).

description: In 2015 and 2016, 203 samples of adzuki bean (Vigna angularis) exhibiting viral disease-like symptoms, such as mosaic, mottle, yellowing, dwarfing, and leaf rolling, were collected from 18 cities and counties in Korea. host_range: MNSV infects mainly cucurbits including melon (Cucumis melo), watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), and cucumber (Cucumis sativus) and causes necrotic spots on leaves, stems, and fruits as well as curled and wilted symptoms on leaves. In China, MNSV was first reported in melon in Jiangsu Province in 2008 and then occurred in Hami melon in Xinjiang Province in 2014. This is the first report of MNSV naturally infecting watermelon in China.
description: During October 2014, necrotic spots and curled symptom as well as mosaic, mottled, and/or crinkle symptoms occurred on watermelon(Citrullus lanatus) and melon(Cucumis melo) in greenhouses in Tai’an, Shandong Province, China. Based on molecular diagnostics showed watermelon be infected by Melon necrotic spot virus (MNSV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of MNSV naturally infecting watermelon in China.  Melon necrotic spot virus (MNSV) is naturally transmitted by the soil-inhabiting fungus Olpidium radicale and by seeds and can also be transmitted by mechanical inoculation.
reference_name: First Report of Melon necrotic spot virus in Watermelon in China

description: In May 2014, necrotic symptoms on leaves, stems, and fruits were observed in watermelon [Citrullus lanatus (Thomb.) Mansf. ‘Dulce maravilla’] produced in a commercial greenhouse from the province of Almeria, in Spain. Almost all plants from the greenhouse were severely affected, and over 80% died. The samples were collected and identified, the causal agent was identified as Melon necrotic spot virus (MNSV) by molecular diagnostics. MNSV affects melon crops worldwide and caused total loss of the melon crops in southeast Spain in the 1980s. A watermelon strain of MNSV that does not cause disease in melon has been described in Japan. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a watermelon strain of MNSV in Spain.
reference_name: First Report of a Novel Melon necrotic spot virus Watermelon Strain in Spain

description: 该病毒是机械地汁液传播的，尽管由于它们的蜡状物覆盖，和蚜虫的非持续方式，有时传播到韭菜的叶片具有一些困难。通过接触和通过植株处理传播是不可能的因为韭菜叶片被蜡状物覆盖且在汁液中试验的传播常常是很难的。LYSV已通过蚕豆蚜（Aphis fabae） (Verhoyen and Horvat, 1973) 和桃蚜（Myzus persicae ）(Bos et al., 1978a)以非持续方式试验上传播，但是无庸置疑地传播于自然界是通过非定居于葱属种类而暂时地探查于它们之上的多数的迁移的蚜虫种类。 The virus is mechanically sap-transmissible, although sometimes with some difficulty to leaves of leek because of their wax cover, and by aphids in the non-persistent manner. Transmission through contact and by plant handling is unlikely because the leek leaves are covered with wax and experimental transmission in sap is often difficult. LYSV has been transmitted experimentally by Aphis fabae (Verhoyen and Horvat, 1973) and Myzus persicae (Bos et al., 1978a) in the non-persistent manner, but is undoubtedly spread in nature by many migrant aphid species that do not settle on Allium species but briefly probe on them.
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc: 在韭菜中，黄条的发病率达到高水平。大多数关于大蒜花叶的发表报道大蒜100％病毒侵染。与麝香石竹潜隐病毒和螨传病毒一起，青葱黄矮病毒(OYDV)的蚜传的大蒜株系和LYSV现在被认为在接踵而至的损害中扮演着显著的角色。当测试许多的大蒜，野生大蒜和遍及全世界的起源的大头大蒜样品时，Van Dijk (1993a)发现它们中的45％含有LYSV-G而73％的含有OYDV-G。这两种病毒常常一起发生。大蒜作物常常呈现生长和发育缓慢，对此栽培者可能已习惯的且他们常常认为是正常的由于作物总的污染。 In leek crops, the incidence of yellow stripe may attain high levels.Most publications on garlic mosaic report 100% virus infection of garlic. Together with carlaviruses and mite-borne viruses, the aphid-borne garlic strains of onion yellow dwarf potyvirus (OYDV) and LYSV are now known to play a prominent role in the ensuing damage. When testing numerous samples of garlic, wild garlic and great-headed garlic of world-wide origin, Van Dijk (1993a) found 45% of them to contain LYSV-G and 73% to contain OYDV-G. The two viruses often occur together. Garlic crops often show poor growth and development, to which growers may have become accustomed and which they often accept as normal because of total infestation of the crop.

Garlic crops often show poor growth and development, to which growers may have become accustomed and which they often accept as normal because of total infestation of the crop. 邻近亚琛（德国）100％的植株常常被侵染(Kupke, 1957)。同样的被发现于秋季和冬季作物中在比利时(Verhoyen and Horvat, 1973)和荷兰(Bos et al., 1978a)在20世纪70年代。Verhoyen (1973)报道发病率的增加在比利时从1971年的40％增加到1972年的64％。在新西兰，几乎100％的植株被侵染在一种存储上(Mohamed and Young, 1980)。在韭菜中产量减少可能是相当大的(在德国29-54% Graichen, 1978b，和在比利时在两种栽培种中高达50％(Matthieu and Verhoyen, 1981)，且保存期限被减小(Bos et al., 1978a)。感病的植株产生更少的种子且萌芽为低于5-15%(Graichen, 1978b)。 Near Aachen (Germany) 100% of the plants were often infected (Kupke, 1957). The same was found in autumn and winter crops in Belgium (Verhoyen and Horvat, 1973) and the Netherlands (Bos et al., 1978a) in the 1970s. Verhoyen (1973) reported an increase in incidence in Belgium from 40% in 1971 to 64% in 1972. In New Zealand, nearly 100% of the plants were infected on one holding (Mohamed and Young, 1980). Yield reduction in leek may be considerable (29-54% in Germany, Graichen, 1978b, and up to 50% in two cultivars in Belgium (Matthieu and Verhoyen, 1981), and the shelf life was reduced (Bos et al., 1978a). Diseased plants produced less seed and germination was 5-15% lower (Graichen, 1978b).

management_info: 运用杀虫剂的昆虫防治对抗非持续的蚜虫传播的病毒是无效的，而用油喷射是太贵的且不被允许的对为人类消费而种植的作物而言。在整个韭菜生产的地区上抗韭菜的时期会打破生态学的侵染循环，但可能是很难执行的。 Insect control with insecticides is ineffective against non-persistently aphid-transmitted viruses, and spraying with oil is too expensive and not permitted for crops grown for human consumption. A leek-free period over an entire leek-producing area would break the ecological infection cycle, but may be hard to enforce.   生长于种子（例如，韭菜）或通过顶端分裂组织培养获得的抗病毒的营养种植材料（例如，大蒜）的作物应该被种植于从同种类的大批滋生的作物中空间的和/或时间的隔离。距离被侵染的作物的少数的数十米大大地降低侵染的影响范围，但成功取决于依据场所，年份的时间和天气条件而不同的蚜虫种群密度，且非持续的蚜虫传播的病毒可能被通过更远的距离携带。感病植株的清除可能降低再次传播在作物内。 Crops grown from seed (for example, leek) or from vegetative planting material obtained virus-free via meristem-tip culture (for example, garlic) should be grown in spatial and/or temporal isolation from infested crops of the same species. A few tens of meters from infected crops considerably reduces the incidence of infection, but success depends on aphid population densities which differ according to location, time of year and weather conditions, and non-persistently aphid-transmitted viruses may be carried over much longer distances. The removal of diseased plants may reduce secondary spread within the crop.

management_info: As HCRSV is disseminated in infected propagules, there is a need to produce, propagate and distribute virus-tested stocks of both natural hosts. management_info: Chemical Control^p^pChemical controls for molluscs have been widely used, and studies show that they can be effective. Types of chemical control include baits (Pappas and Carman., 1980; De Boodt et al., 1990; Barker et al., 1991); attractants, insecticide and molluscicides Gul and Chaudhry, 1980, 1981; Del Rivero, 1989; Schwartz and Capatos, 1990).^p^pLaboratory and field experiments have been conducted in Egypt to investigate the molluscicidal activity of weed extracts from Ambrosia martine, Citrullus colocynthis, Cymbopogon proximus and Glinus sp., and of five fertilizers, against H. aspersa. A. martine extract was shown to be the most toxic, followed by C. colocynthis and C. proximus, while Glinus sp. was the least effective. Snail mortality increased gradually with time. Some commonly used fertilizers showed considerable initial and residual molluscicidal effects. Ferrous sulfate was the most effective against H. aspersa, followed by ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulfate and superphosphate (Zidan et al., 1997).^p^pA new, patented copper complex, formulated as a spray and referred to as copper silicate, shows molluscicidal activity. The product was tested in both spray and granular formulations against H. aspersa in a vineyard and a citrus orchard in Western Australia, where it was compared with methiocarb baits and copper oxychloride spray. The copper complex spray demonstrated a high level of repellence to H. aspersa for extended periods in the field, and proved superior to the other products tested in reducing snail numbers in vines/trees. The product has potential in the management of pest molluscs, especially as part of IPM programmes (Davis et al., 1996).^p^p^Biological Control^p^pIn California, USA, the introduced carnivorous snail Rumina decollata is considered an important predator of H. aspersa (Fisher and Orth, 1985; Auffenberg and Stange, 1986). The rate of decollate snail dispersal depends on the amount of moisture present. Low-volume and sprinkler irrigation are most conducive to snail movement and development. Light supplemental irrigation may be desirable during the establishment of a colony. It is more difficult to establish decollate snails in groves that are irrigated by furrows. ^p^pA study by Altieri et al. (1982) was carried out in a daisy field in northern California to determine the effectiveness of the indigenous coleopterous predator Scaphinotus striatopunctatus in the biological control of H. aspersa. Release of the predator in the field under light metal sheets, together with colonization by garter snakes (Thamnophis elegans) from an adjacent field, resulted in a significant reduction in snail populations.^p^pFrom further investigations in the laboratory and field in California in 1975 on the biology of Staphylinus olens [Ocypus olens], a predator of snails that is of potential value in biological control, predacious behaviour by larvae on H. aspersa is described. Further investigations are necessary before the staphylinid can be reared in the laboratory in large numbers (Orth et al., 1975).^p^pIn South Africa, the native predacious gastropod Natalina cafra is under investigation as a potential biological control agent against H. aspersa, with special attention to the possibility of establishing a viable population of the natural enemy in captivity (Joubert, 1993).Uygun and Sekeroglu (1987) investigated the importance of predators and parasitoids as biological control agents for citrus pests, including H. aspersa.^p^pResearch carried out by the Entomology Division of the Plant Protection Department, Cukurova University, Turkey on the importation of predators and parasitoids as biological control agents (mainly for citrus pests) is described. Predators included a predator of H. aspersa, the coccinellid Hippodamia convergens (Uygun and Sekeroglu, 1987).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pDu Toit and Brink (1993) tested treatments for the control of H. aspersa, including copper sulfate, metaldehyde, methio

potential_eco_desc: O. sulcatus continues to be a serious pest of Taxus and hemlock trees (Tsuga), especially in nurseries in Connecticut, USA, and also attacks rhododendrons (Schread, 1966).^p^pSerious damage to Sansevieria trifasciata by O. sulcatus occurred in a horticultural nursery in Berlin, Germany, in 1967. Larval damage to the roots did not at first result in the visible withering of the leaves noted on less sturdy plants, but it was severe. The adults caused serious damage to the leaves, especially of the rosette-forming variety, causing heavy losses (Skadow and Karl, 1967).^p^pO. sulcatus caused injury to Concord grapes in south-central Washington, USA, by feeding on the berry pedicels and cluster stems. Injury resulted in reduced berry weight and loss of berries or portions of the cluster. Weekly counts on 20 tagged clusters provided estimates of loss (in tons/acre) for grapes grown in different cover-crop conditions; they were 3.36 for no cover crop, 3.45 for oats and vetch, 2.42 for lucerne, 3.08 for creeping red fescue (Festuca rubra), and 3.29 for F. rubra in combination with oats and vetch (Cone, 1963).^p^pIn tests in 1964-67, adults and eggs of O. sulcatus, a pest of Concord grapes in central Washington, USA, were placed in screened cages containing single Concord vines. It was found that 11 adults per cage resulted in complete defoliation and nearly complete fruit loss in the first season. The threshold of economic loss was 1-3 adults per plant per season. An index was developed for estimating root injury caused by larval feeding. The larvae fed first on the phloem tissue, girdling the roots, but the xylem was left intact, except in cases of severe injury. Vigour and fruit yield over a 3-year period were not significantly affected by root injury (Cone, 1968).^p^pAccording to Morris (1997), O. sulcatus is very highly polyphagous and a pest of house plants, garden, greenhouse and orchard crops, as well as vines (in continental Europe).^p^pO. sulcatus caused severe damage to blackcurrant and strawberry at Lincoln College, New Zealand, in 1974. Pruning of the roots of blackcurrant by the larvae significantly reduced cane growth, but had no significant effect on cane initiation. Strawberry plants in an infested bed were separable by visual assessment of leaf area as suffering no damage, moderate damage, severe damage or as dead, for which the numbers of larvae averaged 1.95, 8.35, 37.70 and 39.65/plant, respectively. For the first three classes of damage, there were significant correlations among the various plant factors examined, including leaf area, number of leaves and number of developing berries. Only within the moderate-damage class were there significant correlations between the numbers of weevils and the plant factors. In strawberries, economic loss will occur when there are 2-8 larvae/plant (Penman and Scott, 1976).^p^pO. sulcatus is an important horticultural pest in the Netherlands, especially in connection with arboriculture at Boscop, greenhouse crops at Aalsmeer and strawberry in North Brabant (Evenhuis, 1978).^p^pO. sulcatus is one of the most ubiquitous and damaging species in the genus. Larvae of these flightless, parthenogenetic species destroy roots; adults may cause unacceptable defoliation during 4 weeks of maturation feeding and a 3-month oviposition period. O. sulcatus is generally distributed in much of Europe and North America and in parts of Australia, New Zealand and Japan where it is an occasional pest of conifers in nursery production (Glover, 1989).^p^pIn Pistoia, Italy, economic damage was caused to Camellia japonica, Prunus laurocerasus, Azalea, Rhododendron and Taxus spp. by O. sulcatus (Bene and Parrini, 1986).^p^pO. sulcatus, together with other congeneric species, frequently causes serious problems in ornamental plant nurseries in central-northern Italy where it attacks various plants including Rhododendron, Cotoneaster, Prunus laurocerasus and Cryptomeria (Fregonese and Zandigiacomo, 1992).^p
author: CPC2006

management_info: Cultural Control^p^pIn Washington, USA, it was thought that mowing off strawberry fields after harvest would reduce populations of O. sulcatus. In 1975 and 1976, about 60% of adults died after the foliage was mowed off and removed; there was 0-12% mortality in unmowed plots (Garth and Shanks, 1978).^p^pIn the Dordogne, France, suggestions for prevention of O. sulcatus attacks include the use of healthy plants, careful soil preparation and crop rotation (Felici, 1981).^p^pSteinernema carpocapsae was applied to beds of Euonymus fortunei in an urban park in Philadelphia, USA to evaluate its potential for controlling O. sulcatus. Although no significant difference was attributed to nematode treatments, weevil damage in non-irrigated beds was lower than in irrigated beds. Irrigation management may be helpful for controlling this pest (Owen et al., 1991).^p^p^Biological Control^p^pThe parasitic nematode Heterorhabditis bacteriophora and the fungal pathogens Metarhizium anisopliae and Beauveria bassiana were used in a trial for the control of larvae of O. sulcatus in nursery Rhododendron stock in New Zealand in 1988. Larvae of the pest were added to planter bags containing Rhododendron plants and the control organisms were added 2 weeks later. After 5 weeks, H. bacteriophora, M. anisopliae and B. bassiana had achieved 93, 32 and 39% control, respectively (Barratt et al., 1989a).^p^pThree of five isolates of Heterorhabditis sp. and M. anisopliae controlled larvae of O. sulcatus on Thuja occidentalis in containers in the field in the Netherlands during September-October 1991. In open ground, two of three isolates of Heterorhabditis sp. tested were effective as was M. anisopliae. The efficacy of Heterorhabditis sp. was determined by soil temperature and antagonism in soil (van Tol, 1993).^p^pThe virulence of 10 isolates of M. anisopliae against larvae of O. sulcatus was examined in greenhouses on potted Begonia. The most virulent isolate, 275-86, reduced numbers of larvae by 86% compared with control (untreated) larvae (pots treated with 0.05% Triton X-100 only), and two other isolates reduced the larval population by 80%. Three isolates of M. anisopliae were examined further for their persistence in peat compost. All three strains reduced larval numbers on Begonia compared with the controls. The highest levels of control were recorded with strain 100-82 (67-80%), which was significantly more virulent than strain 35-79. Fungal drenches were most effective when they were applied 8 weeks before the application of eggs of O. sulcatus; however, significant levels of control were also recorded with fungal spores which were applied 16 weeks before the eggs. The results demonstrated that M. anisopliae has considerable potential as a biological control agent of O. sulcatus in greenhouses (Moorhouse et al., 1993).^p^pMortality of O. sulcatus larvae at 10, 15, 20 and 25°C following treatment with 100 million conidia/ml suspensions of six M. anisopliae isolates was temperature-dependent. In all cases, the LT50s (time taken to kill 50% of the test population) were inversely related to temperature, but the nature of this response varied between isolates. Strain 101-82 was the most virulent isolate at 25°C, with an LT50 of 3.7 days, but it was the least virulent isolate at 15°C and it failed to kill any O. sulcatus larvae at 10°C. In contrast, strain 159-83 had the lowest virulence at both 20 and 25°C, whereas it was the most virulent isolate at 10°C with an LT50 of 20 days. The mortality rates followed a similar pattern and were positively related to temperature in all cases with the exception of strain 159-83 at 25°C (Moorhouse et al., 1994).^p^pThree species of nematodes were tested in the field and greenhouse as potential biological control agents against O. sulcatus in British Columbia, Canada. Heterorhabditis heliothidis at doses of from 5000 to 20000 infective stages per 50 ml water reduced the numbers of O. sulcatus on potted strawberr

To our knowledge, this is the first report of IYSV infecting non-alliaceous hosts in Zimbabwe. It is also the first report of A. hybridus as a natural IYSV host anywhere in the world. description: Vector transmission^p^pINSV is propagatively transmitted only by the thrips (Thysanoptera, Thripidae) Frankliniella occidentalis (common name Western flower thrips), but not by Thrips tabaci or F. schultzei and F. intonsa (Wijkamp et al., 1995). All these thrips are able to transmit TSWV and other tospovirus species. Thrips must acquire the virus at the first-instar larval stage and transmission occurs mainly though adults. The virus replicates in thrips but there is no evidence of transovarial transmission. There are no studies on the long-distance movement of thrips and virus transmission. F. occidentalis is highly polyphagous, and thus may provide an efficient means of dispersal of the virus to new host plants.

management_info: Introduction^p^pThe rapid turnover of species and cultivars of ornamental crops pose problems for developing or selecting resistance. For any control approach, both virus and vector must be considered. For greenhouse crops extreme measures are necessary to avoid introduction of virus and thrips. This is not an easy task since movement of plants over long and short distances is common practice. Furthermore, F. occidentalis pupates in the soil and either viruliferous or healthy thrips may enter cultivations masked in this way. Accurate checking for both virus symptoms or signs of thrips damage is necessary. Good practice is to keep new plants in isolation for at least one week and observe them carefully for the appearance of virus symptoms and/or thrip damage. Virus incubation depends on the temperature but usually symptoms develop within about 10 days. Thrip presence may also be monitored by sticky blue traps. Petunia plants are also biological indicators of thrip presence, allowing distinction between healthy and viruliferous insects. If thrips are viruliferous, typical silvery scars will be followed by the appearance within a few days of necrotic lesions. The infected material must be destroyed carefully in a closed bag before wilting, avoiding the dispersal of thrips to other plants during handling. ^p^p^Vector control^p^pChemical control of thrips and in particular F. occidentalis is extremely difficult since populations easily develop resistance to insecticides (Helyer and Brobyn, 1992; for details of vector control see the data sheet on F. occidentalis). It is necessary to plan the alternate use of different chemicals to avoid rapid selection of resistant populations. If greenhouses are located in a warm area, it is necessary to provide nets to prevent thrips entering from outside (Daughtrey et al., 1997).

host_range: CSNV (as Chr 1) was first recognized on chrysanthemum in Sao Paulo State in Brazil (Duarte et al., 1995). It was later found on tomato in Minas Gerais State, Brazil (Nagata et al., 1998). It may also occur in other South American countries (Verhoeven et a
potential_eco_desc: In Brazil, CSNV is increasing in economic importance as it continues to spread to new geographical areas since 1997. It is expected to become widespread and important (Bezerra et al., 1999). Losses are difficult to determine as damage to chrysanthemum and tomato in Brazil due to CSNV has not been quantified. CSNV is now frequently detected on tomato, but had not reached epidemic proportions. No specific data are available on losses in tomato as there are apparently three tospovirus species present on this host in Brazil and their effects differ from region to region. However, experimental work suggests that CSNV could kill tomato plants in a few days. ^p^pThe potential impact elsewhere is difficult to estimate. Tomato and chrysanthemum are crops of major economic importance in Europe. The impact that CSNV would have on either of them is difficult to estimate, as statistics on crop losses from Brazil are not available. It could be expected to be substantial. In addition, it can be noted that the eradication campaign has already cost the Netherlands 25-30,000 EUR.

description: CSNV is transmitted only by its thrips vectors which can spread it between plants, fields or glasshouses in infested areas. In international trade, the virus could be disseminated over long distances in cuttings and other vegetative plants for planting. CSNV is known to have spread to the Netherlands in chrysanthemum cuttings imported from Brazil (Verhoeven et al., 1996) as well as to the UK by the same route (Mumford et al., 2003). These plants may not have shown symptoms at the time of dispatch. As a tospovirus, CSNV is unlikely to be seed-transmitted.Plant parts not known to carry the pest in trade/transport - True Seeds (inc. Grain).
author: CPC2006

remark: CSNV poses a significant threat to chrysanthemum and tomato crops in those parts of the EPPO region where its known vector Frankliniella occidentalis is present and widespread. CSNV causes a more severe disease on chrysanthemum than TSWV. In addition, F. schultzei, which is the major vector in Brazil (Bezerra et al., 1999), is present in glasshouses in the Netherlands and Belgium and has been reported in various southern countries of the EPPO region. The two geographically isolated outbreaks of CSNV in the Netherlands and the UK were both related to imported chrysanthemum cuttings from Brazil, which shows that there is a pathway for introduction (though no such direct pathway exists at the moment for tomato). CSNV also poses a threat to tomato cultivation under glass. Another danger is that, because symptoms of CSNV closely resemble those caused by TSWV, they could easily be mistaken by the grower for this virus in nurseries that already have a TSWV problem. Although isolated outbreaks of CSNV can be eradicated (this has been achieved successfully in the Netherlands and in UK), it is desirable to avoid any further importations from endemic countries.

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl of the disease is essentially targeted at eliminating or excluding the thrips vectors (Frankliniella occidentalis and F. schultzei). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pThrips are generally difficult to control with chemicals. They are very small and hard to detect; the pre-pupal and pupal stages survive in the soil and are difficult to treat. They have a high fecundity, which would hamper eradication in glasshouses. Resistance to the major classes of insecticides has also been reported in thrips. Resistance to insecticides is persistent (Lewis, 1997). ^p^p^Biological Control^p^pNo entirely reliable method of biological control of thrips has been identified. Predatory mites and insects and to a lesser degree pathogenic fungi have been used in glasshouses with varying degrees of success. It may in the future be possible to use hymenopteran parasitoids and parasitic nematodes (Jackson, 1997). ^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pGlasshouse hygiene, such as the eradication of weeds which may serve as thrips hosts, used in conjunction with chemical control measures, may reduce populations of the thrips vectors. Manipulation of the glasshouse environment to suit predators of biological control agents is a future possibility. Some growers report success in controlling F. occidentalis by heating the glasshouse to 30°C for 4-5 days and then washing down the structure with disinfectant (Lewis, 1997). Screens to prevent the entry of thrips into glasshouses and sticky traps within glasshouses have been used as control measures. ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pThere is no published information regarding resistance of chrysanthemum or tomato to CSNV. However, attempts have been made to develop CSNV-resistant tomato genotypes both by conventional breeding techniques (Lourencao et al., 2001; Lima et al., 2003) and by molecular genetic transfer (Rudolph et al., 2003).^p^p^Phytosanitary Measures^p^pCSNV was added to the EPPO A1 action list in 2003, and EPPO member countries are thus recommended to regulate it as a quarantine pest. So far, there are no specific phytosanitary measures to protect against the introduction of CSNV into the EPPO region. Tomato plants from outside the European and Mediterranean area are prohibited entry, as Solanaceae, into the EU (EU, 2000). Imported plants for planting of chrysanthemum are subject only to phytosanitary certification, and consideration could be given to requiring origin from tested mother plants, place of production freedom, or freedom from the vectors F. occidentalis and F. schultzei. In fact, since these thrips are polyphagous, freedom from them could be required for plants for planting of any herbaceous plant species from countries where CSNV occurs. Eradication of isolated outbreaks can be achieved by destruction of affected hosts and of the vector(s), but this is costly and difficult to implement in practice.

host_range: So far, only field peas and peanuts have been reported as fabaceous hosts of GRSV in Brazil. This is the first report GRSV infecting soybeans in Brazil, and soybean is a new host of GRSV.
potential_eco_desc: The overall disease incidence across the three fields was ≈5%.
description: In 2017, plants of soybean cultivar BRS 8180 RR were found exhibiting virus-like symptoms including apical mottling, mosaic, and chlorotic ringspots in three fields in Brasília–DF, Brazil. The overall disease incidence across the three fields was ≈5%. Leaf samples (with and without virus-like symptoms) were collected in all three fields. Based on serological assays and molecular diagnostics confirmed the presence of Groundnut ringspot tospovirus (GRSV). So far, only field peas and peanuts have been reported as fabaceous hosts of GRSV in Brazil. This is the first report GRSV infecting soybeans in Brazil, and soybean is a new host of GRSV.  The persistent presence of viruliferous thrips (mainly Frankliniella schultzei [Trybom]; Thysanoptera: Thripidae) and alternative hosts belonging to native flora, solanaceous weeds, and cultivated plant species around/within soybean-planting areas in central Brazil might increase the importance of orthotospovirus to the crop.
reference_name: First Report of Groundnut Ringspot Orthotospovirus Infecting Soybeans in Brazil

management_info: Adult flight activity is checked by Trap Test samplings. The Trap Test is activated by species-specific female sexual pheromone (Rotundo et al., 1986). Recent research underlined the low attraction ability of the commercial formulation of this pheromone (Speranza, 2000). New blends, with different percentages of pheromones and high attraction ability, have been tested with good results (Frerot et al., 1995). During the peak of the flight activity, treatments with different active ingredients, authorized on chestnut trees and with low environmental impact, can be carried out (Postner, 1978; Gal et al., 1987a, b). This kind of control is widely used in Europe, particularly in France, with pyrethroids as the active ingredient.^p^pNew methods of controlling this species are based on biological control. In Italy, promising results have been achieved using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana.^p^pAgronomic practices are still particularly successful at preventing overwintering larvae from sheltering in the soil. One of the most widely used practices is to put nets beneath the canopy just before fruit drop. In this way, the larvae can be easily killed by predators, parasitoids and abiotic agents, such as drought and low and high temperatures (Speranza, 1999). Another possibility is to pick up chestnut fruits when they drop; in this case the best results are obtained by mechanized harvesting because the entire product is harvested (Paparatti et al., 2000).

Economic impactGeldenhuys (1986) reports economic conflicts of interest in relation to the management of A. melanoxylon in South Africa as its control in areas where it has spread into semi-natural disturbed ecosystems is expensive (negative impact), its value as a timber species reduces exploitation of indigenous species (positive impact), and it performs additional services when it acts as a nurse tree during the restoration of disturbed native forest.^p^p^p^Environmental impactWeber (2003) reports changes in nutrient cycling as the result of deposition of large amounts of litter. This tree uses larger supplies of water than native vegetation so large thickets may change soil moisture conditions (Rutherford et al., 1986). The estimated water use of all the A. melanoxylon in South Africa  is estimated to be 21.8 million m3 per year (Anon., 2000). Geldenhuys (1986) cites research that suggests that A. melanoxylon is more prone to windfall than the dominant native forest species in South Africa, Olea capensis subsp. macrocarpa, and that increased disturbance events could promote further invasion by A. melanoxylon.^p^p^p^Impact on biodiversity^pThe dense thickets formed by A. melanoxylon shades out vegetation, which is out competed for supplies of water and light (Weber, 2003).^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>biodiversity; environment; rare / protected species; native flora^p^p(dayuhao)i>Positive impact on: (dayuhao)/i>forestry production
description: As an exotic, A. melanoxylon has been most extensively grown in India and South Africa, with plantations in New Zealand and several countries in South America (Gleason, 1986; Nicholas and Gifford, 1995). It is also common in the hill country (1400-2000 m) of Sri Lanka (Midgley and Vivekanandan, 1987) and in the high country (>1200 m) of East Africa (e.g. in Kenya and Tanzania) (Streets, 1962). It is regarded as good or promising in parts of China (Wang et al., 1994), in Guangdong surviving the cold at Hekou although killed by frost at Longdouxie (Yang et al., 1994).^p^pAccording to information collated by Le Floc'h (1991), A. melanoxylon was introduced to several countries in the western Mediterranean Basin in the 1800s and has subsequently naturalized in Algeria, France and Portugal. It appears listed as dangerous to natural ecosystems on a recently compiled list of plant invaders in Spain (Dana et al., 2004). It was introduced in the Knysna area of Cape Province, South Africa for the suppression of weeds in forest clearings in order to promote native vegetation, thus it is ironic that is has now become a weed in itself (Pryor, 1991). The species is also invasive in neigbouring Zimbabwe (Nyoka, 2002). In the USA, A. melanoxylon has become invasive in California and Hawaii and has naturalized in Hawaii since the 1980s (Luken and Thieret, 1997). Tunison (1991) classed the tree as potentially invasive in Hawaii as it has spread vegetatively in pine plantations in the Waikamoi Preserve, escaping into drainages in some areas. Tunison (1991) predicts that the species appears to rely on vegetative reproduction in Hawaii, but anticipates that if viable seed is produced and stored in the soil, potential large scale invasions are possible in the future. In California it is reported invasive on Catalina island (Knapp, 2002) and is also known to occur in the San Francisco bay area, in central coastal sites and on Santa Cruz island (California Exotic Pest Plant Council, 1999). It is one of a number of species for which California Exotic Pest Plant Council has identified a need for further information. According to Holm et al. (1979), A. melanoxylon is a weed of unspecified importance in New Zealand, a common weed in South Africa and a principal weed in Australia, though no further information regarding its weediness in Australia is forthcoming, but it is known to be beginning to become invasive in New Zealand.
author: CPC2006

description: Seeds may be dispersed by water and by avian vectors (Cronk and Fuller, 1995). The seed possesses large red funicles that are thought to be attractive to birds (Dean et al., 1986). South African birds known to disperse the seeds include Knysna loerie, Tauraco corythaix and the rameron pigeon, Columba arquatrix (Geldenhuys, 1986).^p^pForestry practice has been to plant the tree in gaps in logged forests, thus enabling it to establish in open forest and forest edges. Most invasive events have been associated with escape from plantations as the tree is well known as a timber species. A. melanoxylon has been widely introduced outside its native Australia and is now grown in Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.
author: CPC2006

remark: A. melanoxylon has become naturalized or invasive in a number of continents and is a particular problem in South Africa where it achieves much higher levels of seed production than in its native Australia. As it exhibits many invasiveness traits it is likely to be rejected by risk assessment before further introduction to similar climates, and existing plantations should be monitored for the first signs of invasive behaviour. In Hawaii, USA, the approach of quarantining trees within pine plantations, controlling the escape of suckers and monitoring for signs of viable seed production has been adopted.
author: CPC2006

management_info: On Hawaii, A. melanoxylon is quarantined inside pine plantations (with control of escaping root suckers) until the extent of potential reproduction and recruitment is more fully understood (Tunison, 1991). If attempting mechanical control, due to the ability of A. melanoxylon to reproduce vegetatively from root suckers it is important to remove the roots completely (Weber, 2003). Mature specimens may be felled in combination with the application of a herbicide to the stump to restrict resprouting (Weber, 2003). Large trees may also be killed by ring barking (Geldenhuys, 1986). On Hawaii the control of root sprouts has been prioritised (Tunison, 1991). In Waikamoi Preserve in Hawaii, garlon has been used experimentally on cut stumps (Tunison, 1991).^p^pA seed predating weevil Melanterius acaciae was tested for specificity for potential release in South Africa (Neser and Kluge, 1986) and was first released in 1985, and the Plant Protection Research Institute now releases this species for control where required (ARC, 2000), reporting that the weevils achieve more than 90% seed predation thus reducing the number of seeds that accumulate in the soil. Tunison (1991) comments that biological control is not yet required and would not be a viable control approach on Hawaii, USA.
author: CPC2006

host_range: C. leucostoma has a very narrow host range. Camellia spp. are the principal hosts, the most important of which is tea. Eurya spp., widely distributed in Assam, India, are heavily attacked by Cydia leucostoma (Das, 1957) and E. japonica is probably a host
potential_eco_desc: C. leucostoma is considered to be a pest only in India and Indonesia. In a severe outbreak, as many as 40% of the shoots are infested, causing a heavy crop loss. Severe infestation by C. leucostoma leads to a deterioration in the quality of black tea; infusions prepared from it are 'flat'. Murthy and Chandrasekaran (1979) reported an increase in the crude fibre content of teas prepared from shoots damaged by C. leucostoma.
author: CPC2006

remark: At present, C. leucostoma is known only from Asia and it is necessary to enforce phytosanitary measures to prevent it being spread by the transport of infested plant materials.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pIn Indonesia, several commercial tea cultivars have been screened for susceptibility to C. leucostoma infestation (Dharmadi and Sudjatmoko, 1981).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pInsecticides are seldom needed to control C. leucostoma. However, a large number of insecticides are effective against this species (Dharmadi, 1981; Muraleedharan, 1991; Das et al., 1992).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pCultural operations, such as harvesting, pruning and shade regulation, influence the numbers and abundance of C. leucostoma. Harvesting (plucking) the shoots every 8-10 days results in the manual removal of large number of shoots infested with C. leucostoma. In the first year after pruning, tea fields harbour a higher number of C. leucostoma than do older fields. Similarly, the population density of C. leucostoma is higher in unshaded tea fields.^p^p^Biological Control^p^pAlthough a large number of parasitoids and predators of C. leucostoma have been identified, no attempts have been made to introduce natural enemies to control it. In south India, parasitism by Apanteles aristaeus is as high as 17% (Muraleedharan et al., 1988). While studying the bioecology of A. aristaeus, Muraleedharan and Selvasundaram (1989) found a positive significant correlation between the percentage of parasitism by this species and the larval population density of C. leucostoma. The carabid Calleida nilgirensis is a common and voracious predator of C. leucostoma in south India (Muraleedharan et al., 1991).^p^p^Integrated Control^p^pUnder normal conditions, the population of C. leucostoma is controlled by the activities of indigenous natural enemies combined with manual removal.

management_info: Phytosanitary Measures^p^pMethyl bromide is effective (Gonzalez, 1980). Alternatively, irradiation with Cesium 137 may not provide 100% adult mortality, but eggs laid by irradiated females apparently do not hatch (Gerstle and Sazo, 1989).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pPolyethylene bands treated with azinphos-methyl and wrapped around the stems of grape plants and trellis stakes to a height of 1.3 m in mid-January can eliminate adults, and consequently eggs, from the vines Ripa, 1984, 1985, 1987). A band width of 4 cm reduced treatment costs by 32% compared with 16 cm-wide bands, and by 58% compared with the cost of conventional spray applications (Ripa and Berho, 1990). Re-application may be necessary if the accumulation of dust renders the bands no longer slippery (Ripa, 1984).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pIn Chile, compounds that have been used to control adults include dieldrin and carbofuran (Caballero, 1972).

description:
在自然界中，CMoV由蚜虫伞形花二尾蚜（Cavariella aegopodii）传播，但只能从也包含CtRLV的植物传播(Watson et al., 1964)。这是因为在单独的侵染中，CoMV的RNA不能变成被壳体包裹，而在与CtRLV一起的混合侵染中，它能通过CtRLV衣壳蛋白来包裹壳体(Murant et al., 1985)。CMoV的媒介关系因此与CtRLV的相同。联合体以持久（循环、非繁殖）方式传播通过C. aegopodii而不能通过百合西圆尾蚜（Anuraphis tulipae [Dysaphis tulipae]）、豌豆蚜（Acyrthosiphon pisum）、欧洲防风二尾蚜（Cavariella pastinacae）、肖鲍尔德二尾蚜（C. theobaldi）、茴香明蚜（Hyadaphis foeniculi）、桃蚜（Myzus persicae）或两个未经确认的长管蚜属品种传播(Stubbs, 1948; Watson et al., 1964; Murant, 1974; Waterhouse, 1981)。
Elnagar and Murant (1978a)发现，C. aegopodii需要一个大约30分钟的最小获取时间来获得CaRLV/CMoV复合，和大约两分钟的最小获取时间来接种病毒。最小的潜伏时间大约是6－8个小时(Watson et al., 1964; Elnagar and Murant, 1978a)。蚜虫在蜕皮之后(Stubbs, 1955; Watson et al., 1964; Elnagar and Murant, 1978a)和至少12连续的每天传播后(Elnagar and Murant, 1978a)继续传毒。没有证据说明病毒在蚜虫内的繁殖或病毒能传播到带病毒蚜虫的后代去(Elnagar and Murant, 1978a, b)。该病毒通过注入带病毒蚜虫的汁液的蚜虫传播(Elnagar and Murant, 1978b)。
Waterhouse and Murant (1983)从血清学中和和其他类型的实验中提出证据证明证明，CtRLV和CMoV的混合侵染中，一些包含CMoV RNA部分被壳体包裹或全部在CtRLV衣壳蛋白的粒子被产生，这使长期被假定的东西得到确定(Elnagar and Murant, 1978b)。Waterhouse and Murant (1983)也显示，当CMoV在与甜菜西方黄化病毒或马铃薯卷叶病毒的混合侵染中被建立时，它就能通过这两个病毒的媒介桃蚜（Myzus persicae）来传播。这说明这些病毒的衣壳蛋白能被在用壳体包裹CMoV RNA中的CtRLV代替，因此给予该病毒它们特有的媒介专化性。
CMoV可通过人工接种传播，而CtRLV不能。CMoV因此在一个单一的人工接种过程后不再是蚜虫传播的。单独受CMoV侵染的叶片含有丰富的借助苯酚可提取出的传染性的单链RNA(Watson et al., 1964;Murant et al., 1969, 1973)。然而，在从单独受CMoV侵染的叶片中提取的缓冲物的侵染性是非常的稳定的，能在室温下存活几个小时，虽然它对结冰和融化以及对有机溶剂的处理非常的敏感(Murant et al., 1969)。这说明，至少一些的受感染的RNA在直径52nm的限制膜结构中受到保护，这能在细胞中以及在经部分净化的制备中观察得到(Murant et al., 1969, 1973)。Murant et al. (1973) 显示克利夫兰烟（Nicotiana clevelandii）叶片提取液在PH8.8的缓冲剂中包含一个侵染性的‘稳定’形态（对胰腺核糖核酸酶有抗性）和一个侵染性的‘不稳定’形态，当PH调整到7时，其受到破坏。不稳定形态在系统侵染的早期占优势（植物接种后5－7天），之后降低，而稳定形态的比例增加，在9天后当直径52nm膜结构在细胞中也会到达最高峰时到达最大值。 In nature, CMoV is transmitted by the aphid Cavariella aegopodii, but only from plants that also contain CtRLV (Watson et al., 1964). This is because in single infections, the RNA of CMoV does not become encapsidated, whereas in mixed infections with CtRLV it becomes encapsidated by CtRLV coat protein (Murant et al., 1985). The vector relations of CMoV are therefore the same as those of CtRLV. The complex is transmitted in a persistent (circulative, non-propagative) manner by the aphid C. aegopodii, but not by Anuraphis tulipae [Dysaphis tulipae], Acyrthosiphon pisum, Cavariella pastinacae, C. theobaldi, Hyadaphis foeniculi, Myzus persicae or two unidentified species of Macrosiphum (Stubbs, 1948; Watson et al., 1964; Murant, 1974; Waterhouse, 1981).
Elnagar and Murant (1978a) found that C. aegopodii require a minimum access time of ca 30 min to acquire the CaRLV/CMoV complex, and a minimum access time of ca 2 min to inoculate the viruses. The minimum latent period is 6-18 h (Watson et al., 1964; Elnagar and Murant, 1978a). The aphids continue to transmit after moulting (Stubbs, 1955; Watson et al., 1964; Elnagar and Murant, 1978a) and after at least 12 serial daily transfers (Elnagar and Murant, 1978a). There is no evidence for multiplication of the viruses in the aphid, nor are they transmitted to the progeny of viruliferous aphids (Elnagar and Murant, 1978a, b). The viruses were transmitted by aphids that had been injected with extracts of viruliferous aphids (Elnagar and Murant, 1978b).
Waterhouse and Murant (1983) presented evidence from serological neutralization and other types of experiment that, in mixed infections of CtRLV and CMoV, some particles are produced that contain CMoV RNA encapsidated partially or entirely in the coat protein of CtRLV, confirming what had long been supposed (Elnagar and Murant, 1978b). Waterhouse and Murant (1983) also showed that when CMoV was established in mixed infection with beet western yellows luteovirus or potato leafroll luteovirus, it became transmissible by Myzus persicae, the vector of these two viruses. This suggests that the coat proteins of these viruses can substitute for that of CtRLV in encapsidating CMoV RNA, and thereby confer on it their own vector specificities.

potential_eco_desc: Groundnut rosette disease is important only in sub-Saharan Africa, where it is by far the most destructive of all groundnut diseases. The disease is not prevalent every year, and its unpredictability is one of its most harmful aspects. When epidemics occur they can be devastating. Thus in 1975 rosette destroyed 0.7 million hectares of groundnut in Nigeria (Yaycock et al., 1976), causing yield losses estimated at over 0.5 million tonnes. Groundnut rosette disease decreased plant height and spread 12 weeks after sowing by 40 and 48%, respectively. Leaf, stem and root dry matter at 8 weeks after sowing were decreased by 73, 81 and 88%, respectively. The number of leaflets/plant was reduced, the LAI was reduced from 1.0 in 1974 to 0.2 in 1975, the number of mature pods/plant was reduced by 80%. The shelling percentage decreased from 65.8-76.4% to 39.3-41.3% and pod yield was reduced from 2.29-2.8 6 t/ha to negligible amounts (Yayock, 1977).^p^pIn Zambia in 1995, losses were estimated at 5 million (Naidu et al., 1998b; P. Subrahmanyam, personal communication).^p^pLosses due to groundnut rosette have also been reported from India. In Tamil Nadu, a survey revealed that rosette was found in 10 districts. The disease incidence was 4.92% in bunch and 3.26% in spreading varieties of groundnut and was nearly twice as high in irrigated as in rainfed crops. The loss in yield varied from 27 to 100%. Maximum infection was found when the crop was 75 days old (Kousalya et al., 1973).

potential_eco_desc: RTBV is widely distributed in rice-growing areas in South and South-East Asia, and in southern China, where rice is the staple food. Tungro is the major threat to stable rice production in irrigated areas in South and South-East Asia (Hibino, 1989; Thresh, 1991; Bos, 1992). It has become increasingly important since the mid-1960s; major outbreaks occurred in 1969 and thereafter repeatedly in many countries (Hibino, 1989). ^p^pTungro became a serious problem after the release of high-yielding rice cultivars which are short statured and photo-insensitive, have shorter growth duration, and allow rice growers two crops of rice in a year. Staggered planting under the double-cropping rice systems is the major reason why tungro disease predominated after the 1960s. The genetic uniformity of rice planted after the introduction of such cultivars has also had an effect (Thresh, 1991; Bos, 1992; Hibino, 1995).^p^pRice production in these regions relies largely on irrigated areas where tungro is endemic; its incidence is low or nil in rainfed or upland rice fields. When it reaches epidemic proportions, tungro is disastrous and can damage rice fields in a huge acreage even in rainfed or upland areas (Hibino, 1989; Thresh, 1991; Bos, 1992). Tungro spreads fast even in fields where the vector population is not too high; rice is often totally damaged in one area.^p^pRTBV does not occur as an independent disease, but is associated with its helper virus rice tungro spherical waikavirus (RTSV). Together they cause rice tungro disease. RTBV causes the tungro symptoms, while RTSV does not cause any distinct symptoms except mild plant stunting. However, it does enhance the symptoms caused by RTBV (Hibino et al., 1978). ^p^pUnder experimental conditions, yield loss due to tungro infection was 20-100% depending on the cultivars tested (Lin and Palomar, 1966; Hino et al., 1972; Chowdhury and Mukhopadhyay, 1975; Srinivasan, 1979; Rao and Anjaneyulu, 1980; John and Ghosh, 1981; Rao et al., 1983; Yadaf and Mishra, 1985). In an experiment using rice plants infected with RTBV and RTSV separately or together, yield reduction was 18-97% in RTBV and RTSV infected plants and 16-91% in RTBV alone infected plants (Hasanuddin and Hibino, 1989). Thus, losses due to tungro are largely due to RTBV infection.^p^pRice tungro disease is one of the most destructive diseases of rice in the Asian tropics. The incidence of tungro is generally high in irrigated areas, where rice is planted throughout the year. It is generally endemic but occasionally becomes epidemic and causes devastating losses over huge areas. Tungro has caused average annual losses of more than US$ 1500 million (Herdt, 1988).^p^pTungro-like diseases have been known to occur in Indonesia since 1859, in Malaysia since 1938, and in the Philippines since 1940 (Ou, 1985) before the viral nature of tungro disease was reported (Rivera and Ou, 1965). At least some of these diseases are now considered to be tungro disease.^p^pIn India, tungro reached an epidemic level in West Bengal, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh in 1969, and in Kerala in 1973-1974 (Anjanyulu et al., 1994). In 1981, a high incidence of tungro was recorded in Bihar and West Bengal (Singh et al., 1982), and in Andhra Pradesh, Orissa and West Bengal 90,000 ha of land were affected (Anjyanyulu, 1994). In 1984-1985, a tungro outbreak occurred in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. The area damaged was 30,000 ha with an estimated yield loss of 20,000 t in Tamil Nadu (V. Mariappan, personal communication, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore, India); 49,000 ha were affected in Andhra Pradesh (G. Venkata Rao, personal communication, Andhra Pradesh Agricultural University, Hyderabad, India). In 1998, an outbreak of tungro-like yellow stunt syndrome occurred in the Punjab and damaged 40,000 ha of the 490,000 ha planted to rice in the area (Azzam et al., 1999). remark: RTBV is widely distributed in the major rice-growing areas in the Asian tropics and partly in the subtropics; its distribution corresponds with that of the principal vector Nephotettix virescens. RTBV is not considered to be of quarantine importance in temperate countries and in most parts of subtropical Asia: because rice is not planted in the winter season, rice stubbles carrying tungro disease do not overwinter, and the population of N. virescens (monphagous to rice) is not high or absent. If tungro is introduced in the early crop season in those areas, the disease may cause local damage to rice produced in that season, because vector species other than N. virescens may predominate in those areas.

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl measures are required in irrigated areas where rice planting is staggered in time.^p^p^IPM Programmes^p^pAn integrated management scheme has been practised in South Sulawesi, Indonesia (Sama et al., l991). The scheme has four components: planting two crops in the months when the vector population is low; scheduled planting to ensure nearly synchronous growth in each area; rotation or deployment of cultivars with different degrees of resistance to the vector Nephotettix virescens; and applying insecticide to reduce vector density in fields that are affected with tungro. Tungro incidence has been low during the scheme: this may be explained by the slow rate of vector population increase and the few or no sources of tungro in the area.^p^p^Chemical Control^p ^pInsecticide may be applied to reduce the vector population and thus manage tungro (Heinrichs, 1979). Economic thresholds based on the vector population are of little practical value in control (Heinrichs, 1979); tungro spreads fast even when the vector population is relatively low, and thus the threshold is low if tungro virus(es) are present in nearby fields. ^p^pIn areas where tungro is endemic, insecticide application gives limited control in susceptible cultivars, better control in moderately resistant cultivars, and is not required for resistant cultivars. ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pRice cultivars with resistance to the vector N. virescens are planted widely in South and South-East Asia (Khush and Virmani, 1985). Such cultivars exhibit little or no tungro (Hibino et al., 1987). In many locations, however, many vector-resistant cultivars that formerly had a little tungro have had severe tungro after a few years of intensive cultivation (Hibino, 1995). The breakdown of resistance is thought to result from the development of a vector population that overcame the resistances Dahal et al., 1990, 1997). management_info: 杀虫剂可能被运用来减少媒介昆虫的种群数而这样管理东格鲁病害(Heinrichs, 1979)。基于媒介昆虫种群数的经济阈值在防治中的实用价值很低(Heinrichs, 1979)，甚至当媒介昆虫种群数相对较低时，东格鲁传播很快，而这样如果东格鲁病毒是存在于附近田间的，那么阈值是较低的。 Insecticide may be applied to reduce the vector population and thus manage tungro (Heinrichs, 1979). Economic thresholds based on the vector population are of little practical value in control (Heinrichs, 1979); tungro spreads fast even when the vector population is relatively low, and thus the threshold is low if tungro virus(es) are present in nearby fields. 具抵抗二点黑尾叶蝉的水稻栽培种被广泛种植于南亚和东南亚地区(Khush and Virmani, 1985)。这些栽培显示很少或没有东格鲁病害(Hibino et al., 1987)。 Rice cultivars with resistance to the vector N. virescens are planted widely in South and South-East Asia (Khush and Virmani, 1985). Such cultivars exhibit little or no tungro (Hibino et al., 1987). 综合管理方案在南苏拉威西，印度尼西亚已经被实行(Sama et al., l991)。这个方案有四个部分：在媒介昆虫的种群数较低的月份种植双季作物，定期种植保证每个地区几乎同步生长发育，对媒介昆虫二点黑尾叶蝉的抗性的不同等级的栽培种轮作或调配，运用杀虫剂减少在受东格鲁感染的田间的媒介昆虫的密度。东格鲁的发病率在这种方案期间已经被降低，这可能解释为媒介昆虫种群比例缓慢增长和这些地区很少或没有东格鲁病原。 An integrated management scheme has been practised in South Sulawesi, Indonesia (Sama et al., l991). The scheme has four components: planting two crops in the months when the vector population is low; scheduled planting to ensure nearly synchronous growth in each area; rotation or deployment of cultivars with different degrees of resistance to the vector Nephotettix virescens; and applying insecticide to reduce vector density in fields that are affected with tungro. Tungro incidence has been low during the scheme: this may be explained by the slow rate of vector population increase and the few or no sources of tungro in the area.

description:
RTBV不能机械传播而是通过叶蝉（半翅目叶蝉科）传播(Hibino et al., 1979; Hibino, 1983a; Khan et al, 1991)。它们是二点黑尾叶蝉，二条黑尾叶蝉、黑尾叶蝉、马来亚黑尾叶蝉、N. parvus和电光叶蝉。二点黑尾叶蝉是最有效的媒介昆虫且是南亚及东南亚东格鲁病害最重要媒介昆虫。
RTBV不是独自通过叶蝉传播的。叶蝉传播发生于受RTBV和RTSV一起侵染的植物，而不是仅来自受RTBV侵染的植物(Hibino et al., l978)。仅当叶蝉已暴露于受RTSV侵染的植物，叶蝉能从受RTBV侵染的植物获得RTBV病毒(Hibino, 1983b; Cabauatan and Hibino, 1985)。这依赖RTSV与产生于受RTSV侵染的植物的辅助成分有关(Hibino, 1983b; Cabauatan and Hibino, 1985; Hibino and Cabauatan, 1987)。 RTBV is not mechanically transmissible and is transmitted by leafhoppers (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) (Hibino et al., 1979; Hibino, 1983a; Khan et al, 1991). They are Nephotettix virescens, N. nigropictus, N. cincticeps, N. malayanus, N. parvus and Recilia dorsalis. N. virescens is the most efficient vector and it is also the most important vector of tungro disease in South and South-East Asia. 
RTBV is not transmitted by the leafhoppers on its own. Leafhopper transmission occurs from plants infected with RTBV and RTSV together, but not from plants infected with RTBV alone (Hibino et al., l978). A leafhopper can acquire RTBV from plants that are infected with RTBV alone only when it has already been exposed to RTSV-infected plants (Hibino, 1983b; Cabauatan and Hibino, 1985). This dependence on RTSV is related to the presence of a helper component produced in RTSV-infected plants (Hibino, 1983b; Cabauatan and Hibino, 1985; Hibino and Cabauatan, 1987).

remark: SVBV is listed as an A2 quarantine pest by EPPO (OEPP/EPPO, 1978) and is also of quarantine significance for IAPSC. The most important factors in evaluating the potential of SVBV in a new area are the presence of aphid vectors and their mobility. Because of the range of vector species, conditions can be defined only in so far as they affect aphids in general. For example, extremely low winter temperatures killing overwintering nymphs and adults; windy climates restricting activity of alatae. ^p^pPhytosanitary Measures^p^pEPPO (EPPO, 1990) recommends that importing countries can require that Fragaria ananassa plants for planting, from countries where the pest occurs, should be derived from mother plants tested and found free from SVBV during the last three growing seasons and should have been maintained under conditions preventing their reinfestation; the consignment must come from a field found free (in the immediate vicinity) of the virus during the last growing season.

management_info: There are no specific control measures. SVBV is highly resistant to inactivation by heat therapy but it can be eliminated from plants by means of meristem tip culture. As a consequence, the use of certified planting material is the best control procedure, and certification schemes for the production of healthy planting material of strawberry are in operation in several EPPO countries. EPPO is at present (November 2000) preparing an internationally acceptable certification scheme for strawberries. Control of aphids with insecticides could reduce the incidence of the disease.^p^pElimination of the virus from mother plants by runner tip culture (Miller and Belkengren, 1963) or by heat treatment for 10 days at 42°C (Bolton, 1967) has been reported. The elimination of the type strain of SVBV from experimentally infected Hood plants by meristem tip culture was 100% whether or not the plants were preheat treated for 6 weeks at 37°C (Mullin and Schlegel, 1978). In these tests, the cultured plants were indexed and discarded after 6 months. This could prove to be an insufficient incubation period for cloned meristems, as some dahlia plants similarly treated to eliminate dahlia mosaic virus remained symptomless for up to 10 months (Mullin and Schlegel, 1978).

通过匍匐尖端培养或通过10天里在42℃的热处理(Bolton, 1967)的母系植株的病毒的消除已经被报道。来自于通过分生组织尖端培养的实验性地受侵染的Hood植株的SVBV的典型株系的消除是100％植株在6周内在37℃是否被预热处理(Mullin and Schlegel, 1978)。在这些试验中，培养的植株被表明和被丢弃在6个月后。这能证明是不适合的接种期就无性分生组织而言，因为一些大丽花植株同样地被处理以消除保持无症状多达10个月的大丽花花叶病毒(Mullin and Schlegel, 1978)。 There are no specific control measures. SVBV is highly resistant to inactivation by heat therapy but it can be eliminated from plants by means of meristem tip culture. As a consequence, the use of certified planting material is the best control procedure, and certification schemes for the production of healthy planting material of strawberry are in operation in several EPPO countries. EPPO is at present (November 2000) preparing an internationally acceptable certification scheme for strawberries. Control of aphids with insecticides could reduce the incidence of the disease.
Elimination of the virus from mother plants by runner tip culture (Miller and Belkengren, 1963) or by heat treatment for 10 days at 42℃ (Bolton, 1967) has been reported. The elimination of the type strain of SVBV from experimentally infected Hood plants by meristem tip culture was 100% whether or not the plants were preheat treated for 6 weeks at 37℃ (Mullin and Schlegel, 1978). In these tests, the cultured plants were indexed and discarded after 6 months. This could prove to be an insufficient incubation period for cloned meristems, as some dahlia plants similarly treated to eliminate dahlia mosaic virus remained symptomless for up to 10 months (Mullin and Schlegel, 1978).

description:
Acyrthosiphon pelargonii，Amphorophora rubi，A. idaei，Aphis idaei，叶悬钩子蚜（A. rubifolii），茄沟无网蚜(Aulacorthum solani)，草莓钉蚜（Chaetosiphon fragaefolii），杰氏中瘤钉毛蚜（C. jacobi），四红中瘤钉毛蚜（C. tetrarhodum），汤穆中瘤钉毛蚜（C. thomasi），蔷薇长管蚜(Macrosiphum rosae)，M. pelargonii，冬葱瘤额蚜（Myzus ascalonicus），饰瘤蚜（M. ornatus）和桃蚜（M. persicae）都是SVBV的媒介昆虫。虽然这些中瘤钉毛蚜属种类在温室实验里是最有效的媒介，但是其它种类可能是重要的媒介当它们大量地发生且频繁地从植株移动到另一植株时。蚜虫在30-120分钟内能获得和传播病毒，但持续在媒介昆虫很短时间，通常少于8小时（半持久性类型）。蚜虫的无性品系的效率不同，且那些种类仅会传播SVBV的某些株系是有证据的。棉蚜（Aphis gossypii），蚕豆蚜（A. fabae），茄沟无网蚜（Aulacorthum solani）和马铃薯长管蚜（Macrosiphum euphorbiae）在有限数量的实验里传播不成病毒。
SVBV通过嫁接和微内藏菟丝子（Cuscuta subinclusa）传播。试图机械传播SVBV还未成功。在指示寄主里得潜伏期从2到5周变化决定于株系。 Acyrthosiphon pelargonii, Amphorophora rubi, A. idaei,  Aphis idaei, A. rubifolii, Aulacorthum solani, Chaetosiphon fragaefolii, C. jacobi, C. tetrarhodum, C. thomasi, Macrosiphum rosae, M. pelargonii, Myzus ascalonicus, M. ornatus and M. persicae are vectors of SVBV. Of these, Chaetosiphon species are the most efficient vectors in glasshouse experiments, although other genera are probably important vectors when they occur in large numbers and frequently move from plant to plant. Aphids can acquire and transmit the virus in 30-120 minutes, but persistence in the vector is short, usually less than 8 h (semipersistent type). There are differences in the efficiency of clonal lines of aphids, and evidence that some species will transmit only certain strains of SVBV. Aphis gossypii, A. fabae, Aulacorthum solani and Macrosiphum euphorbiae failed to transmit the virus in a limited number of trials.
SVBV is transmissible by grafting and by Cuscuta subinclusa. Attempts to transmit SVBV mechanically have been unsuccessful. The incubation period in the indicator host varies from 2 to 5 weeks depending on the strain.
