host_range: Dahlia mosaic virus (DMV) has been shown to infect 25 species from four families (Solanaceae, Amaranthaceae, Chenopodiaceae, and Compositae); however, only dahlias (Dahlia variabilis) were found naturally infected. Chili pepper had been reported as an experimental host for DMV.
description: In 2013, 10 chili pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) plants exhibiting symptoms of chlorotic and mild upward leaf curling were observed in a field in Changsha, Hunan Province, China. The samples were collected and identified, in both serological and molecular methods showed that the pathogen was Dahlia mosaic virus (DMV). DMV has been shown to infect 25 species from four families (Solanaceae, Amaranthaceae, Chenopodiaceae, and Compositae); however, only dahlias (Dahlia variabilis) were found naturally infected. Chili pepper had been reported as an experimental host for DMV, this is the first report of it as a natural host of DMV. This may have epidemiological consequences for chili pepper, which is planted worldwide. The molecular characterization and pathogenicity of DMV in chili pepper are under investigation.
reference_name: First Report of Chili Pepper (Capsicum annuum) as a Natural Host Plant for Dahlia mosaic virus

management_info: Cultural Control^p^pThe most important control procedure is to limit or prevent virus infection of seedlings in seedbeds, because the effects of infection are greater when seedlings are infected at a young stage, and infected seedlings are the most important source of infection within a crop (Pound, 1946; Broadbent, 1957). Infection can be minimized by establishing seedbeds in isolation from susceptible crops or, if this is impractical on small farms, by surrounding the seedbeds with a barrier of cereals (mixture of barley and oats) or, if the costs are justifiable, by growing the seedlings under insect-proofed conditions such as fine-meshed cages. It is suggested that seedbeds should be no wider than 12 rows if barriers are used and, if wider, should have barriers at 12-row intervals (Broadbent, 1957). ^p^pSeedbeds should be sprayed with insecticide when aphids are numerous to minimize spread.^p^pWhen seedlings are transplanted in the field, those from the outer rows of the seedbed and any with virus-like symptoms should be discarded (Broadbent, 1957).^p^pEarly roguing of any infected plants can reduce subsequent spread significantly (Caldwell and Prentice, 1942b).^p^pIn areas where CaMV is endemic and causes severe annual epidemics, the culture of an intervening immune crop can sometimes break the infection cycle. ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pBrassica cultivars that are resistant and/or tolerant to infection are available. If valuable Brassica breeding material becomes virus-infected, virus-free plants can be readily obtained by meristem tip culture (Walkey et al., 1974).^p^pAlthough not yet available for commercial use, transgenic virus-resistant plants have been produced for experimental use.^p^p^Mild Strain Cross Protection^p^pMild strains of CaMV have been produced and shown to be potentially useful in protecting inoculated plants from the effects of severe virus strains (Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978).  ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pInsecticidal treatment of seedbeds is beneficial or preventative when aphid populations are high. Although insecticidal sprays are unlikely to limit much spread in growing crops, they can on occasions be beneficial in limiting the number of aphids available to carry virus to seedbeds.

potential_eco_desc: 当流行的时候，CaMV引起十字花科作物的质量和产量的严重损失(Caldwell and Prentice, 1942b; Broadbent, 1957)；例如，该病毒在法国布列塔尼引起可销售的花椰菜头25-59％的损失(Kerlan et al., 1989)，在捷克共和国，分别引起芜菁和芜菁甘蓝鲜重超过60％和90％的损失(Kerlan et al., 1989)。该病毒被认为在世界范围内的许多国家中都有主要的重要性(Tomlinson, 1987)。 When prevalent, CaMV can cause severe losses of quality and yield of Brassica crops (Caldwell and Prentice, 1942b; Broadbent, 1957); for example, the virus can cause 25-59% loss of marketable cauliflower heads in Brittany, France (Kerlan et al., 1989), and up to 60 and 90% of turnip and turnip rape fresh weight, respectively, in the Czech Republic (Spak, 1989a). The virus is considered to be of major importance in many countries worldwide (Tomlinson, 1987).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
该病毒的多数分离种是通过甘蓝蚜（Brevicoryne brassicae）、桃蚜（Myzus persicae）和至少25个其他的蚜虫种以半持久的方式传播的(Kennedy et al., 1962)。
蚜虫能在感染植物上取食1-2分钟后获得病毒，其后在1分钟之内把病毒传播到健康植物中去。然而，不像由蚜虫以非持久方式传播的病毒，带病毒的蚜虫在取食和16-72个小时的禁食期间能保持它们传播病毒的能力达3-8个小时(Hamlyn, 1955; Day and Venables, 1961; Chalfont and Chapman, 1962; Namba and Sylvester, 1981; Markham et al., 1987)。一些株系通常不能由蚜虫传播；然而，长时间已知的是，蚜虫的传播能力是由一个引起蚜虫传播的因素的存在所决定的(Lung and Pirone, 1973, 1974)，这因素被鉴定为开放阅读框架II的蛋白质产物（见鉴定）。不可传播分离种如果它们允许通过在受蚜虫传播分离种侵染的植物上或在部分纯净的蛋白质制剂上第一次取食而获得蚜虫传播非结构蛋白的话，那蚜虫会有缺陷地传播不可传播的分离种 (Lung and Pirone, 1973, 1974)．
没有证据证明CaMV是种传的。 Most isolates of the virus are transmitted in a semi-persistent manner by Brevicoryne brassicae, Myzus persicae and at least 25 other aphid species (Kennedy et al., 1962).
Aphids can acquire the virus by feeding on infected plants for 1-2 minutes and then thereafter transmit it within 1 minute to healthy plants. Unlike viruses transmitted by aphids in the non-persistent manner, however, viruliferous aphids can retain their ability to transmit the virus for 3-8 hours while feeding and for 16-72 hours if fasting (Hamlyn, 1955; Day and Venables, 1961; Chalfont and Chapman, 1962; Namba and Sylvester, 1981; Markham et al., 1987). Some strains are normally not transmissible by aphids; however, it has long been known that aphid transmissibility is dependent upon the presence of a virus-induced aphid transmission factor (Lung and Pirone, 1973, 1974) which has been identified as the protein product of open-reading frame II (see Identification). Aphids will transmit defective non-transmissible isolates if they are allowed to acquire the aphid transmission non-structural protein by first feeding on plants infected with an aphid-transmissible isolate or on partially purified preparations of the protein Lung and Pirone, 1973, 1974).
There is no evidence for CaMV being seedborne.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
当蚜虫种群数量较高的情况下，苗床的杀虫剂处理是有益的或具预防性的。虽然杀虫剂喷雾不可能限制生长作物中较多的传播，但它们能限制携带病毒进入苗床的蚜虫数量。 Insecticidal treatment of seedbeds is beneficial or preventative when aphid populations are high. Although insecticidal sprays are unlikely to limit much spread in growing crops, they can on occasions be beneficial in limiting the number of aphids available to carry virus to seedbeds. 对侵染有抗性和/或耐病性的十字花科品种是可利用的。如果有价值的十字花科育种材料受到病毒的感染，那无病毒的植物很容易通过顶端分生组织培养而得到(Walkey et al., 1974)。
虽然目前不可利用作商业用途，但转基因抗病毒植物被生产作实验用途。
CaMV的轻微株系已产生，并显示可能对保护接种植物免受严重病毒株系的侵染有作用(Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978)。 Brassica cultivars that are resistant and/or tolerant to infection are available. If valuable Brassica breeding material becomes virus-infected, virus-free plants can be readily obtained by meristem tip culture (Walkey et al., 1974).
Although not yet available for commercial use, transgenic virus-resistant plants have been produced for experimental use.
Mild strains of CaMV have been produced and shown to be potentially useful in protecting inoculated plants from the effects of severe virus strains (Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978). 最重要的防治方法是限制或保护苗床内的幼苗受病毒的侵染，因为当幼苗在较年幼的时候受到侵染，侵染的影响是更为严重的，受感染的幼苗是作物当中最重要的侵染来源(Pound, 1946; Broadbent, 1957)。能通过在与敏感作物隔离的地方建立苗床，或如果这在小型的农场是不实际的话，通过在苗床周围以谷类的作为屏障（大麦或燕麦的混合），或如果花费是有理由的话，通过在防虫条件下（如网孔精细的笼）种植幼苗，来使侵染减到最小化。如果使用屏障植物的话，苗床被建议应该不宽于12行，如果想要更宽，应有一个12行的屏障间隔(Broadbent, 1957)。
当蚜虫数量很大的时候，苗床应该用杀虫剂喷晒来将传播减少到最小化。
当幼苗在田间移植的时候，那些来自苗床较外面的行的幼苗和任何有类似病毒症状的幼苗应被丢弃(Broadbent, 1957)。
任何受感染的植物的早期除杂能减少后来重大的传播(Caldwell and Prentice, 1942b)。
在CaMV是地方性的和引起严重的每年流行的地方，一种干扰免疫的作物的栽培有时候能打破侵染循环。 The most important control procedure is to limit or prevent virus infection of seedlings in seedbeds, because the effects of infection are greater when seedlings are infected at a young stage, and infected seedlings are the most important source of infection within a crop (Pound, 1946; Broadbent, 1957). Infection can be minimized by establishing seedbeds in isolation from susceptible crops or, if this is impractical on small farms, by surrounding the seedbeds with a barrier of cereals (mixture of barley and oats) or, if the costs are justifiable, by growing the seedlings under insect-proofed conditions such as fine-meshed cages. It is suggested that seedbeds should be no wider than 12 rows if barriers are used and, if wider, should have barriers at 12-row intervals (Broadbent, 1957). 
Seedbeds should be sprayed with insecticide when aphids are numerous to minimize spread.
When seedlings are transplanted in the field, those from the outer rows of the seedbed and any with virus-like symptoms should be discarded (Broadbent, 1957).
Early roguing of any infected plants can reduce subsequent spread significantly (Caldwell and Prentice, 1942b).
In areas where CaMV is endemic and causes severe annual epidemics, the culture of an intervening immune crop can sometimes break the infection cycle.
author: zhangjianjun

host_range: Carnation (Dianthus caryophylinus)
description: In 2008, during a survey conducted in commercial carnation greenhouses in Coatepec Harinas County, in the State of Mexico, symptoms of yellow streak were observed in many young carnation (Dianthus caryophylinus) plants and severe deformation and dwarfing in blooming state being both symptoms similar to those recorded for viral diseases in carnation crops. The samples from 24 symptomatic plants were collected and identified, the results showed that, CarMV (all analyzed samples) and CERV (two samples) were observed by dot-blot analysis. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CERV in Mexico. The severe deformation observe in some carnation plants with both CarMV and CERV represent a serious threatens to the carnation crop in Mexico.
reference_name: First Report of Carnation mottle virus (CarMV) and Carnation etched ring virus (CERV) in Carnation From Mexico

host_range: Citrus yellow mosaic virus has a restricted host range in the family Aurantioideae. Natural infection of the virus has been found in sweet orange (Citrus sinensis) cultivars Satgudi, Mosambi and Chini, Nagpur orange (C. reticulata) and pummelo (C. grandis
potential_eco_desc: CiYMV is widespread in India and of great economic importance to the citrus industry. It is particularly common on sweet orange, on which it is locally very damaging. Losses range from 10 to 70% in orchards in Andhra Pradesh. In some areas, orchards have had to be abandoned because of the disease. Losses in fruit yield of 77% have been recorded in infected trees of sweet oranges. CiYMV has also been found in many commercial nurseries. The disease also commonly occurs on pummelo, but this species is not grown commercially in India, so the extent of losses is not known (Ahlawat et al., 1996a).
author: CPC2006

description: CiYMV is transmitted by a mealybug, Planococcus citri, in a persistent manner (Ahlawat and Pant, 1999). Because spread by mealybugs occurs over short distances and sources of infection other than citrus are not known, the spread of the virus is mainly through contaminated budwood as is evident from infection of nursery plants and the very high incidence of the disease (70%) in orchard trees. The virus disseminates through movement of contaminated plants and budwood from one region to another, and this is the most likely means of distribution in international trade (Ahlawat et al., 1999).Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bark: borne internally; invisible.^p - Fruits (inc. Pods): borne internally; visible to naked eye.^p - Flowers/Inflorescences/Cones/Calyx: borne internally; invisible.^p - Leaves: borne internally; visible to naked eye.^p - Roots: borne internally; invisible.^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches: borne internally; invisible.^p - Wood: borne internally; invisible.Plant parts not known to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bulbs/Tubers/Corms/Rhizomes.Transport pathways for long distance movement - Travellers And Baggage: Budwood
author: CPC2006

remark: CiYMV has only recently been characterized, and no real risk assessment of it as a quarantine pest has yet been undertaken. Citrus mosaic disease in India is widespread and important, and has been established to be caused by a badnavirus Ahlawat et al., 1996a, b. In addition, this virus is able to infect most species of Citrus cultivated in the EPPO region. On this basis, CiYMV certainly presents a very significant risk to the production of virus-free citrus budwood. More information is needed on the biology of the virus (multiplication at different temperatures, damage at different temperatures) before its potential to cause losses in citrus orchards in Mediterranean countries can be estimated. The identification of the mealybug vector can pose a possible risk in phytosanitary programmes. However, more research is required on this newly characterized virus and this should lead to a clearer estimation of risk.^p^pPhytosanitary measures^p^pImport of citrus planting material from India should be prohibited. This is already so on account of a number of more serious citrus pests, for example, citrus greening bacterium (EPPO/CABI, 1996b).
author: CPC2006

management_info: The use of virus free budwood is the only control measure currently recommended. No work on breeding for resistance has been undertaken to date. Planococcus citri has recently been identified as the vector of the virus. However, it is presently only controlled in its capacity as a pest and not as a vector of CiYMV.

potential_eco_desc: CiYMV广泛分布于印度，并对柑桔产业有巨大的经济重要性。它在甜橙上特别的普遍，在甜橙上它具有很大的局部破坏性。在安得拉邦的果园中损失范围从10％到70％。在一些区域中，因为该病害有些果园不得不被弃置。77％的果实产量损失已被记录发生在感染的甜橙树上。CiYMV也在很多商业苗圃上被发现。该病害也普遍地发生在柚子上，但这品种在印度不是商业地种植，所以损失的大小是未知的(Ahlawat et al., 1996a)。 CiYMV is widespread in India and of great economic importance to the citrus industry. It is particularly common on sweet orange, on which it is locally very damaging. Losses range from 10 to 70% in orchards in Andhra Pradesh. In some areas, orchards have had to be abandoned because of the disease. Losses in fruit yield of 77% have been recorded in infected trees of sweet oranges. CiYMV has also been found in many commercial nurseries. The disease also commonly occurs on pummelo, but this species is not grown commercially in India, so the extent of losses is not known (Ahlawat et al., 1996a).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
虽然柑桔黄花叶已在印度被发现了很多年，但它只是现在被归类为一个特定德病毒(Ahlawat et al., 1996a, b)。CiYMV通过嫁接(Dakshinamurti and Reddy, 1975)和通过菟丝子引诱(Reddy et al., 1985)传播。这杆状DNA病毒是通过芽、树皮和叶片嫁接传播，症状在30-50天内在接种植物上出现。该病毒也能通过常规的叶片接种程序使用0.05 M磷酸盐缓冲液中的幼嫩组织作为接种体来传播。在近来的试验中，只有橘红（C. maxima）、C. jambin和甘蔗是以这种方法被侵染(Ahlawat et al., 1996a; Reddy, 1997)。该病毒也能实验性地通过粉蚧(柑橘粉蚧（Planococcus citri）)以持久的方式传播(Ahlawat and Pant, 1999)。种子传播也在较早的文献中被报道，但这到了现在似乎是不合理的。
CiYMV被认为是通过桃蚜（Myzus persicae）和苜蓿蚜（Aphis craccivora）(Ahlawat et al., 1984)和大桔蚜（Toxoptera citricidus ）(Pandey et al., 1986)传播的。一些先前被归类到CiYMV的特性可能是由于与其他病毒混淆。 While citrus mosaic has been known for many years in India, it has only recently been attributed to a specific virus (Ahlawat et al., 1996a, b). CiYMV is transmitted by grafting (Dakshinamurti and Reddy, 1975) and by dodder laurel (Reddy et al., 1985). This badnavirus is transmitted by bud, bark and leaf patch grafting; symptoms appear within 30-50 days in inoculated plants. The virus is also mechanically transmissible by conventional leaf inoculation procedures using young tissue ground in 0.05 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.6) as inoculum. In a recent trial, only C. maxima, C. jambin and sugarcane were infected in this manner (Ahlawat et al., 1996a; Reddy, 1997). The virus has also been experimentally transmitted by mealybugs (Planococcus citri) in a persistent manner (Ahlawat and Pant, 1999). Seed transmission has also been reported in earlier literature, but this now seems implausible. 
CiYMV was thought to be aphid-transmitted by Myzus persicae and Aphis craccivora (Ahlawat et al., 1984) and Toxoptera citricidus (Pandey et al., 1986) but the badnavirus was not transmitted by these aphids (Pant and Ahlawat, 1997). It is possible that some of the properties previously attributed to CiYMV were due to confusion with other viruses.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info: 无病毒芽木的使用是当前推荐的唯一的防治方法。到目前为止没有作出育种抗性的研究。柑橘粉蚧（Planococcus citri）最近被鉴定为该病毒的传播媒介。然而，目前它只作为害虫作防治而不是作为CiYMV的传播媒介。 The use of virus free budwood is the only control measure currently recommended. No work on breeding for resistance has been undertaken to date. Planococcus citri has recently been identified as the vector of the virus. However, it is presently only controlled in its capacity as a pest and not as a vector of CiYMV.

host_range: 蒌叶（叶） Piper betle (leaf)
description: During surveys in two subsequent years 2013-2014 for virus diseases, the natural occurrence of yellow vein mosaic disease was noticed with 22 to 25% disease incidence on P. betel growing in various barejas at Mahoba (Uttar Pradesh), India. Leaf samples from infected Piper betel plants were collected and processed for detection of viruses. The presence of Canna yellow mottle virus (CaYMV) in these samples were confirmed by PCR/RT-PCR tests and nucleic acid spot hybridization tests. Occurrence of CaYMV on P. betel is being reported for the first time.  Piper betle is being propagated through its vine cuttings, hence the virus may be considered as a phytosanitary risk.
reference_name: First Report of Canna yellow mottle virus Associated With Yellow Vein Mosaic Disease of Betel Vine (Piper betel) in India

host_range: 美人蕉Canna indica
description: During a survey in September 2012, necrotic striping, severe veinal chlorosis, yellow mosaic and veinal streaking symptoms were observed on the leaves of different canna cultivars, with the disease incidence between 17 and 35% at NBRI. Subsequently, similar symptoms were found on canna in other gardens in Lucknow. Based on sequence comparison and phylogenetic analysis, the virus isolates in this study were identified as CaYMV. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of natural occurrence of CaYMV on canna from India.

potential_eco_desc: 危害一般。

Observations suggest that CBV has little effect on crop yields, but experimental data are lacking. Plants rarely show signs of infection and, of those that do, recovery is rapid suggesting that  effects on corm yield are minimal. The fatal disease in Solomon Islands associated with CBV is at odds with this, but the presence of lethal taro diseases elsewhere in the country calls for caution before ascribing the symptoms to CBV alone.^p^pCBV is of concern because of its association with colocasia bobone disease (?) rhabdovirus (CBDV) in alomae disease of 'male' taro (Gollifer and Brown, 1972). Alomae is known only from Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands, but CBV is probably more widespread than its known distribution suggests.  Plants affected by alomae die rapidly.
author: CPC2006

remark: Because of the association of CBV with alomae, and its seemingly  restricted distribution to six Pacific island countries, it is of quarantine concern to all countries and regions where it has not yet been detected.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Introduction^p^pIt is not practical to attempt to control CBV in the field because of the difficulty in recognizing symptoms, and the fact that few plants show signs of infection. There is also the possibility that the virus is latent in plants and, in those countries where it has been reported, most taro are already infected. ^p^p^Regulatory Control^p^pInternational movement of taro germplasm should be as virus-indexed, sterile plants growing in tissue culture medium, and subject to post-entry quarantine for one crop cycle  in the importing country, according to published guidelines (Zettler et al., 1989).^p^pA period in post-entry quarantine of one crop cycle is advisable with periodic examination of negatively stained leaf extracts by electron microscopy (Zettler et al., 1989).

potential_eco_desc: MCDV primarily infects maize in states in the south-eastern quadrant of the USA (Damsteegt, 1977; Gordon and Nault, 1977). These states are found from the Atlantic coast to Texas and northward to southern Missouri and Ohio. It may also occur sporadically in nearby states, such as Arizona (Gordon, unpublished data) and Pennsylvania (Ayers et al., 1978).^p^pWhile the virus unquestionably has had a major impact on maize production in the southern USA, there are no statistically valid estimates of total yield losses from virus infection (Gordon et al., 1981). Nevertheless, yield losses in field tests, mostly in fields with infestations of MCDV and maize dwarf mosaic potyvirus-infected Johnson grass, are estimated to range from 9% to more than 90%, with an average of 44%, depending on the susceptibility of the maize genotype, time of infection, and possibly other factors such as which of the viruses infects individual plants (Findley et al., 1970; Josephson and Hilty, 1970; Poneleit and Evans, 1970; Anon., 1973; Findley et al., 1973; Genter et al., 1973;Poneleit and Evans, 1973a, b; Anon., 1974; Findley et al., 1974; Genter et al., 1974; Poneleit and Evans, 1974; Anon., 1975; Findley et al., 1975; Findley et al., 1976; Genter et al., 1976; Josephson et al., 1976; Anon., 1977; Findley et al., 1977a; Gordon et al., 1981).^p^pThe virus reduced maize yields by an average of 60% (Scott et al., 1977), with the later the infection the lower the yield reduction (Pitre, 1968c; Keaster et al., 1969; Scott et al., 1977). A susceptible maize plant with symptoms by 52 days after planting produced no grain, whereas a plant with no symptoms by 108 days showed no yield reduction (Scott et al., 1977). Between these limits, the yield progressively and linearly decreased. In another instance yields were reduced by 13.3 to 18.4 bushels per acre (bu/ac) for each unit increase in the virus severity index (Josephson et al., 1978), whereas the average yield reduction for each 1% increase in the number of virus-infected plants was 0.6 to 0.9 bu/ac.^p^pIn other instances, yields were reduced by 22.5 and 14.4 bu/ac for each unit increase in virus severity (Josephson and Hilty, 1970) and yield reductions due to virus infection ranged from 23 to 91% (Josephson et al., 1969). The yield reduction for a susceptible hybrid not treated with the systemic insecticide carbofuran to control the leafhopper vector was 55% compared with that of the insecticide-treated hybrid (Kuhn et al., 1975).^p^pThe yield of the same susceptible hybrid under no-tillage was reduced by 50% for nontreated compared with insecticide-treated maize (All et al., 1977), whereas under conventional tillage this hybrid had a 28% (not significant) reduction in yield in nontreated compared with treated plots. More recently, experimental virus inoculations of seedling maize, including the 10 most frequently used maize inbreds in the USA in 1980 and 46 maize hybrids, caused significant yield reductions (72% average) (Louie et al., 1990). These reductions are somewhat greater than those reported for the previous field evaluations involving occurrences of both maize dwarf mosaic potyvirus and MCDV.^p^pThe results from the experimental inoculations highlight the potential of the virus for major economic impact in the absence of maize dwarf mosaic potyvirus under field conditions where MCDV control is not practised.^p^pThus, the virus has the potential to cause significant yield reduction and consequently significant economic impact on maize production in the southern USA and the southern border of the Corn Belt where the virus is indigenous. However, this impact is dependent on an abundant source of the virus and infection of susceptible maize hybrids at an early stage of plant growth, both over a wide geographical area.^p^pIn the 1960s and 1970s these conditions apparently existed in this area of the USA as judged by numerous reports of major yield reductions attributed to the virus. management_info: Introduction^p^pThe recommended method for control of MCDV in maize is the cultivation of virus resistant or tolerant maize hybrids Findley et al., 1977a, 1981; All et al., 1981; Josephson and Scott, 1981; Scott et al., 1981; All, 1983; Scott, 1983;Rosenkranz and Scott, 1986, 1987; Louie et al., 1990). However, no maize hybrids are immune to the virus and only a few hybrids have a high degree of resistance. Further, some of these hybrids may not possess agronomic characteristics suitable for production. Thus, where suitable resistant or tolerant hybrids are not available or the level of resistance is inadequate, other means of virus control are required. These other means include early planting; herbicide eradication of Johnson grass, the virus overwintering host; leafhopper vector (Graminella nigrifrons) control with the systemic insecticide carbofuran (2, 3 dihydro-2,2-dimethyl-7-benzofuranyl methylcarbamate); and irrigation (All et al., 1981; All, 1983).^p^pGenetics^p^pAs a result of breeding efforts over many years, maize inbreds with resistance or tolerance to MCDV are available Fleming, 1974, 1983; Russell and Hallauer, 1974;Findley et al., 1977a, 1978, 1979, 1980, 1981, 1983;Wallin et al., 1978, 1980; Dale and York, 1979; Cross, 1980; Josephson and Scott, 1981; Scott and Davis, 1981; Scott and Rosenkranz, 1981; Warren, 1982;West et al., 1986, 1987, 1988; Rosenkranz and Scott, 1987; Louie et al., 1990; Pratt et al., 1994).^p^pIn addition, resistant composite PRMo2 (Wallin et al., 1979) and synthetic TSGP (Josephson et al., 1982) populations are available. Several studies have indicated that general combining ability mean squares for virus resistance are considerably greater than specific combining ability mean squares (Johnson, 1971; Loesch and Zuber, 1972; Nelson and Scott, 1973; Scott et al., 1981). However, the estimates for general combining ability may have been biased upward (Scott et al., 1981). Nevertheless, virus resistance seems to be inherited mostly as a dominant to partially dominate trait (Loesch and Zuber, 1967; Dollinger et al., 1970; Josephson and Naidu, 1971; Naidu and Josephson, 1976), although other authors conclude that dominance for resistance or susceptibility is lacking (Grogan and Rosenkranz, 1968;Rosenkranz and Scott, 1986, 1987).^p^pMinor genes also may be necessary for a high level of resistance, whereas tolerance to the virus may be conditioned by a few major genes in association with a modifier gene complex or by many genes with small additive effects (Zuber et al., 1973). These conflicting early findings and interpretations are summarised in Scott et al. (1981).^p^pRecent efforts to identify sources of resistance have selected superior MCDV resistant progenies. These selections have employed exposure of test maize seedlings to high levels of inoculum involving multiple inoculations with viruliferous leafhoppers (Findley et al., 1985; Louie et al., 1990; Louie and Anderson, 1993; Pratt et al., 1994). Virus resistance genes have been identified on maize chromosomes 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10 and possibly 2 and 8 (Findley et al., 1973; Scott and Rosenkranz, 1977; Scott et al., 1981; McMullen and Louie, 1989; Rufener et al., 1996; Louie et al., 1997). Inbreds with a high level of tolerance or resistance to the virus have been used to develop virus-resistant commercial dent and sweet corn hybrids with agronomically satisfactory characteristics (All et al., 1977; Josephson et al., 1978; Knoke et al., 1981; Eberhart, 1983). Significantly, hybrid vigour frequently enhances plant performance to create the appearance of resistance (Scott et al., 1981; Pratt et al., 1994).^p^pResistant hybrids are currently available for planting by producers in areas of where the virus severely limited maize production in the 1960s and 1970s. potential_eco_desc: In south and southeast Asia, tungro, a composite disease caused by RTSV and RTBV, is a major threat to stable rice production in irrigated areas (Hibino, 1989). In these regions, where rice is the staple food, rice production relies largely on irrigated areas where tungro is endemic and has caused serious damage (Hibino, 1989; Thresh, 1991; Bos, 1992). Generally, tungro incidence is low or nil in rainfed or upland ricefields. When it reaches epidemic proportions, tungro is disastrous and damages ricefields in a huge acreage, even in rainfed or upland fields.^p^pRTSV occurs as an independent disease in Kyushu, Japan (Saito, 1977; Hibino, 1996), possibly in central China (Xie et al., 1994), and commonly but unnoticeably in south and southeast Asia (Bajet et al., 1986; Hibino, 1996). In Japan RTSV was called rice waika virus (Furuta, 1977; Shinkai, 1977). ^p^pRTSV causes mild stunting, occasional moderate yellowing and grain discoloration (Hibino et al., 1987; Furuta, 1997). Infected plants showed a yield reduction of 20-30% in Japan (Ishimaru et al., 1975). Economic losses due to rice waika virus in Japan appear to be much higher than the estimated yield loss. This is because harvested rice contaminated with discolored grains are graded lower, resulting in a lower selling price. In the Asian tropics, the yield loss due to RTSV alone is not known. Under experimental conditions, yield losses of 2-40% have been recorded, depending on the cultivars used (Hasanuddin and Hibino, 1989).^p^pIn south and southeast Asia, tungro disease has probably occurred since the 1850s (Ou, 1985). Thus, RTSV has been present for many years in the area. Major outbreaks of tungro have occurred in many countries from time to time since the mid 1960s and have caused devastating damage in rice (Hibino, 1996)(see Economic Impact of RTBV for further details). Rice tungro disease causes an average annual loss of more than US$ 1,500 million (Herdt, 1988).^p^pIn Kyushu, Japan, rice waika virus (RTSV) was recorded in 1964 and reached an epidemic level in 1971-1973 (Furuta 1977; Shinkai, 1977). The area affected was 1,647 ha in 1971, 11,924 ha in 1972 and 24,825 ha in 1973. In 1973, the area affected reached 7.4% of the total rice-growing area in Kyushu and the yield loss was estimated as 10,000 t. Rice cultivar Reiho which was commonly planted in Kyushu at the time was particularly susceptible to the virus (Shimura, 1977). The incidence declined to a low level and eventually disappeared in most places after 1975.
author: CPC2006

remark: It is likely that rice is the only host naturally infected with RTSV. Infected rice stubbles and volunteer rice plants also serve as RTSV sources for nearby fields or for the next crop season. ^p^pIn Japan, ratoons infected with RTSV overwintered better in years when the winter temperature was higher (Iwasaki et al., 1983). RTSV incidence was very high when the average temperature during the winter season was higher in 1972 and 1973 (Shinkai, 1977; Furuta, 1977; Iwasaki et al., 1983).^p^pAs it is distributed widely in the Asian tropics and subtropics, RTSV is not important as a quarantine objective in those areas. Introduction of RTSV may create problems for temperate countries where tungro is absent but where the vector Nephotettix cincticeps predominates, as was the case in Kyushu, Japan (Furuta, 1977; Shinkai, 1977; Hibino, 1983a).
author: CPC2006

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl measures may not be required for RTSV alone if grain quality is not a major concern or if high incidence of RTSV is not expected in the area. In irrigated areas in the tropics where rice planting is staggered, control measures against tungro (RTSV and RTBV) will probably be needed.^p^p^IPM Programmes^p^pAs diagnosis is difficult, no IPM programme has been developed for RTSV.^p^pAn integrated management scheme for tungro has been practised in South Sulawesi, Indonesia (Sama et al., 1991). The scheme has four components: planting two rice crops in those months when the vector population is low; scheduled planting to ensure nearly synchronous growth in each area; rotation or deployment of cultivars with different degrees of resistance to the vector Nephotettix virescens; and application of insecticide to reduce vector density in fields where tungro is present. Tungro incidence has been low under this scheme: this low incidence is thought to result from the slow rate of vector population increase and the few or no sources of tungro in the area.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pApplication of insecticides to reduce the vector leafhopper population in the seedling box immediately before transplanting or at the early stage after transplanting controls RTSV effectively (Furuta, 1977; Shinkai, 1977). ^p^pInsecticide application to reduce the vector population is practised widely to manage tungro. Economic threshold levels based on vector populations are of little practical value; tungro spreads fast even when the vector population is relatively low, and therefore the threshold must be set at a low level if tungro is present in nearby fields (Heinrichs, 1979).^p^pIn areas where tungro is endemic, insecticide application gives limited control in susceptible cultivars, better control in moderately resistant cultivars, and is not required for resistant cultivars. Insecticide gives better control of tungro when it is applied in fields after transplanting, at an early growth stage, than when it is applied at an earlier (in the nursery bed) or later stage of growth (Tiongco et al., 1993).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pRice cultivars with resistance to N. virescens have been planted widely in South and South-East Asia (Khush and Virmani, 1985). Such cultivars have little or no tungro (Hibino et al., 1988). In many locations, however, after a few years of intensive cultivation, many vector-resistant cultivars that formerly had only a little tungro disease have shown severe tungro (Hibino, 1995). The breakdown of resistance was due to development of a vector population that overcame the resistance Dahal et al., 1990, 1999). Cultivar reactions to N. virescens populations at different locations were often different (Dahal, 1988; Hibino, 1995).^p^pMany commercial cultivars with resistance to RTSV are available (Hibino et al., 1988; Imbe et al., 1993). Resistances to RTSV appear to be abundant in rice germplasm (Furuta 1977; Hibino et al., 1990; Imbe et al., 1993; Cabunagan et al., 1993; Wu et al., 1994) and some of them have been used in the rice breeding programme (Habibuddin et al., 1991). RTSV-resistant cultivars effectively reduced RTSV incidence in Kyushu, Japan (Furuta, 1977; Shinkai, 1977) and tungro disease (RTBV and RTSV) in the Philippines Hibino et al., 1987, 1988;Cabunagan et al., 1989a, 1989b). When tungro is present, RTSV-resistant cultivars are only sporadically infected with RTBV and do not provide sources of tungro to surrounding fields (Hibino et al., 1990;Cabunagan et al., 1989a, b). A virulent strain of RTSV that infects many RTSV-resistant cultivars occurred in the Philippines (Cabauatan et al., 1995). Rice plants transformed with coat protein on replicase genes of RTSV show resistance to RTSV infection (Hu et al., 1999; Sivamani et al., 1999).^p^p^Cultural Control^p ^pSynchrony in planting (scheduled uniform planting to have uniform fallow periods in the areas) provides an effective control of tungro disea

description: RTSV通过叶蝉（半翅目：叶蝉科）传播(Yokoyama and Sakai, l975; Hirao and Inoue, 1978; Hibino et al., 1979; Hibino, 1983a; Khan et al., 1991)。它们是二点黑尾叶蝉，二条黑尾叶蝉、黑尾叶蝉、马来亚黑尾叶蝉、N. parvus和电光叶蝉。二点黑尾叶蝉是最有效的媒介昆虫且是南亚及东南亚东格鲁病害最重要媒介昆虫(Hibino et al., 1979; Khan et al., l991)。在日本和中国南部，黑尾叶蝉是重要的媒介昆虫。 RTSV is transmitted by leafhoppers (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae) (Yokoyama and Sakai, l975; Hirao and Inoue, 1978; Hibino et al., 1979; Hibino, 1983a; Khan et al., 1991). They are: Nephotettix virescens, N. nigropictus, N. cincticeps, N. malayanus, N. parvus, and Recilia dorsalis. N. virescens is the most efficient vector of RTSV and the most important as the vector of tungro in South and South-East Asia (Hibino et al., 1979; Khan et al., l991). In Japan and southern China, N. cincticeps is important as the vector.

Such cultivars have little or no tungro (Hibino et al., 1988). 因为诊断很难，所以没有IPM方案已被发展来防治RTSV。
综合管理方案在南苏拉威西，印度尼西亚已经被实行(Sama et al., l991)。这个方案有四个部分：在媒介昆虫的种群数较低的月份种植双季作物，定期种植保证每个地区几乎同步生长发育，对媒介昆虫二点黑尾叶蝉的抗性的不同等级的栽培种轮作或调配，运用杀虫剂减少在受东格鲁感染的田间的媒介昆虫的密度。东格鲁的发病率在这种方案期间已经被降低，这可能解释为媒介昆虫种群比例缓慢增长和这些地区很少或没有东格鲁病原。 As diagnosis is difficult, no IPM programme has been developed for RTSV.

Tungro incidence has been low under this scheme: this low incidence is thought to result from the slow rate of vector population increase and the few or no sources of tungro in the area.

description: In 2013, a novel virus named Carrot torradovirus 1 (CaTV1) was identified in the U.K. in asymptomatic carrots (Daucus carota) during an investigation of the causes of root internal necrosis. Epidemiological studies carried out in the U.K. in 2014 and 2015 indicated levels of infection up to 26.7 and 64.5%, respectively. In October 2016, asymptomatic and symptomatic leaf samples with reddening, chlorosis, or necrosis were collected from several carrot fields in Aquitaine, in the southwest of France. Based on molecular diagnostics, the results showed CaTV1 were presence in one of the fields sampled. This is the first report of the virus in France and outside the U.K.  Experiments also suggested that CaTV1 may be transmitted by the aphid species Myzus persicae and Cavariella aegopodii (Rozado-Aguirre et al. 2016).

remark: Satusma dwarf virus was recently added to the EPPO A2 list, but has not been considered as a quarantine pest by any other regional plant protection organization. The virus typically infects Satsuma (Citrus unshiu), rather than other Citrus species, and this species is not widely grown in the EPPO region. In Turkey, where Satsuma is grown in the Aegean region, and where Satsuma dwarf virus has presumably been introduced in budwood imported from the Far East, the virus has only been reported on this species. It does not appear to have spread to other Citrus species, to other regions of Turkey, or elsewhere in the EPPO region. No vector is definitely known in the Far East, and no vector appears to occur in the EPPO region. Satsuma dwarf virus therefore, does not seem to present a very high risk for the EPPO region. However, it has been reported from other Citrus species, and Citrus mosaic virus is increasing in importance in Japan. It therefore seems justified to prevent further spread of Satsuma dwarf virus and Citrus mosaic virus, and in particular the introduction of new strains of Citrus mosaic virus from the Far East.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Satsuma dwarf virus already occurs in the EPPO region, but does not at present seem to present a major risk. So, within the EPPO region, citrus planting material should be certified free from the virus by methods such as those of the EPPO certification scheme for citrus (OEPP/EPPO, 1995). Since Satsuma dwarf related viruses in the Far East include the more devastating Citrus mosaic virus and others, with a wider host range, import of citrus planting materials from these origins should be prohibited. This is already the case for a number of serious citrus pests, for example, Citrus greening bacterium and Citrus tatter-leaf virus (Frison and Taher, 1991; EPPO/CABI, 1996).

host_range: RpRSV occurs in a very wide range of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous species. Cultivated host species include artichoke (Roca et al., 1986), cherry (Klinger et al., 1985), currants (Janeckova and Svobodova, 1995; Jones and McGavin, 1996), Cytisus prae
potential_eco_desc: In natural outbreaks, RpRSV infection is usually associated with patchy infections in crops, reflecting the distribution of the vector nematode. In infected plants, leaf symptoms, if any, are often dependent on the virus isolate, plant genotype and ill-defined environmental conditions. ^p^pIn raspberry, infection is associated with vein yellowing, mosaic, chlorotic ringspots or flecks, or leaf curling symptoms, depending on the cultivar. Symptoms may fade in mid-summer but return in the autumn. Plants of sensitive cultivars are stunted and may die within 2-3 years of the first appearance of symptoms; other cultivars merely show decreased vigour. Some raspberry cultivars are immune to some strains of the virus (Murant, 1987; Jones et al., 1989). In the very susceptible cultivar Norfolk Giant, part or all of the canes may die in winter. Those that survive produce stunted and brittle shoots which have rolled leaves and show die-back progressively from the tip, accompanied by necrosis. In less susceptible cultivars, such as Malling Jewel, Malling Enterprise and Malling Notable, symptoms appear on the leaves of new shoots in spring, but are mild or absent on the leaves of fruiting canes. Young, expanding leaves develop a conspicuous, yellowish-green, ringspot or oak-leaf pattern; chlorotic blotches and a net-like chlorosis along the smaller veins may also be present; some necrosis and die-back may occur. Malling Promise develops few symptoms and does not die back; Lloyd George and Malling Landmark are immune to the common strain but are susceptible to the Lloyd George yellow blotch strain (Murant, 1987). However, cultivars may be infected without showing obvious symptoms, either because their roots are newly infected and the virus has not yet invaded the shoots, or due to seasonal fluctuations in symptom expression or because they are tolerant of infection (Jones et al., 1989).^p^pAffected strawberry plants may show chlorotic spots or rings or generalized chlorosis, depending on the cultivar, the symptoms tending to fade in mid-summer. The plants become progressively stunted and die prematurely. However, symptoms may vary according to season and virus strain. On cv. Huxley, clearly defined, irregularly shaped chlorotic blotches develop, often with a necrotic centre; there are no line patterns or rings. Symptoms are less conspicuous on leaves developed in summer or at high temperatures. On cv. Royal Sovereign, there is striking development of local necrotic spots (Murant and Lister, 1987). In general, seedlings of Fragaria vesca show yellow blotches during the first year of infection, but not thereafter.^p^pIn cherry, in association with viruses of the prunus necrotic ringspot type, RpRSV induces rasp leaf symptoms (Cropley, 1961). The leaves of affected trees are usually reduced in size, narrow and tough, with abnormally coarse serrations. Depending on varietal sensitivity, enations on the lower surface of the leaves may be few or numerous, large or small and confined to areas of the leaf close to the midrib. Both types of enations may occur on the same tree, either simultaneously or at different stages of infection. Young trees of the sensitive cv. Bing, inoculated by bud grafts in summer, usually show conspicuous symptoms in the following year (Cropley, 1961).^p^pIn grapevine, an English serotype was associated with fanleaf-type symptoms (Jones et al., 1994).
author: CPC2006

management_info: In the absence of resistant material, healthy planting material should be used in areas free from known infection with RpRSV and in soil free from viruliferous Longidorus vectors. Although immunity to some isolates of the virus is reported in some raspberry cultivars, such cultivars are susceptible to other virus isolates (Jones et al., 1989). Control in areas of infestation can only be achieved by treating infected soil with nematicides or other soil sterilants prior to planting with virus-tested healthy stock (Murant and Taylor, 1965; Harrison and Murant, 1996). However, good weed control is necessary to prevent nematode acquisition of virus from weed seedlings infected through seed (Murant, 1987).^p^pThe virus has been eliminated from developing shoot tip cultures (2 mm) of infected plants of several species, including carnation, Daphne and grapevine, by heat treatment and meristem tip culture, either alone or in combination (Stellmach, 1973; Stone, 1973; Schmidt, 1974; Anon., 1978; Sweet et al., 1979).

description: In May 2014, 224 grapevine leaf samples were collected in major grape-growing areas of Gimcheon, Yeongdong, Okcheon, Cheonan, and Songsan in Korea and tested by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for previously reported viruses（Grapevine leafroll-associated viruses (GLRaV) 1 and 3,Grapevine fleck virus (GFkV), and Grapevine pinot gris virus (GPGV)）infecting grapevine and Blueberry leaf mottle virus (BLMoV). The RT-PCR results showed that the grapevines were infected in Gimcheon (61.0%), Yeongdong (51.1%), Okcheon (70.0%), Cheonan (47.7%), and Songsan (16.3%) by BLMoV, no mixed infections with the other viruses were detected. Our results indicate that BLMoV was distributed in grapevine fields of Korea, though with no major damage. To our knowledge, this is the first report of BLMoV in Korea and outside of North America and Europe.

嫁接传播：嫁接是传毒的重要途径，根部嫁接也可以传染。

host_range: ToRSV has a wide natural host range, including both herbaceous and perennial crops. Reports of natural spread are largely confined to the USA and Canada. Primary hosts include Prunus (cherry, almond, peach, nectarine, and plum; Schlocker and Traylor, 1976), Malus (apple; Stouffer et al., 1977). Rubus (raspberry; Stace-Smith, 1962, blackberry; Alcorn et al., 1955), Vaccinium (blueberry; Ramsdell, 1987), Vitis (grapevines; Gooding and Tilez, 1970), Ribes (red currant; Hildebrand, 1942), Fragaria (strawberry; Frazier et al., 1961; Converse and Stace-Smith, 1987), and Pelargonium (pelargonium; Kemp, 1969),Although diseases in these primary hosts account for nearly all of the virus problems, there are a few reports of the virus being isolated from other crops, including gladiolus (Bozarth and Corbett, 1958), hydrangea (Brierley, 1954), elderberry (Uyemoto, 1970), orchid (Goff and Corbett, 1977), dogwood, (Reddick et al., 1979), bird's-foot trefoil (Ostazeski and Scott, 1966), cucumber (McKeen, 1960) and ash (Hibben and Reese, 1983).
potential_eco_desc: ToRSV is widespread in perennial plant species and causes severe decline in productivity so it is one of the most damaging plant viruses in North America. The virus is prevalent in dandelion and other weeds (Powell et al., 1982), and may be disseminated over considerable distances in windblown seeds of infected dandelion (Rosenberger et al., 1983). Furthermore, dandelion and other perennial weeds provide reservoirs for virus acquisition by nematode vectors.ToRSV constitutes a serious economic problem in areas where the nematode vectors occur (see Biology and Ecology). Fortunately, pockets of active virus spread are restricted to certain soil types. In the raspberry-growing region of the Pacific Northwest, for instance, relatively few fields are infected, but where the virus is prevalent, crop losses are extensive (Converse et al., 1970).Yield reduction in the various perennial hosts is difficult to assess because the response to infection varies according to cultivar and the duration of infection. In studies on raspberries, between 10 and 80% of raspberry canes were partially or completely killed 3 years after becoming infected (Freeman and Stace-Smith, 1968). In other field studies, Converse and Stace-Smith (1971) observed that fruit from infected canes weighed 21% less than normal fruit and that the yield of diseased plants was reduced by >50%.

description: Incidence^p^pToRSV has been demonstrated to be seedborne in several species including soyabean (Kahn, 1956; D McGee, Iowa State University, Iowa, USA, personal communication, 1998), strawberry (Mellor and Stace-Smith, 1963), raspberry (Braun and Keplinger, 1973), pelargonium (Scarborough and Smith, 1977) and dandelion (Mountain et al., 1983). Pollen transmission to seed has been demonstrated in pelargonium (Scarborough and Smith, 1977). ^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pRaspberries infected with ToRSV may exhibit reduced berry size and a crumbly berry because infection affects seed quality. In a controlled study involving 10 cultivars, some showed a reduction in yield in the third cropping year whereas other varieties showed no significant yield reduction (Freeman et al., 1975). Drupelet set also varied with the cultivar, some showing a particularly adverse affect whereas others were unaffected or affected to a lesser extent (Daubeny et al., 1975).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pWith the exception of strawberry (Mellor and Stace-Smith, 1963), there is no conclusive evidence for transmission of ToRSV from seed to seedlings in any host. Seeds harvested from inoculated soyabean plants grown in a greenhouse were planted in the greenhouse and the pathogen was recorded in 76% of seedlings. The presence of the virus on 3-week-old seedlings was confirmed by symptom development and by inoculating tissues onto cowpea indicator plants (Kahn, 1956). However, there was no indication that precautions were taken in this study to preclude alternate sources of inoculum. Furthermore, seed transmission has not been demonstrated by seeds from naturally infected soyabean plants. ^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pSerology^p^pIowa State University Seed Health Testing Laboratory has adapted a diagnostic kit manufactured by Agdia Unc, Elkhart, Indiana, USA, to test for ToMRV in seeds. The method is available on the USDA National Seed Health System website at www.seedhealth.org.^p^pGrow-out (Mellor and Stace-Smith, 1963)^p^pThe virus has been detected in infected strawberry seed by germinating the seed and mechanically transmitting the virus from infected seedlings to herbaceous test plants.

management_info: Introduction^p^pToRSV infections are usually not detected in field plantings of perennial crops until the virus has spread to produce circular patches of unthrifty plants. At this stage little can be done to prevent the progress of the virus and its control is difficult. Plants showing symptoms can be removed and replanted with healthy stock but, unless measures are taken to destroy viruliferous nematodes, the virus will soon spread into the healthy plants in the replanted area. Prevention and control requires several strategies to be undertaken in concert.^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pVirus-free planting stock is the foundation for the prevention of nepovirus diseases. In California, USA, millions of grapevine scions and cultivars grafted onto rootstocks are propagated as free from virus as a result of thermotherapy and shoot-tip culture (Nyland and Goheen, 1969). Recent developments in therapy and virus detection methods have resulted in effective therapeutic procedures (Spiegel et al., 1993). ^p^pAlthough the dissemination of tomato ringspot nepovirus from North America to other parts of the world has been limited, there are sufficient reports in the literature to raise concern. Collecting, conservation and utilization of plant genetic resources and their global distribution are essential components of international crop improvement programmes. Inevitably, the movement of germplasm involves the risk of accidentally introducing plant quarantine pests along with the host plant material, particularly with viruses such as tomato ringspot nepovirus that are often symptomless. The ever-increasing volume of germplasm exchanged internationally has created a need for the phytosanitary safety of germplasm transfer. This has prompted the development of internationally accepted guidelines and recommendations for the safe and expeditious movement of germplasm (Frison and Ikin, 1991; Dickmann et al., 1994) The general recommendations are that under no circumstances should germplasm be moved as rooted plant material, that germplasm should preferably be moved as in vitro cultures, that when available, accessions or cultivars should be obtained from a pathogen-tested collection or from the area of lowest risk possible and that all material should undergo therapy and indexing procedures (Spiegel et al., 1993).^p^pWeed Control to Restrict Virus Spread^p^pMuch attention has been paid to the possible role of weeds in the epidemiology and spread of tomato ringspot nepovirus. In a study to assess the extent of orchard weeds that were infected with tomato ringspot nepovirus in virus-diseased apple and peach orchards in the eastern USA, 21 species of annual and perennial weeds were found to be infected with the virus (Powell et al., 1984). Infected nursery stock provides the initial introduction of the virus into fruit production areas. A change from clean cultivation by discing to minimum tillage has facilitated transmission of the virus by nematodes into dandelions (Taraxacum officinale) and other weed species. As the number of infected dandelions increases, so the probability of virus transmission to healthy trees also rises. It appears that the virus is endemic in dandelions and other weeds and their deep-rooted nature provides reservoirs of the virus.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pOne of the potentially most effective long-term strategies to control nepovirus diseases is that of genetic resistance. Ideally, a rootstock should possess resistance to direct feeding damage by the nematode and immunity to the virus. Alternatively, own-rooted woody plants could be developed to tolerate both nematode feeding and virus infection. In tree fruits, there is good promise that own-rooted ‘ Stanley‘  plum will remain free from tomato ringspot virus infection when grown in soil infested with viruliferous Xiphinema spp. (Gonsalves et al., 1983). Infected raspberry cultivars show considerable differences in their ability to survive and produce reasonable yields and, in areas where the virus is a problem, planting resistant cultivars is recommended (Stace-Smith and Converse, 1987).^p^p^ Chemical Control^p^pFallowing is not an effective means of disease control because weeds and remaining roots of woody crop plants act as carryover hosts for the nematode vector and the virus. Soil fumigation is an alternative to fallowing. The use of soil fumigants is contentious and the range of effective soil fumigants is dwindling. Many have been declared powerful carcinogens and their future availability is doubtful. Soils that contain a considerable amount of clay or high organic matter are difficult to fumigate effectively. There are problems associated with soil fumigation and plant health. Phytotoxicity may occur if soils are not sufficiently aerated between the time of fumigation and planting. In replant situations where virus and vector nematodes are present in a field with infection foci, the cost per unit area will be high. However, in order to stop the further spread of the disease, a seemingly high initial cost may well be worth the ultimate benefit of saving the orchard or vineyard (Stace-Smith and Ramsdell, 1987). ^p^pMuch interest has been generated in the use of systemic organic phosphate and carbamate nematicides. Systemic nematicides are relatively nonphytotoxic, are usually in a granular form, and are applied to the soil, disced into the upper soil layers, and irrigated to allow the chemical to permeate the main root zone. They disrupt the nervous system of the nematodes, interfering with their ability to feed. Although excellent yield increases have resulted from the use of systemic nematicides to control nematodes, this type of nematicide is not particularly useful for the control of virus spread. Although nematode feeding is disrupted, some feeding does occur and virus transmission may still result. Perhaps the best use of this type of nematicide is as a follow-up treatment to preplant soil fumigation to maintain nematode populations at a low level for a longer time (Stace-Smith and Ramsdell, 1987).

management_info: The simplest control method would be the use of virus-free propagation material. This concept is consistent with the quality norms issued in the European Community Directive concerning propagative materials of vegetables [Directives nr. 93/61 on 02.07.93 and 93/62 on 05.07.93 "Conformitas Agraria Communitatis"(CAC)], which regulate the European nursery production of artichoke and chicory. According to bylaws, the assessment of the phytosanitary status of propagation material belonging to the above crops is compulsory and certified nursery production must be true to type and free from virus and virus-like organisms (virus-free category). If virus infection has been established, elimination of infected plants could have important effects, because the perennating inoculum in nepoviral infections is small and the spread of viruliferous vector from plant to plant is slow (Martelli, 1978). The notion that AILV is persistently transmitted by a nematode vector and is dependent on the vector for spreading at the site, indicates that nematode control by nematicides is highly advisable (Roca, 1984).

description:
媒介传播
AILV通过茅线型线虫阿普利亚长针线虫有效传播(Vovlas and Roca, 1975; Lamberti and Bleve Zacheo, 1977)。在传播实验中，带病毒的手选的线虫从菊苣被传播到菊苣(Vovlas and Roca, 1975)和从菊芋到番茄(Roca et al., 1975)，分别约为60％和高达67％，饵苗被侵染。希腊的隔离种群被显示通过茅线型线虫横带长针线虫传播(Roca et al., 1982)。病毒粒子被发现于带病毒的线虫媒介的消化道的前部(Taylor et al., 1976)。

种传传播
通过菊苣的种子传播尚未被报道(Vovlas et al., 1971)。但是，Bottalico et al. (2002)报道在朝鲜蓟的真实种子中病毒的传播。

农业实践
病毒通过短距离传播依赖于线虫活性，而受病毒感染的未受控制的分布范围的种植材料扮演着重要的角色在远范围的传播中，因为菊芋是营养繁殖的。来自受感染的母株的繁殖材料表现出一种有效的病毒传播方式，这样引进病毒的接种体到传播媒介可能存在的位点。而且，种植材料对媒介传播有帮助是可能的，因为大批滋生的土壤伴随着菊芋长插条。 Vector transmission

AILV is efficiently transmitted by the dorylamoid nematode Longidorus apulus (Vovlas and Roca, 1975; Lamberti and Bleve Zacheo, 1977). In transmission experiments, in which viruliferous hand-picked nematodes were transferred from chicory to chicory (Vovlas and Roca, 1975) and from artichoke to tomato (Roca et al., 1975), about 60% and up to 67%, respectively, of bait seedlings were infected. The Greek isolate was shown to be transmitted by the dorylamoid nematode Longidorus fasciatus (Roca et al., 1982). Virus particles were observed in the fore part of the alimentary tract of viruliferous nematode vectors (Taylor et al., 1976). 

Seedborne spread

Transmission through seed of chicory has not been reported (Vovlas et al., 1971). However, Bottalico et al. (2002) report transmission of the virus in true seed of globe artichoke. 

Agricultural practices

Virus dissemination over short distances relies on nematode activity, whereas uncontrolled distribution of virus-infected propagating material plays a major role in long-range spread, because artichoke is vegetatively propagated. Propagation material from infected mother plants represents an effective means of virus dispersal, thus introducing viral inoculum to sites where vectors may be present. Moreover, it is possible that propagation material can contribute to vector dispersal, because of the infested soil accompanying artichoke sets.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info: 最简单的防治方法是运用免疫病毒的繁殖材料。这种观念是与发行于关于蔬菜的繁殖材料的欧盟指令一致的[Directives nr. 93/61 on 02.07.93 and 93/62 on 05.07.93 "Conformitas Agraria Communitatis"(CAC)]，这指令控制着菊芋和菊苣的欧洲苗圃生产。依据内部章程，属于上述的作物的繁殖材料的植物检疫性的估价是强制的，且被鉴定的苗圃生产必须是真正的典型的和对病毒和象病毒的生物是免疫的（对病毒免疫的种类）。如果病毒侵染已被确定，受侵染的植株的消除可能有重大的意义，因为多年生接种体在线虫传多面体病毒侵染中是很少的，且带病毒的传播媒介从植株到植株的传播是很慢的(Martelli, 1978)。AILV通过线虫类媒介持续传播及取决于在定点的传播媒介的观念指出通过杀线虫剂控制线虫是高度可取的(Roca, 1984)。 The simplest control method would be the use of virus-free propagation material. According to bylaws, the assessment of the phytosanitary status of propagation material belonging to the above crops is compulsory and certified nursery production must be true to type and free from virus and virus-like organisms (virus-free category). If virus infection has been established, elimination of infected plants could have important effects, because the perennating inoculum in nepoviral infections is small and the spread of viruliferous vector from plant to plant is slow (Martelli, 1978). GFLV is responsible for fanleaf degeneration disease, one of the most damaging viral diseases of grapevine causing malformation of leaves and affecting fruit quality and yield.
description: To monitor the phytosanitary status of vines to ensure the sustainability of the industry in the UK, four samples were collected in April 2017. These were one dormant cane, selected at random, from each of four geographically separated vineyards which were from Pinot Noir clones (119, 336, 792 and 924) reciprocally grafted upon Gravesac, SO4 or 3309 Couderc rootstocks. RNA was extracted from cambial scrapings and tested using specific primers for nine grapevine viruses by RT-PCR. All samples tested positive for Grapevine rupestris stem pitting-associated virus (GRSPaV) and two of the samples, clones 119 and 792, had mixed infections with Grapevine fleck virus (GFkV) and Grapevine fanleaf virus (GFLV), respectively. To our knowledge, this is the first report of GFLV in the UK.
reference_name: First report of Grapevine fanleaf virus infecting grapevine in the United Kingdom

potential_eco_desc: The economic impact of GFLV varies according to the cultivar, the viral isolate (Walter et al., 1990), the rootstock (Gallay et al., 1955; Walker et al., 1994), the climatic conditions and the age of the vine. American Vitis species and their hybrids do not show any resistance to GFLV (Egger et al., 1985). In fact, rootstocks transfer, in a sense, their susceptibility to GFLV to Vitis vinifera which, because of the co-evolution with the virus, shows a generalized tolerance to GFLV when self-rooted (Hewitt, 1968; Martelli, 1978).^p^pYield reduction has been reported on different cultivars: 12% on Thompson Seedless in Chile (Auger et al., 1992), 23% on Moscato Bianco in Italy (Gay et al., 1981), 50-77% on Chardonnay and Muscat a Petits Grains in France (Vuittenez, 1958; Boubals et al., 1964; Legin, 1972), 44-94% on Traminer in Germany (Rudel, 1984) and 78-98% on Chasselas, Merlot and Pinot Noir in Switzerland (Bovey, 1970).^p^pOddly enough, in Italy, an average yield increase of 26% and 19% was observed in GFLV-infected clones of Barbera and Nebbiolo, but a concomitant reduction of the sugar content of 3% and 1%, respectively, was registered (Gay et al., 1981).^p^pIn Australia, a 50% crop reduction was estimated in Thompson Seedless clones affected by vein banding (Woodham and Alexander, 1966), a disease caused by the combined effect of GFLV and the yellow speckle viroid (Szychowski et al., 1995).^p^pRegarding rootstocks, in Italy the weight of the wood collected from GFLV-inoculated hybrids was found to decrease by up to 46%, depending on the rootstock type (Babini et al., 1981). In Germany, the rooting success of the rootstock SO4 was 25% when heavily infected by GFLV compared to 75% when non-infected; graft take of Riesling on SO4 dropped from 30-45% to 6-10% with non-infected or GFLV-infected SO4, respectively (Bruckbauer, 1962).^p^pFollowing the simultaneous elimination after thermotherapy of GFLV and grapevine fleck virus (GFkV) from the Italian clone Michet of Nebbiolo, the vigour was higher, the breaking of dormancy was earlier and the yield increased by 50% (Mannini, 1994).

management_info: Regulatory Control^p^pPlant quarantine^p^pFor the detection of GFLV, ELISA can be applied and/or indexing by mechanical inoculation on herbaceous hosts or grafting on a grapevine indicator (Vitis rupestris St George) (Frison and Ikin, 1991).^p^pCertification^p^pThis is the only way today to limit, to some extent, the dissemination of GFLV by providing growers with virus-tested, better performing clones. Selection based only on visual examination is not sufficient. Field selection must be supplemented by indexing on V. rupestris and by laboratory tests. All candidate clones in a selection programme should be tested for the absence of GFLV or treated for the elimination of GFLV before entering the repository for further selection. management_info:
一个受GALV感染的无性繁殖系的健康植株能通过温热疗法和分生组织的顶端培养来获得(Goheen and Luhn, 1973; Barlass et al., 1982)。 Healthy plants of a GFLV-infected clone can be obtained by thermotherapy and meristem-tip culture (Goheen and Luhn, 1973; Barlass et al., 1982). 对GFLV的化学防治是不可能的。在种植葡萄树前，杀线剂被用来减少标准剑线虫（X. index）的种群数量。因为地下水污染的危险，在一些国家，这些杀线剂的使用是受到控制或甚至被禁止的。 Chemical control is impossible against GFLV. Nematicides are used to reduce the populations of X. index before planting a vine. In some countries the use of these nematicides is strictly controlled or even forbidden because of the risk of groundwater pollution. 目前没有对GALV或对它的媒介标准剑线虫（Xiphinema index）有抗性的品种被葡萄种植者所使用。添加物被利用在育种程序中，被描述为：
- 标准剑线虫（X. index）的无寄主
- 对GFLV由标准剑线虫（X. index）传播的抗性
- 对GFLV嫁接传播的抗性  (Walter, 1996).
估计通过交互保护来防治GFLV的可能性的实验正在进行(Walter et al., 1993)。 Today no cultivar resistant either to GFLV or to its vector Xiphinema index is used by grape growers. Accessions are being used in breeding programmes which are described as:
- non hosts for X. index,
- resistant to the transmission of GFLV by X. index,
- resistant to the transmission of GFLV by grafting (Walter, 1996).
Trials are being carried out to evaluate the possibility of controlling GFLV by cross-protection (Walter et al., 1993). 植物检疫：
对于GFLV的检测，ELISA能被使用和/或通过在草本寄主上机械接种或在葡萄指示寄主(Vitis rupestris（沙地葡萄）St George)上嫁接来作作病毒指示 (Frison and Ikin, 1991)。
鉴定：
这是目前唯一能通过提供经病毒测试的和更好操作的无性繁殖系给种植者来限制GFLV在一定范围内分布的方法。只根据肉眼检查的挑选是不足够的。田间挑选必需要通过在V. rupestris上作病毒指示和通过实验室实验来作补充。在一个挑选程序中所有的候选的无性繁殖系应该在进入贮藏室作进一步挑选前测试GFLV的不存在或测试GFLV的消除。应地通过以下的方法来努力保持繁殖材料尽可能长时间的不含有GALV：
- 与可能受感染的来源的田块的隔离
- 休耕和在种植前用杀线剂作土壤消毒（当允许时）
-通过肉眼检查和ELISA方法定期检查母系田块(Walter and Martelli, 1997).
北美洲和欧洲具有最长的葡萄鉴定的经历 (Martelli and Walter, 1998)。 Plant quarantine
For the detection of GFLV, ELISA can be applied and/or indexing by mechanical inoculation on herbaceous hosts or grafting on a grapevine indicator (Vitis rupestris St George) (Frison and Ikin, 1991).
Certification
This is the only way today to limit, to some extent, the dissemination of GFLV by providing growers with virus-tested, better performing clones. Selection based only on visual examination is not sufficient. Field selection must be supplemented by indexing on V. rupestris and by laboratory tests. All candidate clones in a selection programme should be tested for the absence of GFLV or treated for the elimination of GFLV before entering the repository for further selection. Efforts should be made to keep the propagation materials uncontaminated by GFLV for as long as possible by the following methods:
- isolation of the plots from possible sources of contamination,
- fallow and soil disinfection with nematicides before planting (when allowed),
- periodical checking of the mother plots by visual examination and ELISA (Walter and Martelli, 1997).
The longest experiences of grapevine certification is in North America and Europe (Martelli and Walter, 1998).

potential_eco_desc:
GFLV的经济影响是根据品种、病毒株系(Walter et al., 1990)、初生主根(Gallay et al., 1955; Walker et al., 1994) 、气候条件和葡萄树的年龄而有所变化。美洲葡萄品种和它们的杂交种对GALV不显示任何抗性(Egger et al., 1985)。事实上，在某种意义上来说初生根转移，它们对因为与病毒的联合发展而在自我生根的时候显示对GFLV的一个一般化的耐病性的葡萄（Vitis vinifera）对GFLV的敏感性(Hewitt, 1968; Martelli, 1978)。
产量的减少已在不同的品种上被报道：智利Thompson Seedless上12％(Auger et al., 1992)、意大利Moscato Bianco 上23% (Gay et al., 1981)、法国Chardonnay 和Muscat ?Petits Grains 上50-77% (Vuittenez, 1958; Boubals et al., 1964; Legin, 1972)、德国Traminer上44-94% (R黡el, 1984)以及瑞士Chasselas、Merlot 和Pinot Noir上78-98% (Bovey, 1970)。
很奇怪的是，在意大利，平均产量26％和19％的增加在分别在Barbera 和Nebbiolo的受GFLV感染的无性繁殖系中观测到，但伴随着分别含糖量3％和1％的减少已被记录(Gay et al., 1981)。
在澳大利亚，50％的产量减少在受沿脉变色病害感染的Thompson Seedless无性繁殖系上被估计出(Woodham and Alexander, 1966)，这个病害是由GFLV与葡萄黄点类病毒一起联合影响而引起的(Szychowski et al., 1995)。
不管根砧木，在意大利，从接种GFLV的杂交种中收集的木的重量被发现减少超过了46％，这是由根砧木的类型所决定的(Babini et al., 1981)。在德国，当受到GFLV严重感染时，与不感染的时候相比，根砧木SO4的生根成功率是25％；Riesling在SO4上的嫁接成功率从30-45％下降到了6-10％，这分别在不感染的或受GFLV感染的SO4上的数字。
在对意大利无性繁殖系Michet of Nebbiolo 的GFLV和葡萄斑点病毒(GFkV)的温热疗法后病毒同时的消除后，其活力是更高的，休眠的打破是更早的和其产量增加了50％(Mannini, 1994)。 The economic impact of GFLV varies according to the cultivar, the viral isolate (Walter et al., 1990), the rootstock (Gallay et al., 1955; Walker et al., 1994), the climatic conditions and the age of the vine. American Vitis species and their hybrids do not show any resistance to GFLV (Egger et al., 1985). In fact, rootstocks transfer, in a sense, their susceptibility to GFLV to Vitis vinifera which, because of the co-evolution with the virus, shows a generalized tolerance to GFLV when self-rooted (Hewitt, 1968; Martelli, 1978).
Yield reduction has been reported on different cultivars: 12% on Thompson Seedless in Chile (Auger et al., 1992), 23% on Moscato Bianco in Italy (Gay et al., 1981), 50-77% on Chardonnay and Muscat ?Petits Grains in France (Vuittenez, 1958; Boubals et al., 1964; Legin, 1972), 44-94% on Traminer in Germany (R黡el, 1984) and 78-98% on Chasselas, Merlot and Pinot Noir in Switzerland (Bovey, 1970).
Oddly enough, in Italy, an average yield increase of 26% and 19% was observed in GFLV-infected clones of Barbera and Nebbiolo, but a concomitant reduction of the sugar content of 3% and 1%, respectively, was registered (Gay et al., 1981).
In Australia, a 50% crop reduction was estimated in Thompson Seedless clones affected by vein banding (Woodham and Alexander, 1966), a disease caused by the combined effect of GFLV and the yellow speckle viroid (Szychowski et al., 1995).
Regarding rootstocks, in Italy the weight of the wood collected from GFLV-inoculated hybrids was found to decrease by up to 46%, depending on the rootstock type (Babini et al., 1981). In Germany, the rooting success of the rootstock SO4 was 25% when heavily infected by GFLV compared to 75% when non-infected; graft take of Riesling on SO4 dropped from 30-45% to 6-10% with non-infected or GFLV-infected SO4, respectively Riesling.
Following the simultaneous elimination after thermotherapy of GFLV and grapevine fleck virus (GFkV) from the Italian clone Michet of Nebbiolo, the vigour was higher, the breaking of dormancy was earlier and the yield increased by 50% (Mannini, 1994).

病毒中等距离和长距离的传播是通过感染的繁殖材料。 There is circumstantial evidence of the soil-borne nature of Grapevine chrome mosaic virus (GCMV). Infected vines may have a patchy distribution in the field and healthy vines acquire the virus when planted in these soils (Martelli et al., 1970), which frequently contain Xiphinema vuittenezi, sometimes in mixture with X. index (Martelli and Sarospataki, 1969; Mali et al., 1975). Nematode transmission was suggested but although virus particles were detected by immunosorbent electron microscopy (ISEM) in X. index extracts (Roberts and Brown, 1980), trials with both nematode species gave negative results (Martelli and Sarospataki, 1969; Mali et al., 1975; Mali, 1976) or inconclusive results (Taylor and Brown, 1997).

description: Incidence^p^pCLRV is seedborne in several plant species including birch (Buttner et al., 1996), walnut (Quacquarelli and Savino, 1977; Topchiiska, 1993), black cherry (Schimanski et al., 1976) and olive (Saponari et al., 2002). CLRV is pollen-transmitted. Cooper et al. (1984) showed that in CLRV-free birch trees which received pollen from an infected tree, CLRV antigen was introduced into, and multiplied within, the embryos but not the seed coat or the pericarp/wings. Embryos in seeds from CLRV-infected birch that received CLRV-free pollen differed from their healthy counterparts in being shrunken and suspended in a loosely fibrillar matrix that contained numerous virus-like particles in tubular inclusions. In two trees, CLRV-free pollen tended to fertilize a greater percentage of ovules than CLRV-infected pollen. Cooper et al. (1984) also showed that few embryos seemed to escape invasion by CLRV when the maternal tissue was naturally infected. Seeds from infected walnut trees were stored at 2-5°C for periods of 1 year. Within 45 days the virus was isolated from 5 of 8 seeds tested, whereas after 1 year it was recovered from 2 of 12 (Quacquarelli and Savino, 1977).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pThe proportion of seeds germinating after crosses in which both parents were CLRV-free was greater than when either or both parents were infected, but the largest difference occurred with infection in the female parent (Cooper et al., 1984).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSeedling tests on walnut seeds from infected trees, stored at 2-5°C for a period of 1 year, showed seed transmission of the virus (Quacquarelli and Savino, 1977). Schimanski et al. (1976) showed that a small percentage (0.5 and 0.8%) of seedlings from two infected black cherry plants were infected with CLRV, but no seedlings from a healthy plant were infected. Field observations on the patterns of virus spread, as measured by seedling infection, were consistent with seed transmiision; about 3% of seedlings from a tree 6.9 m away from the nearest source of inoculum were infected but no infected seedlings were detected in more distant trees, even though each was experimentally infectible with CLRV, and pollen from the infected tree germinated on their stigmas (Cooper et al., 1984).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pSerological ^p^pCLRV has been detected in seeds of walnut by ELISA (Topchiiska, 1993).^p^pPCR^p ^pImmunocapture RT-PCR has been used to demonstrate that CLRV isolates and strains could be detected in birch by direct sequencing of their PCR products. The virus was readily found throughout the year in seeds (Buttner et al., 1996). CLRV was detected in 45 of 50 olive seeds by RT-PCR (Saponari et al., 2002).

description:
不像许多线虫传多面体病毒的那样，CLRV不能通过生活在土壤中的线虫传播(Jones et al., 1981; Fulton and Fulton, 1970)，尽管较早声明是如此(Fritzsche and Kegler, 1964; Flegg, 1969)，在自然中也不普遍地侵染草本野草品种。有证据证明胡桃(Juglans regia)和桦树(Betula spp.)中的株系能通过花粉传播到授粉植物中去(Mircetich et al., 1980; Cooper et al., 1984)；没有进行测试来证明是否这种传播模式发生在其他的自然寄主上。在实验上，该病毒容易通过汁液的机械接种传播到大范围的草本品种中去(Jones, 1985)。它也能通过嫁接接种传播。
缺乏自然寄主，在实践上，CLRV通常有侵染种子或植物随人类的运动或通过花粉传播。 Unlike many nepoviruses, CLRV appears not to be transmitted by soil-inhabiting nematodes (Jones et al., 1981; Fulton and Fulton, 1970) despite earlier claims (Fritzsche and Kegler, 1964; Flegg, 1969), nor is it reported to infect commonly herbaceous weed species in nature. There is evidence that strains in walnut (Juglans regia) and birch (Betula spp.) are pollen-transmitted to the pollinated plant (Mircetich et al., 1980; Cooper et al., 1984); no tests have been made to see if this mode of transmission occurs in other natural hosts. Experimentally, the virus is readily transmitted by mechanical inoculation of sap to a wide range of herbaceous species (Jones, 1985). It is also transmitted by graft-inoculation. 
Lacking a natural vector, in practice, CLRV is often dispersed by human movement of infected seeds or plants, or by pollen.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
CLRV通过花粉传播，这使到它在作物的传播的防治有困难，除了使用免疫性或抗性品种。对CLRV的免疫性、抗性和耐病性在黑核桃（Juglans spp.）上被报道(Dosba and Germain, 1993)。在这些抗性材料的缺乏额情况下，健康种植材料应被使用在远离已知发生CLRV侵染的种植作物品种的地方中。
该病毒能通过分生组织顶端培养和通过维持幼苗在40℃下7天或32℃下20天来从一些植物上根除(Cooper and Walkey, 1978)。 The transmission of CLRV by pollen makes its spread in crops difficult to control except by the use of plants immune or resistant to infection. Immunity, resistance and tolerance to CLRV in Juglans spp. is reported (Dosba and Germain, 1993). In the absence of such resistant material, healthy planting material should be used in areas free from known infection with CLRV in the crop species planted.
The virus can be eliminated from some plants by meristem tip culture and by maintaining seedlings for 7 days at 40℃or 20 days at 32℃(Cooper and Walkey, 1978).
