description: In March 2016, a plant of Phlox stolonifera ‘Blue Ridge’ with mild leaf mottle symptoms was received at the Plant Health and Environment Laboratory (PHEL, Auckland, New Zealand). The plant originated from a commercial plant nursery in Christchurch on the South Island. The causal agent was identified as Spiranthes mosaic virus 3 (SpMV3) by sequences analysis. Samples from a further 12 phlox plants (including two plants of P. drummondii and five each of P. stolonifera and P. subulata) that had been collected from different regions in the North and South Islands of the country, were tested for the presence of SpMV3 using the SpMV3-specific primers. Four plants (two plants each of P. stolonifera and P. subulata) from both North and South Islands tested positive. To our knowledge, this is the first report of SpMV3 in New Zealand.
reference_name: First Report of Spiranthes mosaic virus 3 in Phlox spp. in New Zealand

description: During spring 2015, in a patch of Columbus grass (Sorghum almum) growing near a sugarcane field at Canal Point in Florida, patterns of contrasting shades of green were observed on leaves of several plants. The samples of these plants with mosaic-looking symptoms were collected and identified, TEM, ISEM, ELISA, RT-PCR, and sequence analysis from multiple plants confirmed the presence of Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) in S. almum. This is the first report SCMV infect S. almum in the United States.

host_range: 穇子Eleusine coracana
description: In 2011, maize lethal necrosis (MLN) was reported from Bomet, Kenya as a result of coinfection of maize with Maize chlorotic mottle virus (MCMV) and Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV). MLN was later reported from other locations in Kenya and other African countries. During a survey (March to June 2014) for alternate hosts of MCMV and SCMV in MLN hotspots of Bomet (0.8490°S, 35.3874°E) and Nyamira (0.7866°S, 34.9843°E), leaves from finger millet with symptoms of viral infection were sampled. Based on biological detection, serological and molecular diagnostics showed that the causal agent was Maize chlorotic mottle virus (MCMV) and Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV). To our knowledge, this is the first report on occurrence of lethal necrosis in finger millet from Kenya or elsewhere. The transmission of MCMV and SCMV from finger millet to maize or other hosts remains to be investigated and considered in management programs for lethal necrosis of maize and millets.  Aphids (Rhopalosiphum sp., Sitobion avenae) and corn thrips (Frankliniella williamsi), which are known vectors of SCMV and MCMV, respectively, were collected from the finger millet .
reference_name: First Report of Lethal Necrosis Disease Associated With Co-Infection of Finger Millet With Maize chlorotic mottle

host_range: 侧钝叶草Stenotaphrum secundatum cv. Floratam
description: Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) causes a mosaic disease of St. Augustinegrass (Stenotaphrum secundatum [Walt.] Kuntze) first documented in Florida in 1963. Symptomatic St. Augustinegrass was found in lawns, pastures, and sod farms near Canal Point and Belle Glade, FL, an area that was dominated by sugarcane production. In December 2013, symptoms of mosaic and necrosis on St. Augustinegrass were reported from more than 50 residential lawns within a 10-km radius of the Bayway Isles community in south St. Petersburg, FL. Samples were collected from cv. Floratam sod, then developed severe mosaic and later necrosis by September 2013. The presence of SCMV was confirmed with triplicate assays from two Floratam samples from two different lawns using a DAS ELISA kit and RT-PCR. One amplicon from each of two symptomatic Floratam plants was cloned into pGEM T-easy and sequenced. The two nucleotide sequences were 98.9% similar to each other. The Blastn analysis using the nonredundant database showed highest percent similarity to SCMV-Ohio (JX188385) and SCMV-JAL-1 (GU474635). Pairwise similarity analysis indicated that the CP nucleotide sequences of the two St. Augustinegrass isolates were 90.7 and 90.3% similar to those of SCMV-Ohio and SCMV-JAL-1, respectively. Five additional lawns with mosaic were sampled in December 2013 and tested positive by ELISA. Fifteen additional samples were collected in September 2014 that tested positive by ELISA and RT-PCR. This is the first report of a large-scale outbreak of mosaic and necrosis associated with SCMV in central Florida and signifies an important movement of the pathogen geographically within the state to an area where no sugarcane is produced. This is also the first report of the disease occurring on Floratam, the predominant cultivar of St. Augustinegrass used for lawns in Florida. The disease has killed cv. Floratam lawns, and diagnosticians should be alerted to the potential for outbreaks outside sugarcane-growing regions.
reference_name: Severe Symptoms of Mosaic and Necrosis in cv. Floratam St. Augustinegrass Associated with Sugarcane mosaic virus in Neighborhoods of St. Petersburg, FL

host_range: 玉米Zea mays
description: Maize lethal necrosis（MLN） caused by MCMV and the potyvirus Sugarcane mosaic virus (SCMV) was identified in Kenya in 2012 and associated with significant damage. Subsequent to the outbreak in Kenya, MLN symptoms have been associated with MCMV and SCMV in Tanzania and Uganda and, based on our initial findings, MCMV but not SCMV in Rwanda. In March and June 2013 samples of maize showing signs of MLN symptoms were received from the Northern Province of Rwanda for MCMV and SCMV testing. The test demonstrated,the Complete genomes of MCMV shown to have a very close relatedness with MCMV from Kenya(99% homology). The SCMV isolated from Rwandan samples is distinct from that isolated in Kenya (87% identity) and most closely related (95% identity) to strain SCMV-DMB (BA00797). These data would support a shared origin for MCMV in Rwanda and Kenya, but different sources for SCMV. This report confirms that MLN, caused by MCMV and SCMV, is now present in Rwanda and that this is most probably due to the recent introduction of MCMV.
reference_name: First report of maize lethal necrosis disease in Rwanda

potential_eco_desc: Introduction^p^pIn the past, SCMV has caused alarming losses in various sugarcane-growing regions, including Hawaii, Egypt, Natal (South Africa), Argentina, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Australia and the USA (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). Epidemics have been followed by replacement of susceptible noble-type canes by hybrid canes with tolerance or, better still, resistance. The evolution of new strains of SCMV has required a continuing breeding programme to prevent heavy losses.^p^pLosses caused by SCMV are mainly (1) a reduced yield of the crop, (2) the need to include mosaic resistance when breeding new cultivars, and (3) the slowing of the interchange of cultivars between countries because of quarantine concerns over the introduction of new strains of SCMV. ^p^p^Crop Losses^p^pCrop losses caused by SCMV depend on many factors, including the susceptibility of the cultivars to the prevailing strains of SCMV, the incidence of infection, the prevailing environmental conditions, the stage of growth when infection occurs, and interaction with other agents affecting the crop. Crop losses can vary from negligible to severe. Some recent instances of heavy losses in sugarcane crops due to mosaic outbreaks are as follows. ^p^pIn the 1980s, losses on some farms in the Isis district of Queensland, Australia, were estimated to be about 50% (Jones, 1987). In some commercial plantings of cv. Q95 from an infected source, the infected plants had fewer tillers and were less vigorous than apparently healthy plants nearby (Ryan and Jones, 1986).^p^pIn Guatemala in 1974-1976, many stunted stools of mosaic-affected cv. Q83 were responsible for lack of uniformity in fields near Santa Lucia. The cane tonnage in these fields was seriously reduced (Fors, 1978). ^p^p^Estimations of Potential Losses in Experiments^p^pSugarcane^p^pIn Natal, South Africa, plots of sugarcane cv. NCo376 (highly susceptible) and N12 (moderately resistant) were established with either infected or healthy cane. The plots were harvested regularly and tested serologically for SCMV to the 6th ratoon. There was a decline in the number of shoots showing mosaic symptoms in both cultivars during the experiment. However, mean yield reductions were 22% for infected NCo376 and 16% for N12 compared with yields of initially healthy cane (Cronje et al., 1994). ^p^pIn Brazil, plots in two locations were planted with 0, 25, 50 and 100% initial SCMV infection. Virus spread was noticeable for cv. CB46/47, but negligible for cv. IAC50/134. For CB46/47 yield losses between initially healthy and 25% infected plots were 27% and 19% in the two locations; with 100% infection, yield reduction was 71% in both areas. For IAC50/134 the only significant difference in yield was between 0 and 100% infection, an 18% reduction in diseased plots in both areas (Matsuoka and Costa, 1974). ^p^pIn Java, Indonesia, field trials with 0 and 100% SCMV-infected seed cane gave sugar yield reductions of 9.3% for POJ3016 and 11.1% for POJ3067 associated with the disease (Kuntohartono and Legowo, 1970). ^p^pIn Spain, when healthy sugarcane was planted between rows infected by SCMV, the cultivars CO62/175 and NA56/79 were sufficiently resistant for commercial production, but losses of 0.4-0.5 t/ha were found for every 1% infection between the 2nd and 4th cutting (Olalla-Mercade et al., 1984a). ^p^pIn Pakistan, mosaic-free seed cane gave a significantly higher yield of cane (48.5 t/ha) than mosaic-infected seed cane (44.5 t/ha)(Ahmad et al., 1991). ^p^pMaize^p^pIn East Africa, 10 susceptible maize hybrids had yield losses of 18-46% when inoculated with SCMV in the seedling stage (Louie and Darrah, 1980). ^p^pIn Germany, SCMV was more prevalent than MDMV, but had a similar effect on growth and yield of maize. description: Incidence^p^pSCMV has not been reported in sugarcane seed or to be transported by sugarcane seed. However, seed cane (stalk pieces or setts), used to propagate sugarcane vegetatively, commonly transmits SCMV and other viruses from one crop to the next.^p^pWith maize, SCMV-MB (Maize dwarf mosaic virus strain B) has been detected in the pericarp, but rarely in the endosperm or embryo of seeds at 21 days after pollination. In mature seeds, it was occasionally detected in the pericarp and endosperm, but not in the embryo (Mikel et al., 1984).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pIn Pakistan, sugarcane seed cane (stalk pieces or setts) free from infection with an SCMV-like virus gave 5-11% more germination and 1.34 more tillers per plant than infected setts (Ahmad et al., 1991).^p^p^Seed Transmission^p^pThere have been no reports of seed transmission of SCMV in sugarcane and most other hosts. However, a low level of seed transmission of isolates resembling SCMV-A was reported in maize (Baudin, 1977; Fuchs et al., 1990). SCMV was also transmitted to seedlings grown in sterilized soil from infected seeds harvested from plants inoculated with MDMV strains A and B (Mikel et al., 1984).^p^p^Seed Treatments^p^pThe effects of sorghum hybrids and imidacloprid seed treatment on infestations by the vectors Rhopalosiphum maidis and Schizaphis graminum, and on the spread of MDMV-B [SCMV] have been evaluated in Kansas, USA. Imidacloprid controlled R. maidis for 3-4 weeks but not for 7 weeks after planting and reduced the spread of SCMV in a S. graminum-susceptible hybrid (Northrup King S9750) in one year but not in another. Differences among hybrids in the incidence of SCMV did not appear to be related to the hybrids' reaction to S. graminum. However, one S. graminum-resistant hybrid (Dekalb DK-39Y) appeared to be highly resistant to natural infection by SCMV, even though it was susceptible when inoculated mechanically (Harvey et al., 1996).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pSerological test^p^pELISA successfully detected SCMV in seed parts (Mikel et al., 1984).

management_info: Control of SCMV^p^pAttempts to eradicate SCMV by roguing infected plants have rarely been successful (Abbott, 1961; Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). Roguing by digging out or applying herbicides may be useful in maintaining mosaic-free seed plots of cane if the level of infection is lower than 5% (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). The use of mosaic-free seed cane is an effective control measure where inoculum pressures are not intense. Thermotherapy of planting material can result in some plants that are free of SCMV (Mirza et al., 1986; Benda et al., 1989).^p^pMosaic in sugarcane has long been controlled by the development and use of resistant clones. Breeding programmes may be designed to produce resistant clones which can be tested against the prevalent virus strains (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989).^p^p^p^Control of Aphid Vectors^p^pA close relationship exists between ants and aphid vectors of SCMV (Charpentier, 1963). Ants can carry the aphids from one sugarcane plant to another, from grass to cane and from cane to grass. Presumably, ants also decrease attacks on aphids by parasitoids and predators, which would otherwise exert better control.^p^pBecause aphids which transmit SCMV come from outside as well as inside the sugarcane crop, care should be given to reduce the build up of the vector species in the vicinity. Crops of maize and sorghum are good hosts of vectors such as R. maidis, and should not be grown near infected sugarcane crops. Altering the times of planting and harvesting so that they do not coincide with high aphid vector populations can reduce losses (Bailey and Fox, 1980).^p^pThe use of insecticides failed to prevent aphid vectors from spreading SCMV (Charpentier, 1956).

description:
SCMV由蚜虫介体以非持久性的方式传播。与澳大利亚的自然传播有关的蚜虫的种可能是玉米蚜，棉蚜和桃蚜 (Noone et al., 1994)；玉米蚜和狗尾草蚜是与美国路易斯安那州有关(Abbott, 1961)；玉米蚜和禾谷缢管蚜与南非有关(Anon., 1986)。在澳大利亚，高梁蚜，甘蔗蚜虫和狗尾草蚜（一种野草蚜虫）是非介体，然而有双子叶寄主的棉蚜和桃蚜能够传播SCMV。在生长的早期阶段，甘蔗对感染更敏感(Srisink et al., 1994)。

SCMV在营养种植材料的传播是另外一个重要的传播病毒的方法。有轻微症状的成熟甘蔗可被作为种植材料，于是，病毒能广泛传播(Srisink et al., 1993)。 SCMV is transmitted by aphid vectors in the non-persistent manner. Aphid species involved in natural spread in Australia may be Rhopalosiphum maidis, Aphis gossypii and Myzus persicae (Noone et al., 1994); R. maidis and Hysteroneura setariae are involved in Louisiana, USA (Abbott, 1961); and R. maidis and R. padi are involved in South Africa (Anon., 1986). In Australia, Melanaphis sacchari, the sugarcane aphid, and H. setariae, a grass aphid, were non-vectors, whereas A. gossypii and M. persicae, which have dicotyledonous hosts, were able to transmit SCMV. Sugarcane is more susceptible to infection if in an early stage of growth (Srisink et al., 1994). 

Transmission of SCMV in vegetative planting material is an additional important method of spreading the virus. Mature sugarcane plants with mild symptoms may be used as planting material, and thus the virus may be distributed widely (Srisink et al., 1993).

management_info:
一种密切的关系存在于SCMV的蚂蚁和蚜虫媒介之间(Charpentier, 1963)。蚂蚁能从一株甘蔗植株携带到另一株，从牧草到甘蔗和从甘蔗到牧草。可推定，蚂蚁也减少蚜虫上的攻击由拟寄生和捕食者，会不同地应用更好的控制。
因为传播SCMV的蚜虫来自于甘蔗作物的外面和里面，所以在周围地区减少媒介昆虫种类的建立应该小心。玉米和高粱的作物是像玉米蚜一样的媒介昆虫的良好的寄主，且不应该被种植于感病的甘蔗作物附近。改变种植和收获的时间这样它们不与高的蚜虫媒介种群同时发生可以降低损失(Bailey and Fox, 1980)。
杀虫剂的使用对防止蚜虫媒介传播SCMV而言是失败的(Charpentier, 1956)。 A close relationship exists between ants and aphid vectors of SCMV (Charpentier, 1963). Ants can carry the aphids from one sugarcane plant to another, from grass to cane and from cane to grass. Presumably, ants also decrease attacks on aphids by parasitoids and predators, which would otherwise exert better control.
Because aphids which transmit SCMV come from outside as well as inside the sugarcane crop, care should be given to reduce the build up of the vector species in the vicinity. Crops of maize and sorghum are good hosts of vectors such as R. maidis, and should not be grown near infected sugarcane crops. Altering the times of planting and harvesting so that they do not coincide with high aphid vector populations can reduce losses (Bailey and Fox, 1980).
The use of insecticides failed to prevent aphid vectors from spreading SCMV (Charpentier, 1956).   试图通过去杂感病的植株根除SCMV是很少有成功的(Abbott, 1961; Koike and Gillaspie, 1989)。通过取出或运用除草剂去杂可能是有用的在保持甘蔗的抗花叶的种子区里如果侵染水平低于5%(Koike and Gillaspie, 1989)。抗花叶的种子甘蔗的使用是一种有效的防治方法而接种压力不是强烈的。种植材料的热治疗可能导致一些植株摆脱SCMV(Mirza et al., 1986; Benda et al., 1989)。
甘蔗中的花叶已经长期被无性抗性的发展和使用控制。繁殖方案可能被设计来生产能被测试对抗普遍存在的病毒株系的无性抗性(Koike and Gillaspie, 1989)。 Attempts to eradicate SCMV by roguing infected plants have rarely been successful (Abbott, 1961; Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). Roguing by digging out or applying herbicides may be useful in maintaining mosaic-free seed plots of cane if the level of infection is lower than 5% (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). The use of mosaic-free seed cane is an effective control measure where inoculum pressures are not intense. Thermotherapy of planting material can result in some plants that are free of SCMV (Mirza et al., 1986; Benda et al., 1989).
Mosaic in sugarcane has long been controlled by the development and use of resistant clones. Breeding programmes may be designed to produce resistant clones which can be tested against the prevalent virus strains (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989).

potential_eco_desc:
联合病害
SCMV和马铃薯Y病毒有关系的病毒可能与其它植物病原物一齐发生；加成或增效作用可能发生。
在美国路易斯安娜州，在CP67-412品种中甘蔗损失由高粱花叶病毒（正式称为SCMV-H）和截根苗矮缩病害(RSD, 由Clavibacter xyli细菌引起)会产生加成作用，但在品种CP65-357上产生增效作用（比各个病害单独作用加起来作用更强）(Koike, 1982)。在西班牙，RSD症状是与SCMV的存在有关，在田间由RSD引起的损害比清晰的花叶症状更严重(Olalla-Mercade et al., 1984b)。
在泰国，用类似SCMV病毒去接种霜霉病易感玉米品种Guatemala只会轻微的增强其对Sclerospora sorghi的易感性，然而对于抗性玉米品种Suwan 1，该病毒增加其易感性27－61% (Sutabutra et al., 1976)。 Disease Complexes

SCMV and related potyviruses may occur in disease complexes with other plant pathogens; either additive or synergistic effects may occur. 

In Louisiana, USA, losses in sugarcane caused by sorghum mosaic virus (formerly called SCMV-H) and ratoon stunting disease (RSD, caused by the bacterium Clavibacter xyli) were additive in cv. CP67-412, but synergistic (greater than the sum of each disease separately) in CP65-357 (Koike, 1982). In Spain, RSD symptoms were associated with the presence of SCMV, and damage by RSD was greatest in fields with clear mosaic symptoms (Olalla-Mercade et al., 1984b).

In Thailand, inoculation of the downy mildew-susceptible maize cv. Guatemala with an SCMV-like virus increased susceptibility to Sclerospora sorghi only slightly, whereas with the resistant Suwan 1 maize cv., the virus increased susceptibility from 27-61% (Sutabutra et al., 1976). 产量损失：
由SCMV引起的作物损失由许多因素决定，其中包括栽培品种对SCMV优势品种的易感性，侵染的发病率，主要的环境条件，感染时生长的阶段，和影响作物的其它因素的交互作用。作物损失能从可以忽略到严重有所不同。由于花叶爆发引起的近来的一些重大的甘蔗作物损失实例如下。 
         在20世纪80年代，澳洲昆士兰Isis地区的某些农场的损失估计达到50% (Jones, 1987)。在某些从感染来源种植Q95经济种植品种的农场，感染植株较少分蘖，并且比附近健康的植株明显地弱小(Ryan and Jones, 1986)。
         1974-1976年间在危地马拉，许多被Q83花叶品种侵染是造成Santa Lucia附近出现均匀矮化的新枝的原因。在那些田地上茎的产量锐减(Fors, 1978).。 Crop Losses

Crop losses caused by SCMV depend on many factors, including the susceptibility of the cultivars to the prevailing strains of SCMV, the incidence of infection, the prevailing environmental conditions, the stage of growth when infection occurs, and interaction with other agents affecting the crop. Crop losses can vary from negligible to severe. Some recent instances of heavy losses in sugarcane crops due to mosaic outbreaks are as follows. 

In the 1980s, losses on some farms in the Isis district of Queensland, Australia, were estimated to be about 50% (Jones, 1987). In some commercial plantings of cv. Q95 from an infected source, the infected plants had fewer tillers and were less vigorous than apparently healthy plants nearby (Ryan and Jones, 1986).

In Guatemala in 1974-1976, many stunted stools of mosaic-affected cv. Q83 were responsible for lack of uniformity in fields near Santa Lucia. The cane tonnage in these fields was seriously reduced (Fors, 1978).

potential_eco_desc:
SCMV和相关的马铃薯Y病毒可能发生于具其它植株病原的病害复合体中；或者附加或者协同效应可能发生。

在泰国，有软毛的易受霉影响的玉米栽培种危地马拉与像SCMV的病毒的接种仅稍微增加对Sclerospora sorghi的易受影响性，而与抗病的Suwan 1玉米栽培种，病毒增加易受影响性27-61% (Sutabutra et al., 1976)。 SCMV and related potyviruses may occur in disease complexes with other plant pathogens; either additive or synergistic effects may occur.
In Louisiana, USA, losses in sugarcane caused by sorghum mosaic virus (formerly called SCMV-H) and ratoon stunting disease (RSD, caused by the bacterium Clavibacter xyli) were additive in cv. CP67-412, but synergistic (greater than the sum of each disease separately) in CP65-357 (Koike, 1982). In Spain, RSD symptoms were associated with the presence of SCMV, and damage by RSD was greatest in fields with clear mosaic symptoms (Olalla-Mercade et al., 1984b).
In Thailand, inoculation of the downy mildew-susceptible maize cv. Guatemala with an SCMV-like virus increased susceptibility to Sclerospora sorghi only slightly, whereas with the resistant Suwan 1 maize cv., the virus increased susceptibility from 27-61% (Sutabutra et al., 1976). 在过去，SCMV已经造成惊人的损失在各种各样的甘蔗种植区里，包括夏威夷，埃及，Natal（南非），阿根廷，波多黎各，古巴，澳大利亚和美国(Koike and Gillaspie, 1989)。流行学已经被由具耐抗或更好的抗性的杂交植物细茎代替易受影响的非凡型的细茎追随。SCMV的新株系的进化要求防止严重损失的不断的繁殖方案。
由SCMV造成的损失主要是（1）作物产量的降低，（2）当繁殖新栽培种时包括花叶抗性的需要，和（3）国家之间栽培种的交换缓慢由于检疫隔离关注SCMV的新株系的引种。 In the past, SCMV has caused alarming losses in various sugarcane-growing regions, including Hawaii, Egypt, Natal (South Africa), Argentina, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Australia and the USA (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). Epidemics have been followed by replacement of susceptible noble-type canes by hybrid canes with tolerance or, better still, resistance. The evolution of new strains of SCMV has required a continuing breeding programme to prevent heavy losses.
Losses caused by SCMV are mainly (1) a reduced yield of the crop, (2) the need to include mosaic resistance when breeding new cultivars, and (3) the slowing of the interchange of cultivars between countries because of quarantine concerns over the introduction of new strains of SCMV.

management_info:
使用杀虫剂不能阻止蚜虫介体传播SCMV (Charpentier, 1956)。 The use of insecticides failed to prevent aphid vectors from spreading SCMV (Charpentier, 1956). 蚜虫介体防治：

Crops of maize and sorghum are good hosts of vectors such as R. maidis, and should not be grown near infected sugarcane crops. 　　甘蔗花叶长期通过抗性的无性繁殖的运用和发展来控制。饲养程序可设计的产生能够测试普遍病毒品种的抗性无性繁殖(Koike and Gillaspie, 1989)。 Control of SCMV

Roguing by digging out or applying herbicides may be useful in maintaining mosaic-free seed plots of cane if the level of infection is lower than 5% (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989). The use of mosaic-free seed cane is an effective control measure where inoculum pressures are not intense. Thermotherapy of planting material can result in some plants that are free of SCMV (Mirza et al., 1986; Benda et al., 1989).

Mosaic in sugarcane has long been controlled by the development and use of resistant clones. Breeding programmes may be designed to produce resistant clones which can be tested against the prevalent virus strains (Koike and Gillaspie, 1989).

host_range: The reports of TuMV infecting the species belonging to the Amaryllidaceae family are limited to the Allium genus. This is the first report of TuMV infection in a species of the Amaryllidaceae family in Chile and the first report of TuMV affecting a species of the genus Leucocoryne.
description: During the last few seasons, symptoms such as violet spots on the leaves, curling of the stems, and off color mosaic patterns on the tepals, have been increasingly observed and were attributed to a viral infection. Following a preliminary analysis that narrowed the search for the cause, Leucocoryne purpurea plants were selected for RNA extraction with RNeasy Plant Mini Kit (QIAGEN). Based on DAS-ELISA and RT-PCR the causal agen was identified as Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV). This is the first report of TuMV infection in a species of the Amaryllidaceae family in Chile and the first report of TuMV affecting a species of the genus Leucocoryne.
reference_name: First Report of Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV) Infecting Leucocoryne purpurea(Amaryllidaceae) in Chile
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: This is the first report of infection of garlic mustard with TuMV and WClMV.
description: In spring 2015, 12 weedy garlic mustard (Alliaria petiolata) plants with mosaic symptoms were found in a garden in State College, PA. The same symptoms are seen on many weedy garlic mustards in the area each spring, as they were in previous years at this location. Incidence was ～10% in the garden, with 2 of ～20 groups of 4 to 6 plants infected. The samples were collected and identified, results revealed that White clover mosaic virus (WClMV) and Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV) mixed infection on garlic mustard (Alliaria petiolata). To our knowledge, WClMV and TuMV have not been previously reported in garlic mustard plants in Pennsylvania. Other potyviruses including TuMV have been reported in garlic mustard and Brassicaceae while WClMV to our knowledge was never reported in Brassicaceae or in garlic mustard before. This is the first report of infection of garlic mustard with TuMV and WClMV, which have the potential to reduce the fitness of this plant species that is considered invasive in North America.  Turnip mosaic virus (TuMV) is transmitted by aphids in a nonpersistent manner, and causes a variety of symptoms in many Brassica spp. The presence on garlic mustard of a strain of TuMV very similar to a strain already reported in Europe on arugula (Eruca or Brassica vesicaria subsp. sativa) could indicate that this virus can be transmitted between cultivated and not cultivated Brassicaceae and that wild Brassicaceae can potentially serve as virus reservoir.
reference_name: First Report of White clover mosaic virus and Turnip mosaic virus Mixed Infection on Garlic Mustard in Pennsylvania

host_range: TuMV has a very wide host range infecting at least 318 species in 156 genera of 43 families (Edwardson and Christie, 1991), including weed species belonging to 14 different families (Shattuck, 1992). It has the widest known host range of any potyvirus in
potential_eco_desc: In a recent survey of plant virologists in 28 countries and regions, TuMV was ranked as the second most important virus infecting field-grown vegetables (Tomlinson, 1987). It was considered to be the most important virus in northern China and in Taiwan, the second most important in the UK, Greece, Japan and Sweden, the third most important in Eastern China and Ireland and the fourth most important in New South Wales (Australia), Denmark, Poland and Thailand.^p^pOf the brassicaceous crops sampled around Beijing, China, 69% were infected with TuMV (Feng et al., 1990). Considerable production losses in rape and other cultivated Brassicaceae were recorded as long ago as 1940 (Ling and Young, 1940). Similarly, it is widespread in Taiwan in commercial Brassica crops (Yoon et al., 1993). In the UK, TuMV has caused serious losses in swede (Tomlinson and Ward, 1978), white cabbage (Walkey and Webb, 1978; Walkey and Neely, 1980), Brussels sprouts (Tomlinson and Ward, 1981), cauliflower (Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978) and rape (Hardwick et al., 1994). In Canada, the virus has caused severe production losses in rutabaga (Brassica napus var. napobrassica) (Shattuck and Stobbs, 1987).^p^pEpidemics have occurred periodically in many regions of the world causing serious losses in statice (Limonium perezii) (Niblett et al., 1969) and lettuce in California (Zink and Duffus, 1970), Matthiola incana in Argentina (Pontis, 1973), endive and escarole (Cichorium endiva) in New Jersey and New York (Citir and Varney, 1974b; Provvidenti et al., 1979), collards (B. oleracea) in Georgia and South Carolina (Khan and Demski, 1982), brassicaceous crops in New Zealand (Palmer, 1983), Matthiola incana in the Middle East (Bahar et al., 1985), turnips in Alabama (Wilson and Stevens, 1986) and horseradish in Sweden (Shattuck, 1992).^p^pIn addition to reducing yield, TuMV affects quality. In the UK, infected crops of cauliflower have been downgraded and sent for freezing rather than fresh market, representing a considerable economic loss. In Canada, changes in glucosinolate levels have been demonstrated in rutabaga due to TuMV infection and it was suggested that such changes may affect flavour (Stobbs et al., 1991). The virus can also delay crop maturity, e.g. delaying harvest date in cauliflowers by 31 days (Pink and Walkey, 1988). In the UK, complete crop failure has occurred due to TuMV in which whole fields of swede have been ploughed in.

management_info: Control of turnip mosaic potyvirus is quite difficult due to the very wide host range of the virus, the ineffectiveness of insecticides in controlling the spread of non-persistently transmitted viruses, and the lack of immune crop cultivars.^p^pHost-Plant Resistance^p^pThe use of resistant cultivars would be the simplest, cheapest, most environmentally friendly and possibly the most effective means of control.^p^pExtreme forms of 'race'-specific resistance to the virus have been identified in swede (Tomlinson and Ward, 1978; 1982; Shattuck and Stobbs, 1987; Doucet et al., 1990; Shattuck, 1992) and rape (Walsh and Tomlinson, 1985; Walsh, 1989; Stobbs et al., 1989), forms of B. napus and in B. rapa (Chen, 1980; Provvidenti, 1980; Niu et al., 1983; Green and Deng, 1985; Yoon et al., 1993; Suh et al., 1995). Some of these sources of resistance may be immunity where the virus fails to replicate (Provvidenti, 1980; Tomlinson and Ward, 1982; Shattuck and Stobbs, 1987; Walsh, 1989). However, no such major sources of resistance have been found in B. oleracea types (Walkey, 1982; Pink et al., 1986; Pink and Walkey, 1988; Walkey and Pink, 1988). Where known, the B. napus resistance genes are in the A genome of B. napus, suggesting that there are no genes for extreme forms of resistance to TuMV in the C genome of B. oleracea.^p^pSome more recently identified sources of resistance to turnip mosaic potyvirus in B. rapa appear to have resistance to a broad spectrum of pathotypes (Suh et al., 1995; J A Walsh, Horticulture Research International, Wellesbourne, UK, 1996). For one of these resistances, no isolate of TuMV so far tested has been found to overcome the resistance. The resistance is not immunity, replication is detected in inoculated leaves, but the viruses do not appear to spread systemically indicating that the resistance is effective against long-distance movement of the virus. One Brassica resistance gene (TuRB01) has been mapped (J A Walsh, Horticulture Research International, Wellesbourne, UK, 1997) and others are currently being mapped (J A Walsh, Horticulture Research International, Wellesbourne, UK, 1996). This will facilitate rapid incorporation of resistance to TuMV into desirable genetic backgrounds via marker-assisted breeding. Inter-species transfer from B. rapa to B. oleracea is also being attempted using these techniques.^p^pSources of resistance to the virus have also been identified in non-Brassica species. The dominant Tu gene in lettuce confers resistance to infection by TuMV and this gene has been mapped (Robbins et al., 1994). Most accessions of chicory (Cichorium intybus) tested by Provvidenti et al. (1979) were found to be resistant to TuMV and were proposed as a valuable source of resistance for endive and escarole (Cichorium endivia), all accessions of which tested were susceptible to the virus. Resistance to one strain of the virus has been reported in Impatiens balsamina (Provvidenti, 1982). Other sources of resistance have been reviewed by Shattuck (1992).^p^pVector Control^p^pNon-persistently transmitted viruses are difficult to control with insecticides. Most insecticides do not kill the insects rapidly enough to prevent virus introduction during brief feeding probes. There are examples of their use increasing the incidence of virus in crops (Rice et al., 1983; Roberts et al., 1993) by causing increased probing activity and movement of aphids. Additionally, widespread use of broad-spectrum insecticides is known to reduce populations of beneficial insects including aphid predators and parasitoids and has led to aphids with insecticide resistance. The use of selective insecticides is likely to reduce secondary spread of TuMV in crops following primary infection. There are reports of insecticidal sprays proving ineffective in the control of the virus (Evans and MacNeil, 1983; Niu et al., 1983). As new insecticides are produced and aphid-repellent substances developed, they will have to be evaluated

description:
TuMV是通过蚜虫以非持久的口针传方式传播。跳甲(Phyllotreta spp.) (Carden and Gladders, 1984)和一些蓟马品种(Tompkins, 1939)也能传播病毒。29个属的89个种的蚜虫被鉴定未传播媒介(Edwardson and Christie, 1991)。在安大略省，玉米蚜（Rhopalosiphum maidis）和桃蚜（Myzus persicae）是TuMV的主要媒介(Lowery, 1988)。在中国北方，菜缢管芽（R. pseudobrassicae ）[Lipaphis erysimi]、桃蚜（Myzus persicae）和甘蓝蚜（Brevicoryne brassicae）被认为是最重要的传播媒介(Kennedy et al., 1962; Shukla et al., 1994).。所有龄期的昆虫都能传播。病毒的获得和接种需时不到1分钟，没有潜伏期而且蚜虫在获得病毒后典型地保持其侵染性一段短的时期(Sylvester, 1953)。被显示，桃蚜（Myzus persicae）能保持TuMV 3-5个小时，虽然当在健康植株上取食时其侵染能力迅速丧失(Sylvester, 1954; Nishi, 1969)。
通过蚜虫的非持久性传播通常发生在短距离上（超过几百米），特别是顺风和包括迁飞的有翅蚜虫。天气的条件和温度影响蚜虫的活动和轮流影响TuMV分散的迁飞型。温暖的冬天接着一个干燥和温暖的春天会适合蚜虫繁殖和分散，因此会提早和增加病毒的传播。凉爽、湿润和多风的夏天会减少蚜虫的繁殖和运动，因此病毒传播会减少。病毒的浓度和它在感染植物中的分散影响病毒的获得和蚜虫的传播(Broadbent, 1954)。
一旦初侵染在田间建立，如果没有防治蚜虫的话TuMV可相对快速地在植物间传播。
感染的一年生或多年生观赏植物如紫罗兰（Matthiola incana）、桂竹香（Cheiranthus cheiri）、百日草属（Zinnia spp.）和矮牵牛属（Petunia spp.），以及多年生蔬菜如大黄(Rheum rhabarbarum)，也能是重要的病毒储存场所。
营养繁殖的作物，例如在一些国家的豆瓣菜、一些芸苔属（Brassica spp.）品种和大黄，在整个繁殖过程中携带TuMV。 TuMV is transmitted in the non-persistent stylet-borne manner by aphids. It has been suggested that flea beetles (Phyllotreta spp.) (Carden and Gladders, 1984) and various thrips species (Tompkins, 1939) can also spread the virus. Eighty-nine species of aphids in 29 genera have been identified as vectors (Edwardson and Christie, 1991). In Ontario, Rhopalosiphum maidis and Myzus persicae are the main vectors of TuMV (Lowery, 1988). In northern China, R. pseudobrassicae [Lipaphis erysimi], M. persicae and Brevicoryne brassicae, are thought to be the most important vectors (Chiu and Chang, 1982). Elsewhere M. persicae, B. brassicae, Aphis gossypii and Hydaphis erysirum [Lipaphis erysimi] are thought to be the most important (Kennedy et al., 1962; Shukla et al., 1994). All instars of aphids can transmit. Virus acquisition and inoculation take less than 1 minute, there is no latent period and aphids typically remain infective for a short period after acquiring the virus (Sylvester, 1953). It was shown that M. persicae retained TuMV for 3-5 hours, although infectivity was lost rapidly when feeding on healthy plants (Sylvester, 1954; Nishi, 1969).
The transfer of non-persistently transmitted viruses by aphids usually occurs over short distances (up to a few hundred metres), particularly down-wind and involves migrating alates. Weather conditions and temperature influence aphid activity and migration patterns which in turn affect dissemination of TuMV. Mild winters followed by dry and warm springs favour aphid reproduction and dissemination and hence early and increased spread of the virus. Cool, wet and windy summers reduce the reproduction and movement of aphids and hence spread of the virus. The concentration of virus and its distribution in infected plants influences acquisition of virus and spread by aphids (Broadbent, 1954).
Once primary infections are established in fields, TuMV may spread relatively rapidly from plant to plant if aphids are not controlled.
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc:
在28个国家和地区的一份植物病毒学的最近研究中，TuMV被列为侵染田间种植蔬菜的第二最重要的病毒(Tomlinson, 1987)。它被认为在中国北方和台湾是最重要的病毒，在英国、希腊、日本和瑞典是第二重要的病毒，在中国东部和爱尔兰是第三重要的病毒，以及在新南威尔士（澳大利亚）、丹麦、波兰和泰国是第四最重要的病毒。
在中国北京采集的十字花科作物中的69％被TuMV感染(Feng et al., 1990)。在芸苔和其他的栽培的十字花科品种中的相当大的生产损失早在1940年就有记录(Ling and Young, 1940)。类似地，它在台湾的商业芸苔作物上广泛分布(Yoon et al., 1993)。在英国，TuMV引起蕉青甘蓝(Tomlinson and Ward, 1978)、白色卷心菜(Walkey and Webb, 1978; Walkey and Neely, 1980)、芽甘蓝(Tomlinson and Ward, 1981)、花椰菜(Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978)和芸苔(Hardwick et al., 1994)的重大损失。在加拿大，该病毒在芜菁甘蓝(Brassica napus var. napobrassica)上引起重大的损失(Shattuck and Stobbs, 1987)。
病害的流行在世界上的许多国家周期性地发生，引起加州的匙叶草(Limonium perezii) (Niblett et al., 1969)和莴苣(Zink and Duffus, 1970)、阿根廷的紫罗兰（Matthiola incana）、新泽西和纽约的菊苣和莴苣(Cichorium endiva) (Citir and Varney, 1974b; Provvidenti et al., 1979)、乔治亚州和南加州的羽衣甘蓝(B. oleracea) (Khan and Demski, 1982)、新西兰的十字花科作物(Palmer, 1983)、中东的紫罗兰（Matthiola incana）(Bahar et al., 1985)、阿拉巴马州的芜菁(Wilson and Stevens, 1986)以及瑞典的三葵(Shattuck, 1992)的重大损失。
除了减少产量以外，TuMv还会影响质量。在英国，感染的花椰菜作物被降低等级，并被送到冰冻而不是新鲜的市场，代表一个相当大的经济损失。在加拿大，硫配糖体水平的变化在感染TuMV的芜菁甘蓝上被证明，这说明，这些变化会影响口味(Stobbs et al., 1991)。该病毒也能延迟作物的成熟，例如延迟花椰菜的收获时间31天(Pink and Walkey, 1988)。在英国，由TuMV引起的全部的作物损失在整个已犁入田中的蕉青甘蓝的田地中发生。 In a recent survey of plant virologists in 28 countries and regions, TuMV was ranked as the second most important virus infecting field-grown vegetables (Tomlinson, 1987). It was considered to be the most important virus in northern China and in Taiwan, the second most important in the UK, Greece, Japan and Sweden, the third most important in Eastern China and Ireland and the fourth most important in New South Wales (Australia), Denmark, Poland and Thailand.
Of the brassicaceous crops sampled around Beijing, China, 69% were infected with TuMV (Feng et al., 1990). Considerable production losses in rape and other cultivated Brassicaceae were recorded as long ago as 1940 (Ling and Young, 1940). Similarly, it is widespread in Taiwan in commercial Brassica crops (Yoon et al., 1993). In the UK, TuMV has caused serious losses in swede (Tomlinson and Ward, 1978), white cabbage (Walkey and Webb, 1978; Walkey and Neely, 1980), Brussels sprouts (Tomlinson and Ward, 1981), cauliflower (Tomlinson and Shepherd, 1978) and rape (Hardwick et al., 1994). In Canada, the virus has caused severe production losses in rutabaga (Brassica napus var. napobrassica) (Shattuck and Stobbs, 1987).
Epidemics have occurred periodically in many regions of the world causing serious losses in statice (Limonium perezii) (Niblett et al., 1969) and lettuce in California (Zink and Duffus, 1970), Matthiola incana in Argentina (Pontis, 1973), endive and escarole (Cichorium endiva) in New Jersey and New York (Citir and Varney, 1974b; Provvidenti et al., 1979), collards (B. oleracea) in Georgia and South Carolina (Khan and Demski, 1982), brassicaceous crops in New Zealand (Palmer, 1983), Matthiola incana in the Middle East (Bahar et al., 1985), turnips in Alabama (Wilson and Stevens, 1986) and horseradish in Sweden (Shattuck, 1992).
In addition to reducing yield, TuMV affects quality. In the UK, infected crops of cauliflower have been downgraded and sent for freezing rather than fresh market, representing a considerable economic loss. In Canada, changes in glucosinolate levels have been demonstrated in rutabaga due to TuMV infection and it was suggested that such changes may affect flavour (Stobbs et al., 1991). The virus can also delay crop maturity, e.g. delaying harvest date in cauliflowers by 31 days (Pink and Walkey, 1988). In the UK, complete crop failure has occurred due to TuMV in which whole fields of swede have been ploughed in.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
非持久性传播的病毒是很难用杀虫剂防治的。多数的杀虫剂杀死昆虫的时间不够迅速来防止病毒在短暂的取食针探期间病毒的传入。有它们的使用导致病毒在作物中的发生率增加的例子(Rice et al., 1983; Roberts et al., 1993)，因为它们的使用引起蚜虫针探活动和运动的增加。加之，广谱杀虫剂的大范围使用会减少有益昆虫包括蚜虫捕食者和寄生物的种群，并导致蚜虫对杀虫剂抗性的产生。选择性杀虫剂的使用很可能会减少TuMV在作物间跟随着初侵染的再侵染。有杀虫剂喷雾被证明对该病毒的防治有效的报道(Evans and MacNeil, 1983; Niu et al., 1983)。由于新的杀虫剂的产生和驱避蚜虫物质的发展，它们必须以一个又一个的例子为基础来评估它们对防治TuMV的能力。
油喷雾，虽然昂贵，但已被显示能减少马铃薯Y病毒的传播(Bradley et al., 1966; Simons, 1982)。其效力似乎由所使用的油的类型、乳化剂的选择、喷雾喷嘴的类型、喷雾压力、作物覆盖情况、植物密度和喷雾时间来决定。一些油是具有植物毒性的，它会减少植物的产量。这些处理必须常常重复来去保护新长出的枝芽。在温室实验中，Walkey and Dance (1979)显示，1％的矿物油喷雾会减少通过桃蚜（Myzus persicae）和甘蓝蚜（Brevicoryne brassicae）的传播到印度芥菜上的TuMV传播，而且不具植物毒性。然而，在田间实验中，每周进行的同一比例的喷雾不能保护甘蓝植物免受病毒的侵染，并且具有植物毒性。在加拿大，1-2%的高级油对芜菁甘蓝(Brassica napus var. napobrassica)生产田块的每周使用能减少但不能根除TuMV的侵染(Shattuck, 1992)。Lowery et al. (1990)在田间实验中发现，氯氰菊酯与1％的矿物油的每周使用能使芜菁甘蓝的TuMV侵染由92％降到37％。 Non-persistently transmitted viruses are difficult to control with insecticides. Most insecticides do not kill the insects rapidly enough to prevent virus introduction during brief feeding probes. There are examples of their use increasing the incidence of virus in crops (Rice et al., 1983; Roberts et al., 1993) by causing increased probing activity and movement of aphids. Additionally, widespread use of broad-spectrum insecticides is known to reduce populations of beneficial insects including aphid predators and parasitoids and has led to aphids with insecticide resistance. The use of selective insecticides is likely to reduce secondary spread of TuMV in crops following primary infection. There are reports of insecticidal sprays proving ineffective in the control of the virus (Evans and MacNeil, 1983; Niu et al., 1983). As new insecticides are produced and aphid-repellent substances developed, they will have to be evaluated on a case by case basis for their ability to control TuMV.
Oil sprays, although expensive, have been shown to reduce aphid transmission of potyviruses (Bradley et al., 1966; Simons, 1982). Effectiveness seems to vary depending on the type of oil used, the choice of emulsifier, the type of spray nozzle, spray pressure, crop coverage, plant density and spray timing. Some oils are phytotoxic and reduce plant yield. Such treatments have to be repeated frequently to protect newly developing shoots. In greenhouse experiments, Walkey and Dance (1979) showed that a 1% mineral oil spray reduced the transmission of TuMV by Myzus persicae and Brevicoryne brassicae to Indian mustard and was not phytotoxic. However, in field experiments, weekly sprays at the same rate failed to protect cabbage plants from virus infection and appeared to be phytotoxic. In Canada, weekly applications of 1-2% Superior oil to rutabaga (Brassica napus var. napobrassica) production fields reduced, but did not eliminate TuMV infection (Shattuck, 1992). Lowery et al. (1990) found in field experiments that weekly application of cypermethrin with 1% mineral oil TuMV infection of rutabaga from 92 to 37%. 抗性栽培品种的使用是最简单、最便宜、最具环境适应性和可能最有效的防治方法。

host_range: 花毛茛Ranunculus asiaticus cv. Elegance.
description: During 2013 to 2014, about 20% of Ranunculus asiaticus cv. Elegance plants in a commercial greenhouse in Campania, Southern Italy, were found showing leaf deformation and mosaic. Leaves from twenty-five symptomatic plants were tested by double-antibody sandwich (DAS)-ELISA and Istituto per la Protezione Sostenibile delle Piante (IPSP) tests, all twenty-five symptomatic buttercup plants tested positive for BBWV-2,  twelve of them also tested positive for RanMMV, a virus previously reported on this species in Italy. The pathogenicity test further confirmed the results. To our knowledge, this is the first report of R. asiaticus as a natural host of BBWV-2 and the first report of RanMMV infecting this species in Campania, Southern Italy.
reference_name: First Report of Broad bean wilt virus 2 and Ranunculus mild mosaic virus in Ranunculus asiaticus in Southern Italy

host_range: PSbMV具有较广的寄主范围，可感染12科47种植物，寄主主要有豌豆、蚕豆、巢菜、小扁豆、宽豆、香豌豆、苋色藜、茴香和菜豆等，其中豌豆是主要的自然寄主。
potential_eco_desc: 国际上的研究表明其对豌豆的产量和品质影响很大，在国外已造成豌豆大量减产。
description: PSbMV最早出现在欧洲，后又在日本、美国、加拿大、中国台湾、非洲以及大洋洲有报道，现已成为全世界广泛分布的豌豆上最重要病毒病之一，可严重危害豌豆种植业。目前我国尚无该病毒大规模发生的报道。  PSbMV由蚜虫半持久性和非持久性传播，在传播时不需要辅助病毒。PSbMV可通过种子和病残体远距离传播。有研究发现种皮上有裂缝的种子PSbMV种传率远高于种皮正常完整的种子。

potential_eco_desc: PSbMV can lead to a seed weight reduction as high as 36% (Chiko and Zimmer, 1978; Khetarpal and Maury, 1987). Therefore, PSbMV introduction through seed transmission, followed by dissemination by aphid vectors, possesses the potential for sizeable economic loss. The reduced marketability of seed from infected peas may be the largest contributor of financial loss, due to the inability to import or export infected seed (Shukla et al., 1994).

description: Incidence^p^pOf 1835 pea seed lines tested in the germplasm collection of Pisum sativum in the USA, 420 were infected with PSbMV, symptom intensity varying greatly among the lines of which 37 were infected and symptomless (Hampton and Braverman, 1979). Incidences of seed infection >30% have been reported (Musil et al., 1983). PSbMV is also seedborne on lentils and faba beans (Makkouk et al., 1993). PSbMV was sucessfully eradicated from the USA pea collection by the use of sensitive and accurate techniques to assay for the pathogen in mother plants and seeds and a sound knowledge of the epidemiology of the disease throughout propagative cycles of seeds (Hampton et al., 1993). PSbMV was detected in 31.1% of 219 pea seed samples collected in 1998 and 1999 from farmers' seed lots in Ethiopia (Abraham and Makkouk, 2002).^p^p^pThe virus was isolated from the embryo and cotyledons of mature seed and from the embryo, endosperm and testa of immature developing pea seeds. All parts of inflorescences from infected plants, including carpels, filaments, petals, pollen and sepals, contained the virus. It was transmitted to seed both by the female parent and by pollen (Stevenson and Hagedorn, 1973). Segregation analysis from reciprocal cross-pollination between cultivars using infected plants as pollen recipients and healthy plants as pollen clones, showed that the transmission of PSbMV from the mother plant to seed is controlled by maternal genes and, in a cultivar that shows no seed transmission, is prevented through the action of multiple host genes segregating as quantitative trait loci. These genes control the ability of PSbMV to spread into and/or multiply in the non-vascular testa tissues, thereby preventing the virus from crossing the boundary between the maternal and progeny tissues. Immunocytochemical and in situ hybridization (using a PSbMV RNA-specific antisense probe) studies performed after fertilization suggested that the virus uses the embryonic suspensor as the route for direct invasion of the embryo. The programmed degeneration of the suspensor during embryo development may provide a transient window for embryo invasion by the virus (Wang and Maule, 1994).Roberts et al. (2003) showed that seed transmission of PSbMV depends on symplastic transport of the virus from infected maternal cells to the embryo. Such transport pathways have not been identified in higher plants. To identify these pathways the ultrastructure of the tissues and cells around the micropyle of young developing seeds was studied and transmitted and nontransmitted virus isolates compared. A characteristic of PSbMV infection was the presence of cylindrical inclusions positioned over plasmodesmal openings. The presence of cylindrical inclusions on the testa-endosperm boundary wall, together with immunogold labelling for virus-specific products on the wall and in the endosperm, indicated that symplastic connections existed at this interface. A close examination of the endosperm-suspensor boundary at the base of the suspensor revealed discontinuities in the suspensor sheath wall as pore-like structures, which the virus might pass through en route to the embryo. A nontransmitted PSbMV isolate was able to invade the maternal tissues of the developing seed but was excluded from the embryo, although it was detected at a low level in the endosperm. Since the endosperm did not support virus replication, it appeared that passive accumulation determined the amount, timing and location of the virus relative to the base of the suspensor. Therefore it was rare that the nontransmitted virus isolate could reach the correct location in the endosperm at the correct time for embryo infection via the suspensor to occur.^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pPSbMV infection of parent plants can cause visual damage to developing seeds, but the damage is not economically significant, unlike the reduction in seed weight that often accompanies PSbMV infection (Khetarpal and Maury, 1987).

management_info: Good control can be achieved if virus-free seed is planted (Shukla et al., 1994). The use of pea cultivars that are resistant to the virus or resistant to seed transmission should also be considered. Homozygous, recessive genes from peas confer resistance to individual strains of PSbMV. P1 is unable to infect sbm-1, while sbm-4 confers resistance to P4. Both of these genes are found tightly linked on chromosome 6. Pea genotypes carrying either sbm-2 (chromosome 2) or sbm-3 (chromosome 6) are not susceptible to P2 of PSbMV(Alconero et al., 1986). The elucidation of these resistance genes (Hagedorn and Gritton, 1973;Provvidenti and Alconero, 1988a, b) has lead to the development of numerous PSbMV-resistant pea germplasm, breeding lines and commercially available cultivars (Baggett and Hampton, 1977; Baggett et al., 1994).^p^pControlling aphid vectors on plants will reduce the spread of the virus in the field (Zink et al., 1956). PSbMV has been shown to be transmitted both non-persistently and semi-persistently (Lim and Hagedorn, 1977). Aphids transmitting non-persistently often infect a plant at the first feeding, reducing the effectiveness of insecticides to control virus introduction into a field. However, because seedborne viruses create a within-field inoculum source, insecticides could reduce virus spread (Matthews, 1991). In addition, aphids carrying a persistent virus have the potential to infect numerous plants, and thus eliminating the vector with insecticides will reduce virus spread (Matthews, 1991).^p^pReflective mulches have been used to reduce the incidence of PSbMV by as much as 78% in broad beans in Japan (Tachibana, 1981).

potential_eco_desc: In agricultural practice, the incidence of infection is often high. For example, in Germany, a survey of 63 localities during 1973-80 showed the average incidence of BYMV in faba beans to be 13.3% (Schmidt, 1984). In the Halle district infection averaged 22.9%, but in large fields up to 72% of the plants were affected (Schmidt and Rollwitz, 1978). ^p^pClovers may show high incidences of infection, especially when perennating. In Japan, BYMV was detected in 70% of the red clover plants of an autumn-sown stand and in 90% of a two-year-old stand (Akita, 1981). In subterranean clover in Western Australia, in 1990, incidence of infection per pasture was up to 64%, and in 1989 and 1992 it was up to 90% (McKirdy et al., 1994). Vegetatively propagated plants are likely to have high rates of infection. In a survey in Florida, 92% of all gladioli tested were infected with BYMV (Nagel et al., 1983). ^p^pThe yield of individual plants may be greatly reduced by BYMV. For example, in faba beans, seed yield was reduced to 33% when infected post-bloom, to 42% when infected at full bloom, and to 44% when infected early, at pre-bloom (Kaiser, 1973). In Canada, these figures were 17, 48 and 59%, respectively, for a mild isolate, and 17, 70 and 96%, respectively, for a severe isolate (Frowd and Bernier, 1977). In lentils, yield was reduced by 34% when infected at full bloom and by 96% when infected at pre-bloom (Kumari et al., 1994). In naturally infected Phaseolus vulgaris a reduction in the number of pods per plant of 33% and a reduction in seed yield of 41% was recorded (Hampton, 1975). A severe isolate reduced herbage and root production in two cultivars of subterranean clover in plots by 60-63 and 79-80% (Jones, 1992). Market value of vegetable or grain legumes is reduced when part of the pods are mottled or malformed, or when pods and seeds are necrotic (Kaiser, 1973).^p^pWhen only a few plants scattered throughout the crop are infected, loss by infected plants may be compensated for by the surrounding healthy plants (Bos, 1982). But under conditions of high incidence, as in subterranean clover in Western Australia (McKirdy et al., 1994), a 12-16% decrease in herbage yields and a 37-40% decrease in seed yield of subterranean clover when mown were observed. Within symptom-affected patches, herbage yield losses were 28-49% (Jones, 1994).^p^pBYMV-infected plants may also suffer from decreased root nodulation (Frowd and Bernier, 1977; Orellana and Fan, 1978), and from increased susceptibility to leaf fungi (Kaiser, 1973; Omar et al., 1986) and root rots (Patil, 1973). Thus, longevity of clovers in pastures may be greatly affected by viruses (Barnett and Diachun, 1984) including BYMV (Jones, 1994). Accumulation of infection by BYMV and other viruses in breeding plots, particularly of perennial clovers, may seriously impede agronomic genotype evaluation during breeding and may constitute a threat to the ensuing production of commercial seed.

description: Incidence^p^pBYMV is seedborne in faba bean. Sasaya et al. (1993) detected the virus in seeds of 15 of the 17 faba bean cultivars tested. The virus also was detected in seed of 10 of 18 commercial faba bean samples tested during 1989-92, the range of seed infection being 0-9.2%, as determined by grow out tests on the harvested seeds. Kaiser (1973) found that pods of faba beans, infected with BYMV, occasionally developed necrotic ring spotting and discolored seeds. The virus was also transmitted during grow out from 0.19 to 0.95% of the seed from plants inoculated at pod set or flowering. The pathogen was reported as seedborne in lentil in a field experiment, when inoculation of lentil plants with BYMV at pre-flowering and flowering stages led to seed transmission rates of 0.83 and 0.30%, respectively, determined by grow outs (Kumari et al., 1994). Mali et al. (1983) reported an incidence of infection of 3.4-41.6% in nine cowpea seed samples, as determined by serological tests.^p^p^Effect on Seed QualityKaiser (1973) found that pods of faba beans infected with BYMV occasionally developed necrotic ring spotting and discolored seeds.^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pIn Iran, seed transmission of BYMV in faba beans ranged from 0.2 to 1% in 60% of the faba bean lines tested, but was subsequently spread by aphids with disease incidence in plots grown from these seeds increasing from 4-34% at 15 weeks to 90-100% after 22 weeks. In 45 of 56 faba bean lines from 14 countries, seed transmission was 0.1-2.4% (Kaiser, 1973). BYMV was stylet-borne by Aphis craccivora, A. fabae, Acyrthosiphon pisum, A. sesbaniae and Myzus persicae. ^p^pSeed transmission of BYMV has been investigated in other crops, but shown not to occur. In Western Australia, where BYMV is common in Trifolium subterraneum pastures with incidences up to 90%, the virus was not found to be seed transmitted. Over summer, when subterranean clover and most other herbaceous plants die, the virus is thought to persist in seeds of naturalized Medicago polymorpha, Trifolium arvense, T. campestre and T. glomeratum, and to generate sufficient sources of infection for spread by aphids (McKirdy and Jones, 1995). No symptoms developed on soyabean seedlings grown under greenhouse conditions from 138 seeds harvested from BYMV-infected soyabeans, nor was the pathogen detected by indexing onto Chenopodium amaranticolor (Roechan et al., 1978). Similarly, Faccioli (1997) showed that BYMV was not seed transmitted by Phaseolus vulgaris. ^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pPCR (Bariana et al., 1994)^pA reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay was developed that can simultaneously test a sample, in one tube, for the presence of five seedborne legume viruses, including BYMV. Primers were designed so that the size of the RT-PCR product was indicative of the virus amplified and, where sequences of more than one strain of virus were available, conserved regions were given preference as primer targets. ^p^pSerology (Raizada et al., 1991)^pELISA, immunosorbent EM (ISEM) and dot immunobinding assay (DIBA) were used to detect BYMV in faba bean seeds. A complete correlation was observed for the three techniques on faba bean seeds.^p^pWhen whole seeds are indexed serologically for virus infection and seed transmission, false-positive reactions may result from non-infective degraded virus coat protein remaining in the seed coat during seed maturation.

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl, as for most other virus diseases in general, is only preventive and meant to reduce the risks of infection and/or plant damage. Control measures, therefore, address the sources of infection, the ways of spread and host susceptibility and sensitivity. They mostly consist of a combination of hygienic measures integrated in regular cropping practices and comprise spatial and temporal isolation, choice of resistant cultivars, use of virus-free seed, dense sowing, and removal of infected plants. Most of the measures are also directed to several other viruses that may occur separately or in mixed infection.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pControlling sources of infection^pSeed or planting material should be free of propagule-borne virus if possible. The risk of seed as a source of infection for the virus has so far received little attention because seed transmission is usually low and likely to be overlooked or neglected. Rates of infestation in seed from infected plants are often around 0.1-1% and will be much lower when seed is harvested from a partially infested crop. However, when aphid population densities are high, seed used for new crops must be virtually free from virus, as required for lettuce mosaic potyvirus in California where, for certification of commercial seed, representative samples of 30,000 lettuce seed are required to test zero for the virus. In Iran, rates of seed infestation of faba bean of (dayuhao)1% were found to lead to 90-100% of crop infestation 22 weeks after planting (Kaiser, 1973). In yellow lupin, where seed infestation may be high, the use of seed with low rates of infestation is recommended in combination with other measures of control (Corbett and Edwardson, 1957). ^p^pOf vegetatively propagated ornamental crops, virus-free plants have been obtained through aseptic meristem-tip culture and repeated testing of individual explants for absence of the virus, as for freesia (Oertel, 1980; Bertaccini et al., 1989), gladiolus (Aminuddin and Singh, 1993) and iris (Bertaccini and Bellardi, 1991). For ornamental bulbs, in certain countries certification schemes are operative including testing for the absence of BYMV.^p^pRemoval of sources of infection is important to prevent or reduce secondary spread in crops once the virus has been introduced in propagules or has been brought in by aphids, and this is especially important in crops grown for seed. However, plants that have become infected after virus introduction by aphids may already have become sources for further spread by aphids long before systemic symptoms appear (Proeseler and Karl, 1973). ^p^pSources of infection may also be avoided by spatial isolation of some 100 m, depending on wind direction and vector pressure (Hampton, 1967). The planting of perennial crops (such as clovers and gladiolus) near annual legumes such as bean, faba bean and pea should be avoided. Temporal isolation may prevent overlap with sources of infection or avoid the time of peak flights of aphids that bridge source and target crop, as of freesia to be planted early (before mid May) so that plants have reached mature-plant resistance when aphids arrive (Derks et al., 1991).  ^p^p^pControlling virus spread^pControl of spread of BYMV with (systemic) insecticides is difficult; aphids are not killed rapidly enough to prevent virus introduction during brief probes by incoming aphids. The insecticides may stimulate virus spread by making the insects more restless. When used over large areas over three years, a significant reduction (63.2%) in the incidence of BYMV was observed in faba bean in Germany (Schmidt et al., 1977), but the effect may have been on the overall aphid-population density and is likely to initiate insecticide tolerance and to adversely affect beneficial insects. Similar objections hold for synthetic pyrethroids, with which promising results have been obtained because of their rapid knock-down effect on insects (Asjes, 1985). Mineral oil

description: Incidence^p^pBCMV is seedborne on a range of legumes. Klein et al. (1988) found BCMV in accessions of Phaseolus vulgaris, Phaseolus acutifolius, Phaseolus aborigineus and Phaseolus angustifolius seeds in a survey of the USDA Phaseolus germplasm collection. BCMV appeared to be a serious problem in P. vulgaris accessions; approximately 60% of the 207 tested were contaminated, incidences of infection of up to 70% being found in individual accessions. Other hosts on which seedborne BCMV has been detected include Clitoria ternatea (Lima et al., 1993), cowpeas (Patil and Gupta, 1992), mung beans (Jeyanandarajah and Brunt, 1993), Phaseolus coccineus (Chamberlain, 1939), Phaseolus acutifolium var. lactifolius [Phaseolus acutifolius] (Provvidenti and Cobb, 1975), Macroptilium lathyroides (Provvidenti and Bravermen, 1976) and Vigna mungo (Agarwal et al., 1979a, b).^p^pEarly work reported BCMV as being transmitted by pollen (Reddick, 1931). More recently, electron microscopy of leaf extracts and pollen grains of BCMV-infected bean plants revealed filiform particles 750 μm long which were absent from healthy plants (Omar et al., 1978a). The virus was not present in cotyledons and disappeared from the seedcoats of mature dried seeds. This study also showed that plants infected at an early stage produced up to 57% of seeds carrying the virus. Hagita et al. (1975) showed that when the primary leaves were inoculated, seed transmission was 89% compared with 40%, 5% and 1%, respectively, following inoculation of the first, second and third trifoliate leaves. No infection occurred when inoculation was delayed until 7-10 days after flowering. The importance of time of plant infection is also indicated by transmission of the pathogen by seeds: maximum seed transmission was achieved when plants were inoculated at the primary leaf stage, whereas few cultivars transmitted the virus in seed when plants were inoculated 30 days after sowing (Morales and Castano, 1987).Sharma et al. (1999) have shown that cotyledon infection results in maximum disease expression and subsequent seed transmission.^p^pThe virus is located mainly in the embryo (Quantz, 1961; Provvidenti and Cobb, 1975), but also exists in other seed parts (Ekpo and Saettler, 1974; Raizada et al., 1990). 棉蚜（Aphis gossypii） (Anderson, 1955; Mali and Kulthe, 1980; Mali et al., 1988)

 该病毒通过豇豆种子以不同的传播的频率传播，传播的频率由一些因素如基因型、病毒株系、母本植物的侵染时间和种子的储藏时间所决定的。 The virus is transmitted by aphids in a non-persistent manner; disease may occur in fields where viruliferous aphids are present. The following aphid species have been used in experimental transmission experiments and found to be vectors of the virus: 
Aphis craccivora [an average transmission rate of 59% (Zettler et al., 1967); transmission rates ranging from 24 to 55% (Bashir and Hampton, 1994)]
Aphis gossypii (Anderson, 1955; Mali and Kulthe, 1980; Mali et al., 1988)
Macrosiphum euphorbiae (Anderson, 1955; Murphy et al., 1987)
Myzus persicae [an average transmission rate of 60% (Dijkstra et al., 1987b); Zettler et al., 1967; Lin et al., 1981b; Mali et al., 1988].
The virus is transmitted through cowpea seed with varying frequencies depending on factors such as the genotype, the virus strain, time of infection of the mother plant, and storage time of the seed.

host_range: ZTMV was firstly observed from zucchini fields in Guadeloupe (French West Indies) as a divergent strain of Papaya ringspot virus (PRSV) in 1982, but biological, serological, and molecular biology studies revealed that it should be a distinct species in the genus Potyvirus. description: In July 2014, foliage shrinking, blistering, mosaic, mottling, chlorotic, and dark-green vein banding in pumpkin were observed in fields of Yuxi City, Yunnan Province, China. Disease incidences ranged from 80 to 90% in two fields. Affected leaf samples were collected for confirmation of pathogen identity. Based on dot-ELISA, (RT)-PCR, and biological detection, the pathogen was identified as Zucchini tigre mosaic virus (ZTMV). Our results showed that the virus was distributed widely and might be a major causal agent of the viral diseases in Yunnan. To our knowledge, this is the first report of ZTMV infecting cucurbit plants in China and cucumber as a new host of the virus.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini tigre mosaic virus Infecting Several Cucurbit Plants in China

host_range: This is the first report of Peru tomato mosaic virus on tamarillo (Solanum betaceum) orchards of Ecuador.
description: In Ecuador, tamarillo (Solanum betaceum) disorders caused by potyviruses have been reported in the past. In 2013, leaves from tamarillo plants showing severe virus-like symptoms (mosaic, mottling, and leaf deformation) were collected from orchards in Pichincha and Tungurahua. Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) was extracted from three independent batches and used to generate cDNA libraries to screen for RNA viruses by shotgun cloning. Sequencing revealed the presence of the potyviruses Potato virus Y (PVY), Potato virus V (PVV), and Peru tomato mosaic virus (PTV), and the polerovirus Potato leaf roll virus (PLRV). To determine the occurrence of the viruses, leaf samples tested by RT-PCR. Total RNA extraction and reverse transcription was done. For symptomatic plants, PVY and PLRV were the most common with 64% and 30%, respectively. PVV and PTV were found in 8% and 10%, respectively, with only 4% of the plants coinfected by both viruses. Plants coinfected by PVY and PLRV were the most common with 22%, followed by plants coinfected by PVY and PTV (10%). PVY has long been considered the most common virus in tamarillo in Ecuador. This communication reports for the first time in tamarillo the presence of PVV and PTV, two potyviruses once considered strains of PVY. Further studies are needed to determine the significance of PVV and PTV in single and mixed infections in tamarillo.
reference_name: First Report of Potato virus V and Peru tomato mosaic virus on Tamarillo (Solanum betaceum) Orchards of Ecuador

management_info:
化学防治不能在田间规模上用作消除感染植株上的BCMNV。然而，它们可用作防治病毒媒介和因此可减少感染的传播。1975年在CIAT的实验证明，杀蚜虫剂喷雾能减少BCMNV的传播(CIAT, 1975)。其他研究已显示，控制非持久性蚜虫传播病毒如BCMNV的杀蚜虫剂的使用可能是无效的(Walkey, 1991)。
Walkey and Dance (1979)利用稀释的矿物油来减少由温室中桃蚜（Myzus persicae）、甘蓝蚜（Brevicoryne brassicae）和蚕豆蚜（Aphis fabae）来传播的BCMNV的蚜虫传播。然而，这矿物油在高浓度时会产生植物性毒素的作用，并且在田间，不引起危害植物的毒性时的浓度不能防治蚜虫。在非洲利用化学方法去防治蚜虫即使是有效的，但在财政上是不可实行的。对长期病害防治的最有效和经济的方法是提供对BCMNV的抗性品种给农民。 Chemicals cannot be used to eliminate BCMNV in infected plants on a field scale. However, they may be used to control the virus vectors and, consequently may reduce the spread of infection. Experiments at CIAT in 1975 demonstrated that spraying with aphicide could reduce transmission of BCMNV (CIAT, 1975). Other studies have shown that the use of aphicides to control the spread of non-persistently aphid transmitted viruses, such as BCMNV may be ineffective (Walkey, 1991).
Walkey and Dance (1979) reduced aphid transmission of BCMNV by Myzus persicae, Brevicoryne brassicae and Aphis fabae in the glasshouse using diluted mineral oils. However, the mineral oils had a phytotoxic effect at higher concentrations and, in the field, concentrations which did not cause phytotoxicity failed to control the aphids. The use of chemicals to control aphids in Africa is not financially practicable, even if effective. The most effective and economic method for long-term disease control is to provide farmers with cultivars with host resistance to BCMNV. potential_eco_desc: 在整个非洲、欧洲、南美和拉丁美洲，BCMNV在经济上是重要的。侵染水平可能达到100％，估计的产量损失范围为35％到98％(Galvez, 1980)。在美国俄勒冈州由BCMNV引起的在菜豆作物上的产量减少从53％到达68％，这是由株系的严重程度决定的(Hampton, 1975)。在1972年和1974年摩洛哥，BCMNV严重爆发，所有菜豆植株中的50％显示由蚜虫传播的种传侵染的BCMNV的症状(Lockhart and Fischer, 1974)；产量损失估计达到50％以及34％的收获种子被感染。 BCMNV is economically important throughout Africa, Europe, North America and Latin America. Infection levels may reach 100% and estimated yield losses range from 35 to 98% (Galvez, 1980). Yield reductions in bean crops due to BCMNV ranged from 53 to 68% in Oregon, USA, depending on severity (Hampton, 1975). Severe outbreaks of BCMNV in Morocco in 1972 and 1974, in which 50% of all bean plantings showed BCMNV symptoms from a seedborne infection spread by aphids (Lockhart and Fischer, 1974); yield losses were estimated at 50% and 34% of seed harvested was infected.

一些传播BCMNV的其他的蚜虫品种包括棉蚜（Aphis gossypii）、苜蓿蚜（A. medicaginis）、蚕豆蚜（A. fabae）、藜蚜（Hayhurstia atriplicis）、Uroleucon ambrosiae、Acyrthosiphon pisi和大戟长管蚜（Macrosiphum euphorbiae ）(Zaumeyer and Thomas, 1957)。
BCMNV传播的效率是由桃蚜（Myzus persicae）取食行为之前和之后来决定的(Zettler and Wildinson, 1966)。 Vectors provide a means of secondary spread of the virus within a crop or primary infection of a healthy crop. BCMNV can be transmitted in a non-persistent manner by several aphid species which normally do not colonise P. vulgaris but transmit BCMNV as winged migrants, especially Acyrthosiphon pisum, Aphis fabae and Myzus persicae (Kennedy et al., 1962; Zettler and Wilkinson, 1966). 
Several other aphid species transmit BCMNV including Aphis gossypii, A. medicaginis, A. fabae, Hayhurstia atriplicis, Uroleucon ambrosiae, Acyrthosiphon pisi and Macrosiphum euphorbiae (Zaumeyer and Thomas, 1957).
The efficacy of BCMNV transmission is determined by pre- and post-feeding behaviour of Myzus persicae (Zettler and Wildinson, 1966).

management_info: Introduction^p^pDue to the economic importance of the papaya crop and the damage caused by papaya ringspot disease, scientists from different parts of the world have made efforts to develop methods to control or minimize the effects of the disease on papaya production. Different approaches have been investigated, such as planting in partially isolated areas and roguing; planting under screenhouses; breeding for resistance or tolerance to the virus; using virus-resistant transgenic plants; and cross protection.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pPlanting in partially isolated areas and roguing^pPRSV may be controlled by preventive practices that reduce or delay the spread of the virus within the orchard. These practices include the use of virus-free seedlings to start new crops, planting in partially isolated areas or as far as possible from old infected papayas, roguing of diseased plants once every 2 weeks, avoidance of cucurbit plants in or near the orchard, and systematic weed control to reduce the aphid population (Costa et al., 1969;  Ishii, 1972; Martinez, 1980; Gonsalves, 1994). Practical application of these measures, especially roguing of diseased plants, has been reported in Hawaii (Namba and Higa, 1977; Gonsalves, 1994). In Brazil, roguing of diseased papayas allowed satisfactory control of the disease in orchards in Espirito Santo for more than 10 years, with an eradication rate of between 5 and 10% of diseased trees per year (JA Ventura, EMCAPA, Vitoria, ES, Brazil, personal communication, 1986). Due to the effectiveness of this practice, the state of Espirito Santo passed a law which requires all growers to adopt roguing of diseased papayas for control of the disease; failure to follow the rules can result in complete elimination of the orchard by official authorities.^p^pIn Sao Paulo, Brazil, Rezende et al. (1986, 1987) demonstrated that papayas could be grown satisfactorily in certain areas in the Ribeira Valley, which is  situated in the south-east of the state between the coastal mountain range and the ocean. The spread of the virus in this region is slower than in other parts of the state due to the reduced aphid population and the partial isolation of areas with native forest (Yuki et al., 1987).^p^pPlanting under screenhouse^pSeveral studies have been carried out in order to find chemical or physical methods of protecting papaya trees from aphid vectors. These methods include the use of insecticides, mineral oils, and protective barriers of other species of plants (Acosta, 1969; Harkness, 1967; Nakasone, 1980; Becerra Leon, 1989). None of these methods have been sufficiently effective in controlling papaya ringspot because of the large number of aphid species that may act as vectors and their non-persistant relationship with the virus.^p^pAnother alternative is to prevent viruliferous aphids landing on papaya trees by planting the crop under screenhouses. This technique was first tried in Taiwan and has produced satisfactory results (Rezende and Costa, 1995). Sheen et al. (1998) reported that Taiwan has more than 1000 ha of papayas growing under screenhouses (net-house) annually. The incidence of PRSV-P in the screenhouse was 0.3%, 6 months after transplanting, compared to 96% plants infected in the field.^p^pPlanting date and mineral nutrition^pStudies in India have shown that transplanting papaya in October, with heavy but balanced fertilization, helped reduce the incidence and severity of papaya ringspot disease in plantations. The best fertilization dose consisted of 10 kg FYM, 2 kg castor cake, 1 kg cake-0-meal, 200 g N, 200 g K2O and 200 g P2O5 (Kudada and Prasad, 1999; Ray et al., 1999). ^p  ^pEffective microorganisms (EM), a mixture of beneficial microoganisms including lactic acid bacteria, yeasts, actinomycetes and photosynthetic bacteria, have been reported to reduce papaya ringspot incidence in Taiwan (Tsai, 1998).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pResistance to PRSV-P does not occur within Carica papay

management_info: Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pA series of cultural practices have been used to control TEV infection, especially in pepper and tomato crops. Use of organic (sawdust, woodchips, and maize-cob mulches) (Kemp, 1978) and aluminium foil mulches (Black, 1980) has contributed to delayed virus spread, and resulted in reduced virus incidence and increased yields. The use of mineral oil sprays to interfere with aphid transmission of potyviruses including TEV has been reported (Simons et al., 1977). A five-fold reduction in virus infection was noted for two pepper varieties receiving a weekly spray of JMS Stylet Oil, despite the presence of virus source plants placed in the centre of research plots. The virus tested was Pepper mottle virus (PepMoV), but similar results would be expected for TEV (Zitter and Ozaki, 1978). ^p^pAn integrated approach for the control of tomato viruses including TEV was successful in Mexico; this included the use of virus-free transplants, eradication of virus weed hosts and the use of mineral oil sprays (Martinez-Ramirez, 1990).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pHost-plant resistance has been used to reduce losses by TEV, especially in pepper. High levels of resistance were identified in several Capsicum introductions and varieties (Sowell and Demski, 1977). Resistance to TEV and other potyviruses is present in bell pepper (Cook et al., 1976), in sweet yellow wax pepper (Villalon et al., 1988) and in hot jalapeno pepper (Villalon et al., 1992).^p^pIn tobacco, resistance to TEV has been reported in Burley varieties (Fischer and Rufty, 1993; Nielsen and Kennedy, 1994).^p^pThere are no reports of TEV-resistant tomato varieties.^p^pTransgenic plants with resistance to TEV have been produced (Tanzer et al., 1997; Fellers et al., 1998) but have not yet been used commercially.

description: 作为典型的蚜虫传播的马铃薯Y病毒属的病毒，TEV以非持久的方式传播。Edwardson and Christie (1991)列出12种烟草蚀纹病毒(TEV)的媒介蚜虫。烟蚜(Myzus nicotianae) 是另一种传播媒介(Lampert et al., 1990)。红色型和绿色型的烟蚜都可以传播TEV，并且两者具同等效率，但红色型在TEV和侵染烟草的其它马铃薯Y病毒在病害流行中被认为是更为重要的类型，因为它有更大的繁殖潜力。桃蚜（Myzus persicae）在辣椒和番茄上是TEV病毒重要的传播媒介(Zitter, 1971; Zitter and Tsai, 1981)。 As is typical of aphid-transmitted potyviruses, TEV is transmitted in the non-persistent manner. Edwardson and Christie (1991) listed 12 aphid species as vectors of TEV. The tobacco aphid (Myzus nicotianae) is an additional vector (Lampert et al., 1990). Both the red and green colour forms of M. nicotianae transmitted TEV with equal efficiency but the red form was considered to be more important in the epidemiology of TEV and other potyviruses affecting tobacco because of its increased reproductive potential. Myzus persicae is an important vector of TEV in both pepper and tomato (Zitter, 1971; Zitter and Tsai, 1981).

management_info: Attempts to control virus introduction and spread by the use of insecticides are likely to be ineffective. In North Carolina, soil treatments with a systemic insecticide failed to delay or reduce virus incidence (Reagan et al., 1979). In Kentucky, suppression of colonizing aphids (primarily Myzus persicae) by a combination of soil-applied and foliar-sprayed systemic insecticides delayed and/or reduced the incidence of the virus in some plots and in some years. Ecological and seasonal factors that affected numbers and movement of aphids into the plots could override the effect of within-field suppression of colonizing aphids (Pirone et al., 1988).^p^pThis virus is primarily a problem on burley tobacco and a number of resistant burley cultivars have been released, all of which derive their resistance from T.I. 1406, also known as the Virgin A Mutant (Gupton, 1980; Miller, 1987; Miller, 1991; Nielsen et al., 1993; Nielsen and Kennedy, 1994). Nesmith and T.P. Pirone, University of Kentucky, USA, personal communication, 1997) are susceptible to, but tolerant of, this virus.
