description: Incidence^p^pSeedborne infection by LMV in lettuce was first reported by Newhall (1923). The incidence has since been found to vary from about 0.1 to 37% (Shukla et al., 1994) depending on the time of infection of the mother plant, virus strain, lettuce variety and temperature at which infected plants are grown (Dinant and Lot, 1992; Revers et al., 1997b).^p^pVirus particles occurred in cells of both the embryonic tissues (cotyledon, hypocotyl and radicle) and the non-embryonic tissues (pericarp and endosperm) of lettuce seed cv. Salinas Hunter and Bowyer, 1991, 1993). Virions have been observed throughout the tissues of the ovule but not the embryo sac (Hunter and Bowyer, 1994a) and both externally on the exine of, and internally within, pollen grains of lettuce (Hunter and Bowyer, 1994b). It has been suggested that seed transmission, at least in lettuce, results only from infection of the embryo by infected pollen during fertilization (Hunter and Bowyer, 1994a), contrary to the conclusion of Ryder (1964) that seed infection results from infection of both pollen and ovules. There is evidence that early invasion of the floral meristem is necessary for infection of mature pollen grains (Hunter and Bowyer, 1997).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pLMV-infected seed cannot be detected visually. There are no reports on effects on germination. It has been suggested that infected seeds germinate as readily as non-infected but mosaic and stunting may become apparent in the seedling within about 4 weeks of germination (J Bowyer, Department of Botany, University of Sydney, Australia, personal communication, 1997).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSeedNewhall (1923) provided direct evidence for the transmission of LMV from seed following the development of mosaic in seedlings grown from seed harvested from infected plants and grown under conditions that excluded transmission by vectors. Seedling grow-outs are the basis of an early method for indexing lettuce seed for LMV infection (Kimble et al., 1975). Seed is the primary source of infection of lettuce crops and has been considered the most important in that a low level of seed transmission (0.1%) may culminate in a much higher incidence of disease through aphid transmission from other infected plants (Grogan, 1983). Survival of the lettuce industry in the Salinas Valley in California was threatened in the 1940s and 1950s before the introduction of seed indexing (Grogan, 1980). A recent outbreak of the virus in Florida, with an incidence of up to nearly 100%, was ascribed to non-compliance with seed certification rules (Raid et al., 1996). The standard in Australia and the USA is no infected seed in a sample of 30,000 seeds but in Europe the tolerance level is higher at 0.1% (Dinant and Lot, 1992). The experience in California was that 0.1% infection was too high to achieve consistent control (Grogan, 1983). ^p^pOther sources^p^pLMV has a non-persistent relationship with its aphid vectors which include 20 species in 12 genera (Shukla et al., 1994). Natural vectors include Acyrthosiphon pisum, Aphis gossypii, Macrosiphum euphorbiae and Myzus persicae, the latter being the most efficient species (Dinant and Lot, 1992). Secondary spread in the field is due to aphid transmission from infected lettuce (Gonzales and Rawlins, 1969) and other hosts such as the weed Picris echioides (Zink et al., 1973) and the ornamentals Osteospermum fruticosum (Opgenorth et al., 1991) and Gazania spp. (Zerbini et al., 1997). LMV is also transmitted in seed of the weed Senecio vulgaris (Phatak, 1974) which may thus play a role in the ecology of the virus. ^p^pThe influence of secondary infection by aphids is the primary reason why LMV is controlled with a tolerance of no infected seeds in 30,000 in California, while in the Netherlands, the tolerance is 0 in 2000. The Netherlands has a cooler climate and thus a lower aphid population than California. Furthermore the growers break the disease cycle with other crops, w

management_info: IPM programmes^p^pBecause spread involves both infected seed and aphid transmission and resistance in lettuce is available, an integrated approach to control has been advocated but not developed (Dinant and Lot, 1992).^p^p^Regulatory control^p^pCurrently, control in Australia, Europe and the USA is based largely on lettuce seed certification. Using ELISA technology for seed testing (see Seed Health Tests above) the standard in Australia and the USA is zero infected seed in a sample of 30,000 seeds but in Europe the tolerance level is higher at 0.1% (Dinant and Lot, 1992). In California, 0.1% infection was too high to achieve consistent control (Grogan, 1983). The certification programme in Australia also includes growing seed crops in geographic isolation from commercial crops in an area inimical to aphid vector activity, and careful inspection of plants to remove any with disease symptoms.^p^p^Host-plant resistance^p^pThe g and mo genes (derived from a lettuce cultivar in Argentina and Egyptian wild Lactuca sativa lines, respectively) have been incorporated into some commercial cultivars in Europe and the USA. They are allelic or closely linked and confer tolerance to LMV but not immunity (Dinant and Lot, 1992; Montesclaros et al., 1997). Another resistance factor, in the lettuce cultivar Ithaca, was discovered by Pink et al. (1992), and further sources of resistance are wild Lactuca species, including L. virosa (Dinant and Lot, 1992) and L. perennis and L. tatarica (Bos et al., 1994).^p^p^Pathogen-derived resistance^p^pThe coat protein (CP) gene of LMV has recently been engineered into lettuce (Dinant et al., 1997). The R2 progeny of one homozygous R1 plant were resistant to the homologous virus and other LMV strains. This approach to LMV control is still experimental but holds promise for the future.

potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pE. destruens has become an increasingly important pest of teak in Java since the 1920s (Browne, 1961;Kalshoven, 1961, 1962) and has the potential to become an important pest in forest plantations and in reforestation projects. It is primarily a pest in areas where a dry season is short or absent, and has the potential to become a pest of teak wherever such conditions occur within its range (Alphen de Veer, 1956; Browne, 1968). These authors note that the wood may become so riddled with the tunnels, and so stained by the associated fungi, that it becomes useless for anything but fuel and inferior pole-wood.^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>forestry production

description: Natural Dispersal^p^pAdult females fly readily and flight is one the main means of movement and dispersal. Of more importance economically, however, is the movement of infested woody material as logs, in ship dunnage and crating.^p^pVector Transmission^p^pE. destruens, like other members of the Xyleborini is dependent for food on a symbiotic ambrosia fungus or fungi. The fungus is transmitted by the female in a mycangial pouch. The position of this has not been specifically investigated in E. destruens, but is likely to consist of paired mandibular pouches, as in Euwallacea fornicatus (Fernando, 1960). Both adult and larvae are dependent on the growth of the fungus on the walls of the gallery system in the wood for their food (Beaver, 1989). According to Kalshoven (1962), the associated fungus is a species of Fusarium. Some species of Fusarium are known to be pathogenic to the host tree. This can be particularly important when live trees are attacked.^p^pMovement in Trade^p^pThe species has frequently been intercepted in logs imported from tropical countries from Malaysia to the Solomon Islands (e.g. Ohno et al., 1987, 1988; Ohno, 1990).Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bark: Adults; borne internally; visible to naked eye.^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches: Eggs, Larvae, Pupae, Adults; borne internally; visible under light microscope.^p - Wood: Eggs, Larvae, Pupae, Adults; borne internally; visible under light microscope.

remark: Several other species of Xyleborini with similar habits to E. destruens have been imported to tropical and subtropical areas around the world. A few have become important pests, either because they may attack living or stressed trees, or because of their abundance in disturbed forest areas, and their very wide host range. An increased tendency for secondary species of ambrosia beetle to attack living trees in recent years has been noted (Kuhnholz et al., 2003). The risk of introduction of the species outside its present geographic range must be considered high. E. destruens is not specifically listed as a quarantine pest, but Xyleborus (in which genus Euwallacea was formerly included) spp. are included in the APHIS Regulated Pest List in the USA, and as quarantine pests in New Zealand.
author: CPC2006

management_info: When Euwallacea species are detected in imported plant material, all of the infested material should be immediately destroyed. When detected in traps, plant material in the vicinity of the trap should be actively inspected, with special attention directed towards imported woody products such as timber, crating, dunnage and lumber milling scraps. If an active infestation is detected, control using insecticides is possible but of limited effectiveness. Chemical control is not generally effective since the adult beetles bore deep into the host material. The following insecticides were effective against a species of Euwallacea destructive to tea: fenvalerate, deltamethrin, quinalphos, cypermethrin and dichlorvos (Muraleedharan, 1995); these insecticides may also be effective against other ambrosia beetles.^p^pThe concealed habitats in which these species feed and reproduce, the difficulties and high costs of insecticide application, and environmental concerns all limit the effectiveness of chemical control. In logging areas, fast removal of the felled timber from the area will reduce attacks, and rapid conversion to sawn timber will reduce the depth of such attacks as have occurred. Attacks on sawn timber are much less frequent, and can be further reduced if the timber is seasoned and its moisture content falls (Roberts, 1987).  In the case of attacks on teak, attacks can be avoided by planting the tree only in areas with a pronounced dry season (Browne, 1968).

potential_eco_desc: Introduction^p^pSome 111 viruses may infect soyabean of which ca 35 have been encountered on soyabean in nature (Irwin and Schultz, 1981; Demski and Kuhn, 1989) and several of them may occur in mixed infections. SMV is considered to be one of the most significant soyabean viruses worldwide (Bos, 1972). Allusions to the direct economic impact of SMV are prevalent, but hardly ever documented quantitatively, even in reviews (Irwin and Goodman, 1981; Irwin and Schultz, 1981), and there are practically no data on financial losses suffered by growers. Most information concerns disease incidence. It may be high because of seed transmission and rapid spread by aphids The literature includes the effect of the virus on inoculated or naturally infected plants observed singly or in groups, merely suggesting potential losses, that is, losses that might occur in crops at high incidence of the disease. To better understand the damage that SMV may cause one must first list the components of loss inflicted by the virus (1) and then look for possible parameters for assessment of losses actually sustained in the field (2). A few indications can be obtained from the literature about likely actual losses caused by the virus (3) and finally, indirect losses to growers and society at large (4) must also be taken into account when considering the economic importance of the virus Bos, 1982, 1999).^p^p^Components of loss^p^pReports on the impact of SMV often deal with its effect on single or various components of yield studied on single plants or groups of plants to better understand the physiological or economic background of loss in quantity and quality. The data are often hard to compare because of considerable variation according to soyabean cultivar, virus strain, and time of infection or inoculation. (See also Parameters of loss and for more detail, see Symptoms).^p^pPlant size or weight^p^pInfected plants and their organs are usually smaller in size and weight; plants are often stunted. Reduction in fresh weight of 60-day-old seedlings ranged from 35-73% depending on the virus strain (Tu, 1989). In 10 soyabean cvs plant height was reduced by 4.0-16.9%, number of pods per plant by 8.4-33.4%, pod length by 10-25.6%, number of seeds per pod by 6.4-15.2%, and total seed weight per plant by 6.6-17.8% (Haque et al., 1993). In field experiments when plants of two cvs (Hampton 266A and Jackson) were inoculated at the first true-leaf stage, average reduction in plant height was 25% (Demski and Jellum, 1975).^p^pPlant composition and physiology^p^pSMV infection usually increases protein content in plants as a whole (Liao et al., 1992) and often does so with N content (Orellana et al., 1983; Suteri, 1985). The number and quantity of amino acids may also be changed (Suteri, 1985). The ureide-N content was increased in two plant introduction lines of wild soyabean (Glycine soja) (Orellana et al., 1983). There is a reduced N-fixation by root nodules of diseased plants (see Root nodulation, below). Enzyme activity is often altered. A decrease was found in the activity of catalase (Suteri, 1985; Shen et al., 1999) and of superoxide dismutase (Zhuang et al., 1993; Shen et al., 1999), although an increase of it has also been reported (Lu and Gao, 1996; Zheng et al., 1999), and an increase in peroxidase activity (Suteri, 1985; Liao et al., 1992; Zhuang et al., 1993; Shen et al., 1999; Zheng et al., 1999). These substances may play a role in the resistance of soyabean to SMV. Lu and Chen (1992) reported a considerable decrease in photosynthesis in infected plants. Plant maturity was delayed in three experiments in Hampton 266A (Demski and Jellum, 1975) and in a number of other susceptible varieties (Tu, 1989). ^p^pSeed size and quality^p^pSMV decreases seed size, particularly in cases of coinfection with BPMV (Ross, 1968). description: Incidence^p^pInfectious SMV was recovered from embryos and cotyledons, but not the testae of mature seeds. However, it was found in the testae of immature seeds (Porto and Hagedorn, 1975a; Tu, 1975; Bowers and Goodman, 1979; Iizuka and Yoshida, 1988) and non-infectious antigen was detected by serology in testae of mature seeds (Bowers and Goodman, 1979; Iwai et al., 1985). The pathogen was found extensively in the flowers and pods of inoculated plants (Bowers and Goodman, 1979) and was transmitted to seeds through both pollen and ovules (Iizuka, 1973).^p^pDong HongPing et al. (1997) used indirect ELISA to detect the percentage of infected embryos of F1 hybrids in four crosses. The results showed that the incidence of SMV-infected embryos from a cross where both parents were susceptible and from a cross where the female was susceptible and the male resistant was higher than in the other crosses. Incidence exceeded 60% at the beginning of podding, whereas it was ca 25% from a resistant female x susceptible male cross. It is suggested that the principle route of soyabean embryo infection was by invasion of the ovules. SEM revealed the location of immunogold labelling in the ovary walls, on the surface of the ovules and cleaving planes in SMV-infected plants. Bands of SMV-like particles were also found in the ovary walls and embryo sacs in thin sections of soyabean ovaries.^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pSeed germination was reduced by SMV by an average of 7% over 4 years in a susceptible cultivar inoculated in the field in the USA (Hartwig and Keeling, 1982) and by an average of 17% in a group of inoculated cultivars in Egypt (El-Amrety et al., 1985a). Oil content was reduced and protein increased by plant inoculation (Suteri, 1980; El-Amrety et al., 1985b). Seed-coat mottling is often associated with SMV infection, but may also be caused or increased by other virus infections and by environmental and genetic factors (see Symptoms). It cannot be used as a parameter of infection by SMV and of seed transmission of the virus.Koning et al. (2001) showed that infection by SMV at or before growth stage R2 increased the susceptibility of soyabean seeds to Phomopsis spp. infection and resulted in poor seed quality and low vigour. Koning et al. (2003) further investigated the extent of seedcoat mottling associated with the accumulation of SMV or Phomopsis spp. infection of the seedcoat in 1996 and 1997. Plants of two SMV-susceptible cultivars, Clark and Williams, were sap inoculated with the G2 strain of SMV at growth stage R2. Control plants (SMV-resistant isolines L78-434 and L78-379, respectively) were not inoculated. Harvested seed were evaluated visually for seedcoat mottling and sorted into four categories (severe, banded, blemish, and none) according to the degree of seed coat pigmentation. Seed infection with Phomopsis spp. was determined and SMV accumulation was assessed by ELISA and nucleic acid hybridization analysis. Phomopsis spp. were isolated from seed of all mottling categories, with the incidence of infection increasing as the degree of seed coat mottling increased. SMV was detected in both mottled and nonmottled seed coats, with generally higher levels of SMV in mottled seed coats. However, the relationship of SMV titre to seedcoat mottling was inconsistent across cultivars and years. Thus, the extent of seedcoat mottling was not directly related to the accumulation of SMV in the seed coat.^p^pSoyabean seed coat mottling also has been a problematic symptom for soyabean growers and the soyabean industry. management_info: ^ Introduction^p^pThe simplest control method would be the use of absolutely virus-free seed or virus-immune cultivars. Since neither of these measures is available, the rates of crop infestation must be kept below an economically acceptable level by a combination of methods, mostly strategically integrated in the grower's cultural practice. They aim at preventing plant infection and damage. Important techniques are the use of seed certified as having low rates of infestation to minimise the number of sources of infection, vector control to reduce the spread of virus, and the use of more resistant cultivars to minimise crop infection and damage.^p^p^Use of Certified Seed^p^pThe use of certified seed is highly advisable. There is remarkably little documentation on certification standards. Absolute freedom from SMV, and other seedborne pathogens, is ideal, but the cost of producing and testing such seed would increase the price of the seed prohibitively. The percentage of seed infestation that is tolerable depends on the vector population density at the location and season of cultivation. For example, for Lettuce mosaic virus in Europe, 0.1% seed infection is the limit, and this requires the testing of representative samples of 2500 seeds. In California, USA, where aphid population densities are much higher, the seed must be virtually virus-free and samples of 30,000 seeds must be tested. For SMV the threshold levels have not yet been determined (Irwin and Schultz, 1981). Without documentation, Ruesink and Irwin (1986) claim that 1% is the upper limit of acceptable seed transmission even without subsequent spread by aphids. In areas with considerable aphid densities, 0.1% may still be acceptable, but when and where vector pressure is high already early during crop development, 0.01% may be the limit. Such areas, it is stated, should import seed every year from a region that can assure them that less than 1 seed in 10,000 is infected. In north-east China, the limit of 0.01 is advised in regions where aphid populations are high, and of 0.05 in coastal regions with fewer aphids (Guo, 1992). The production of certified seed requires high quality foundation seed, production in an area and at a time of low aphid incidence, and early roguing of symptom-bearing seedlings. For seed certification, certification services are responsible for field inspection to assess crop infestation and for sample testing after seed harvest to determine the percentage of infestation of the commercial seed lots with infected seeds (Bos, 1999; see also Special Tests for Seed Certification).^p^p^Vector Control^p^pNon-persistently transmitted viruses are difficult to control with insecticides: they do not kill the insects rapidly enough to prevent virus introduction during brief probes, and may stimulate virus spread by making the insects more restless. Promising results have been obtained with pyrethroids that have a rapid knock-down effect on insects, but the widespread use of such broad-spectrum insecticides has caused concern because of the possible hazardous effects on beneficial insects and the possible selection for insecticide resistance. The same objections hold for insecticide treatments over large areas that aim to reduce the overall population density of the vector. Irwin and Schultz (1981) have stressed that the use of predators and parasitoids to reduce aphid populations might cause the aphids to disperse on the soyabean crop, thus increasing the spread of the virus. The epidemic development of SMV has been significantly impeded in field experiments by frequent spraying with a vegetable oil emulsion (Lu, 1970), or with mineral oil followed by application of synthetic pyrethroid (Nakano et al., 1987). However, such treatments have to be repeated frequently to protect newly developing shoots. They also reduce plant yield, and are too expensive for field crops. description: SMV通过蚜虫以非持续的螯针传方式非明确地传播。SMV的传播是通过一些蚜虫种类（大多数暂定的alatae）(Irwin and Goodman, 1981; Ruesink and Irwin, 1986)，但只有少数种类是病毒的重要媒介。SMV也可能影响种群密度和媒介昆虫蚜虫的行为。据发现玉米缢管蚜在接触后离开受SMV侵染的大豆植株比健株更快，那增加成功传播病毒到其它植株的可能性(Fereres et al., 1999)。 SMV侵染也可能不利地影响蚜虫掠夺者的生物学像那些官能地直接在大豆取食的Orius insidiosus。通过这种掠夺者，SMV可能通过蚜虫增加病毒的传播(Armer et al., 1999)。 SMV is transmitted non-specifically by aphids in the non-persistent stylet-borne manner.  Spread of SMV is by several aphid species (mostly transient alatae) (Irwin and Goodman, 1981; Ruesink and Irwin, 1986), but only a few species are important vectors of the virus. SMV may also affect the population density and behaviour of vector aphids. Rhopalosiphum maidis was found to leave SMV-infected soyabean plants sooner after probing than healthy plants, which increases the probability of successfully transmitting the virus to other plants (Fereres et al., 1999). SMV infection may also adversely affect the biology of aphid predators such as Orius insidiosus that facultatively feeds directly on soyabean. Via the predator, SMV may increase transmission of the virus by aphids (Armer et al., 1999).

management_info: 虽然有一个关于在70℃的热水处理可以从种子完全消除SMV的报道，但是热水处理也大大地降低种子萌芽，所有接着在80℃中处理的没有萌芽。干热处理造成侵染严重性的降低且也逆向影响萌芽，是最低的在80℃时病毒完全钝化(Ghufran-Ul-Haque et al., 1993)。然而，关于携带于胚芽的种传病毒的成功的和实际的根除的其它报道是没有的(Bos, 1978; Mink, 1993)。 There is one report on the complete elimination of SMV from seeds by hot-water treatment at 70℃, but hot-water treatment significantly reduced seed germination as well, with no germination at all following treatment at 80℃. Dry-heat treatment caused a reduction in the severity of infection and also adversely affected germination, which was lowest at 80℃ where there was complete inactivation of the virus (Ghufran-Ul-Haque et al., 1993). However, there are no other reports on the successful and practical eradication of seedborne viruses carried in the embryo (Bos, 1978; Mink, 1993). 非持续传播的病毒是难以用杀虫剂防治的：它们不能快速杀死昆虫以够防止病毒引进在短暂的刺探期间，且可能刺激病毒传播通过使昆虫更加运动不止。有希望的结果已经用在昆虫上有快速击倒的效果的拟除虫菊酯被获得，但这些宽光谱杀虫剂的广泛使用已经造成焦虑由于在有益的昆虫上可能的危险的效果和杀虫剂抗性的可能选择。同样的异议就为了减少昆虫媒介的全部的种群密度的大地区杀虫剂处理而提出。Irwin和Schultz (1981)已经强调减少蚜虫种群的捕食动物和拟寄生的使用可能造成蚜虫传播于大豆作物上，这样增加病毒的传播。SMV的流行发展已经被大大阻止于田间试验通过用植物油乳剂(Lu, 1970)，或用接着合成的拟除虫菊酯的运用的矿物油(Nakano et al., 1987)经常喷雾。然而，这些处理不得不经常重复以保护新发展的幼芽。它们也降低植株产量，且对田间作物而言太贵了。作物选择或增加对病毒媒介昆虫的抗性的繁殖是另一种可能。 Non-persistently transmitted viruses are difficult to control with insecticides: they do not kill the insects rapidly enough to prevent virus introduction during brief probes, and may stimulate virus spread by making the insects more restless. Promising results have been obtained with pyrethroids that have a rapid knock-down effect on insects, but the widespread use of such broad-spectrum insecticides has caused concern because of the possible hazardous effects on beneficial insects and the possible selection for insecticide resistance. The same objections hold for insecticide treatments over large areas that aim to reduce the overall population density of the vector. Irwin and Schultz (1981) have stressed that the use of predators and parasitoids to reduce aphid populations might cause the aphids to disperse on the soyabean crop, thus increasing the spread of the virus. The epidemic development of SMV has been significantly impeded in field experiments by frequent spraying with a vegetable oil emulsion (Lu, 1970), or with mineral oil followed by application of synthetic pyrethroid (Nakano et al., 1987). However, Ramirez and Gamez (1984) reported significant yield reduction in both Xanthosoma sp. and Colocasia esculenta in Costa Rica. management_info: Introduction^p^pInfection or re-infection of greenhouse-grown ornamental aroids can be prevented by the selection of virus free stock and use of standard insect control practices (Wisler et al., 1978; Zettler and Hartman, 1987). Although dasheen mosaic potyvirus is apparently not seed transmitted (Zettler et al., 1978) virus control through seed production is impractical and poses many problems. Many aroids are protogynous, and stigmata are only receptive for short periods making pollination difficult. Furthermore, horticulturally desirable varieties do not flower or flower infrequently and seed only remain viable for short periods of time. Lastly, many aroids do not breed true, thus seedlings exhibit a considerable amount of phenotypic variation (Hartman et al., 1972; Zettler and Abo El-Nil, 1979; Volin, 1980; Volin et al., 1981). No true genetic resistance to dasheen mosaic potyvirus has been reported.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pGiven that dasheen mosaic potyvirus is largely confined to the Araceae, it can be controlled if dasheen mosaic potyvirus-free field-grown aroids are grown in isolation from other aroid crops (Zettler and Hartman, 1986). Unfortunately, given the lack of economic incentives to use pathogen-free planting stock (Zettler et al., 1991), dasheen mosaic potyvirus-free field-grown crops such as Caladium, Xanthosoma, and Colocasia, are not readily available. Likewise, isolated fields are difficult to locate in many commercial production areas. Nevertheless, rogueing of infected plants and isolation of fields as much as possible can delay infection/reinfection for several years (Zettler and Hartman, 1986).^p^p^Vegetative Propagation^p^pVirus-free propagating units can be harvested from some of the vining ornamental aroids such as Philodendron oxycardium by maintaining them under optimal growing conditions and selecting asymptomatic cuttings (Wisler et al., 1978). Accelerated new growth of dasheen mosaic potyvirus-infected plant tissue may be free of virus thus providing a short period in which cuttings can be harvested. However, inasmuch as symptom expression is often seasonal, cuttings should be observed over a period of several months to confirm their virus-free status (Wisler et al., 1978).^p^pFoliage aroids, many of which were ubiquitously infected with dasheen mosaic potyvirus, are now virtually virus free (Zettler and Hartman, 1987; Shishida et al., 1991). While these crops have a relatively high cash value making tissue culture economically feasible, the same is not true for caladiums and the edible aroids. These crops are easily propagated by tissue culture (Hartman, 1974; Gomez et al., 1989; Hu et al., 1994); however, the current low cash value and limited distribution of these crops makes tissue culture uneconomical Zettler and Hartman, 1986, 1987; Zettler et al., 1991).

description:
芋花叶病毒是通过桃蚜（Myzus persicae）以非持久方式传播(Buddenhagen et al., 1970; Zettler et al., 1970; Kenten and Woods, 1973; Debrot and Ordosgoitti, 1974; Paludan and Begtrup, 1982; van der Meer, 1985) 。Rodrigues et al. (1984)报道：芋花叶病毒是通过一个移居到海芋属（Alocasia sp.）的未经鉴定的蚜虫品种而不是桃蚜传播到裂叶喜林芋（Philodendron selloum）中去。Morales and Zettler (1977)不能证明芋花叶病毒通过香蕉交脉蚜（Pentalonia nigronervosa）的传播，香蕉交脉蚜（Pentalonia nigronervosa）通常移居到海芋属（Alocasia sp.）的成员中去。然而，芋花叶病毒是通过苜蓿蚜（Aphis craccivora）传播的 (Buddenhagen et al., 1970; Zettler et al., 1970) 。Jackson and Gollifer (1975)指出：棉蚜（Aphis gossypii）在所罗门群岛可能也是一个传播的媒介。
芋花叶病毒不是通过种子传播的(Zettler et al., 1970; van der Meer, 1985)但它是通过营养繁殖传播的(Zettler et al., 1970; Gollifer et al., 1977; Zettler and Hartman, 1987)。 Dasheen mosaic virus is transmitted in a non-persistent manner by Myzus persicae, (Buddenhagen et al., 1970; Zettler et al., 1970; Kenten and Woods, 1973; Debrot and Ordosgoitti, 1974; Paludan and Begtrup, 1982; van der Meer, 1985). Rodrigues et al. (1984) reported that dasheen mosaic potyvirus virus was transmitted to Philodendron selloum by an unidentified aphid species colonizing Alocasia sp. but not by Myzus persicae. Morales and Zettler (1977) were unable to demonstrate dasheen mosaic potyvirus transmission by Pentalonia nigronervosa, which often colonizes members of the Araceae. Dasheen mosaic potyvirus is, however, transmitted by Aphis craccivora (Buddenhagen et al., 1970; Zettler et al., 1970). Jackson and Gollifer (1975) suggested that Aphis gossypii may also be a vector in the Solomon Islands.
Dasheen mosaic potyvirus is not known to be seed-transmitted (Zettler et al., 1970; van der Meer, 1985) but is transmitted by vegetative propagation (Zettler et al., 1970; Gollifer et al., 1977; Zettler and Hartman, 1987).
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
温室种植的观赏性天南星科植物的侵染或再侵染能通过无病毒砧木的挑选和标准的昆虫防治实践的使用来预防(Wisler et al., 1978; Zettler and Hartman, 1987)。虽然芋花叶病毒显然不是种传的(Zettler et al., 1978)，但通过种子产品的病毒防治是不切实际的并会出现很多问题。许多天南星科植物是雌蕊先熟的，柱头只能在短时间内接受，这使到授粉的有困难。此外，园艺上理想的品种是不开花或很少开花的，种子只在短时间内保持生存能力。最后，很多天南星科植物不能真正地繁殖，于是幼苗表现表型变种的相当大的数量(Hartman et al., 1972; Zettler and Abo El-Nil, 1979; Volin, 1980; Volin et al., 1981)。没有已被报道的真正的对芋花叶病毒的遗传抗性。
芋花叶病毒被很大地限制在天南星科，如果无芋花叶病毒的田间种植天南星科植物与其他的天南星科作物隔离的种植，那该病毒能够防治(Zettler and Hartman, 1986)。可惜的是，使用无病原物种植砧木的使用的经济动机的缺乏，无芋花叶病毒的田间种植作物如贝母、千年芋属、和芋属，是不容易被使用的。同样地，隔离田块很难在许多商业生产区域建立。然而，尽可能多的感染植物的根除和田间的隔离能延迟侵染/再侵染几年(Zettler and Hartman, 1986)。
无病毒繁殖个体能通过在最适合的生长条件和维持和挑选无症状的插条来从一些蔓生的观赏性天南星科植物（如心形喜林芋（Philodendron oxycardium））中收获(Wisler et al., 1978)。芋花叶病毒感染植株组织的催促的新的生长可能是无病毒的，因此提供能够收获插条的一段短的时间。然而，由于症状的表现通常是季节性的，所以插条应观察一个几个月的时期来确定它们无病毒的状况(Wisler et al., 1978)。
普遍地受芋花叶病毒侵染的许多的叶子天南星科植物现在实际上是无病毒的(Zettler and Hartman, 1987; Shishida et al., 1991)。这些作物相当高的价格，这使到组织培养在经济上可实行，而五彩芋和可食用天南星科植物不能。这些作物容易通过组织培养繁殖(Hartman, 1974; Gomez et al., 1989; Hu et al., 1994)；然而，当前的低的价格和这些作物的限制性的分布使到组织培养不经济(Zettler and Hartman, 1986, 1987; Zettler et al., 1991)。 Infection or re-infection of greenhouse-grown ornamental aroids can be prevented by the selection of virus free stock and use of standard insect control practices (Wisler et al., 1978; Zettler and Hartman, 1987). Although dasheen mosaic potyvirus is apparently not seed transmitted (Zettler et al., 1978) virus control through seed production is impractical and poses many problems. Many aroids are protogynous, and stigmata are only receptive for short periods making pollination difficult. Furthermore, horticulturally desirable varieties do not flower or flower infrequently and seed only remain viable for short periods of time. Lastly, many aroids do not breed true, thus seedlings exhibit a considerable amount of phenotypic variation (Hartman et al., 1972; Zettler and Abo El-Nil, 1979; Volin, 1980; Volin et al., 1981). No true genetic resistance to dasheen mosaic potyvirus has been reported.
Given that dasheen mosaic potyvirus is largely confined to the Araceae, it can be controlled if dasheen mosaic potyvirus-free field-grown aroids are grown in isolation from other aroid crops (Zettler and Hartman, 1986). Unfortunately, given the lack of economic incentives to use pathogen-free planting stock (Zettler et al., 1991), dasheen mosaic potyvirus-free field-grown crops such as Caladium, Xanthosoma, and Colocasia, are not readily available. Likewise, isolated fields are difficult to locate in many commercial production areas. Nevertheless, rogueing of infected plants and isolation of fields as much as possible can delay infection/reinfection for several years (Zettler and Hartman, 1986).
Virus-free propagating units can be harvested from some of the vining ornamental aroids such as Philodendron oxycardium by maintaining them under optimal growing conditions and selecting asymptomatic cuttings (Wisler et al., 1978). Accelerated new growth of dasheen mosaic potyvirus-infected plant tissue may be free of virus thus providing a short period in which cuttings can be harvested. However, inasmuch as symptom expression is often seasonal, cuttings should be observed over a period of several months to confirm their virus-free status (Wisler et al., 1978).
Foliage aroids, many of which were ubiquitously infected with dasheen mosaic potyvirus, are now virtually virus free (Zettler and Hartman, 1987; Shishida et al., 1991). While these crops have a relatively high cash value making tissue culture economically feasible, the same is not true for caladiums and the edible aroids. These crops are easily propagated by tissue culture (Hartman, 1974; Gomez et al., 1989; Hu et al., 1994); however, the current low cash value and limited distribution of these crops makes tissue culture uneconomical (Zettler and Hartman, 1986, 1987; Zettler et al., 1991).

potential_eco_desc:
由于每个个体更高的价格，大多数产量研究已在观赏植物而不是可食用植物上开展。然而，Ramirez and Gamez (1984)报道了在哥斯达黎加的千年芋属（Xanthosoma sp. ）和芋（Colocasia esculenta）上重大的产量减少。在Dieffenbachia maculate‘Perfection’上的产量研究中，与60棵感染了芋花叶病毒的植株只有10.1个插条相比，每株植物平均18.8的插条从30棵健康植株上获得。564个健康插条中，98.4％被判定为可销售，而606个感染插条中只有47.3％(Zettler et al., 1980)。在类似的研究中，Chase et al. (1981)报道：受芋花叶病毒感染的D. maculate‘Perfection’植株产生平均每棵植株10.1个插条，而无病毒的‘Perfection’植株产生平均每棵植株26.1个插条。由无病毒植株产生的插条通过研究被判定为可销售的，而那些来自病毒感染的植株则被判定为不可销售(Chase et al., 1981)。Hartman and Zettler (1974)也发现：27棵花叶万年青（D. picta）植物的枝条鲜重和叶片区域比经过防治的那些植物的要少63％和66％。同样地，36棵感染的Philodendron selloum植株的总的鲜重和叶片区域比经过防治的那些植物的分别少30％。
Wisler et al. (1978)报道：有症状的芋花叶病毒侵染的心叶蔓绿绒（Philodendron oxycardium）植株明显地比它们的无症侵染的植株较不健壮。生病植株的平均的叶片数量、叶片区域和蔓的长度分别比健康植株要少38.6％、31.6％和65.6％。感染植株的鲜重和叶片区域比健康的植株要少30％，受芋花叶病毒感染的裂叶喜林芋（P. selloum）植株减少大约80％。
彩叶芋（Caladium hortulanum）的产量损失也被Hartman and Zettler (1974)所报道。69棵感染植株的球茎鲜重和叶片区域分别比健康植株少40％和53％。类似地，Knauss et al. (1975)报道：来自组织培养砧木的后代的总的球茎数量胜过来自商业砧木的那些(499 对 208)。此外，组织培养砧木的发芽比商业砧木的发芽要更统一。 Due to a greater per unit value, most yield studies have been conducted on ornamental rather than edible aroids. However, Ramirez and Gamez (1984) reported significant yield reduction in both Xanthosoma sp. and Colocasia esculenta in Costa Rica. In yield studies on Dieffenbachia maculata ‘Perfection’, an average of 18.8 cuttings per plant were obtained from 30 healthy plants compared to only 10.1 from 60 dasheen mosaic potyvirus-infected plants. Of the 564 healthy cuttings, 98.4% were judged to be saleable compared to only 47.3% of the 606 infected cuttings (Zettler et al., 1980). In a similar study, Chase et al. (1981) reported that dasheen mosaic potyvirus-infected D. maculata ‘Perfection’ plants produced an average of 10.1 cuttings per plant, while virus-free ‘Perfection’ plants produced an average of 26.1 cuttings per plant. Cuttings produced by virus-free plants were judged saleable throughout the study, while those from virus-infected plants were not saleable (Chase et al., 1981). Hartman and Zettler (1974) also found that fresh shoot weights and leaf areas of 27 infected D. picta plants were 63% and 66% less than those of controls. Likewise, respective total fresh plant weights and leaf areas of 36 infected Philodendron selloum plants were 30% less than those of the controls. 
Wisler et al. (1978) reported that symptomatic dasheen mosaic potyvirus infected Philodendron oxycardium plants were significantly less vigorous than their symptomless counterparts. Average leaf numbers, leaf areas and vine lengths of diseased plants were 38.6, 31.6 and 65.6% less than those of healthy plants, respectively. Fresh plant weight and leaf areas of infected plants were 30% less than those of the healthy plants, and fresh weight of dasheen mosaic potyvirus infected P. selloum plants was reduced by about 80%. 
Yield losses of Caladium hortulanum were also reported by Hartman and Zettler (1974). Fresh corm weights of 69 infected plants were 40% less and leaf areas were 53% less than respective healthy plants. Similarly, Knauss et al. (1975) reported that total corm number of progeny resulting from tissue cultured stock exceeded that of commercial stock (499 vs. 208). Furthermore, sprouting of tissue cultured stock was more uniform than that noted for commercial stock.

host_range: ZYMV has also been reported from ridge gourd, melon, and bottle gourd in earlier studies from Pakistan. This is the first documented molecular evidence for the occurrence of ZYMV in Praecitrullus fistulosus in Pakistan.
potential_eco_desc: Praecitrullus fistulosus is infected by ZYMV causing high yield losses across the world. In this survey we detected an average incidence of 60% based on visual observations in the Islamabad Capital territory, Pothowar, Pakistan.
description: In summer 2014, as a part of cucurbit and potyvirus survey in Pothowar, Pakistan, the samples of Praecitrullus fistulosus with symptoms of leaf blistering, shoe-string, and severe mosaic were collected from five fields in the Islamabad Capital territory with an average incidence of 60% based on visual observations. The causal agent was identified as Zucchini yellow mosaic potyvirus (ZYMV) by serologically tested and RT-PCR. This is the first documented molecular evidence for the occurrence of ZYMV in P. fistulosus in Pakistan.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Round Gourd (Praecitrullus fistulosus) in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Sesamum indicum.
potential_eco_desc: The approximate percent of virus diseased plants during our survey was 10%.
description: Surveys of viral diseases on sesame(Sesamum indicum) were conducted in the summer of 2015 in Zhengzhou, Henan Province, China, and the approximate percent of virus diseased plants during our survey was 10%. The samples were collected and identified, the causal agent was identified as Watermelon mosaic virus(WMV), Bean common mosaic virus (BCMV), and Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV) by sequences analysis and DAS-ELISA. WMV and BCMV are already known to infect sesame in China, to our knowledge this is the first report of ZYMV natural infecting sesame.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus Infecting Sesame in China

host_range: For the past two years, we have noticed plants showing disease symptoms including severe mosaic and yellowing of leaves and severe fruit deformation and color cracking in pumpkin and squash in all the cultivars grown in Trinidad. The molecular diagnostics indicates that there were present of ZYMV in pumpkin and squash plants and Squash mosaic virus (SqMV) in pumpkin and watermelon plants.
potential_eco_desc: Virus infection was noticed at all growth stages of the crop and a maximum disease incidence of 74% was recorded in the dry season during 2014 and 2015.
description: For the past two years, we have noticed plants showing disease symptoms including severe mosaic and yellowing of leaves and severe fruit deformation and color cracking in pumpkin and squash in all the cultivars grown in Trinidad. The infection was suspected to be caused by Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV). Detailed surveys to record the severity of disease were conducted during dry and rainy seasons for a two-year period in farmers’ fields in six different locations (Barrackpore, Macoya, Las Lomas, Moruga, Waterloo, and Orange Groove) representing all the major cropping zones of the country. Virus infection was noticed at all growth stages of the crop and a maximum disease incidence of 74% was recorded in the dry season during 2014 and 2015. The molecular diagnostics indicates that there were present of ZYMV in pumpkin and squash plants and Squash mosaic virus (SqMV) in pumpkin and watermelon plants in Trinidad.  In cucurbit fields of Trinidad, high populations of aphids (Aphis gossypii) were noticed. Tests confirmed that the aphid was transmission vector of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV).
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus and Squash mosaic virus Infecting Cucurbits in Trinidad
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: The occurrence of ZYMV has been reported previously from bottle gourd and melon from Pakistan.
potential_eco_desc: Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV) infects several species of cucurbits, including ridge gourd (Luffa acutangula (L.) Rox), and causes significant yield losses worldwide.
description: During summer 2014, surveys were conducted to document major potyviruses infecting important cucurbits in the Pothwar Region of Pakistan. A total of 25 ridge gourd (Luffa acutangula) leaf samples with symptoms of mosaic, leaf malformation, and blistering were collected from three sites in the Rawalpindi-Islamabad area, where incidence of 45 to 60% was recorded based on visual assessment. There was presence of ZYMV by serological and molecular methods. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first confirmed report of ZYMV naturally infecting ridge gourd in Pakistan.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virusin Ridge Gourd in Pakistan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Chrysanthemum morifolium
potential_eco_desc: The incidence of this disease was more than 65% on chrysanthemum plants on farms in Wenxi, Shanxi Province.
description: In July 2014, virus-like symptoms such as foliar yellowing and mottle were observed on chrysanthemum plants on farms in Wenxi, Shanxi Province, China. The incidence of this disease was more than 65%. The samples were collected and identified, based on enzyme linked immunosorbent assay and molecular characteristics the pathogen was identified as Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV). To our knowledge, this is the first report anywhere of ZYMV infecting chrysanthemum.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Chrysanthemum
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: The occurrence of ZYMV has been reported previously in cucumber, pumpkin, bitter gourd, potato, gherkhins, musk melon, and Amarathus viridis in India.
potential_eco_desc: The disease incidence in these locations was variable, ranging between 32 and 58%.
description: While conducting field surveys during 2013 and 2014 to document virus diseases in cucurbitaceous crops in Tamil Nadu, India, snake gourds exhibiting mosaic and malformation of leaves were found in farmers’ fields in Tirunelveli (isolate TN TNV SG1), Tindivanam (Vilupuram, isolate TN TDV SG1), Udumalpet (Tiruppur, isolate TN UDU SG1), and Anamalai (Coimbatore, isolate TN ANA SG2). The disease incidence in these locations was variable, ranging between 32 and 58%. Symptomatic leaves from five plants from each location were tested by DAS-ELISA for the presence of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV). All symptomatic samples tested positive for ZYMV. Total RNA was extracted from symptomatic leaves to RT-PCR test, the results confirmed the presence of ZYMV in symptomatic plants of snake gourds. To our knowledge, this is the first confirmed report of the occurrence of ZYMV on snake gourd in India.  ZYMV is known to be transmissible by seed and aphid vectors.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Snake Gourd (Trichosanthes cucumerina) in India
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 西瓜Citrullus lanatus
description: In June 2012, field-grown watermelon plants (Citrullus lanatus [Thunb.] Matsum and Nakai) showing mild to severe mosaic, mottling, and bubbling followed by leaf deformation with blistering were observed in the Kukulje locality (Region of Banja Luka) in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Incidence of virus infection in the field was visually estimated at 15%. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Zucchini yellow mosaic viru（ZYMV）. To our knowledge, this is the first report of ZYMV in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is an important discovery. It represents expansion of this virus to new geographical area.
reference_name: First Report of Zucchini yellow mosaic virus in Watermelon in Bosnia and Herzegovina

potential_eco_desc: ZYMV occurrence is high and regular in regions with hot climatic conditions (tropical, sub-tropical and Southern Mediterranean regions such as in the Middle East, Central America, or Southern USA). Whenever surveys have been conducted, ZYMV has been found to be one of the most frequent cucurbit viruses, generally in more than 40% of the virus-infected samples (for more details see Geographic Distribution). In more septentrional regions (such as France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Northern USA) ZYMV epidemics are more erratic, not occurring every year or being limited geographically (for more details see Geographic Distribution). However, even there, high infection rates associated with important economic losses can be reached locally in some crops.^p^pAs a general rule, the earlier are the ZYMV infections in a crop, the higher is the impact on the marketable yield (Blua and Perring, 1989; Walkey et al., 1992; Fletcher et al., 2000). In the case of early infections, it is common to observe a complete loss in zucchini squash, cucumber or melon crops (Lecoq et al., 1981, McLeod et al., 1986, Blua and Perring, 1989; Lecoq et al., 1991, Wang et al., 1991; Al-Shahwan et al., 1995). In cantaloupe, the effect of ZYMV on yield is low if the epidemics start after production of the first fruits (Blua and Perring, 1989).

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pNaturally resistant cultivars^p^pResistance has been described in most of the cultivated cucurbit species. In melon (Cucumis melo) the semi dominant gene Zym has been found in PI414723 (Pitrat and Lecoq, 1984a); Zym is possibly complemented by minor genes (Danin-Poleg et al., 1997). However, this resistance can be easily overcome by ZYMV-adapted strains (Lecoq and Pitrat, 1984). An additional resistance mechanism is conferred by the single dominant gene Vat which prevents ZYMV transmission by one of its prevalent vectors, Aphis gossypii (Risser et al., 1981, Pitrat and Lecoq, 1984b).^p^pIn cucumber (Cucumis sativus) resistance has been observed in several cultivars, particularly in Taichung Mou Gua (TMG) and Dina Provvidenti, 1985, 1987; Yang et al., 1986; Abul Hayja and Al Shahwan, 1991; Wai and Grumet, 1995). The resistance in Dina and TMG is governed by different alleles of a single recessive gene zym (Provvidenti, 1987, Abul Hayja and Al Shahwan, 1991; Kabelka et al., 1997).^p^pIn squash, monogenic dominant resistances have been described in Cucurbita moschata (Provvidenti et al., 1984a; Paris et al., 1988; Gilbert Albertini et al., 1993). They have been introduced into Cucurbita pepo through interspecific crosses (Paris and Cohen, 2000). In watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) resistances with different inheritance and specificity have been described in landraces (Provvidenti, 1991, Boyhan et al., 1992, 1994).^p^pZYMV resistances have also been found in wild relatives of the cultivated cucurbit species. These include Cucumis figarei (Osaki et al., 1994), Cucurbita ecuadorensis and Cucurbita foetidissima (Lecoq et al., 1981). The ZYMV resistance of Cucurbita ecuadorensis has been introduced through interspecific crosses into Cucurbita maxima and Cucurbita pepo Herrington et al., 1988, 1991; Robinson et al., 1988; Paran et al., 1989).^p^pCommercial ZYMV-resistant cultivars are presently available for cucumber, Cucurbita maxima and zucchini squash (Cucurbita pepo).^p^pA monogenic dominant resistance to ZYMV has also been described in bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) (Fisher and Kyle, 1994).^p^pGenetically engineered resistant plants^p^pGenetically transformed squash and melon have been obtained expressing the ZYMV coat protein gene either alone or in association with coat protein genes from other viruses (Fang and Grumet, 1993; Gonsalves et al., 1994). When tested in laboratory or in multilocal field conditions these transgenic lines showed high levels of resistance to ZYMV (Arce Ochoa et al., 1995; Clough and Hamm, 1995; Fuchs and Gonzalves, 1995;  Tricoli et al., 1995; Fuchs et al., 1997). Commercial transgenic resistant squash cultivars are presently available in the USA. For regulation reasons these cultivars are not allowed to be cultivated in Europe.^p^pRisk assessment studies have been conducted on some of these transgenic lines. The possibility of transgene spread and introgression into the wild species Cucurbita texana has been demonstrated (Fuchs and Gonsalves, 1997). However, whether this gene transfer to Cucurbita texana will make this species more weedy and invasive in its natural habitats has not yet been evaluated (Fuchs and Gonsalves, 1997). Another concern associated with coat-protein mediated resistance is the possibility of heteroencapsidation with a potyvirus infecting the transgenic plant, and subsequent changes in aphid transmission specificity or efficiency (Lecoq et al., 1993). Using transgenic squash expressing the Watermelon mosaic virus (WMV) coat-protein gene and the ZYMV-NAT strain, Fuchs et al. (1999) showed that this event may indeed occur in the field. These observations emphasise the need for designing new capsid protein transgenes to prevent these risks. These 'tailored' transgenes should have the DAG motif necessary for aphid transmission or/and the amino acids involved in RNA encapsidation either mutated or deleted (Hammond et al., 1999).^p^pZYMV-resistant transgenic mel

description:
ZYMV通过几种蚜虫的不持续吸食而传播的，如：豌豆蚜，苜蓿无网蚜，豆蚜，棉蚜，中肿蚜（Aphis middletonii），绣线菊蚜（Aphis spiraecola），无肘脉蚜，萝卜蚜（Lipaphis erysimi），桃蚜，马铃薯长管蚜，桔二叉蚜（Toxoptera aurantii），茶二叉蚜和Uroleucon ambrosiae (Lecoq et al., 1981; Lisa et al., 1981; Lisa and Lecoq, 1984; Purcifull et al., 1984; Ohtsu et al., 1985; Adlerz, 1987; Abdulsalam et al., 1988; Chao and Chen, 1990; Luis-Arteaga, 1990; Stobbs et al., 1990; Castle et al., 1992; Fereres et al., 1992; Wang et al., 1992; Rivera et al., 1993; Tomassoli et al., 1993; Chao et al., 1994; Orozco-Santos et al., 1994)。
在葫芦科中有一些ZYMV种子传播的报道，其变化的传播率为：0.05% (4196棵苗中的两棵， Schrijnwerkers et al., 1991)，1% (100棵苗中有一棵，Greber et al., 1987)， 0到3.5% (Fletcher et al., 2000) 及 在油类南瓜种子低比率(Tobias and Palkovics, 2003)。ZYMV的种子传播也被报道于扬子毛茛（Ranunculus sardous）中(Al Musa, 1989b)。ZYMV的种子传播通过ELISA和RT-PCR在12堆种子堆中的7堆中确定（收获于受ZYMV感染的北瓜栽培种styriaca植株中）。传播率范围在1 和5%之间(Riedle-Bauer et al., 2002)。在ZYMV不被探测于生长于由感染的葫芦科，黄瓜或柠檬植株中产出的种子的大量苗中的地方也有报道(Lecoq et al., 1981; Greber et al., 1987; Gleason and Provvidenti, 1990; Robinson et al., 1993; Wong et al., 1994; Desbiez and Lecoq, 1997)。
ZYMV在受感染的修剪工具上也能被传播。 ZYMV is transmitted in a non-persistent manner by several aphid species: Acyrthosiphon pisum, Acyrthosiphon kondoi, Aphis craccivora, Aphis gossypii, Aphis middletonii, Aphis spiraecola, Hysteroneura setariae, Lipaphis erysimi, Myzus persicae, Macrosiphum euphorbiae, Toxoptera aurantii and Uroleucon ambrosiae (Lecoq et al., 1981; Lisa et al., 1981; Lisa and Lecoq, 1984; Purcifull et al., 1984; Ohtsu et al., 1985; Adlerz, 1987; Abdulsalam et al., 1988; Chao and Chen, 1990; Luis-Arteaga, 1990; Stobbs et al., 1990; Castle et al., 1992; Fereres et al., 1992; Wang et al., 1992; Rivera et al., 1993; Tomassoli et al., 1993; Chao et al., 1994; Orozco-Santos et al., 1994).
There are a several reports of ZYMV seed transmission in Cucurbita sp. with variable transmission rates: 0.05% (two out of 4196 seedlings, Schrijnwerkers et al., 1991), 1% (one out of 100 seedlings, Greber et al., 1987), 0 to 3.5% (Fletcher et al., 2000) and at low rates in oil pumpkin seeds (Tobias and Palkovics, 2003). Seed transmission has also been reported in Ranunculus sardous (Al Musa, 1989b). Seed transmission of ZYMV was ascertained by ELISA and RT-PCR in seven out of 12 seed lots (harvested from ZYMV-infected C. pepo var. styriaca plants). Transmission rates ranged between 1 and 5% (Riedle-Bauer et al., 2002). There are also reports where ZYMV was not detected in large numbers of seedlings grown from seed produced by infected Cucurbita sp., cucumber or melon plants (Lecoq et al., 1981; Greber et al., 1987; Gleason and Provvidenti, 1990; Robinson et al., 1993; Wong et al., 1994; Desbiez and Lecoq, 1997).
ZYMV may also be transmitted on infected cutting tools.

potential_eco_desc: 作为一个大概的规律，ZYMV越早地侵染作物，在可销售的田间作物就会造成越大的影响(Blua and Perring, 1989; Walkey et al., 1992; Fletcher et al., 2000)。早侵染的病例中，在南瓜，黄瓜或香瓜作物上(Lecoq et al., 1981, McLeod et al., 1986, Blua and Perring, 1989; Lecoq et al., 1991, Wang et al., 1991; Al-Shahwan et al., 1995)造成完全的损失是普遍的。在罗马甜瓜上，若传染在第一次果实出产后，那么田间ZYMV的影响是很少的。 As a general rule, the earlier are the ZYMV infections in a crop, the higher is the impact on the marketable yield (Blua and Perring, 1989; Walkey et al., 1992; Fletcher et al., 2000). In the case of early infections, it is common to observe a complete loss in zucchini squash, cucumber or melon crops (Lecoq et al., 1981, McLeod et al., 1986, Blua and Perring, 1989; Lecoq et al., 1991, Wang et al., 1991; Al-Shahwan et al., 1995). In cantaloupe, the effect of ZYMV on yield is low if the epidemics start after production of the first fruits (Blua and Perring, 1989). ZYMV出现在热带气候条件（热带，亚热带和地中海南部地区，如：中东，美州中部或美国南部）的地区是强烈的和经常的。每当调查实施时，通常在超过40%被病毒侵染的样品上（详见地理分布），会发现ZYMV是几种常见葫芦病毒的其中一种。在更多的北方地区，如：法国，意大利，西班牙及英国，（美国）北部，ZYMV的传染是较不稳定的，不会在每年或地理方面受限制的地区发生（详见地理分布）。然而，就算在那里，伴随重要经济损失的高侵染频率能在一些作物上局部延伸。 ZYMV occurrence is high and regular in regions with hot climatic conditions (tropical, sub-tropical and Southern Mediterranean regions such as in the Middle East, Central America, or Southern USA). Whenever surveys have been conducted, ZYMV has been found to be one of the most frequent cucurbit viruses, generally in more than 40% of the virus-infected samples (for more details see Geographic Distribution). In more septentrional regions (such as France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Northern USA) ZYMV epidemics are more erratic, not occurring every year or being limited geographically (for more details see Geographic Distribution). However, even there, high infection rates associated with important economic losses can be reached locally in some crops.

management_info:
在能抵挡昆虫的隔板室内生长的树苗推荐减少幼苗期的早期污染。在田间，不同种类的覆盖物（穿孔的塑料膜，低隧道）对于防止ZYMV的传播是有效的(Perring et al., 1989; Nencini and Tesi, 1991; Lecoq, 1992b; Reyd et al., 1993; Tomassoli et al., 1993; Espinoza and McLeod, 1994)。然而，阻隔昆虫的覆盖物一定要在花期移除，以免阻碍了昆虫的传粉。
塑料覆盖层（透明的，银色的）和铝箔已显示出对于蚜虫的驱散及延迟了病毒传播到2－3周有效果(Giunchedi et al., 1991; Lecoq 1992b; Brown et al., 1993, Mansour et al., 2000)。然而，当植株生长覆盖了它们的表面时，这有效了保护就会消失。可喷射的银色薄膜覆盖物也被用于延迟ZYMV的传播，它们提出这个生物所能分解的优点及它们在季末的土壤里能被合并(Summers et al., 1995。 Growing seedlings under insect-proof screen-houses is recommended to prevent early contaminations at the plantlet stage. In the fields, covers of different types (unwowen floating covers, perforated plastics, low tunnels) were efficient in preventing ZYMV transmission (Perring et al., 1989; Nencini and Tesi, 1991; Lecoq, 1992b; Reyd et al., 1993; Tomassoli et al., 1993; Espinoza and McLeod, 1994). However, insect-proof covers must be removed at the flowering stage to allow insect pollination. 
Plastic mulches (transparent, silver) and aluminium foils were shown to be efficient as aphid repellents and to delay virus spread for 2-3 weeks (Giunchedi et al., 1991; Lecoq 1992b; Brown et al., 1993, Mansour et al., 2000). However the protective efficiency is lost when plant growth covers their surfaces. Sprayable silver film mulches have also been used to delay ZYMV spread; they present the advantage to be biodegradable and they can be incorporated in the soil at the end of the season (Summers et al., 1995). 很多种方法能够用于限制携带ZYMV的蚜虫及葫芦植株的接触：这些能成为物质的障碍（覆盖物和隔板），防护物（塑料覆盖层及铝箔）或化学药品（无机乳油和杀虫剂）
杀虫剂的应用逐渐减少转移到一株作物上的明显的蚜虫种群数量，但，没有被发现在减少ZYMV在田间的传播上有效果。这可能因为杀虫剂没有足够快的杀死带病毒的有翼蚜虫来防止不持续病毒的传播，及由于多数有效的ZYMV带毒者不是开拓者(Webb and Linda, 1993; Perring and Farrar, 1993; Yuan and Ullman, 1996; Lisa et al., 1997)。
单独的乳油喷雾或一并使用拟除虫菊酯能在某些生态学条件下提供一些保护，但是应用一定随着适合的机器频繁地重复使用才能达到有效(Makkouk and Menassa, 1985, 1986; Raccah, 1985; Webb and Linda, 1993)。 Various methods can be used to limit the chances of contact of aphids carrying ZYMV and cucurbit plants: these can be physical barriers (covers and screens), repellents (plastic mulches and aluminium foils) or chemicals (mineral oils and insecticides).
Insecticide applications generally reduce significantly the aphid population colonizing a crop, but were not found to be effective in reducing ZYMV spread in the fields. This is probably because insecticides do not kill viruliferous alate aphids quickly enough to prevent transmission of a non-persistent virus, and because the most efficient ZYMV vectors are noncolonizers (Webb and Linda, 1993; Perring and Farrar, 1993; Yuan and Ullman, 1996; Lisa et al., 1997).
Mineral oil sprays alone or in association with pyrethroids might provide some protection under certain ecological conditions but applications must be repeated frequently with adapted machinery to be effective (Makkouk and Menassa, 1985, 1986; Raccah, 1985; Webb and Linda, 1993). 自然温和的及蚜虫纯遗传的ZYMV品种(ZYMV-WK)已被分离(Lecoq et al., 1991b)。ZYMV-WK没有影响果实的品质，只是稍微减少了葫芦的产量，它已被显示出有效地保护多种葫芦植株以免受到严重的ZYMV隔离种群的侵染，无论在温室，田间及不同地区，如：法国，台湾，美国，夏威夷，土耳其，加利福尼亚，以色列(Lecoq et al., 1991b; Wang et al., 1991; Walkey et al., 1992; Spence et al., 1996; Yarden et al., 2000)。然而，ZYMV-WK不能防御遗传的多种分歧的ZYMV隔离种群，如来自留尼旺或毛里求斯(Desbiez and Lecoq, 1997)的那些种类。对抗ZYMV的交互保护现在已用于几个以商业为主的地区里(Yarden et al., 2000)。
Gal On (2000)显示了在保护为主的由有助的蛋白质所构成的FRNK对于由ZYMV-WK发展而来的温和症状是有关的。 A natural mild and aphid poorly-transmissible strain of ZYMV (ZYMV-WK) has been isolated (Lecoq et al., 1991b). host_range: 多花水仙 Narcissus tazetta cv. Paperwhite
description: During surveys in January 2013 and 2014, severe chlorotic leaf stripe symptoms were observed on about 40% of Narcissus tazetta plants growing in a garden of CSIR-NBRI, Lucknow, India. The test demonstrated that the causal agent was Cyrtanthus elatus virus A (CEVA). An uncharacterized potyvirus serologically related to Bean yellow mosaic virus and Lycoris potyvirus has been reported to occur in India on N. tazetta; however, occurrence of CEVA potyvirus on N. tazetta is being reported for the first report time.
reference_name: First Report of Cyrtanthus elatus virus A in Narcissus tazetta in India

host_range: OYDV is one of the most widespread viruses in garlic and onion and affects the development and quality of the crops.
potential_eco_desc: The presence of OYDV in leek plants in the field would represent an alternative host for the infection of onion and garlic crops, and could increase leek crop losses in mixed infections with other viruses.
description: In spring of 2015, the leek plants of four different varieties (Curling, Custeau, Megaton, and Pluston), showing symptoms of inverted roots and cracked stems, were collected to analyze the presence of Onion yellow dwarf virus(OYDV) from fields near San Pablo de la Moraleja, Valladolid (Castilla y León, Spain). Test results showed the presence of OYDV in leek plants by molecular diagnostics. This is the first report of the detection of OYDV in leek from Spain.
reference_name: First Report of Onion yellow dwarf virus in Leek (Allium ampeloprasum var. porrum) in Spain
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: To our knowledge, this is the first report of OYDV, LYSV, and GCLV on garlic in Croatia.
description: At the beginning of 2015, symptoms of yellowing and reduced growth were observed on autochthonous garlic cultivars in commercial fields in Zadar County (northern Dalmatia) and in an experimental field in Zagreb (planting material originating from eastern part of Croatia). The symptomatic samples were collected and analyzed. Plants were initially tested with ELISA for the presence of Onion yellow dwarf virus (OYDV), Leek yellow stripe virus (LYSV), and Garlic common latent virus (GCLV) using commercial kits, then we performed the molecular diagnostics, the results showed that OYDV, LYSV, and GCLV were present in garlic. Among these three viruses only OYDV has been previously known to occur in Croatia, that report concerned onion infections. To our knowledge, this is the first report of OYDV, LYSV, and GCLV on garlic in Croatia.  OYDV, LYSV, and GCLV are all transmitted by aphids in a nonpersistant manner.
reference_name: First Report of Onion yellow dwarf virus, Leek yellow stripe virus, and Garlic common latent virus on Garlic in Croatia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Allium sativum.
potential_eco_desc: Study shows the coinfection of the most important viruses from the genera Potyvirus and Carlavirus in Ecuadorian garlic.
description: The garlic leaves were sampled from symptomatic plants showing mild to severe chlorotic streaking and leaf curling in the fields of an experimental farm in Tumbaco (Pichincha Province), these samples corresponded to clove seeds collected during April 2011 from commercial cultivars; some from Pungalá (Chimborazo Province), Cebadas (Chimborazo Province), Pelileo (Tungurahua Province), and local markets in Quito (Pichincha Province). Based on molecular diagnostics showed the presence of Leek yellow stripe virus (LYSV), Shallot latent virus (SLV) and Onion yellow dwarf virus (OYDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of LYSV, OYDV, and SLV in garlic from Ecuador.  Garlic (Allium sativum L.) is affected by several potyviruses and carlaviruses that induce chlorotic leaf striping, growth reduction, and lead to yield losses. The disease is spread by seed bulbils or cloves due to the vegetative propagation of the crop; this causes accumulation of viruses over generations.
reference_name: First Report of Leek yellow stripe virus, Shallot latent virus, and Onion yellow dwarf virus in Garlic From Ecuador
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Allium ascalonicum.
description: During a survey on viruses infecting garlic in the Latium region (central Italy), shallot plants showing virus-like symptoms were noted in one of the farms surveyed. Samples of three local cultivars ('Bianco', 'Violetto romagnolo' and 'Allungato violetto della Romagna') were screened for the most common viruses affecting Allium species. Using DAS-ELISA, Onion yellow dwarf virus (OYDV) was found in all samples. The presence of allexiviruses was assessed by a modified one-step RT-PCR amplification procedure using degenerate oligonucleotide primers. All nucleotide sequences were assembled and BLAST searches identified the presence of Shallot virus X (ShVX). Allexiviruses cause asymptomatic infection on Allium spp. (Katis et al., 2012). The severe symptoms observed on shallot plants in this investigation were due to mixed infections with ShVX and OYDV, the latter being widely found in nearby onion and garlic crops. In Italy, allexiviruses have been reported in garlic (Dovas & Vovlas, 2003; Lanzoni et al., 2006) but this is the first report of ShVX on shallot in Italy and a wider distribution of allexiviruses is feared by farmers in the country.
reference_name: First report of Shallot virus X infecting shallot in Italy
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Allium cepa var. aggregatum
description: In June 2014, approximately 30% of field-grown shallot (Allium cepa var. aggregatum) plants in the Rimski Sancevi locality (South Backa District, Serbia) showed leaf symptoms in the form of yellow stripes accompanied by leaf curling and plant stunting. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Onion yellow dwarf virus (OYDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of OYDV on shallot in Serbia.
reference_name: First Report of Onion yellow dwarf virus Infecting Shallot in Serbia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 蒜Allium sativum （cv. Blanko, Harna?, Jarus, and Mega）
description: A general mosaic and yellowing of leaves of four garlic cultivars (Blanko, Harna?, Jarus, and Mega) was observed in 11 garlic-production fields in the Lodz, Mazowieckie, Ma?opolska, and Pomorskie regions of Poland in July 2012. The 29 samples were collected and identified, results indicated that 6 samples (20.7%) were infected with Onion yellow dwarf virus（OYDV）, 25 samples (86.2%) were infected with Garlic common latent virus（GCLV）, and 23 samples (79.3%) were infected with Shallot latent virus（SLV）. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of OYDV, GCLV, and SLV in garlic plants in Poland.
reference_name: First Report of Onion yellow dwarf virus, Garlic common latent virus and Shallot latent virus on Garlic in Poland

description: 在自然界，OYDV通过桃蚜和蚜科的其它一些种类以不持续方式传播。病毒通过受感染植株的营养繁殖来保持。生长于受侵染的营养繁殖体的植株的病毒的集中可能改变植株阶段，且集中可能使植物生长发育的早期阶段期间的探测水平降低。OYDV通过机械接种实验性的传播。它既不通过植物之间的联系，也不通过种子，更不通过花粉传播。复制不依靠病毒辅助者(Brunt et al., 1996)。 In nature, OYDV is transmitted in a non-persistent manner by Myzus persicae and several other species of the Aphididae. The virus is maintained by vegetative propagation of infected plants. The viral concentration of plants grown from infected vegetative propagules may change with the plant stage and concentrations may drop below detectable levels during the early stages of plant growth. OYDV is experimentally transmissable by mechanical inoculation. It is not transmitted by contact between plants, nor by seed, nor by pollen. Replication does not depend on a helper virus (Brunt et al., 1996).
author: zhangjianjun

description: Parsley plants (Petroselinum crispum) with disease symptoms were observed in a private garden in October 2014 and in a field used for commercial parsley production in September 2016 in central Slovenia. In the commercial field, up to 10% of parsley plants were symptomatic. Symptomatic plants were scattered throughout the field, with no apparent pattern. The presence of Apium Virus Y (ApVY) and Carrot Thin Leaf Virus (CTLV) in the original symptomatic parsley were confirmed by virus-specific ELISA or reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) tests. Further research is needed to determine whether CTLV is responsible for symptomatology alone, or in mixed infections with ApVY. This is the first report of ApVY and CTLV in Slovenia.
reference_name: First Report of Apium Virus Y and Carrot Thin Leaf Virus in Parsley in Slovenia

potential_eco_desc: Of the 20 fields we investigated, four fields with 90% tomato plants were infected.
description: Chilli veinal mottle virus (ChiVMV), a potyvirus, is widespread over the world. In China, it was first reported in chili pepper (Capsicum annuum) in Hainan Province (south China) in 2006. Subsequently, it was reported in tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum) in Yunnan Province (southwest China) in 2011. In May 2012, tomatoes with leaves displaying virus-infected symptoms were observed in several fields of Chengdu, eastern Sichuan Province, southwest China. During 2012 and 2013, six samples were collected from symptomatic tomato leaves based on different symptoms and locations. Based on molecular detection showed that the causal agent was Chilli veinal mottle virus (ChiVMV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of ChiVMV naturally infecting tomato in China. It shows that ChiVMV is spreading in China and is naturally infecting a new solanaceous crop in the southwest area, and the spread of the virus may affect tomato crop yields in China.
reference_name: First Report of Chilli veinal mottle virus Infecting Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) in China

management_info:
对ChiVMV有抗性或耐病性的辣椒（Capsicum annuum）和C. frutescens的栽培品种/品系已经从亚洲蔬菜研究和发展中心(AVRDC) 开展于1986年的育种程序中鉴别出来(Yoon et al., 1989)，直到1989年由亚洲蔬菜网络的胡椒病毒亚网络所补充，这是由亚洲发展银行所资助的(AVRDC, 1990b, c, 1991, 1992, 1993)。这些品种/品系的抗性现在被合并合成为AVRDC的希望育种系。
ChiVMV抗性是由一个单一的隐性基因所控制(Chew and Ong, 1990)。十九个拥有较好园艺特性的ChiVMV抗性育种系在马来西亚通过改良敏感基因型和抗性来源的杂交而产生。研究人员正合并黄瓜花叶病毒(CMV)抗性基因进入现有的来自育种系的抗性ChiVMV后代中。这些多重的病毒抗性品系将在几年当中分发到农民手中(AVRDC, 1993)。 Cultivars/lines of Capsicum annuum and C. frutescens that are resistant or tolerant to ChiVMV have been identified from a breeding programme initiated in 1986 at the Asian Vegetable Research and Development Center (AVRDC) (Yoon et al., 1989) and complemented since 1989 by the pepper virus sub-network of the Asian Vegetable Network, funded by the Asian Development Bank (AVRDC, 1990b, c, 1991, 1992, 1993). The resistances of these cultivars/lines are now being incorporated into AVRDC’s promising breeding lines.
ChiVMV resistance is governed by a single recessive gene (Chew and Ong, 1990). Nineteen ChiVMV-resistant breeding lines with good horticultural characteristics have been developed in Malaysia by crossing adapted susceptible genotypes with resistant sources. Researchers are incorporating cucumber mosaic cucumovirus (CMV) resistance genes into existing ChiVMV-resistant progenies from the breeding lines. These multiple virus-resistant lines could be ready for distribution to farmers within a few years (AVRDC, 1993). 混作玉米和辣椒品种和种植玉米作为屏障作物能减少媒介的种群数量和病毒的发生率(Roff and Ho, 1991; Kittipakorn et al., 1994)。
为了减少蚜虫的种群数量和病毒的发生率、延迟病毒的侵染和增加辣椒的产量，涂上铝涂料或银涂料的聚乙烯薄片的局部反射的覆盖物已被马来西亚和台湾的农民所采用(Chen and Chen, 1980, 1983; Ong, 1984)。这实践通常要伴随着每星期（或更经常）的杀虫剂应用。
实验上，单独使用矿物油或矿物油与反射覆盖物一起的使用已被显示能延迟病毒的侵染和降低病毒的发生率(Su, 1982; Cheng and Tung, 1987)。脱脂喷雾和颜色诱饵技术的使用，（如吸引蚜虫离开作物并令它们溺死的黄色水槽），已显示能减少蚜虫的数量和病毒侵染的发生率以及增加辣椒的产量(Kittipakorn et al., 1994; Ong, 1984)。用80网孔的尼龙或粗棉布来覆盖苗床可使植物远离蚜虫，因此能完全地消除幼苗中的病毒；于是它能延迟病毒的侵染和减少病毒在田间的发生率(Cheng and Tung, 1987; Fujisawa et al., 1990)。
对于在遮蔽下生长的辣椒植株塑料挡板和黄色或白色的粘性陷阱的使用能明显地减少蚜虫的种群数量(Cheng and Tung, 1987; Kuo and Wu, 1989) (Su, 1982; Cheng and Tung, 1987)。
一种防治辣椒品种上的病毒病害的综合的防治方案已在马来西亚产生(Green, 1992)，这方案是利用银色反射薄片、生长中幼苗的防虫笼、预防性杀虫剂的使用和常规（每两周）叶面肥料处理。 Intercropping of maize with Capsicum species and planting maize as a barrier crop reduce vector populations and virus incidence (Roff and Ho, 1991; Kittipakorn et al., 1994).
To reduce aphid populations and virus incidence, to delay virus infection, and to increase the yield of capsicums, reflective mulches of locally produced aluminium-painted or silver-coated polyethylene sheets have been applied by farmers in Malaysia and Taiwan (Chen and Chen, 1980, 1983; Ong, 1984). This practice is usually accompanied by weekly (or more frequent) applications of insecticide.
Experimentally, the use of mineral oil alone or in combination with reflective mulches has been shown to delay virus infection and to reduce virus incidence (Su, 1982; Cheng and Tung, 1987). Use of skimmed milk sprays and colour-bait techniques, (e.g. yellow water-troughs which attract aphids away from the crop and kill them by drowning), has been shown to reduce the number of aphids and incidence of virus infection and to increase the yield of capsicums (Kittipakorn et al., 1994; Ong, 1984). Covering the seedbeds with 80 mesh Nylon or cheesecloth protects plants from the aphids and so can eliminate the virus completely in seedlings; thus it can delay virus infection and reduce virus incidence in the field (Cheng and Tung, 1987; Fujisawa et al., 1990).
For capsicum plants grown under shelter, the use of plastic mulch and yellow or white sticky traps has been shown significantly to reduce the aphid populations (Cheng and Tung, 1987; Kuo and Wu, 1989) (Su, 1982; Cheng and Tung, 1987).

Little Sweet Scent) with deformed flowers displaying colour break and mild chlorotic streaking of the leaves. In the vicinity of the orchid nursery, passionfruit (Passiflora edulis) vines were observed with leaves displaying mosaic, “green islands”, and severe rugosity. These symptoms on passionfruit were subsequently observed at two other locations in Honolulu. The samples were collected and identified, all sequences had highest sequence similarity to Watermelon mosaic virus (WMV). The WMV present in honohono orchids and passionfruit were closely related, with a nucleotide identity of 96% over the entire genome. However, they had nucleotide identities of only 89% to 93% to the sequences of other WMV strains present in GenBank. Phylogenetic analysis based on the full-length polyprotein sequence using a neighbour-joining algorithm placed these strains in a distinct lineage within the WMV clade. This is the first reliable report of a distinct lineage of WMV naturally infects honohono orchid and passionfruit in Hawaii.
reference_name: A distinct lineage of Watermelon mosaic virus naturally infects honohono orchid (Dendrobium anosmum) and passionfruit (Passiflora edulis) in Hawaii

management_info: Cultural Control^p^pCrop management^pCrop management practices reported to affect the incidence of WMV in cucurbits include plant population (Fegla and Badr, 1979), planting date and fertilizer level (Abo-Elyazid et al., 1990). Where possible planting dates should be adjusted to avoid the main aphid flights during early growth stages (Mansour, 1997a).^p^pMulches^pVarious plastic mulches (reflective, transparent and coloured) have been shown to reduce losses due to WMV in a number of crops including squash (Lamont et al., 1990; Brown et al., 1993), muskmelon (Lecoq et al., 1983) and marrow (Giunchedi et al., 1991). The mulches repel aphids during the early stages of crop growth, delaying virus infection and reducing crop losses. Mansour et al. (2000) found that aluminium foil boards performed better than aluminium foil mulch for squash (Cucurbita pepo).^p^pFloating row covers^pThe exclusion of virus vectors by floating row covers has been shown to delay and reduce the incidence of WMV in melons, with resultant yield increases in some instances (Perring et al., 1989; Orozco et al., 1994; Espinoza and McLeod, 1994). However, in autumn plantings, where light levels were low, Perring et al. (1989) reported no resultant yield increase.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pInsecticides^pThe use of insecticides against aphid vectors has little effect on WMV spread in field crops.^p^pOil sprays^pSeveral authors have reported either delayed infection or reduced WMV incidence and spread in crops sprayed with light mineral oils (Chalfant and Young, 1984; Webb and Linda, 1993; Orozco et al., 1994). However, melon yields were reduced due to the phytotoxic effects of the oil sprays (Orozco et al., 1994; Webb and Linda, 1993). For squash, Mansour (1997b) found that weekly applications of JMS stylet oil alone was unsatisfactory, but in combination with aluminium foil mulch it reduced losses from 30 to 16%.^p^p^Biological ControlKameya-Iwaki et al. (1992) produced a mild strain of WMV that conferred protection in squash, cucumber, muskmelon and watermelon against a virulent isolate of WMV under greenhouse conditions.Kosaka and Fukunishi (1997) assessed mild strain cross protection of grafted cucumbers for a combination of WMV, ZYMV and CMV under field conditions. When viruses were most prevalent inoculation with mild strains improved yields compared to unprotected treatments, but reduced yields by 15% compared to healthy controls.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pConventional plant breeding^pMany cultivars of Phaseolus vulgaris show resistance to WMV (Provvidenti, 1974). Two resistance genes that have been well documented are Wmv, which prevents systemic spread of the virus, and Hsw which reduces viral replication (Kyle and Provvidenti, 1987; Kyle and Dickson, 1988; Scully et al., 1995). WMV resistance has also been incorporated into cultivars of bottle gourd (Lagenaria suceraria) (Provvidenti,1995), cucumber (Takeda and Gilbert, 1975; Wai and Grumet, 1995), melon (Moyer et al., 1985; Munger, 1991; Gilbert et al., 1994), pumpkin (Herrington et al., 1991), squash (Gilbert-Albertini et al., 1993) and watermelon (Anon., 1996; Gillaspie and Wright, 1993; Graves Gillaspie and Jarret, 1997). Kristkova and Lebeda (2000) screened 279 Cucurbita pepo and 159 Cucurbita maxima accessions and found 2 and 5 highly resistant accessions, respectively. Resistance to aphid vectors of WMV has also been reported in melon (Pitrat et al., 1982; Gray et al., 1986; Kishaba et al., 1992).^p^pTransgenic plants^pSeveral groups have generated transgenic plants with resistance to WMV and other cucurbit viruses. These include: Cucumis melo (Fuchs et al., 1997; Huttner et al., 1999; Wang et al., 2000) and C. pepo (Arce-Ochoa et al., 1995; Tricoli et al., 1995; Fuchs et al., 1998). As with conventional breeding it may be necessary to combine WMV resistance with Cucumber mosaic virus and/or Zucchini yellow mosaic virus resistance to obtain good yields (Fuchs and Gonsalves, 1995).

management_info: As SPFMV is transmitted in the non-persistent manner by aphids, control of the aphid vectors in field crops is not economically feasible. The main control measures are the production and use  of virus-free planting material, sanitation, and the use of resistant varieties (Kai et al., 2000; Karyeija et al., 2000b; Gibson et al., 2004; Iwanami, 2004). Virus-free plants have been obtained in many countries by meristem tip culture (e.g., Wambugu, 1991; Mason and Beetham, 1998; Gao et al., 2000; Carroll et al., 2004; Jeeva et al., 2004b; Zhang et al., 2005) and thermotherapy (Jeeva et al., 2004b). Resistance to SPFMV is conferred by two recessive genes (Mwanga et al., 2002).^p ^pSPFMV is perpetuated between cropping cycles in infected cuttings, the lack of symptoms in the foliage makes it difficult for farmers to select SPFMV-free cuttings. Some wild species of Ipomoea are reservoirs of SPFMV and, if present, should be removed (Clark et al., 1986).^p^pThere is a possibility that transgenic resistant plants may in future be useful in limiting the deleterious effects of SPFMV (Cipriani et al., 2001;Okada et al., 2001, 2002; Wambugu, 2003).

description: 甘薯羽状斑驳病毒(SPFMV)是最具特征性的甘薯病毒(Brunt et al., 1990)。甘薯羽状斑驳病毒(SPFMV)有许多马铃薯Y病毒组病毒的生物学的、物理化学和细胞病理学的特性，其中包括蚜虫传播特性、风轮状内含物的存在产生和相对窄的寄主范围。SPFMV可由很多种类的蚜虫以非持久的方式传播(Pozzer et al., 1993, 1995; Ames et al., 1996)，科学实验依靠营养繁殖。 SPFMV is the most thoroughly characterized sweet potato virus (Brunt et al., 1990). SPFMV has many of the biological, physico-chemical and cytopathic characteristics of potyviruses, including aphid transmissibility, occurrence of pinwheel inclusions, and a relatively narrow host range. SPFMV is transmitted by a large number of aphid species in the nonpersistent manner (Pozzer et al., 1993, 1995; Ames et al., 1996) and experimentally also by vegetative propagation.

However, in areas where no appropriate agrotechnical practices are used, BtMV infection may reach 100% incidence; for example 100% incidence was reported in fodder beet crops close to seed beet in Uzbekistan (Rogov et al., 1992).
