management_info: SPCSV is perpetuated through cropping cycles in infected tubers and cuttings. ^p^pThe main measure to control SPCSV is the production or selection and use of virus-free plants as sources of planting material, sanitation and the use of resistant or tolerant varieties (Gibson et al., 1997). Meristem tip culture is the procedure usually used for the production of virus-free plants (e.g., Zhang et al., 2005). Strategies for the control of SPCSV in Africa have been reviewed by Gibson et al. (2004).^p^pIn recent years there has been increased interest in the development of virus-resistant genotypes Mwanga et al., 2002a,b; resistance has been shown to be mediated by two recessive genes (Mwanga et al., 2002c). Some land races of sweet potato in sub-Saharan countries are also possible superior resistant genotypes (Gibson et al., 2000). The effects of SPVD in Uganda can be minimised by the use of high-yielding resistant selections combined with phytosanitation (Gibson et al., 2004).
author: CPC2006

potential_eco_desc: 单独由甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）引起的产量损失在第一年可能只是很小的，但第二年要增长到30％。然而，当它连同甘薯羽状斑驳病毒((SPFMV)，会引起SPVD—— 一个在非洲和以色列造成几乎所有产量损失的严重的病害(Hahn, 1979; Milgram et al., 1996)。在阿根廷，甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）能造成80％的产量损失(Di Feo et al., 1995).。 SPCSV alone may cause only small yield losses in the first year, but up to 30% in the second year. However, in combination with SPFMV it causes SPVD, a severe disease associated with almost complete yield loss in Africa and Israel (Hahn, 1979; Milgram et al., 1996). In Argentina, the chlorotic dwarf disease can result in yield losses of up to 80% (Di Feo et al., 1995).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）是由烟粉虱（Bemisia tabaci）以半持久的方式传播。该病毒不能由机械接种或植物间接触传播。它可以由人工嫁接传播。
因为该病毒系统地侵染甘薯，所以它由被侵染的营养繁殖体（茎插条和根）传播。那些由带毒繁殖体繁殖而成的植株是主要的侵染源，特别是当它们自生自长。 SPCSV is transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in a semi-persistent manner. The virus is not transmitted by mechanical inoculation nor by contact between plants. It is transmitted experimentally by grafting.
Because the virus infects sweet potato plants systemically, it is disseminated in infected vegetatively-produced propagules (stem cuttings and roots). Plants grown from such propagules are primary sources of infection, especially if they occur as volunteers.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）通过感染插条在种植周期上永久存在。甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）通常被识别为是与甘薯的羽状斑驳病毒((SPFMV)一起联合侵染植株引起甘薯病毒病害（SPVD）。
控制甘薯褪绿矮化病毒（SPCSV）主要的方法是避免带病植株作为植物材料，注意环境卫生和选用抗病或耐病品种(Gibson et al., 1997).。 SPCSV is perpetuated through cropping cycles via infected cuttings. SPCSV is generally identified in combination with SPFMV causing the severe disease SPVD.
The main measure to control SPCSV is avoidance of diseased plants as sources of planting material, sanitation and the use of resistant or tolerant varieties (Gibson et al., 1997).
author: zhangjianjun

host_range: LCV has recently been reported to infect green bean in Spain. This is the first report of a natural infection of LCV on tomato in China.
potential_eco_desc: Approximately 30% of tomato plants exhibited chlorosis symptom on leaves and fruits in Shouguang County, Shandong Province, China
description: During a survey of greenhouse tomato diseases in September 2015, approximately 30% of tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) plants exhibited chlorosis symptom on leaves and fruits in Shouguang County, Shandong Province, China. Leaf samples of tomato plants were collected and total RNA was extracted, based on BLASTn searches and RT-PCR assay the pathogen was Lettuce chlorosis virus (LCV). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of a natural infection of LCV on tomato in China.  Lettuce chlorosis virus (LCV) is transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) in a semipersistent manner.
reference_name: First report of Lettuce chlorosis virus infecting tomato in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 菜豆Phaseolus vulgaris
description: In September 2011, symptoms typically associated with Bean yellow disorder virus (BYDV) such as intervenal mottling and yellowing on middle and lower leaves combined with brittleness were observed in green bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) produced in commercial greenhouses from Granada and Almeria provinces, Spain. But, collected samples tested negative for BYDV, the pathogen was Lettuce chlorosis virus（LCV）. This is also the first report of LCV in Spain that infects members of the family Leguminosae.
reference_name: First Report of Lettuce chlorosis virus Infecting Bean in Spain
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: The crops of main economic importance are lettuce and cucurbits. Many weed species are host to both the virus and its vector.
potential_eco_desc: Severe losses (20-70%) caused by LIYV were thought to be associated with unprecedented increases in the population of the whitefly vector Bemisia tabaci. The establishment of LIYV in Florida may result in heavy losses in lettuce, cucurbits and other susceptible crops (Brown et al., 1990).^p^pLIYV has a wide host range and causes economically significant losses in a number of important crop plants.
author: CPC2006

description: LIYV could be transported in infected plant material originating from the USA. The whitefly vector, Bemisia tabaci, is widespread in many regions.
author: CPC2006

management_info: General^p^pThe integration of scouting, cultural and insecticidal control tactics is the best approach to managing the disease until biological control and host-plant resistance can be developed for long term management. Five cultural practices recommended to supplement the use of insecticides in controlling whiteflies in Florida, USA, are: avoiding the establishment of new crops that are susceptible to whiteflies in or near fields or greenhouses infested with whiteflies; screening transplant production houses to exclude whiteflies; removing volunteer crops and weeds, which serve as whitefly hosts, from fields well in advance of the crops; scouting plants for whiteflies; and spraying and destroying crop residues after harvest (Brown et al., 1990).^p^pThe use of floating covers to protect young seedlings from the whitefly vector may be effective but results are unclear. While spun-bonded polyester as a floating cover to rows of squash seedlings was reported to be more successful than endosulfan in reducing whitefly numbers, in other trials, yields were said to be the same with or without screens, as screened crops suffered from poorer light conditions, thus offsetting any advantage given by keeping the whitefly off the crop.^p^pMore than 12 weed species have been identified as sources of the virus and its vectors, including bindweed (Ipomoea sp.), wild lettuce (Lactuca canadensis), sunflowers and ground cherry (Physalis heterophylla). Removal of these weeds should control B. tabaci and the virus. ^p^pHost-Plant Resistance^p^pResistance/tolerance to LIYV has been found in wild lettuce and efforts to transfer this trait to commercially acceptable varieties are underway (Brown et al., 1990).^p^pThe level of tolerance exhibited by 'Climax' and a few other lettuce cultivars will not prevent the occurrence of lettuce infectious yellows, but could ameliorate its effect on lettuce production.
author: CPC2006

description: LIYV通过甘薯粉虱，烟粉虱，而非种子或机械地方式传播。该病毒被认为以半持续方式传播，通过粉虱媒介在少于1小时内获得。随后在6小时内传播，且保持在昆虫内3－4天而不增值于媒介内。 LIYV is transmitted by the sweet potato whitefly, Bemisia tabaci, but not by seed or by mechanical means. The virus is considered to be transmitted in a semi-persistent manner being acquired in less than 1 hour by the whitefly vector. It is subsequently transmitted within 6 hours, and is retained in the insect for 3-4 days but does not multiply within the vector.
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc:
由LIYV引起的严重损失被认为与粉虱媒介烟粉虱种群空前的增加有关。在佛罗里达州LLIYV的建立可能导致莴苣，葫芦和其它的易受侵染的作物的巨大损失(Brown et al., 1990)。
LIYV有着广泛的寄主范围且造成大多数重要的作物植株的经济上的重大损失。 Severe losses (20-70%) caused by LIYV were thought to be associated with unprecedented increases in the population of the whitefly vector Bemisia tabaci. The establishment of LIYV in Florida may result in heavy losses in lettuce, cucurbits and other susceptible crops (Brown et al., 1990).
LIYV has a wide host range and causes economically significant losses in a number of important crop plants.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info: 为保护幼苗以免受粉虱媒介的侵袭的浮顶的使用可能是有效的但结果是不清楚的。当作为成排的南瓜苗的浮顶的纺粘聚酯被报道比降低粉虱数量的硫丹更成功时，在其它的实验中，据说产量与或不与筛选一样，随着筛选的作物遭受更差的光度条件，这样抵消由保持粉虱与作物的距离而产生的任何益处。 The use of floating covers to protect young seedlings from the whitefly vector may be effective but results are unclear. While spun-bonded polyester as a floating cover to rows of squash seedlings was reported to be more successful than endosulfan in reducing whitefly numbers, in other trials, yields were said to be the same with or without screens, as screened crops suffered from poorer light conditions, thus offsetting any advantage given by keeping the whitefly off the crop.   LIYV的抗性/耐性已被发现于野生的莴苣中且商业上可接受的品种的转移这个特性的成就是起步的(Brown et al., 1990)。 Resistance/tolerance to LIYV has been found in wild lettuce and efforts to transfer this trait to commercially acceptable varieties are underway (Brown et al., 1990). 对在美国佛罗里达州中控制粉虱杀虫剂的运用的补充有可取之处的五种栽培实践，是：避免在粉虱大批滋生的田间或温室或其附近里易受粉虱影响的新作物的建立；筛选移植生产房已排斥粉虱；消除自生作物和杂草，自生作物和杂草为粉虱寄主，来自田间也在作物之前；为粉虱搜索植株；和喷射及毁灭收获后的作物残余(Brown et al., 1990)。 Five cultural practices recommended to supplement the use of insecticides in controlling whiteflies in Florida, USA, are: avoiding the establishment of new crops that are susceptible to whiteflies in or near fields or greenhouses infested with whiteflies; screening transplant production houses to exclude whiteflies; removing volunteer crops and weeds, which serve as whitefly hosts, from fields well in advance of the crops; scouting plants for whiteflies; and spraying and destroying crop residues after harvest (Brown et al., 1990).
author: zhangjianjun

description: During spring 2016, virus-like symptoms including leaf mottle, distortion, chlorosis, reddening, and stunted plants were observed on strawberry plants in commercial fields in Fujian Province, China. Strawberry plants (n = 108) showing various virus-like symptoms were collected from eight regions of the province for further investigation. Based on sequences analysis indicated that the causal agent was Strawberry pallidosis-associated virus (SPaV). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of SPaV infecting strawberry in China.
reference_name: First Report of Strawberry pallidosis-associated virus on Strawberry in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: ToCV可侵染茄科、十字花科、夹竹桃科、藜科和菊科等多科植物。这是ToCV侵染黄瓜的首次发现。
description: 2017年9月在湖南省蔬菜研究所基地发现黄瓜Cucumis sativus表现疑似ToCV感染症状，同时在叶背面发现大量烟粉虱。采集症状明显的黄瓜叶片及烟粉虱并通过ToCV特异性引物进行鉴定，最后确认ToCV侵染黄瓜，这是ToCV侵染黄瓜的首次发现。  ToCV只能通过韧皮部侵染的方式，由媒介昆虫以半持久方式传播，其中以烟粉虱Bemisia tabaci的传播能力最为高效。
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

potential_eco_desc: Almost 100% of the plants in the surveyed fields showed symptoms.
description: In January and February 2017, symptoms of yellowing and leaf curling were observed in open-field Roma-type tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) plants in seven states (Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebby, Jigawa, Sokoto, and Zamfara) of northern Nigeria. Almost 100% of the plants in the surveyed fields showed symptoms and were also heavily infested with the whitefly (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) Bemisia tabaci. Leaf samples were collected from seven states. Based on molecular diagnostics confirming the presence of Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV). This is the first report of the presence of ToCV in Nigeria.  ToCV was an emergent whitefly-transmitted virus. The tomato plants in the surveyed fields were heavily infested with the whitefly (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) Bemisia tabaci.
reference_name: First Report of Tomato chlorosis virus Infecting Tomato in Nigeria
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: The infection of some solanaceous (tomato, pepper, eggplant) and cucurbit (pumpkin) crops with ToCV has been previously reported in China. Although ToCV can experimentally infect three leguminous plants: pea (Pisum sativum), dwarf French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris), and broad bean (Vicia faba), no natural leguminous host of ToCV has been reported. To our knowledge, this is the first report of cowpea as a natural host of ToCV.
potential_eco_desc: The disease incidence was around 87% for tomato plants and 5% for cowpea plants.
description: In the summers of 2014 and 2016, leaves of cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) plants exhibiting interveinal chlorotic yellowing, dark green veins, and curling were observed in greenhouses that were growing cowpeas and tomatoes in Liaocheng prefecture, Shandong Province, where natural infection of ToCV in tomato is widespread. Tomato plants (cultivar Oudun) with interveinal chlorotic yellowing symptoms and heavy whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) infestations were observed in the sampling sites. The disease incidence was around 87% for tomato plants and 5% for cowpea plants. The leaves of symptomatic cowpea and tomato plants were collected. Based on RT-PCR and transmission test via Bemisia tabaci confirming cowpea as a natural host of ToCV.  Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) was whitefly-transmitted crinivirus.
reference_name: Natural Occurrence of Tomato chlorosis virus in Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: ToCV has been detected in many plant families, such as Solanaceae, Asteraceae, and Chenopodiaceae. ToCV infection in Cucurbitaceae has been reported in Costa Rica, and this study is the first report of ToCV infecting pumpkin in China.
potential_eco_desc: Results showed the incidence of ToCV infection in pumpkin was 5.3% throughout the surveyed areas.
description: In August 2014, chlorotic spots were observed on pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata) leaves in fields near or around greenhouses containing tomato plants heavily infected with Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) in Wenshang County, Jining Prefecture, Shandong Province, China. Leaf samples were taken from symptomatic pumpkin plants. The occurrence of ToCV in pumpkin plants was verified and confirmed by RT-PCR and sequencing. This is the first report of ToCV infecting pumpkin in China.  Tomato chlorosis virus is a whitefly-transmitted virus. A large number of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) were observed at the sampling site near or around greenhouses containing tomato plants heavily infected with ToCV.
reference_name: Natural Occurrence of Tomato chlorosis virus in Pumpkin in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) was confirmed on tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) and Datura stramonium growing among/near tomato crops in Mpumalanga Province of South Africa, this is the first report of ToCV on D. stramonium in South Africa.
potential_eco_desc: Datura stramonium could be playing an important role in the epidemiology of ToCV on tomato as a virus reservoir in/near tomato fields as these annual shrubs are prevalent in South Africa.
description: Large populations of the weed Datura stramonium growing among/near tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) crops in Mpumalanga Province of South Africa exhibited severe interveinal leaf chlorosis. Similarly, these symptoms were prevalent on nearby field and tunnel grown tomato crops. In addition to interveinal chlorosis, bronzing, leaf rolling, and brittleness was also observed on older tomato leaves. The presence of Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) was confirmed using RT-PCR. To our knowledge, this is the first report of ToCV on D. stramonium in South Africa.  The abundance of whiteflies observed on the abaxial surface of the Datura stramonium and tomato leaves suggested the possibility of a virus reservoir and cross infection of tomato crops.
reference_name: Occurrence of Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) on Datura stramonium Near Tomato Crops (Solanum lycopersicum) in South Africa
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: ToCV hosts have been reported in 10 botanic families, including members of the Brassicaceae family. However, to our knowledge, this is the first report of ToCV infecting Raphanus spp. in South America and the first worldwide report of garden rocket as a ToCV host. Wild radish plants are weeds very often associated with tomatoes in subtropical climates due to their natural level of tolerance to herbicides commonly employed in this crop. Garden rocket is cultivated in family-based systems, which are quite diversified and include also tomatoes. In South America, ToCV has been detected so far only infecting tomatoes and other solanaceous crops and weeds. The identification of these Brassicaceae species as natural ToCV hosts can have epidemiological implications since they may serve as sources of inoculum to the tomato crop in which ToCV infection has become a major problem in the subtropical regions of South America.
description: Wild radish (Raphanus sativus L. and R. raphanistrum L.) and garden rocket [Eruca sativa (Mill) Thell] plants displaying interveinal yellowing in the lower leaves were found in Mauá da Serra (Paraná State, Brazil). The garden rocket field with symptomatic plants was in close vicinity to tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) fields with high frequency of plants displaying symptoms similar to that induced by the Crinivirus (familyClosteroviridae) species Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) and Tomato infectious chlorosis virus (TICV). Symptomatic wild radish plants were distributed throughout the tomato fields. Total RNA was extracted from the foliar tissue of garden rocket (isolate CR-190) and wild radish in order to examine crinivirus infection in these species. The pathogen was identified as Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) by RT-PCR and dot blot hybridization. However, to our knowledge, this is the first report of ToCV infecting Raphanus spp. in South America and the first worldwide report of garden rocket as a ToCV host.  Symptomatic wild radish plants were distributed throughout the tomato fields. All plants were heavily colonized by Bemisia tabaci biotype B (MEAM-1 species).
reference_name: Wild Radish (Raphanus spp.) and Garden Rocket (Eruca sativa) as New Brassicaceae Hosts of Tomato chlorosis virus in South America
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: This is the first formal report of S. melongena and S. aethiopicum as natural hosts of ToCV in the continent and the first worldwide report of scarlet eggplant as a crinivirus host.
description: Samples of the eggplant(Solanum melongena) cultivars ‘Napoli’ and ‘Ci?a’ with interveinal yellowing in the older leaves similar to that induced by criniviruses were collected in fields heavily colonized by Bemisia tabaci MEAM-1 species in Cangu?u-Rio Grande do Sul State in February 2013 (isolate named as CR-131) and Formosa-Goiás State in April 2015 (isolate CR-173). Scarlet eggplants(Solanum aethiopicum) ‘Comprido’ showing identical symptoms were also sampled in Venda Nova do Imigrante–Espírito Santo State in April 2013 (isolate CR-148), Bragan?a Paulista-S?o Paulo State in June 2013 (isolate CR-155), and Brasília–Federal District in June 2015 (isolate CR-193). The presence of Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) in these samples were confirmed by RT-PCR and transmission tests. In South America, ToCV has been detected so far on solanaceous crops and weeds. However, this is the first formal report of S. melongena and S. aethiopicum as natural hosts of ToCV in the continent and the first worldwide report of scarlet eggplant as a crinivirus host. The wide geographical distribution of these new ToCV hosts in Brazil may have direct epidemiological implications since they are very often cultivated side-by-side with tomatoes. Therefore, they may serve as sources of inoculum to the tomato crop in which ToCV infection has become a major problem throughout many producing regions in the Southern Cone of South America.  There was heavily colonized Bemisia tabaci MEAM-1 species in the eggplant and scarlet eggplants fields infected by Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV).
reference_name: First Report of Tomato chlorosis virus Infecting Eggplant and Scarlet Eggplant in Brazil
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Tomato chlorosis virus causes “yellow leaf disorder” in tomato plants, resulting in severe damage to production and also has been reported to infect some cultivars of pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) and tobacco (Nicotiana benthamiana Domin). This is the first report of ToCV infecting eggplants in China.
potential_eco_desc: The percentage of eggplant plants exhibiting symptoms was 80%.
description: In September 2014, yellowing and interveinal chlorosis was observed on the leaves of eggplants grown under greenhouse conditions in Haidian District, Beijing. Mature leaves showed more intense interveinal chlorosis than young leaves and the percentage of plants exhibiting symptoms was 80%. The samples were collected and identified, based on molecular diagnostics showed that the causal agent was Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of ToCV infecting eggplants in China.  A dense population of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) was observed in the growning eggplant greenhouse. In the test, adult B. tabaci whiteflies reared on virus-free eggplants were allowed for a 48-h virus acquisition access period (AAP) on source tomato plants infected with ToCV, followed by a 48-h inoculation access period (IAP) on eight healthy eggplant plants at two true leaf stage, using six adult B. tabaci per plant. Symptoms were reproduced in all tested plants after 5 weeks, and ToCV infection was confirmed via RT-PCR.
reference_name: First Report of Tomato chlorosis virus Infecting Eggplant (Solanum melongena) in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Solanum lycopersicum
description: During January 2014, symptoms of interveinal yellowing, bronzing, thickening, and downward rolling of lower leaves were observed in plastichouse- and open-field-grown tomato plants in Jordan Valley, Jordan. Leaf samples were collected and identified, based on molecular diagnostics showed that the causal agent was Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV). To our knowledge, this is the first evidence of the presence of ToCV on tomato in Jordan.  A large number of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) were also observed. The symptoms and the presence of whiteflies in the affected fields suggested a viral etiology.
reference_name: First Report of Tomato chlorosis virus Infecting Tomato Crops in Jordan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 蒜芥茄Solanum sisymbriifolium，少花龙葵Solanum americanum
description: Sticky nightshade (S. sisymbriifoliumLam.) and American nightshade (S. americanum Mill.) plants showing severe foliar interveinal yellowing similar to crinivirus-induced symptoms were found during surveys carried out from 2012 to 2014 in Salto, Uruguay. Leaf samples were collected and total RNA was extracted to verify if these weeds function as reservoirs of tomato criniviruses. The causal agent was identified as Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) by molecular diagnostics. To our knowledge, this is the first report of these solanaceous weeds as natural ToCV hosts in South America.  Sticky nightshade (S. sisymbriifoliumLam.) and American nightshade (S. americanum Mill.) plants were heavily colonized by Trialeurodes vaporariorum and  Bemisia tabaci biotype Q. The confirmation that weeds frequently found within tomato fields can be infected by ToCV will contribute to a better understanding of pathogen epidemiology as well as to establish more effective integrated disease management strategies.
reference_name: First Report of Solanum sisymbriifolium and S. americanum as Natural Weed Hosts of Tomato chlorosis virus (Genus Crinivirus) in South America
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Solanum lycopersicum
description: During January 2014, open field and greenhouse tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) crops in the peripheral areas of Riyadh region, Saudi Arabia, were surveyed. In all surveyed tomato crops, yellowing symptoms were observed on the lower leaves, possibly infected by a whitefly transmitted crinivirus such as Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) and/or Tomato infectious chlorosis virus (TICV). Dense population of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci G.) were present in all affected plants. Incidence of the yellowing disease varied between four greenhouses and three open field tomato crops, but in the majority of the tomato crops surveyed, symptoms typical of Begomovirus infection such as severe stunting, degeneration, upward cupping, distortion and interveinal yellowing of upper leaves, and flower abortion were also observed. Leaf samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Tomato chlorosis virus（ToCV）. To our knowledge, this is the first report of ToCV infecting tomato crops in Saudi Arabia.  Dense population of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci G.) were present in all affected tomato plants, possibly infected by a whitefly transmitted crinivirus. In the transmission tests, ToCV was detected to all tomato indicator plants which revealed yellowing symptoms 6 weeks post inoculation, whereas no transmission was obtained when non-viruliferous whitefly adults fed on two asymptomatic tomato leaves.
reference_name: First Report of Tomato chlorosis virus (ToCV) in Tomato Crops in Saudi Arabia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Solanum lycopersicum
description: A survey of viral diseases was carried out during 2012 to 2013 in two major tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) producing regions in Uruguay (Salto and Canelones). Lower leaves of fruit-bearing plants were observed displaying yellowing and interveinal chlorosis under greenhouse conditions. The symptoms were similar to those associated with magnesium deficiency. However, the chlorosis displayed a tendency to move up affecting medial and apical leaves and prevailed even after supplementary magnesium applications to the soil, indicating potential infection by either Tomato chlorosis virus(ToCV) or Tomato infectious chlorosis virus (TICV). Four leaf samples were collected from two sites in Canelones and 28 samples were collected from distinct commercial fields in Salto. The test demonstrated that the pathogen was ToCV. Incidence of symptomatic plants in tomato crops varied from 30 to 100%, even under low whitefly pressure.  Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci biotype Q and Trialeurodes vaporariorum) were present in all sampling sites.

remark: ToCV presents a significant risk of further spread in the EPPO region. management_info: Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pControl of ToCV is mainly dependent on the control of its whitefly vectors. Roguing of severely infested plants reduces whitefly populations. Tomato seedlings for transplanting should be kept free from infection. Eradication of isolated outbreaks in glasshouse-grown tomatoes can probably be achieved by destruction of affected hosts and of the vector(s). However, eradication is unlikely to be achieved for outbreaks in the field in southern Europe. Weed hosts may act as reservoirs for ToCV.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pThe vector Bemisia tabaci appears to develop resistance to all groups of insecticides. A rotation of insecticides that offer no cross resistance must therefore be used to control B. tabaci infestations. ^p^p^Biological Control^p^pThe biocontrol agent Encarsia formosa (parasitic wasp) is used to control Trialeurodes vaporariorum, but is less efficient against B. tabaci. Repeated introductions of larger numbers of E. formosa than B. tabaci are necessary if eradication is required. The predatory beetle Delphastus pusillus is very effective against B. tabaci (MAFF, 2000). ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pThere are no resistant tomato cultivars as no resistance to ToCV has yet been identified in tomato. No differences in the incidence of yellowing due to ToCV in fields containing different cultivars of tomato were observed in southern Spain (Navas-Castillo et al., 2000). ^p^p^Phytosanitary Measures^p^pToCV was added to the EPPO A2 action list in 2005, and endangered EPPO member countries are thus recommended to regulate it as a quarantine pest. At present, there are no specific measures against ToCV in Europe and in particular there are no restrictions on the movement of tomato seedlings from areas where the disease occurs. Possible measures would be equivalent to those proposed for Cucumber vein yellowing virus (CVYV; OEPP/EPPO, 2005b).

management_info: Carnation clones can be freed from the virus following common protocols used for eliminating carnation viruses. management_info:
麝香石竹无性系能在被用作清除麝香石竹病毒的普通的规程后不受该病毒侵染。这些基本是由结合顶端分生组织的热处理，接着是仔细的检查受感染植物苗的早期察觉和根除组成的。在实践上，来自麝香石竹斑驳病毒已通过治疗而根除的地方的麝香石竹材料，也能不受其他病毒的侵染，其中包括麝香石竹坏死斑点病毒(EPPO, 1991)。如此获得的植株必须在避免再感染的条件下繁殖。也可利用于麝香石竹的病毒消灭程序的普通信息由Walkey (1991)给出，并由Spiegel 和 Loebenstein (1995)对于观赏植物作出查阅。无病毒麝香石竹的生产的方案在一些国家使用，其中一个例子是由欧洲和地中海植物保护组织作出在欧联使用的鉴定方案(OEPP/EPPO, 1991)。
因为感染的麝香石竹是主要部分，如果健康植物的感染来源不是唯一的，那感染繁殖材料的小心的避免能很大地降低感染的危险。被鉴定无病毒商业麝香石竹插条的使用因此是非常可取的。
在苗圃中、在田间或在在遮蔽下种植的作物中，对于作物感染的存在，用杀虫剂防治蚜虫能降低病毒进一步传播的危险。 Carnation clones can be freed from the virus following common protocols used for eliminating carnation viruses. These basically consist of heat treatment combined with meristem-tip culture, followed by careful checks for early detection and elimination of infected plantlets. In practice, carnation material from which carnation mottle carmovirus has been eliminated by therapy, is also free from other viruses including carnation necrotic fleck closterovirus (EPPO, 1991). Plants so obtained must be propagated under conditions that avoid reinfection. General information on procedures for virus elimination applicable also to carnations is given in Walkey (1991) and reviewed, with regard to ornamentals, by Spiegel and Loebenstein (1995). Protocols for production of virus-free carnations are applied in several countries, and an example is the certification scheme prepared for the European Union by the European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (OEPP/EPPO, 1991).
Since infected carnations are the main, if not the only, source of infection for healthy plants, careful avoidance of infected propagation material greatly reduces the risk of infection. The use of certified virus-free commercial carnation cuttings is therefore highly advisable.
In the presence of infection, in nurseries, in the field or in crops grown under cover, control of aphids with insecticides can reduce the risk of further virus spread.

description:
病毒颗粒主要地在韧皮部组织中被发现，但也存在于表皮和薄壁组织中。它们主要受到表现症状组织所限制。该病毒在感染细胞当中引起特征性的球形或椭圆形庖囊（膜状体）。这些结构含有病毒颗粒(Cadhilac et al., 1975; Bar-Joseph et al., 1979, Brunt et al., 1997)。
该病毒通过蚜虫以半持久的方式传播。桃蚜（Myzus persicae）是唯一已知的实验媒介。该病毒在取食时间获得，范围从30分钟到24个小时，取食时间中的传播从30分钟到24小时；带病毒的蚜虫能保持侵染性达超过2天(Inouye, 1974; Smookler and Loebenstein, 1974; Poupet et al., 1975; Rana et al., 1977; Bar-Joseph et al., 1979)。然而，病毒的传播可能更多的由于受感染母株植物的营养繁殖而不是蚜虫的传播(Lommel et al., 1983b; Mokra et al., 1988)。该病毒不能通过植物间的接触而传播(Brunt et al., 1996)。 Virus particles are mostly found in phloem tissue but are also present in the epidermis and parenchyma. They are mainly confined to symptom-expressing tissues. The virus induces characteristic spherical or elliptical vesicles (membranous bodies) in infected cells. These structures contain virions (Cadhilac et al., 1975; Bar-Joseph et al., 1979, Brunt et al., 1997).
The virus is transmissible in the semi-persistent manner by aphids. The green peach aphid, Myzus persicae, is the only known experimental vector. The virus is acquired in feeding times ranging from 30 minutes to 24 hours and transmitted in feeding times from 30 minutes to 24 hours; viruliferous aphids retain infectivity for up to 2 days (Inouye, 1974; Smookler and Loebenstein, 1974; Poupet et al., 1975; Rana et al., 1977; Bar-Joseph et al., 1979). However, the spread of the virus is probably due more to vegetative propagation of infected mother plants than to aphid transmission (Lommel et al., 1983b; Mokra et al., 1988). The virus is not transmitted by contact between plants (Brunt et al., 1996).

potential_eco_desc: CTV is the most economically important virus pathogen of citrus worldwide. Millions of citrus trees on sour orange have been killed by CTV decline epidemics in Argentina, Brazil, Venezuela, Peru, Florida, California, Israel, Spain, and other locations. It is estimated that worldwide there are over 200 million trees on sour orange rootstock which are at risk to this disease. Sour orange is popular because it produces a vigorous tree with high quality fruit, is adaptable to many soil conditions including high lime and salt content and has tolerance to many other viruses, viroids and virus-like pathogens, and to Phytophthora. Use of tristeza-tolerant rootstocks often risks losses from other factors. In addition to decline, many severe CTV isolates cause stem pitting diseases of susceptible scions cultivars and these occur even when tolerant rootstocks are used. Stem pitting weakens trees and eventually reduces fruit size, quality and quantity (Marais et al., 1996). Grapefruit and lime are very sensitive to stem pitting. Sweet orange is more tolerant but can be severely affected by some isolates.

management_info: Control strategies for CTV differ according to the incidence and severity of the CTV isolates in a particular area and with the cultivars and rootstocks used. No single control strategy is applicable to all situations (Garnsey et al., 1996a; Lee et al., 1994).^p^p^Exclusion and Quarantine^p^pWhen CTV is absent or rare, preventive efforts should be made to avoid introduction of CTV into the growing area by forbidding importation of live citrus tissue. A practical and safe method to legally introduce cultivars from other regions and to free these of infection is necessary and reduces industry pressure to illegally introduce new cultivars or germplasm resources. Procedures for safe international movement of citrus germplasm have been devised (Frison and Taher, 1991).^p^p^Certification Programmes^p^pCareful control of propagating material remains the single most effective means to avoid rapid and extensive CTV epidemics. Most commercial citrus are clonally propagated by using buds from a selected scion cultivar to a nucellar seedling as a rootstock. Budwood is usually taken from a mature, vigorous tree and used directly or increased in a nursery block to produce thousands of buds from a single source. Thus, propagation of CTV-infected trees can be prevented by using virus-free scion trees protected from natural infection by isolation or use of insect-free screenhouses or by shoot tip grafting (Navarro, 1993). Rapid indexing tests are available to verify freedom from CTV infection.^p^p^Eradication and Suppression^p^pIf a few trees become infected in a CTV-free area and indigenous aphids are poor vectors, natural spread can be slowed appreciably by a vigilant eradication and suppression programme. However, an effective survey programme is essential and when CTV is detected, infected trees must be removed immediately and surveillance maintained (Garnsey et al., 1996a). Eradication is rarely effective once infections are well established, especially in the presence of favourable vector conditions.^p^p^Resistant/Tolerant Rootstocks^p^pNumerous rootstocks are tolerant or resistant to CTV decline and use of these is essential for economic production of citrus in many areas. Some examples are Cleopatra and Sunki mandarins, rough lemon, Rangpur lime, trifoliate orange, and trifoliate orange hybrids such as Troyer and Carrizo citranges (Poncirus trifoliata x Citrus sinensis) and Swingle citrumelo. CTV resistant/tolerant rootstocks are often susceptible to other problems such as citrus blight, viroids, nematodes or poor soil conditions. ^p^pTolerant Scions^p^pMost mandarins are generally tolerant of CTV, although some hybrids, such as some tangelos, are seriously affected by stem pitting. In most areas in Asia where CTV isolates are severe, mandarins are the principal varieties produced due, in part, to their tolerance to stem pitting. There are no CTV-tolerant limes although Persian limes are more tolerant than small acid limes. All grapefruits are susceptible to grapefruit stem-pitting isolates of CTV. Sweet oranges vary in susceptibility to sweet orange stem pitting, but none is truly tolerant. Pera orange, a major variety in Brazil, is very susceptible while Valencia is one of the more tolerant cultivars.^p^p^Cross Protection^p^pInfection with a mild isolate of CTV may protect a tree from becoming infected with, or showing symptoms of, a more virulent CTV strain (Gonsalves and Garnsey, 1989). This is a strategy for control of stem pitting in areas where severe isolates of CTV and Toxoptera citricidus are endemic. Cross protection is used for production of grapefruit in South Africa (van Vuuren et al., 1993) and Australia (Broadbent et al., 1991), and Pera sweet orange and Galego lime in Brazil (Muller and Costa, 1972; Costa and Muller, 1980). In these countries, protective isolates have been selected from vigorous trees that remained in areas destroyed by the disease and their protective capacity confirmed in controlled experiment

description:
CTV的自然传播主要通过感染芽木的繁殖和通过蚜虫传播。CTV不是种传的。来自感染植株的芽的新植株的繁殖是CTV长距离传播的原因，来自单一植株的广泛的芽的繁殖能迅速地增加接种体的中心。使用感染芽种植作新接穗品种的整顶嫁接的老柑桔是CTV在一些国家中传播的普遍方法。树木间的传播是通过蚜虫。
CTV是通过一些蚜虫品种半持久性地传播的(Bar-Joseph and Lee, 1989)。蚜虫媒介从感染树木上获得病毒，取食时间从5分钟到几个小时，然而，不能通过短暂的探针探查来获得病毒。获毒和取食时间的增加超过24小时，媒介传播效率的增加。没有潜伏的时期，该病毒不能在蚜虫中繁殖和传播。接种一个植物需要的时间与获毒的时间相同。蚜虫在感染植物取食后能保持毒性24-48个小时。经ELISA检测，许多在感染的柑桔树上取食的蚜虫品种能获得病毒(Cambra et al., 1981)，但只有少许品种能传播到新的植株中去。桔蚜（T. citricidus）是最有效的传播媒介，在它存在的地方，它通常是柑桔上最为大量的蚜虫(Yokomi et al., 1994)。包括严重茎痘的分离种的大多数CTV分离种能通过桔蚜（T. citricidus）有效地传播，但少量分离种的传播的效率较低。棉蚜（瓜或棉蚜）能有效地传播一些分离种，在桔蚜（T. citricidus）不存在的地方它是最重要的CTV传播媒介(Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984; Roistacher et al., 1984; Yokomi et al., 1989; Ballester-Olmos et al., 1993)。与桔蚜（T. citricidus）作对比，它有广泛的寄主范围，并只是有时移居到柑桔上。桔二叉蚜（Toxoptera aurantii）能传播一些CTV的分离种，但比褐桔蚜或瓜蚜的传播效率要低(Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984)。它也有一个广泛的寄主范围并有时向柑桔移居。绣线菊蚜（A. spiraecola (spirea aphid)） 在实验条件下是CTV的一个效率低的传播媒介，但在世界范围内的柑桔上非常地普遍，它也是非常地杂食的(Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984; Yokomi and Garnsey, 1987)。这些蚜虫，除了桔蚜（T. citricidus），都是分布在全世界范围内。一些其他的蚜虫已被显示能实验性地传播CTV，但不大可能是重要的。 Natural spread of CTV is primarily through propagation of infected budwood and by aphids. CTV is not seedborne. Propagation of new plants from buds from infected plants is responsible for long-distance spread of CTV and extensive bud propagation from a single plant can rapidly increase foci of inoculum. Topworking old citrus plantings to new scion varieties using infected buds has been a common means of CTV spread in some countries. Tree to tree spread is by aphids. 
CTV is semipersistently transmitted by several aphid species (Bar-Joseph and Lee, 1989). Aphid vectors acquire the virus from an infected tree with feeding times ranging from 5 minutes to hours, however, not by brief probes. The transmission efficiency of the vector increases as the acquisition and feeding times are increased up to 24 hours. There is no latent period, and the virus does not multiply or circulate in the aphid. The time required to inoculate a plant is the same as for acquisition. Aphids remain viruliferous for 24-48 hours after feeding on infected plants. Many aphid species that feed on an infected citrus tree can acquire CTV, as detected by ELISA (Cambra et al., 1981), but only a few species can transmit it to new plants. T. citricidus is the most efficient vector, and where it exists, is often the most abundant aphid on citrus (Yokomi et al., 1994). Most isolates of CTV, including severe stem-pitting isolates, are effectively vectored by T. citricidus, but a few isolates are vectored less efficiently. Aphis gossypii (melon or cotton aphid) can transmit some isolates efficiently and is the most important CTV vector in regions where T. citricidus is not present (Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984; Roistacher et al., 1984; Yokomi et al., 1989; Ballester-Olmos et al., 1993). In contrast to T. citricidus, it has a wide host range and only occasionally colonizes citrus. Toxoptera aurantii can transmit some CTV isolates but is less efficient than brown citrus aphid or melon aphid (Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984). It also has a wide host range and occasionally colonizes citrus. A. spiraecola (spirea aphid) is an inefficient vector of CTV under experimental conditions, but is very common on citrus worldwide and also is extremely polyphagous (Hermoso de Mendoza et al., 1984; Yokomi and Garnsey, 1987). These aphids, except T. citricidus, are distributed worldwide. Several other aphids have been shown to transmit CTV experimentally, but are not likely to be significant.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
当CTV不存在和很少出现的时候，应作出预防性的工作，通过禁止活的柑桔组织的进口来避免CTV传入到正在种植的区域当中。一种合法地从其他地区引入栽培植物以及远离侵染的实践和安全的方法是必需的，并能减少不法地引入新的栽培品种或种质资源的产业压力。柑桔的安全的国际间移动的程序已被作出(Frison and Taher, 1991)。
繁殖材料的小心的防治仍然是一个单一的最有效的避免迅速和广泛的CTV流行的方法。大多数商业柑桔是通过利用来自一个经挑选的接穗品种到核幼苗作为一个根砧木的芽来进行无性繁殖的。芽木通常被从成熟、健壮的树木中得到，并直接的使用或在苗床中增加来从单一的来源中产生数千个芽。因此，CTV感染树木的繁殖能通过使用隔离而防止自然侵染的无病毒接穗树木或无昆虫的筛选房的使用或通过枝尖嫁接来防止(Navarro, 1993)。迅速的鉴定测试可利用作检验是否受到CTV侵染。
如果少数树木在无CTV的地区受到感染以及本土的蚜虫是弱势的传播媒介的话，那自然传播能通过警惕性的根除和抑制程序来稍微地降低。然而，一种有效的测量程序是基本的，当CTV被检测到时，侵染的树木必需立刻移除和保持监测(Garnsey et al., 1996a)。一旦侵染很好地建立，特别在适合媒介的条件存在时，根除是很难有效的。
大量的根砧木对CTV衰退是有抗性和耐病性的，这些根砧木的使用是许多区域柑桔的经济生产所必需的。一些例子是Cleopatra 和Sunki 柑橘、粗柠檬、兰卜莱檬和枳杂交种，如Troyer 和Carrizo 枳橙(Poncirus trifoliata x Citrus sinensis) 和施文格枳柚。CTV抗性/耐病性根砧木通常对其他的问题敏感，如柑桔枯萎病、类病毒、现重或贫瘠的土壤条件。
大多数的桔一般对CTV有耐病性，虽然一些如桔柚的杂交种会受到茎痘的严重侵染。在亚洲大多数的CTV分离种严重发生的区域中，桔是主要的种植的品种，这部分地因为它们对茎痘的耐病性。没有对CTV有耐病性的来檬，虽然波斯来檬比普通的酸来檬更具耐病性。所有的柚子对CTV的柚子茎痘分离种敏感。甜橙在对甜橙茎痘的敏感性上有所不同，但没有一个具真正的耐病性。秘鲁橙（Pera orange）是一种巴西的主要品种，它是非常的敏感的，而Valencia是更具耐病性的品种之一。
一种轻微的CTV分离种的侵染可保护树木不受更具毒力的CTV株系的侵染或不显示更具毒力的CTV株系的的症状(Gonsalves and Garnsey, 1989)。这是在CTV严重分离种和大桔蚜（Toxoptera citricidus）是地方性病害的地方的一个防治茎痘的策略。交互保护在南非(van Vuuren et al., 1993)和澳大利亚(Broadbent et al., 1991)以及巴西的Pera甜橙和Galego来檬(M黮ler and Costa, 1972).上被用作柚子的生产。 When CTV is absent or rare, preventive efforts should be made to avoid introduction of CTV into the growing area by forbidding importation of live citrus tissue. A practical and safe method to legally introduce cultivars from other regions and to free these of infection is necessary and reduces industry pressure to illegally introduce new cultivars or germplasm resources. Procedures for safe international movement of citrus germplasm have been devised (Frison and Taher, 1991).
Careful control of propagating material remains the single most effective means to avoid rapid and extensive CTV epidemics. Most commercial citrus are clonally propagated by using buds from a selected scion cultivar to a nucellar seedling as a rootstock. Budwood is usually taken from a mature, vigorous tree and used directly or increased in a nursery block to produce thousands of buds from a single source. Thus, propagation of CTV-infected trees can be prevented by using virus-free scion trees protected from natural infection by isolation or use of insect-free screenhouses or by shoot tip grafting (Navarro, 1993). Rapid indexing tests are available to verify freedom from CTV infection.
If a few trees become infected in a CTV-free area and indigenous aphids are poor vectors, natural spread can be slowed appreciably by a vigilant eradication and suppression programme. However, an effective survey programme is essential and when CTV is detected, infected trees must be removed immediately and surveillance maintained (Garnsey et al., 1996a). Eradication is rarely effective once infections are well established, especially in the presence of favourable vector conditions.
Numerous rootstocks are tolerant or resistant to CTV decline and use of these is essential for economic production of citrus in many areas. Some examples are Cleopatra and Sunki mandarins, rough lemon, Rangpur lime, trifoliate orange, and trifoliate orange hybrids such as Troyer and Carrizo citranges (Poncirus trifoliata x Citrus sinensis) and Swingle citrumelo. CTV resistant/tolerant rootstocks are often susceptible to other problems such as citrus blight, viroids, nematodes or poor soil conditions. 
Most mandarins are generally tolerant of CTV, although some hybrids, such as some tangelos, are seriously affected by stem pitting. In most areas in Asia where CTV isolates are severe, mandarins are the principal varieties produced due, in part, to their tolerance to stem pitting. There are no CTV-tolerant limes although Persian limes are more tolerant than small acid limes. All grapefruits are susceptible to grapefruit stem-pitting isolates of CTV. description: The survey of a vineyard north of the Krasnodar region was conducted in September 2017. Twenty-six samples (one sample from each vine) with leaf curling, yellow or red leaves were collected from five table Vitis vinifera cultivars: Landish (five samples), Uybilei Novocherkasska (five samples), Kolobok (five samples), Livia (five samples), and Veles (six samples). Laboratory testing of the most important viruses (Grapevine virus A, Grapevine rupestris stem pitting-associated virus [GRSPaV], GLRaV-1, GLRaV-2, and GLRaV-3) was done by reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). As the result, two samples tested positive for GLRaV-3, three samples tested positive for GRSPaV, and four samples (～15% of total samples taken) of V. vinifera cultivar Livia tested positive for GLRaV-2 by PCR. No information was available on the presence of GLRaV-2 in Russia before we focused on GLRaV-2. This is the first report of GLRaV-2 in grapevines in Russia.  GLRaV-2 can be transmitted through grafting.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 2 in Russian Grapevines (Vitis vinifera)
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 葡萄Vitis spp.
description: Grapevine leafroll disease (GLD), caused by the grapevine leafroll-associated viruses (GLRaVs, family Closteroviridae) is an important disease in all grapevine-growing regions of the world. It negatively affects vine vigor, fruit yield, and grape quality (e.g., sugar accumulation). Currently, there is limited information on the presence of either GLRaV-2 (genus Closterovirus) or GLRaV-3 (genus Ampelovirus) in Texas state. During the 2012 season, symptomatic grapevines (cv. Lenoir and cv. Blanc du Bois) were sampled from one vineyard site in Richards, TX. Based on molecular detection showed that some samples tested positive for Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 2（GLRaV-2）and Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 3（GLRaV-3）. To our knowledge, this is the first report of GLRaV-2 and GLRaV-3 in the state of Texas.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine leafroll-associated virus-2 and -3 in Texas Vineyards
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 葡萄 grapevines
description: Grapevine leaf roll-associated viruses (GLRaVs) has been reported in the states of California, Michigan, Missouri, New York, Oregon, Washington, and Wisconsin of United States, but not in Ohio before 2012. During 2012, grapevines with typical leaf roll symptoms were reported by owners of several Ohio vineyards. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogens were GLRaV-2 and -3, This results report for the first time the detection of GLRaV-2 and -3 in Ohio.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine leaf roll-associated virus-2 and -3 in Ohio Vineyards

description: During the 2013 and 2014 growing season, the presence of sugar beet plants with symptoms of yellowing was sporadically observed in commercial fields located in eastern Croatia (i.e., Tovarnik, Bo?njaci, and Virovitica). In late July 2014, a significant number of sugar beet plants, located mainly on the field edges, with the aforementioned symptoms were noticed in experimental fields of various sugar beet cultivars located at the University of Zagreb, Faculty of Agriculture. The samples were collected and identified, based on ELISA and molecular diagnostics, Beet yellows virus (BYV) was determined to be the causal agent. To our knowledge, this is the first report of BYV in Croatia and its detrimental effect on actual sugar beet cultivars grown under Croatian environmental conditions.  Beet yellows virus are transmitted by several aphid species in a semipersistent manner.
reference_name: First Report of Beet yellows virus (BYV) on Sugar Beet in Croatia

potential_eco_desc: Introduction^p^pBeet yellows virus (BYV) is the type member of the genus Closterovirus. The members of this group are characterised as aphid-transmitted viruses with flexuous, filamentous particles. ^p^pAt least 121 species in 15 families are experimentally susceptible to BYV (Duffus, 1973; Peters, 1988) and most potential host species occur in the Amaranthaceae, Aizoaceae, Caryophyllaceae or Chenopodiaceae. The last family contains over half of the known hosts of BYV as well as the susceptible crop species (sugarbeet, fodder beet, beetroot, Swiss chard and spinach). By far the most important crop host is sugarbeet (Beta vulgaris ssp. vulgaris) which is primarily grown in temperate regions between 30° and 60°N in Europe, Asia, North America and Africa, with a small amount produced in South America. Annual beet sugar production is approximately 40 million tonnes which supplies about 37% of the world sucrose demand (Cooke and Scott, 1993). BYV is frequently found in association with beet mild yellowing virus (BMYV; genus Polerovirus) because they share Myzus persicae as their principal vector. These viruses are responsible for virus yellows disease which is one of the most important diseases of sugarbeet. The two viruses were not distinguished until 1958 (Russell, 1958) and therefore research before this date must be interpreted with caution.^p^pIn the field, BYV is maintained between seasons in a variety of reservoirs such as sugarbeet clamps, seed crops and groundkeepers as well as weed species such as Senecio vulgaris and Capsella bursa-pastoris (Costa et al., 1959). More recent work has suggested that weed hosts are of limited importance (Stevens et al., 1994). Alate aphids carry BYV from the overwintering host to the sugarbeet crop in spring, while apterous aphids and later alates spread the virus from the primary focus of infection within the crop (Hull, 1963). The aphid loses infectivity when it moults at ecdysis which, combined with the short retention time of the virus, means that the incidence of the disease is high adjacent to the virus source but decreases rapidly with distance. These characteristics frequently lead to the development of yellow patches in infected fields. BYV is transmitted semi-persistently by at least 22 aphid species; M. persicae is the principal vector (Watson et al., 1951) although Aphis fabae, Macrosiphum euphorbiae, Myzus ascalonicus and M. certus are also important. Brief aphid feeding does not spread semi-persistently transmitted viruses and there is no latent period during which the aphid is non-infective following acquisition. In the case of BYV, optimum acquisition occurs when aphids have fed for more than 12 hours on infected plants; transmission is optimised if infected aphids are allowed to feed for at least 6 hours on healthy plants (Russell, 1970). BYV is not seed-transmitted and is only spread mechanically with difficulty in vitro.^p^pThe first symptoms of BYV infection appear as a yellow patch at the point of infection that spreads to cover the whole leaf. Cytological studies of infected sugarbeet seedlings have shown that the virus is initially restricted to the phloem and parenchyma from which it spreads to adjacent mesophyll cells and eventually to the epidermal layer (Esau, 1960). Systemic movement of the virus follows the path of photosynthate transport in the phloem, thus the older leaves which, at the time of infection, are exporters of photosynthates do not become infected (van der Werf, 1989a). The virus is also moved much more slowly between cells via the plasmodesmata (Esau et al., 1967). In the most pathogenic strains, vein clearing or yellowing is followed by vein chlorosis and etching on the undersurface of leaves (Russell, 1970). As time progresses, the older leaves turn pale yellow, and reddish or brown necrotic spots often appear. Eventually the leaves turn bronze and become thickened and brittle. management_info: Control of `virus yellows', and of BYV as one of the viruses forming this complex, includes physical separation of beet root and seed crops, elimination of the overwintering sources of the virus inoculum between seasons, and control of the aphid vectors (Duffus et al., 1983). Seed treatment with imidacloprid gave the best control of aphid vectors (Myzus persicae) over aphicidal granules applied at drilling or aphicidal sprays (Dewar et al., 1996). BYV has no significant weed reservoirs of infection (Stevens et al., 1994); unlike BMYV and BWYV, it is transmitted semi-persistently, i.e. BYV is retained in aphids for a much shorter time, and the only sources of the virus are overwintered beet plants left in the field. Consequently, systematic use of the control measures described shifts the relative proportion of different viruses in the virus yellows complex. Indeed, in Europe the relative incidence of BYV in disease-affected sugarbeet decreased while the incidence of BMYV increased (Bjorling and Mollerstrom, 1974).

description: BYV是以半持久方式通过22种蚜虫传播的，其中包括豌豆蚜（Acyrthosiphon pisum）、A. primulae、茄无网蚜 （Acyrthosiphon solani [Aulacorthum solani]）、菟丝子蚜（Aphis cusutae）、蚕豆蚜（A. fabae）、棉蚜（A. gossypii）、鼠李马铃薯蚜（A. nasturtii）、接骨木蚜（A. sambuci）、藜蚜（Brachycolus atriplicis [Hayhurstia atriplicis]）、甘蓝蚜（Brevicoryne brassicae）、茴香明蚜（Hyadaphis foeniculi）、萝卜蚜（H. erysimi [Lipaphis erysimi]）、马铃薯长管蚜（Macrosiphum euphorbiae）、饰瘤蚜（Myzus ornatus）、紫堇瘤蚜（M. certus）、桃蚜（M. persicae）、M. persicae dyslycialis、冬葱瘤额蚜（M. ascalonicus）、假金鱼草瘤蚜（M. cymbalariae）、环球无网蚜（Neomyzus circumflexus [Aulacorthum circumflexum]）、和省沽油囊管蚜（Rhopalosiphoninus staphyleae） (cf. Duffus, 1973)。该病毒不能通过媒介的后代传播，而且在蚜虫蜕皮后不能在保持。BYV能通过机械传播虽然有困难，它不能通过种子传播。 BYV is transmitted semi-persistently by at least 22 species of aphid, including Acyrthosiphon pisum, A. primulae, Acyrthosiphon solani [Aulacorthum solani], Aphis cusutae, A. fabae, A. gossypii, A. nasturtii, A. sambuci, Brachycolus atriplicis [Hayhurstia atriplicis], Brevicoryne brassicae, Hyadaphis foeniculi, H. erysimi [Lipaphis erysimi], Macrosiphum euphorbiae, Myzus ornatus, M. certus, M. persicae, M. persicae dyslycialis, M. ascalonicus, M. cymbalariae, Neomyzus circumflexus [Aulacorthum circumflexum], and Rhopalosiphoninus staphyleae (cf. Duffus, 1973). The virus is not transmitted to the progeny of vectors, and is not retained in the aphid after moulting. BYV can be transmitted mechanically although with difficulty; it is not transmitted through seed.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info: 病害防治主要以该病害的蚜虫媒介为目标，主要通过化学手段如杀蚜虫剂喷雾（如氨基甲酸盐或拟除虫菊酯）或种子处理（如吡虫啉）来实现。 Disease controls are primarily aimed at the aphid vectors of the disease, principally by chemical means either as aphicidal sprays (for example, carbamates or pyrethroids) or seed treatments (for example, imidacloprid). 虽然没有特别的注意这方面，但已有BYV的抗性育种方案，这些导致新的品种如Maris Vanguar的引入。更最近的研究指导了表现院子病毒的基因材料的转基因甜菜的产生，例如，衣壳蛋白媒介抗性。 Although not a particular focus of attention, there have been breeding programmes to develop BYV resistance and these have led to the introduction of such cultivars as Maris Vanguard. More recent research has been directed into transgenic sugarbeet which express virus-derived genetic material, for example, coat protein mediated resistance. 栽培方法也被采用来减少BYV的侵染来源，例如，根作物和秋播的种子作物的物理隔离、储藏根的严格卫生以及清除收获后的病残体。 Cultural methods have also been adopted to reduce the sources of BYV infection, for example the physical separation of root crops and autumn-sown seed crops, rigorous hygiene of root clamps and removal of groundkeepers left after harvesting.

Duffus, 1973)。该病毒不能通过媒介的后代传播，而且在蚜虫蜕皮后不能在保持。BYV能通过机械传播虽然有困难，它不能通过种子传播。 BYV is transmitted semi-persistently by at least 22 species of aphid, including Acyrthosiphon pisum, A. primulae, Acyrthosiphon solani [Aulacorthum solani], Aphis cusutae, A. fabae, A. gossypii, A. nasturtii, A. sambuci, Brachycolus atriplicis [Hayhurstia atriplicis], Brevicoryne brassicae, Hyadaphis foeniculi, H. erysimi [Lipaphis erysimi], Macrosiphum euphorbiae, Myzus ornatus, M. certus, M. persicae, M. persicae dyslycialis, M. ascalonicus, M. cymbalariae, Neomyzus circumflexus [Aulacorthum circumflexum], and Rhopalosiphoninus staphyleae (cf. potential_eco_desc: BYV对甜菜生理有显著的影响，它严重地减少甜菜的生长和产量。这生长上的减少是由净光合作用以及被绿色叶片截取的分散组织的数量的减少而不是做工的叶片区域的减少而造成的(Hall and Loomis, 1972; de Koeijer and van der Werf, 1995; Clover et al., 1999a)。于是，没有证据证明感染植物的产量损失能通过在周围健康植物的田间的改进而补偿。 BYV also has marked effects on sugarbeet physiology and significantly reduces growth and yield. This reduction in growth is due to decreases in both net photosynthesis and the amount of radiation intercepted by green leaves (Hall and Loomis, 1972; de Koeijer and van der Werf, 1995; Clover et al., 1999a) rather than a decrease in total leaf area. Therefore, there is no evidence that the yield loss of infected plants is compensated for by improvements in the yield of surrounding healthy plants. 甜菜受BYV侵染的糖产量减少是由于储藏根重量的减少、储藏根糖浓度的减少和储藏根中汁液杂质的增加而造成的。 The reduction in sugar yield from BYV-infected sugarbeet results from a decrease in storage root weight, a reduction in storage root sugar concentration and an increase in juice impurities in the storage roots.

host_range: X. dispar is very polyphagous. It attacks many deciduous trees, probably all in its distribution range (Schvester, 1954; Balachowsky, 1963; Bright, 1968; Schedl, 1981; Wood, 1982; Wood and Bright, 1992; Pfeffer, 1995). Recently it was also found on Eucaly
potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pThe economic damage caused by X. dispar is not easy to estimate. The beetle preferentially attacks stressed trees. Such trees might often have a chance of recovery without beetle attack.^p^pIn several countries of Europe and North America, X. dispar is sporadically a serious pest of fruit trees such as apple, apricot, peach, nectarine, pear, cherry and plum, and of hazel (Mathers, 1940; Linsley and MacLeod, 1942; Vasseur and Schvester, 1948; Schvester, 1954; Balachowsky, 1963; Postner, 1974; Viggiani, 1979; Mani and Schwaller, 1983; Hesjedal and Edland, 1988; Schick and Thines, 1988; Juillard-Condat and Perrau, 1989;Mani et al., 1990, 1992; Natali et al., 1994; Schroder, 1996; Lagowska and Winiarska, 1997; Saruhan and Tuncer, 2001). Less often, damage occurs in vineyards (Ioakimov, 1925; Russ, 1966;Mani et al., 1990, 1992).  In the north-western states of America and western Canada, X. dispar is an important pest in chestnut (Castanea spp.) orchards (Bhagwandin, 1993; Kuhnholz et al., 2003).^p^pIn most cases, only single trees or groups of trees are attacked and destroyed, but sometimes whole new plantings of young trees are severely damaged. This happens mostly in the second year after planting, to young plants in poor condition (Mani and Schwaller, 1983; Mani et al., 1992; Morone and Scortichini, 1998). In such cases, important economic losses can occur.^p^pIn European forests, losses due to X. dispar are sometimes important. Severe attack has been observed in young plantations of maple and oaks (Postner, 1974), of chestnut (Schvester, 1954; Bud, 1972), Chinese chestnut (Tsankov and Ganchev, 1988) and in some stands of birch, poplar and alder (Balachowsky, 1963). In Austria, sometimes massive attacks up to 4 m high have been observed both on fungus-infected and healthy trees of sycamore maple, ash, oak and cherry (Perny, 1998).^p^p^Impact on biodiversityMudge et al. (2001) note that the species is more abundant than native species of Scolytidae at some sites in Oregon, USA, and suggest that the ecosystem may have been permanently altered as a result of its introduction. However, it is not clear whether it has significantly reduced the abundance of the native species, or is occupying host material that would otherwise have remained unexploited.^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>crop production; forestry production
description: In Europe, X. dispar is widespread from Spain to the Urals and from Italy to Finland (Stark, 1952; Balachowsky, 1963; Postner, 1974; Schedl, 1981; Pfeffer, 1995).^p^pIn Asia, it is known from the Middle East through Siberia to Sakhalin Island and north-eastern China. In Africa, it is present only in the North in Mediterranean countries (Stark, 1952; Balachowsky, 1963; Postner, 1974; Schedl, 1981; Pfeffer, 1995; Yanovskii, 1999).^p^pIn North America, where it was accidentally introduced from Europe before 1817 (Wood, 1977), X. dispar now occurs in eastern North America west to the Great Lakes states and south to South Carolina, western Canada, the Pacific Northwest states and California (Linsley and MacLeod, 1942; Bright 1968; Wood, 1982; Kovach and Gorsuch, 1985; Hobson and Bright, 1994). The distribution in North America suggest two introductions, one in the east and one in the west.

description: Natural Dispersal^p^pAdult females fly readily, and flight is one the main means of movement and dispersal to previously uninfected areas.^p^pVector Transmission^p^pIn addition to the ambrosia fungus Ambrosiella hartigii, the females of ambrosia beetles often also transfer other microorganisms (Schneider-Orelli, 1913; Francke-Grosmann, 1956; Zimmermann, 1973). Natali et al. (1994) found that X. dispar females, collected in three different biotopes of hazel growing in Italy, transferred 15 bacterial species, three yeasts and three fungi. Tiberi and Ragazzi (1998) (see also Sousa, 2002) found that X. dispar collected from oak trees (Quercus) in decline, transmitted the fungi Fusarium eumartii [Nectria haematococca), F. solani and Verticillium dahliae, and suggest that the beetles can exploit the trees more easily as a result of the activity of these fungi.Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bark: Adults; borne internally; visible to naked eye.^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches: Eggs, Larvae, Pupae, Adults; borne internally; visible under light microscope.^p - Wood: Eggs, Larvae, Pupae, Adults; borne internally; visible under light microscope.Plant parts not known to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bulbs/Tubers/Corms/Rhizomes^p - Fruits (inc. Pods)^p - Growing Medium Accompanying Plants^p - Flowers/Inflorescences/Cones/Calyx^p - Leaves^p - Seedlings/Micropropagated Plants^p - Roots^p - True Seeds (inc. Grain).

remark: A number of species of Xyleborus and related genera with similar habits to X. dispar have become important pests of tree crops, ornamental and native trees in tropical, subtropical and warm temperate zone areas where they have been introduced. The risk of introduction for X. dispar must be considered high, most probably in the branches of imported plants, although other pathways are also possible. Once established, such species are difficult to eradicate, and are likely to spread with the movement of infested plants, as well as by normal dispersal of the adults. X. dispar is included on the New Zealand Regulated Pest List, and Xyleborus spp. on the APHIS Regulated Pest List in the USA.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Cultural Control^p^pIn most areas, X. dispar is considered to be a secondary pest (Schneider-Orelli, 1913; Linsley and MacLeod, 1942; Balachowsky, 1963; Postner, 1974; Zoggeler, 1987; Schick and Thines, 1988; Juillard-Condat and Perrau, 1989; Keimer, 1990;Mani et al., 1990, 1992; Schroder, 1996; but compare Bhagwandin, 1993; Perny, 1998; Kuhnholz et al., 2003). Weakened trees are especially attractive to this beetle.^p^pFor this reason all cultural measures improving the health of trees must have priority. New plantations are at risk, particularly during the first and the second spring after planting. Avoid drying of roots before and after planting. Remove and destroy infected trees and branches immediately when attack is observed, or at the latest before the beetles of the new generation leave the galleries the following spring.^p^p^Biological Control^p^pNo method of biological control of X. dispar exists at present. The natural enemies listed do not provide effective control, and augmentation is not likely to produce much improvement. Canganella et al. (1994) suggest that the bacteria (Pseudomonas chlororaphis and Bacillus subtilis) they found on the insect and in the galleries may represent the starting point for future research.^p^p^Biotechnical ControlSchvester (1954) observed that attacked trees often produce an odour of alcohol. He explained this by the interruption or slowing down of plant sap transport and by the fermentation of this sap. Roling and Kearby (1975) showed that oak trees injected with ethanol attracted ambrosia beetles. Ethanol is apparently a good signal for a suitable host plant, especially for an ambrosia beetle cultivating a fungus in wet plant tissue (Klimetzek et al., 1986). All these observations may explain why many ambrosia beetles are attracted by alcohol traps.^p^pIn forests, window flight traps baited with ethanol are used, often in combination with pheromones, to estimate the flight periods and flight pattern of bark and ambrosia beetles (Moeck, 1970; Roling and Kearby, 1975; Annila, 1977; Schroeder and Lindelow, 1989; Markalas and Kalapanida, 1997).^p^pThe red wing trap, baited with ethanol (Rebell rosso), has been developed in Switzerland to attract X. dispar in orchards and vineyards. It has proved to be useful in monitoring and in control systems Mani et al., 1986, 1988, 1990, 1992). This method has become accepted in several countries (Zoggeler, 1987; Juillard-Condat and Perrau, 1989; Schroder, 1996; Lagowska and Winiarska, 1997). For other designs of trap using ethanol as a bait, see, for example, Bambara et al. (2002), Oliver and Mannion (2001) and Gregoire et al. (2003).^p^pFor monitoring, one or two traps per hectare of orchard or vineyard have to be placed in spring, when maximum temperatures rise above 17°C. In favourable weather conditions, the lure (250 ml 50% ethanol denatured with 1% toluene) has to be replaced every 2-3 days. When catches reach 20 beetles per trap per day, the risk of attack of some importance is indicated.^p^pFor control of X. dispar in an endangered orchard or vineyard, eight traps per hectare need to be placed. Such a control system will reduce the beetle population and the damage considerably.^p^pThe red wing trap attracts a variety of other insect species (especially Diptera), but only a few honey bees and known natural enemies of insect pests.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pChemical control of X. dispar is very difficult and expensive due to its protected breeding sites and its resistance to many insecticides. Therefore, sprays are only applied in exceptional cases. Compounds used previously, such as DDT, lindane and endosulfan (Schvester, 1954; Roediger, 1956; Mani and Schwaller, 1983; Juillard-Condat and Perrau, 1989), are no longer registered in most countries. host_range: 葡萄Vitis spp.
description: Grapevine leafroll disease (GLD), caused by the grapevine leafroll-associated viruses (GLRaVs, family Closteroviridae) is an important disease in all grapevine-growing regions of the world. It negatively affects vine vigor, fruit yield, and grape quality (e.g., sugar accumulation). Currently, there is limited information on the presence of either GLRaV-2 (genus Closterovirus) or GLRaV-3 (genus Ampelovirus) in Texas state. During the 2012 season, symptomatic grapevines (cv. Lenoir and cv. Blanc du Bois) were sampled from one vineyard site in Richards, TX. Based on molecular detection showed that some samples tested positive for Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 2（GLRaV-2）and Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 3（GLRaV-3）. To our knowledge, this is the first report of GLRaV-2 and GLRaV-3 in the state of Texas.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine leafroll-associated virus-2 and -3 in Texas Vineyards

During 2012, grapevines with typical leaf roll symptoms were reported by owners of several Ohio vineyards. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogens were GLRaV-2 and -3, This results report for the first time the detection of GLRaV-2 and -3 in Ohio.

potential_eco_desc: In Hawaii, MWP causes reduction in fruit yield by 30-55%. In Ghana, fruit yield loss due to MWP has been estimated to be at about US$248 per hectare.
description: To understand the association between viruses and MWP in Ghana, pineapple plant samples showing typical symptoms of MWP, including tip dieback, and descending curling, reddening, and wilting of the leaves which can prompt a complete breakdown of the plant, were collected during a survey of the Central region of Ghana in 2019. Pineapple mealybug wilt-associated virus-1 (PMWaV-1) and Pineapple mealybug wilt-associated virus-3 (PMWaV-3) were detected in the samples using RT-PCR and BLASTn analysis. This is the first report of the presence of the PMWaV-1 and PMWaV-3 in Ghanaian pineapple fields as well as in Africa.  MWP associated with one or a combination of Pineapple mealybug wilt-associated virus-1 (PMWaV-1), PMWaV-2, PMWaV-3, PMWaV-4 and/or PMWaV-5 that transmitted by two types of mealybug, the pink pineapple mealybug (Dysmicoccus brevipes) and the gray pineapple mealybug (D. neobrevipes).
reference_name: First report of Pineapple mealybug wilt-associated virus-1 and -3 in Ghanaian pineapple

potential_eco_desc: GLRaV-1 is one of five genetically distinct viruses that cause grapevine leafroll, one of the most damaging viral diseases of grapevines. GVA and GLRaV-1 have the potential to spread and cause damage to the United Kingdom’s developing grapevine industry.
description: In 2014, a phytosanitary screening program was initiated to establish the viral status of the approximately 100 grapevine (mainly Vitis vinifera) cultivars collected and grown by the Royal Horticultural Society in Wisley since the 1970s. Vines were inspected for symptoms every 2 weeks from June to September 2014. In July, interveinal reddening and downward rolling of leaf margins developed on mature leaves of the red-fruited cultivar Queen of Esther. Yellowing and downward rolling of leaf margins developed from August on mature leaves of the white-fruited cultivar Theresa. Both cultivars were observed to have swelling above the graft union. Samples of leaves and petioles were collected in August 2014, based serological and molecular methods confirmed the presence of Grapevine virus A (GVA)， Grapevine fleck virus(GFkV) and Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 1 (GLRaV-1). These are the first reports of GVA, GFkV, and GLRaV-1 in the United Kingdom and the first report of a virus infecting Vitis in the country.  Grapevine virus A (GVA), Grapevine fleck virus (GFkV) and Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 1(GLRaV-1), all three viruses are transmitted via vegetative propagation. GVA and GLRaV-1 are also transmitted by mealybugs (Pseudococcidae) and scale insects (Coccidae).

description: In a 2016 survey of viruses infecting diverse peach cultivars in Korea, we examined different peach cultivars grown in five orchards. Of the peach cultivars showing viral disease symptoms, Daeok (DO), a kind of common peach from an orchard in Wonju, Korea, showed discoloration, yellowishness, and spotting in the leaves, along with stem-pitting symptoms. Five DO plants were symptomatic. Based on RT-PCR confirming Plum bark necrosis stem pitting-associated virus(PBNSPaV)  and Nectarine stem pitting-associated virus (NSPaV) were presence in Symptomatic DO plants. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of NSPaV and PBNSPaV infecting a peach cultivar in Korea. Furthermore, the coinfection of Apple chlorotic leaf spot virus (ACLSV), Hop stunt viroid (HSVd), and Peach latent mosaic viroid (PLMVd) in five peach trees for the DO cultivar was confirmed by RT-PCR.
reference_name: First Report of Nectarine stem pitting-associated virus and Plum bark necrosis and stem pitting-associated virus Infecting a Peach Cultivar in Korea

host_range: Host range of PBNSPaV includes cultivated (almond, apricot, cherry, peach, and plum) and ornamental Prunus species. Graft inoculation experiments had already demonstrated that P. serrulata was a host of PBNSPaV, but to the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of PBNSPaV infecting this host.
description: During a recent survey (2015), five Japanese flowering cherry trees (Prunus serrulata Lindl.) samples were collected in Japan with diverse virus-like discolorations and spotting on their leaves but without obvious bark or stem symptoms, three of them collected in parks in Kyoto. Based on molecular diagnostics demonstrated that flowering cherry trees infected with Plum bark necrosis stem pitting-associated virus (PBNSPaV). This is the first report of PBNSPaV infecting Prunus serrulata or PBNSPaV presence in Japan. As is almost always the case, the trees analyzed were multiply infected with several other viruses, including Cherry virus A, Little cherry virus 2 and, for some of them, Little cherry virus 1 or Cherry necrotic rusty mottle virus, precluding any efforts to link the observed foliar symptoms with the presence of PBNSPaV.  No vector of PBNSPaV is currently known, but the virus is readily transmitted by grafting and other vegetative propagation methods.
reference_name: First Report of Plum bark necrosis stem pitting-associated virus Infecting Flowering Cherry in Japan

host_range: European plum (unknown cultivar) and Japanese plum cultivars —Akihime, Formosa, Hollywood, Gadam, and Yeonsik.
potential_eco_desc: Japanese plum cultivars were infected by PBNSPaV, they did not show any visible disease symptoms associated with PBNSPaV. Therefore, the risk caused by PBNSPaV in Japanese plum cultivars in Korea might be very low.
description: To identify viruses that infect plum trees in Korea, we collected leaf samples from a European plum (unknown cultivar) displaying necrosis and stem pitting in the bark of the trunk in September 2012. We further collected leaf samples from Japanese plum cultivars showing chlorotic leaf spots in May 2013. Based on molecular diagnostics confirmed Plum bark necrosis stem pitting-associated virus(PBNSPaV) infecting European plum trees and Japanese plum trees. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of PBNSPaV infecting plum trees in Korea.
reference_name: First Report of Plum bark necrosis stem pitting-associated virus Infecting Plum Trees in Korea

description: In autumn 2015, a survey was conducted in Ferzoul and Zahle areas of central Bekaa (Lebanon) in three vineyards of red fruited cultivars (Red Globe, Black Pearl, and Crimson) to investigate the presence of viruses that cause leafroll disease in vineyards, i.e., Grapevine leafroll-associated virus 1 (GLRaV-1), GLRaV 2, GLRaV-3, GLRaV-4, and GLRaV-7. To our knowledge, this is the first report of GLRaV-4 strain 6 in Lebanon.

host_range: PDV was first reported in Prunus domestica by Thomas and Hildebrand (1936). PDV infects all species of the genus Prunus (Gilmer et al., 1976). It is one of the most economically important viruses of stone fruit trees, especially peach, sweet and sour cher
author: CPC2006

description: Incidence^p^pPDV is seed transmitted, but levels of transmission differ in different Prunus species (Cation, 1949; Gilmer and Kamalsky, 1962; Megaded and Moore, 1967; Mink and Aichele, 1984; Kelly and Cameron, 1986; Digiaro and Savino, 1992; Johansen et al., 1994; Boari et al., 1998a) and varies according to conditions during pollination and seed ripening. Although infection levels in seed stocks of P. mahaleb ranged from 0 to 18%, the overall average infection of seedlings was 3% (Mink and Aichele, 1984). The virus has also been shown to occur in 20-70% of seedlings of P. cerasus and 11-56% of those of P. avium and P. cerasifera in the USA (Mink, 1982), and in 1.9-70% of seeds of four cherry cultivars in Germany (Schimanski and Meyer, 1991). Infection was detected in 59.4, 30.2 and 40%, respectively, of integuments, cotyledons and true leaves of P. mahaleb seedlings (Savino et al., 1997).^p ^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pInfected cherry seedlings grown from infected seeds are usually symptomless (Cation, 1949). The weight of seeds harvested from plum trees of cultivars Achermann and Grosse Grune Reneklode infected with both PDV and Prunus necrotic ringspot virus was increased, but was accompanied by a decrease in the number of seeds produced (Schimanski et al., 1991). Two PDV-infected mazzard cherry (P. avium) trees produced more sterile fruits than healthy trees; the viability of seed from infected trees was reduced, and those that survived were slow to germinate (Schimanski, 1990).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pPDV is also pollen-transmitted in sour cherry (George and Davidson, 1963), sweet cherry (Kelly and Cameron, 1986), almond (Digiaro and Savino, 1992) and other Prunus species (Gilmer, 1965; Barnard et al., 1973).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pPDV was detected by Triple Antibody Sandwich (TAS)-ELISA in the integuments and cotyledons of seeds (Casper, 1977; Boari et al., 1998b).
author: CPC2006

description: No animal vectors are known to be involved in the transmission of PDV. It has been reported that virus is present in the pollen of cherry, almond, plum and apricot (Digiaro, 1992b). Seed and pollen constitutes the main method of natural transmission (Cation, 1949; Cochran, 1950; Johnsen, 1984; Digiaro et al., 1992b; Mink, 1993) especially in Prunus avium, P. cerasus and P. mahaleb (Gilmer et al., 1976; Savino et al., 1997). PDV occurs in the pollen grains of almond (Kelley and Cameron, 1986; Digiaro 1992b), peach, plum and apricot, both exernally and internally; the attachment of virus particles to the pollen surface appears to be relatively stable; more than three washings or drastic treatment with a denaturating agent is needed to clean the pollen grains (Digiaro, 1992). PDV was also found in the ovules of plum and apricot, supporting the notion that the disease is seed transmitted.^p^pThrips-facilitated virus trasmission to cucumber seedlings was obtained with Frankliniella occidentalis and fresh pollen from sweet cherry. The rate of transmission varied greatly with the virus isolate used. No transmission was obtained when pollen from P. mahaleb was used (Greber, 1992).
author: CPC2006

remark: PDV is not a quarantine pathogen.

management_info: There are no chemicals that can be used for field control of virus diseases. PDV, like other ilarviruses, is pollen- and seedborne and it may therefore be impossible to control natural transmission (Dunez, 1998). The only possibility for controlling the disease is the use of virus-free or certified propagating material of cultivars and rootstocks that have been selected as being healthy (or obtained by meristem tip culture, thermotherapy and/or micrografting); material so produced should be tested for the absence of the virus, tested for trueness-to-type, and kept under conditions that preclude re-infection (Savino, 1998). Early detection using sensitive diagnostic methods is necessary to support this work.^p ^pMethods used to obtain virus-tested material from infected plants include thermotherapy, in vitro culture of meristem tips and micrografting (Barnard et al., 1973; Baumann et al., 1984; Deogratias et al., 1989; Saponari et al., 1999).
