potential_eco_desc: TSV is prevalent in south-eastern Brazil, and can limit yields of soyabeans in some years (Costa and Carvalho, 1961). Epidemics of soyabean bud blight, caused by TSV, were monitored in two soyabean cultivars sown on seven different dates in 1987-88 in Arapoti County, Parana. The highest final level of disease incidence was 60% in 1987 and 90% in 1988 (Almeida et al., 1994a). Brazilian bud blight is also a serious disease in the Santa Fe province of Argentina (Laguna et al., 1988). It occurs in the USA (Fagbenle and Ford, 1970; Kaiser et al., 1982; Sherwood and Jackson, 1985) but is of no economic significance on soyabeans because varieties are resistant and conditions are not conducive to the development of the problem.

description: Incidence^p^pSeveral reports have demonstrated recovery of the pathogen from soyabean seed coats, cotyledons and embryos of seed harvested from plants inoculated in the field. The pathogen was detected by inoculation of seed parts onto indicator plants (Fagbenle and Ford, 1970; Ghanekar and Schwenk, 1974; Ghanekar and Schwenk, 1980; Kaiser et al., 1982). Assays of embryos showed infection levels as high as 36% but virus was not recovered from pollen in this host, suggesting that it probably enters the developing seed directly from the mother plant (Ghanekar and Schwenk, 1974). ^p^pTSV is transmitted through seed of Phaseolus vulgaris (Kaiser et al., 1991), Chenopodium quinoa, Datura stramonium (Brunt et al., 1996), strawberry and tomato from 40 to 76% (Sdoodee and Teakle, 1988). TSV-BRL is seed transmitted in black raspberry and, in addition, this virus is transmitted to the plant pollinated (Converse and Lister, 1969; Jones and Mayo, 1975). ^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pTSV-infected soyabean seeds may have a diffuse brown stain (Truol et al., 1987; Laguna et al., 1988).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSeed^pTSV was transmitted through 90.6% soyabean seeds from experimentally inoculated plants grown in sterilized soil (Kaiser et al., 1982). In other work involving six soyabean cultivars inoculated with either a soyabean or tobacco strain of TSV, the soyabean strain was transmitted through 2.6 to 30.6% of seed harvested depending on the cultivar and the age at which plants were inoculated. The tobacco strain was not seed transmissible in soyabeans (Ghanekar and Schwenk, 1974). Truol et al. (1987) showed that seed transmission varied from 30 to 80% among several soyabean cultivars grown in Argentina. High levels of seed transmission of TSV have been reported for Phaseolus vulgaris (Kaiser et al., 1991) and strawberry (Johnstone et al., 1984).^p^pOther means^pSweet clover (Melilotus alba) was the primary overwintering host for the pathogen in eastern Washington, USA (Kaiser et al., 1982), and solanaceous weeds also may act as reservoirs of inoculum (Ford et al., 1989). Thrips are involved in the  transmission of TSV between hosts, but they have not been shown to be a vector in soyabeans (Kaiser et al., 1982; Sdoodee and Teakle, 1987). ^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pGrow-out^pSeeds were planted in moist vermiculite. Seedlings were then transferred to sterilized soil and 2-4 weeks later were indexed onto Chenopodium quinoa (Kaiser et al., 1982). In another report, seeds were grown in steam-sterilized soil and assayed for the virus by inoculation of cowpea indicator plants (Ghanekar and Schwenk, 1974).^p^pSerology^pAn ELISA kit for TSV detection in plant tissues is available from Agdia, 30380 County Rd. 6, Elkhart, Indiana 46514, USA. However, virus isolates can differ greatly antigenically and some may not react to heterologous antiserum (Jones and Mayo, 1975).

management_info: No control methods are known for TSV. The removal and destruction of infected perennial weeds, inoculum reservoirs around tobacco fields, is not always practicable or effective. Cultural practices, such as late sowing of bean crops, can decrease the spread of infection (Almeida et al., 1994a), as can controlling the Thrips vector (Almeida and Corso, 1991). Late sowing is often coincident with rainy periods, and rains drastically reduce Thrips populations. ^p^pThe use of healthy, certified seed could control virus spread on crops infected through seed, such as soyabean (Laguna and Ploper, 1995). Using ELISA, Spiegel et al. (1995) found that up to 30% of plantlets from infected strawberry plants multiplied and grown in vitro were TSV-free. ^p^pNo resistant variety of cultivated species is known at present, but a resistance gene has been found in Lycopersicon pimpinellifolium (Govorova, 1989). Plants transgenic for the TSV coat protein (CP) are resistant to infection, both escaping it and reducing necrotic lesions sites or, if infected, delaying the spread of systemic symptoms (Beachy, 1990). Plants expressing CP of the serologically unrelated Alfalfa mosaic virus were susceptible to TSV infection, showing that resistance arises only by inserting CP-RNA of homologous ilarvirus (Van Dun et al., 1988).

description: Spinach (Spinacia oleraceae - Amaranthaceae), referred to as Japanese spinach. A severe wilting and death in Japanese spinach (cv. Megaton, Takii Seeds) was observed in roughly 50% of plants in a commercial plantation at Colonia Tozan do Brasil, Campinas, SP (22°47′34″ S, 47°01′45″ W), in June 2014. Base on electron microscopy (TEM), PTA-ELISA, and RT-PCT indicated that the causal agent was an isolate of Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV). There are previous reports of wilting/blight in Japanese spinach, caused either by CMV in the U.S. or by Broad bean mottle virus (BBMV) in Europe, Asia, and the U.S. This is the first report of spinach (Spinacia oleracea) wilt caused by CMV in Brazil.
reference_name: First report of spinach (Spinacia oleracea) wilt caused by cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) in Brazil
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

description: From the spring of 2015 to the summer of 2016, castor bean (Ricinus communis) weeds in four commercial glasshouses around Yazd, Iran, had symptoms suggestive of those caused by CMV. In April 2016, the symptomatic leaves were sampled from castor bean plants growing around four glasshouses. The samples tested positive for the presence of CMV by ELISA and RT-PCR.  CMV infecting castor bean might indicate a potential role of castor bean in the epidemiology of CMV, by acting as a natural virus reservoir.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Infecting Ricinus communis in Iran
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: CMV infects more than 1,000 species in 85 families worldwide and causes appreciable losses in vegetables, ornamentals, and agricultural crops.
description: In summer of 2016, cherry leaves with mosaic or mottle symptom were collected from the cities of Yantai and Tai’an, Shandong Province. Based on molecular diagnostics confirming Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) was presence in the samples. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CMV naturally infecting cherry in Shandong Province of China.  CMV can be transmitted by more than 80 species of aphids as well as by mechanical inoculation and grafting.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Infecting Cherry (Prunus avium) in Shandong Province of China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: The existence of CMV on banana was reported from India. This is the first report of M. × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa as a natural host of CMV in Sikkim, northeast India.
potential_eco_desc: Symptoms of yellow mosaic disease was noticed on few Musa × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa plants.
description: Symptoms of yellow mosaic disease at Rorathang village (27.19° N, 88.61° E), east Sikkim, northeast India, were noticed on few Musa × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa plants in 2015. M. × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa plants exhibited yellow mosaic and interveinal chlorosis on leaves. Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) infection was confirmed by RT-PCR. This is the first report of M. × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa as a natural host of CMV in Sikkim, northeast India.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Infecting Musa × paradisiaca cv. Chini Champa in Sikkim, Northeast India
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Wisteria sinensis is an invasive, perennial plant with extreme longevity (can live for 50 years or more), it could act as a virus reservoir. This finding has potentially significant implications for the successful production of CMV susceptible crops.
description: Five samples of Wisteria sinensis showing virus-like symptoms including mosaic accompanied by leaf deformation and severe shoestring were collected in 2010 from the Porodin locality (Brani?evo District, Serbia). A large number of aphids were present on the leaves of naturally infected plants. The presence of Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) was confirmed using serologically and RT-PCR test. To our knowledge, this is the first report on the occurrence of CMV in W. sinensis worldwide.  A large number of aphids were present on the leaves of naturally infected plants.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Infecting Wisteria sinensis in Serbia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Iris tectorum
description: In July 2015, a large number of iris plants showing virus-like symptoms, such as streak mosaic, severe chlorosis, and eventually streak necrosis, were collected from the green belts and gardens of Tai’an, Shandong Province, China. PCR results showed that the samples were infected by Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV). The samples were also tested by indirect DAS-ELISA with the CMV specific antisera. The ELISA results confirmed the presence of CMV in the iris samples. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CMV on iris in China. More importantly, this is the first time to report CMV IB infected iris in the world.  CMV is easy to spread to other crops because it can be transmitted by aphid and the huge range of host plants it can infect.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus on Iris tectorum in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: This is the first report of a Cucumber mosaic virus  infection in Stevia rebaudiana.
description: In June 2010, 4-month-old stevia plants(Stevia rebaudiana) (<0.1%) in an experimental plot in Granada, Spain, showed dwarfing and mild mosaic. Symptomatic plants were tested positive in ELISA tests for Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV), all known to occur in the neighboring tobacco crops. Total RNA was extracted from an ELISA-positive sample, RT-PCR tests demonstrated that the causal agent was CMV. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a CMV infection in S. rebaudiana.
reference_name: Natural Infection of Stevia rebaudiana by Cucumber mosaic virus in Spain and by Sclerotium rolfsii in Greece
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Mazus reptans ‘Alba’ .
description: Mazus reptans N.E. Br (creeping mazus; Phrymaceae) is a perennial flowering groundcover plant. A plant of M. reptans‘Alba’ with mild mosaic symptoms was obtained from a Maryland nursery in 2010. Ligustrum necrotic ringspot virus (LNRV), Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) subgroup I and Alternanthera mosaic virus (AltMV) were detected from Mazus reptans ‘Alba’ plants by molecular diagnostics. To our knowledge, this is the first report of LNRV, CMV, or AltMV in M. reptans, a commonly grown groundcover plant. While CMV and AltMV are known to have wide host ranges, LNRV has previously been reported only from Ligustrum and Impatiens sp. The mild symptoms hinder symptom-based detection, and M. reptans may thus serve as a conduit for LNRV, CMV, and AltMV infection of other ornamentals.  Mazus reptans may thus serve as a conduit for LNRV, CMV, and AltMV infection of other ornamentals.
reference_name: First Detection of Ligustrum necrotic ringspot virus, Cucumber mosaic virus, and Alternanthera mosaic virus in Mazus reptans in the United States
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Calendula officinalis
potential_eco_desc: Disease incidence was estimated at 30%.
description: In July 2014, 10 samples of Calendula officinalis showing virus-like symptoms including chlorotic mottling and leaf deformation were collected in one field at ?ur?evo locality (South Ba?ka District, Serbia). Disease incidence was estimated at 30%. The diseased leaf samples were collected, based on immunological methods and molecular diagnostics,  Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) was determined to be the causal agent. To our knowledge, this is the first report of natural infection of C. officinalis with CMV in Serbia. As a new CMV host in Serbia, pot marigold represents a potential virus reservoir and additional source of inoculum to recognize the known host range and prevalence of CMV in weed hosts.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Causing Chlorotic Mottle on Pot Marigold (Calendula officinalis) in Serbia

host_range: 花生Arachis hypogaea
description: As part of a survey for viral infection of peanuts conducted in June 2013, some peanut leaf samples showing mosaic and yellowing mosaic symptoms were collected from the Chilgok-gun region, Gyeonsangbuk-do Province, South Korea. Based on molecular diagnostics, the sample was infected with CMV. This is the first report, to our knowledge, of a CMV infection of the peanut plant in South Korea.  CMV has a wide host range and is transmitted by aphids and insects as well as by seeds.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virusInfection of Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) in South Korea
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 顶花板凳果Pachysandra terminalis
description: Pachysandra terminalis (Japanese pachysandra, spurge) is widely used as a groundcover. In early 2012, Japanese pachysandra plants from Missouri, which originated in Pennsylvania, showed symptoms of light and dark green mosaic, leaf deformation, concentric ringspots, and stunting. The test demonstrated that the pachysandra had a mixed infection of AMV and a Type II isolate of CMV. This is the first report of pachysandra co-infected by AMV and CMV in the United States.  A potential source of AMV and CMV co-infection could occur when plants are grown near alfalfa fields (AMV infection by aphids) and undergo vegetative propagation (CMV infection by contaminated tools).
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Infection in Pachysandra in the United States
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 茄子Solanum melongena
potential_eco_desc: Symptomatic plants showed reduced growth, with nearly 50% fewer fruits than from healthy plants.
description: During a survey of family-owned farms in April of 2014 in Barisal region of Bangladesh, we observed a farmer's field (0.25 acres) of 3-month-old eggplants with nearly 90% of plants showing mild mosaic and mottling of leaves. Symptomatic plants showed reduced growth, with nearly 50% fewer fruits than from healthy plants. Symptomatic leaves tested positive for Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV). To our knowledge this is the first confirmed report of the occurrence of CMV subgroup 1B in eggplant in Bangladesh.  No aphids were observed on eggplants, it is likely that CMV was introduced into the farmer's field through seedlings raised from seed carrying the virus.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus from Eggplant (Solanum melongena) in Bangladesh
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Solanum lycopersicum（cv. Roma VF）
description: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) is a major economic crop consumed globally in fresh or processed forms. During a routine field survey of major tomato-producing areas of southwestern Nigeria in May/June 2013, tomato plants cv. Roma VF showing virus-like symptoms were observed in 10 farmers' fields with varying levels of incidence averaging ~27%. The test demonstrated that the pathogen was Cucumber mosaic virus subgroups IA and IB. Although Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV)  has been reported from tomato from several countries worldwide, to our knowledge, this is the first empirical evidence for the occurrence of CMV subgroups IA and IB in cultivated tomato in Nigeria.  Moderate to high aphid infestations were also observed in affected fields, and fruit production was significantly impacted based on visual observations.
reference_name: Occurrence of Cucumber mosaic virus Subgroups IA and IB Isolates in Tomatoes in Nigeria
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Tulipa sp.
description: In May 2013, during a survey to determine the presence of Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV, Cucumovirus, Bromoviridae)  on ornamentals in Serbia, virus-like symptoms, including the presence of bright streaks, stripe and distortion of leaves, and reduced growth and flower size, were observed in an open field tulip production in the Krnjaca locality (a district of Belgrade, Serbia). Disease incidence was estimated at 20%. Symptomatic tulip plants were collected and identified, the pathogen was CMV. To our knowledge, this is the first report on the occurrence of CMV causing mosaic on Tulipa sp. in Serbia.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus in Tulipa sp. in Serbia
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 千手兰Yucca aloifolia
potential_eco_desc: 个别侵染，未造成危害。
description: In 2013, during a survey for viruses in ornamental plants in the Campania region of southern Italy, symptoms consisting of bright chlorotic spots and ring spots 1 to 3 mm in diameter with some necrotic streaks were observed on leaves of two plants of Y. aloifolia growing in a nursery located in the Pignataro Maggiore municipality, Caserta Province.  The test demonstrated that the pathogen was Cucumber mosaic virus（subgroup IA）. To our knowledge, this is the first report of Cucumber mosaic virus infection of Y. aloifolia in the world.  Particular attention should be given to the presence of the virus in donor mother plants in order to avoid the dispersion of infected plants that could serve as sources for aphid transmission to other susceptible plant species.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Subgroup IA Isolate Infecting Yucca aloifolia in Italy

To our knowledge, this is the first report of CMV infection on periwinkle in Korea.

The samples were collected and identified， the causal agent was Cucumber mosaic virus. These results revealed the association of CMV（subgroup I） with symptomatic scotch bonnet leaf samples. Although CMV has been reported from scotch bonnet, this is the first report of its occurrence in Florida.
reference_name: First Report of Cucumber mosaic virus Associated with Capsicum chinense var. Scotch Bonnet in Florida

description: In 2013 to 2015, we collected 179 leaf samples of cereals (wheat, barley, oat, rye, triticale) showing the chlorotic mottle or stripes, yellowing, reddening, stunting, or other symptoms characteristic of possible viral infection from 46 different locations. Total RNA was extracted and BLASTn analysis was completed, Brome mosaic virus (BMV) was present in the samples of winter wheat (Triticum aestivum) cv. Ada. This is the first report of BMV occurrence in Estonia, found sporadically in two locations in 2013 to 2015.

Camus) plants, or the plants with mild leaf mosaic symptoms were collected in research plots of the Plant Breeding Station in Szelejewo (Poland, the Wielkopolska region) July of 2013. Base on DAS-ELISA, electron microscopic and molecular methods showed that the coinfection WSMV with Brome mosaic virus (BMV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of BMV in triticale in Poland and the first molecular identification of BMV/WSMV coinfection.  BMV is transmitted mainly by beetles (several species of Oulema and Phylotrella genera) and WSMV is transmitted by the wheat curl mite (Aceria tosichella (Keifer)). The natural incidence of mixed infection of WSMV and BMV in triticale crops raises the question of their interactions and the possibility of transmission by a common vector.

Based on molecular diagnostics showed that the causal agent was Cowpea chlorotic mottle virus (CCMV). To our knowledge, this is the first evidence of the presence of CCMV in yardlong bean, and the first report of CCMV transmission by chrysomelid beetle Ledesmodina auricollis. This is an important information for the Venezuelan cowpea’s market as CCMV-infected yardlong bean plants could act as virus sources for secondary spread by beetle vectors.  To our knowledge, this is the first report of CCMV transmission by chrysomelid beetle Ledesmodina auricollis. This is an important information for the Venezuelan cowpea’s market as CCMV-infected yardlong bean plants could act as virus sources for secondary spread by beetle vectors.

potential_eco_desc: T. portulacastrum is a widely distributed weed in cotton, sugarcane, pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum), sorghum, maize, direct-seeded rice, summer and rainy season pulses, oilseed crops, fodder crops, vegetables and horticultural crops in India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Holm et al. (1979) indicate T. portulacastrum to be a 'serious' weed in Australia, Ghana, India, Philippines and Thailand, and a 'principal' weed in Cambodia, Guyana and Nicaragua.^p^pIt appears in the early stages of crop development and causes yield reduction up to 50% or more in pulses, oilseed crops, vegetables, cereals, cotton, sugarcane and orchard crops (Bhan and Malik, 1986; Sidhu, 1991). At high population densities, it forms a strong mat and smothers crops.^p^pThe leaves and stems are sometimes eaten as a vegetable, but cause toxic effects in the form of diarrhoea. The plant is also used as fodder, but may cause poisoning in cattle (Chandra, 1976). Root decoction causes mild contraction of uterus, but larger doses induce abortion (Lewis, 1977). ^p^pT. portulacastrum is a suitable host for the red hairy caterpillar (Amsacta moorei) (Saini, 1993).
author: CPC2006

management_info: Introduction^p^pManual weeding 3 and 5 weeks after sowing maize, pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum) green gram (Vigna radiata) and cowpea is necessary to avoid crop loss due to early competition from T. portulacastrum. Green gram (Vigna radiata) is the least competitive of these crops (Balyan and Bhan, 1989). Application of nitrogenous fertilizers at high rates promotes competition in favour of pearl millet (Rathee et al., 1992). Mechanical weed control or inter-row cultivation is useful in cotton and sugarcane. ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pDue to early weed competition, herbicides applied at sowing are more effective. Effective herbicides include: trifluralin, pendimethalin, and fluchloralin for cotton, pulses, soyabean, potatoes, onion, okra, aubergine and garlic (Balyan and Bhan, 1989; Panwar et al., 1991; Nandal and Pandita, 1988; Phogat et al., 1991), atrazine in pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum), maize, sorghum and sugarcane (Kanwar et al., 1992; Balyan and Bhan, 1989; Balyan et al., 1993) fomesafen in green gram (Vigna radiata) (Balyan and Malik, 1989), 2,4-D in cereals (Tiwari and Jain, 1993), glyphosate as a post-emergence spray in orchards and chlorimuron in soyabean and rice (R.K. Malik, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, India, personal communication, 1966). In rice, Ampong-Nyarko and de Datta (1991) note resistance of T. portulacastrum to butachlor, piperophos and propanil, but susceptibility to pendimethalin and dimethametryn. Henty and Pritchard (1975) indicate susceptibility to ametryn, prometryn, diuron and fluometuron.^p^p^Integrated Weed Management^p^pPrevention^pT. portulacastrum should never be allowed to reach maturity. In heavily infested fields, it should be controlled at the seedling stage. Plants in the fruiting stage should not be cut and left in the field, as they retain enough viability for the fruit to mature and the seed to be dispersed. Farmyard manure should not be used before it is well rotted. ^p^pCultural Practices^pSoil solarization using polyethylene sheets for one month reduced T. portulacastrum germination by 90%, but such methods have limited scope in peasant farmers' fields (Kumar et al., 1993). Sowing of crops before the onset of rains helps in early crop establishment. Application of high levels of nitrogenous fertilizers immediately after the first hoeing promotes competition in favour of pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum) but not in favour of cotton (Rathee et al., 1992; Malik et al., 1990).^p^pIntegration of herbicides with intercultivation or hoeing^pThree hoeings, or fluchloralin supplemented with one intercultivation, provided better energy and monetary economics for controlling T. portulacastrum along with other weeds in cotton (Malik et al., 1990). Herbicides applied alone are not successful in rainy-season crops (Balyan and Bhan, 1989). Tank mixtures of herbicides or using them with surfactants in sugarcane (Webb and Feez, 1987), or using a post-emergence herbicide such as fomesafen at the two-leaf stage of T. portulacastrum in green gram (Vigna radiata) provided better control at reduced doses (Balyan and Malik, 1989).

potential_eco_desc: A. signatus is classified as a key pest of strawberries and a secondary pest of raspberries and dewberries in the eastern and north-eastern half of North America. In southern New Jersey, USA, at the beginning of the century (Headlee, 1918), A. signatus completely destroyed the strawberry crop over considerable areas and greatly reduced it in others. Reductions of 75% were not uncommon. Similar losses were reported by Schaefers (1978) in New York, USA, and Paradis (1979) in Quebec, Canada. However, losses are less obvious with vigorously growing cultivars producing 40 or more buds per plant (Gorham, 1936). Dorval (1938) noted that early strawberry cultivars were more susceptible than late cultivars.

remark: A. signatus is listed as an A1 quarantine pest by EPPO (OEPP/EPPO, 1989). In the EPPO region, A. signatus is likely to be at least as important a pest as A. rubi. Temperature development curves (Mailloux and Bostanian, 1993) show its base temperature to be 0°C, which is typical of northern European species, and the general pattern of its geographical distribution suggests that it could survive perfectly well in most of Europe. In the EPPO region it is potentially dangerous to strawberries and, in northern countries especially, also to Rubus species.^p^pPhytosanitary Measures^p^pIn general, the EPPO requirements on soil cover the risk of its presence in soil. EPPO recommends that all countries importing plants of Fragaria, Rosa, Rubus and Vaccinium from countries where A. signatus occurs, should require that the consignment has been grown in an area free from the pest and derive from plants found to be free from A. signatus during the growing season (OEPP/EPPO, 1990).

management_info: Once overwintering adults appear in a field, they rapidly build up to infestation levels. A predictive model indicates that the adults attain maximum abundance anywhere from 500 to 670 degree-days (DD) calculated from 1st April at temperatures above 0°C (Bostanian et al., 1999). Furthermore, certain cultivars (Seneca, Mohawk, Mira, Kent and Jewel), grown in perennial matted rows, are able to compensate for the removal of secondary flower buds (the preferred site of weevil attack) by increasing the berry weight of the remaining buds, as well as increasing the number of higher order buds to maturity. Other cultivars, (Northeaster and Honeoye) lack this compensatory ability (English-Loeb et al., 1999; Pritts et al. 1999). As a rule infestations begin in strawberry beds in their second year of production (3-year-old plants) and usually on the side of a field adjacent to wooded areas, shrubs, un-mowed weeds, etc. The infestation progresses about 12 m per year across the field (Kovach et al., 1999). ^p^pThe latest management strategy involves: planting the perimeter of the field with cultivars that can compensate the most for weevil injury; and treating the perimeter (12 m) of the field with an appropriate insecticide (chlorpyrifos, cypermethrin or lambda-cyhalothrin) when at least 500 DD above 0°C have been accumulated.

host_range: A. sarta is polyphagous in deciduous trees and may cause damage on many species of Ulmus, Populus, Salix, Platanus, Malus, Prunus, Pyrus, Juglans, Quercus, Betula, Fraxinus, Acer, Morus, Gleditsia, Robinia, Elaeagnus and many other hardwoods and fruit tre
potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pA. sarta is one of the most important pests of forest, ornamental and deciduous fruit trees in Central Asia Yagdyev, 1975, 1979, 1987; Yagdyev and Tashlieva, 1976; Ahmad et al., 1977; Sengupta and Sengupta, 1981; Krivosheina and Tokgaev, 1985; Maslov, 1988; Khudaibergenov and Khodzhaev, 1992; Vorontsov, 1995). It attacks both stressed and healthy trees of different ages. A number of generations can remain on the same tree for several consecutive years, eventually causing its death. Sometimes, young larvae encircle a tree feeding on the cambium, which leads to the rapid death of the tree. Young trees with a thin bark are most susceptible to the beetle and the presence of one to three larvae per tree may be enough to kill it.^p^pIt frequently occurs in avenues or parks in urbanized areas and has caused major damage to city plantations; for example, there are no more large trees in Tashauz city, Turkmenistan, because of A. sarta (Orlinskii et al., 1991). Serious damage is also observed in shelterbelts and in fruit (especially apple) orchards (Krivosheina, 1984; Vorontsov, 1995).^p^pA. sarta has killed large areas of mountain forests (Pavlovskii et al., 1955; Krivosheina, 1984; Orlinskii et al., 1991; Maslov, 1988; Vorontsov, 1995).^p^p^Environmental impact^pBecause it is a tree-killer, A. sarta is able to alter ecological relationships where its hardwood hosts are important component of ecosystems. The main environmental impact is caused in cities and towns in countries of Central Asia (Yagdyev, 1987; Orlinskii et al., 1991; Vorontsov, 1995). Usually, these cities are in hot and dry climatic regions, where large deciduous trees have a special environmental importance and are difficult to grow.^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>forestry production

Trees can also be treated with chemical and biological insecticides, and more resistant species and varieties may be planted to combat the pest.

potential_eco_desc: G. macleayi is a regularly-occurring pest of cereals sown in spring and summer, oilseed sunflower, and legumes in eastern Australia. Cotton, maize, and other crops are occasionally attacked. Seedling losses can be high enough to necessitate replanting over hundreds of hectares in some years. G. macleayi often co-exists with other soil-dwelling pests, and losses can seldom be attributed to one species.^p^pG. simplex is widespread in Africa south of the Sahara, and a wide variety of crops are affected. Economic losses have not been quantified, and this pest also occurs with other soil-dwelling pests (Mlambo, 1983). Severe thinning of stands of sunflower and maize seedlings are recorded in some years in South Africa (Drinkwater, 1992). In one report from India, Gonocephalum sp. damaged 5% of pods of groundnut in Andhra Pradesh (Reddy et al., 1992). Gonocephalum spp. appear to cause sporadic damage over most of their distribution.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Chemical Control^p^pSpecific control methods have not been developed for most Gonocephalum species. Exceptions are for G. macleayi in Australia, and G. simplex in southern Africa. Insecticide-treated baits are routinely applied against adults when planting summer crops in central Queensland, and seed is treated with insecticide when sowing in spring for control of G. macleayi (Robertson, 1993). Insecticide-treated baits have also been used in Zimbabwe (Mlambo, 1983) and South Africa (Drinkwater, 1992) to control G. simplex adults.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pPresswheels which firm the soil over the seed furrow at planting alleviate damage from false wireworms in Queensland, possibly due to faster emergence of seedlings (Radford and Allsopp, 1987).^p^pRetention of stubble on the surface when planting, using direct-drilling or no-till methods, reduced damage by G. macleayi, compared to stubble removal (Robertson and Kettle, 1994). This is due to G. macleayi adults switching to feed on newly planted seedlings when residues from the previous crop are burnt or ploughed into the soil before planting (Robertson, 1993).Robertson (1993) describes an IPM programme for G. macleayi in Australia, based on preplant checking of fallows for infestations, application of action thresholds for treatment, recording levels of crop residues retained on the soil surface at planting, previous crop type, and strategic baiting or seed treatment if needed.

management_info: Control measures for cucurbit crops have not been investigated in great detail, but measures involving increased frequency crop rotation (Park et al., 1996) and chemical control (Madaan and Grover, 1979; Peregrine and Ahmad, 1983; Maheshwari and Gupta, 1992; Oostendorp et al., 1996) using standard formulations such as benomyl, mancozeb, captafol and blitox [copper oxychloride], have ben used. It has been established that environmental conditions strongly affect disease incidence and spread, with high humidity being necessary for effective infection. This has been attributed to the role which the conidial matrix surrounding the spores plays in germination and appressorium formation (McRae and Stevens, 1990). As many cucurbit crops are grown in greenhouse conditions and with artificial irrigation, control of humidity is particularly important. There has been considerable experimentation into acquired systemic resistance of cucurbit crops to anthracnose disease (Huang and Kuc, 1995; Oostendorp et al., 1996). Resistant cultivars have been identified (Rego et al., 1995), and it has been postulated that anthracnose resistance is under single-gene control (Love and Rhodes, 1988).

host_range: A number of Liposcelis spp. are pests of stored grains and grain products. They have a wide range of hosts and habitats, infesting stored produce at all stages in the postharvest system, from farm storage to the kitchen of the final consumer. They are com
potential_eco_desc: Psocid damage commodities by direct feeding, resulting in the loss of weight and/or quality the infested commodities (McFarlene, 1982; Pike, 1994c). Liposcelis spp. are often found in large numbers infesting grains and grain products. Vast numbers of L. decolor and/or L. bostrychophila were found infesting bulk-stored grain in Australia (Rees, 1994). L. bostrychophila, have been reported to be a major cause of consumer complaints, and is becoming a problem in some sectors of the food industries in Denmark, Netherlands and the UK (Turner, 1987; Turner and Ali, 1996).^p^pThere is some evidence that liposcelids can illicit an allergic response in susceptible people (Rijckaert et al., 1981; Wyniger, 1985; Turner et al., 1996). Psocids also present a health risk to workers who may suffer allergic responses to them when they work in heavily infested stores. Even when not actually causing allergic responses their presence may result in labour disputes.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pGood store hygiene plays an important role in limiting infestation by Liposcelis spp. The removal of all spillage is important and cracks and crevices in store floors and walls should be filled (Leong and Ho, 1993). Infestation is also limited by the storage of good quality grain and, in the case of milled rice, a high milling degree (at least 95%) (Pike, 1994c; Kleih and Pike, 1995).^p^p^Physical Control^p^pLow temperatures and relative humidity effectively control L. bostrychophila (Turner and Maude-Roxby, 1988). This includes strategies such as proper drying of stored grains, dehumidification and cooling of storage environment. The critical equilibrium humidity (60%) together with the minimum temperature for development can be used to decide on storage conditions that prevent Liposcelis development. These conditions can be achieved by the use of dehumidification and/or refrigeration. However such interventions are not economically feasible in most situations.^p^p^Biological Control^p^pCertain predators are known e.g. Cheyletus sp. (Haines, 1991). However no attempts have been made to use them for biological control of psocids. Turner (1988) studied the use of entomopathogenic fungi and endotoxins of several cultivars of Bacillus thuringiensis. They were found inefficient in controlling L. bostrychophila.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pA number of synthetic pyrethroid insecticides, such as permethrin (Pranata et al., 1983), permethrin, deltamethrin, cypermethrin and allomethrin were found to be ineffective against Liposcelis (Turner et al., 1991). However, the performance of permethrin, in this laboratory experiment was increased by the use of a synergist, piperonyl butoxide. Fenitrothion and diazinon were found to be very effective in this laboratory experiment (Turner et al., 1991). Among the OP insecticides tested by Leong and Ho (1993), malathion, the commonly used OP was the least effective in the control of L. bostrychophila. The results on the efficacy of insecticides in the laboratory tests against Liposcelis may be different from the results of experiments done in stores. Hodges et al. (1992) found that store spraying in Indonesia, even with insecticides which in laboratory tests appear to be effective such as fenitrothion, does not significantly limit Liposcelis populations.^p^pIn Australia, grain is no longer routinely sprayed with insecticide on intake into storage. In many stores, surface applications have been discontinued. In others the chemicals used are fenitrothion, chlorpyriphos-methyl and azamethiphos. Of these residual insecticides, fenitrothion is the most effective, thus appears to be the chemical of choice for use against Liposcelis infestation in West Australia (Rees, 1994).^p^pThe most reliable method for controlling psocids is by fumigation. Methyl bromide and phosphine are the most commonly used fumigants for controlling storage insect pests. Methyl bromide is very effective against Liposcelis and will kill all stages of the pest at normal dosage rates (Pike, 1994b). However, the use of this fumigant will be gradually reduced and perhaps eventually phased out due to its negative effects on the ozone layer (Banks, 1994). Liposcelis are tolerant of phosphine, especially the eggs (Pike, 1994a; Rees 1994). However, fumigation with this gas should be effective if carried out according to instructions in a sealed structure (Rees, 1994), or by extending the fumigation period up to 10 days. This extended period of fumigation requires a high degree of gas-tightness to give an adequate phosphine concentration throughout this long exposure (Roesli et al., 1995). ^p^pAlternative fumigants which are effective against Liposcelis under laboratory conditions are carbonyl sulphide, carbon disulphide, ethyl formate and hydrogen cyanide (Rees, 1994).^p^pIn less-developed countries like Indonesia and India, insect pests in milled rice stores are usually controlled by using the

host_range: C. japonicus is polyphagous, attacking more than 100 plant species belonging to 40 genera placed in 24 families, including many crop and ornamental plants (Ben-Dov, 1993; Pellizzari and Camporese, 1994). The most common host plants are Citrus, persimmon,
potential_eco_desc: C. japonicus is a pest of ornamentals in towns and nurseries in northern and central Italy, but is not recorded as a pest in southern Italy (Pellizzari and Camporese, 1994). It is also a pest of ornamental plants in urban environments in Japan, a major local pest of jujube trees in Zhejiang, China (Luo et al., 1994), a pest of Citrus, mulberry, persimmon and fruit trees in western parts of the Republic of Georgia (Borchsenius, 1957) and a pest of Citrus and subtropical crops in southern Russia (Prokopenko and Mokrousova, 1981). In addition to the direct feeding damage, the honeydew secreted forms a substrate for the growth of black sooty moulds, which screen light from the leaves and impair gas exchange and photosynthesis. Sooty mould also reduces the market value of plants and produce.
author: CPC2006

remark: C. japonicus is often injurious to crops and ornamental plants, especially when introduced into new geographical areas. All life stages of the scale may be carried on consignments of plant material and produce.^p^pC. japonicus has a restricted distribution in southern Russia, where it is a pest of Citrus and subtropical crops (Prokopenko and Mokrousova, 1981). Quarantine measures apply to C. japonicus in Russia to prevent its spread.

management_info: Biological Control^p^pThe coccinelid, Chilocorus kuwanae, is among the most efficient predators of C. japonicus in Japan and China and its rearing, acclimatization and release is being investigated in Italy (Pellizzari and Camporese, 1994). Populations of the parasitoid, Microterys clauseni, were imported into Russia from Japan in 1982 and 1984 and released along the Black Sea coast. They acclimatized and were successful in controlling C. japonicus on trees with low essential oil content (Kravchenko, 1991).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pField experiments were conducted to investigate the efficacy of the insect growth regulators, fenoxycarb, buprofezin and the fenoxycarb derivatives NKI-43049 and NKI-35120 on C. japonicus on holly in Padova, Italy, in 1990. C. japonicus was most affected by NKI-35120 and none of the treated nymphs developed into adults (Darvas et al., 1994). Luo et al. (1994) carried out control trails in China using omethoate, monocrotophos, methamidophos and methidathion. Omethoate application to twigs and branches gave the best control of adult C. japonicus, resulting in 96% and 93% mortality, respectively. However, pesticide use may kill natural enemies of C. japonicus, so they should only be used where absolutely necessary.

host_range: Alfalfa mosaic virus(AMV) has also been shown to infect tamarillo (Solanum betaceum) cultivars in Ecuador, this is the first report of AMV in red pepper in Ecuador.
description: In a survey of viral diseases conducted in November 2014 in Imbabura Province, Ecuador, we observed severe yellow mosaic, chlorosis, and leaf deformation symptoms in approximately 70% of the red pepper (Capsicum annuum) plants. Leaves were collected from symptomatic plants of a commercial field located in the Antonio Ante Canton. Samples were analyzed to determine the presence of Alfalfa mosaic virus(AMV), which is known to infect pepper plants inducing similar symptoms and has also been shown to infect tamarillo (Solanum betaceum) cultivars in Ecuador. The presence of AMV was confirmed using RT-PCR. To our knowledge, this is the first report of AMV in red pepper in Ecuador. Further studies will make it possible to determine the geographic distribution and incidence of AMV in pepper fields and the routes through which this virus may have been introduced to Ecuador.
reference_name: First Report of Alfalfa mosaic virus in Red Pepper Plants in Ecuador

description: Pachysandra terminalis (Japanese pachysandra, spurge) is widely used as a groundcover. In early 2012, Japanese pachysandra plants from Missouri, which originated in Pennsylvania, showed symptoms of light and dark green mosaic, leaf deformation, concentric ringspots, and stunting. The test demonstrated that the pachysandra had a mixed infection of AMV and a Type II isolate of CMV. This is the first report of pachysandra co-infected by AMV and CMV in the United States.  A potential source of AMV and CMV co-infection could occur when plants are grown near alfalfa fields (AMV infection by aphids) and undergo vegetative propagation (CMV infection by contaminated tools).

This pattern was exemplified in a study during 1988-90, in which burr medic (Medicago polymorpha) cultivars were grown in field trials in which plots were sown with healthy seed or seed that carried varying levels of AMV. management_info: Introduction^p^pAs AMV is both seed and aphid transmitted, a range of control measures are required. Use of virus-free seed is an obvious initial requirement. Seed potatoes have been freed of virus by thermotherapy (Kaiser, 1984). Control of spread from overwintering hosts by spatial separation or by controlling the vector is the next major step. Insecticides are of limited use as the virus is transmitted non-persistently by aphids. However, combining insecticides with mineral oil (Reagan et al., 1979) or application of mulches between the rows (Kemp, 1978) gives sufficient insect control to limit infection. Various sources of resistance to AMV have been reported (see Hull, 1969) but these do not appear to be very effective. Transgenic protection has been reported (Fincham and Beachy, 1993; Brederode et al., 1995) and may be an effective future approach.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pTwo sorts of transgenic protection have been demonstrated. Expression of AMV coat protein (CP) gene in tobacco, tomato, pea, medicago and lucerne leads to a significant delay in symptoms and a reduction in virus accumulation (Fitchen and Beachy, 1993; Jayasena et al., 1997;Xu et al., 1998, 1999; Jayasena et al., 2001; Timmerman-Vaughan et al., 2001). Transformation of tobacco with mutated AMV replicase genes gave high levels of protection (Brederode et al., 1995). By analogy with other systems it is expected that CP-mediated protection would be effective against a wider range of strains than that afforded by the replicase.

种子侵染通常高于早期侵染发生(Nain et al., 1994a)。通过胚珠和花粉病毒都可以进入种子，而随花粉传播比胚珠传播更经常(Frosheiser, 1974; Hemmati and McLean, 1977)；然而，Bailiss和Offei (1990)认为胚珠传播比花粉传播经常。紫苜蓿种子中可探测的有侵染性的病毒的数量随发育过程快速减少，而抗原的数量处于低比率减少(Bailiss and Offei, 1990)。
收成的苜蓿属植物种子的AMV侵染减少达到76％在喷射杀虫剂的小块土地里(Jones and Ferris, 2000)。

亲本苜蓿植株的AMV侵染会导致种子萌芽减少30－50％(Hemmati and McLean, 1977)。
病原传播
在确定主要的来自通过蚜虫媒介的再传播的侵染中，种子传播通常被认为很重要。在1988－90年期间的研究中这模式被作为例子，有关的研究是将刺果苜蓿属植物(Medicago polymorpha)栽培种种植于那被播上健康种子或携带AMV的水平不同的种子的小块土地里，作为田间试验。种子被侵染的植株是后来的的病毒通过蚜虫传播的主要来源。AMV侵染的水平通常达到80-100%在播有感染种子的草皮中，无论它们有没有被收割，擦伤或落叶，大多数传播都发生在生长季节晚期。收成的种子的侵染常常比播种的种子少。然而，在自我再生的擦伤的草地里AMV传播较早且在收成的种子中的侵染比在种子再生之前多达10倍还多(Jones and Nicholas, 1992)。
可能影响AMV通过种子到一年生苜蓿属植物的传播的比率的因素和它的种子传播率的大小的遗传控制，在来自17棵早期开花的南苜蓿的增加物的植株中和在包括作为亲本的Medicago murex cv. Zodiac X增加物5320的杂交的后代中，调查研究。当植株长到6周大时被嫁接接种以确保成功且统一侵染。在种子传播率中排斥变种应归于病毒分离物或温度，且只有一种AMV分离物是有用的，并且植株被保存在统一的温度条件下。在刺果苜蓿中，重大的不同被发现于AMV通过种子传播到后代树苗的水平中的增加物之间，SA 8250有着种子传播的最高平均水平（52％）而SA 4188最低(3%)。病毒集聚和症状严重度都不影响被公认的种子传播率。然而，发现于这些增加物的种子传播率中的部分变异与它们的开花时期有关，种子传播率随着接种与开花之间的增加的时间间隔而增加。在来自（1）从杂交及相应的杂交的F2产生和（2）回交杂种后代的M. murex的个别嫁接接种植株的种子样本中，AMV通过种子传播到树苗的传播比率范围为0到77％且显示个不断的变异模式。同样，对于低的种子传播率情况是有越亲分离的根据的。这预示着在苜蓿属植物中AMV低种子传播率情况是数量上遗传且在多基因控制下。 对比下，当检查来自杂交及相应杂交的F2后代植株的荚果时，被公认的分离比显示来自亲本增加物5320的光滑的荚果特性是受单个的隐性基因控制的，就这名字sp被提议。基因sp的植株，或来自其它的亲本cv. Zodiac的多刺状的决定荚果的等位基因的存在，与AMV的低种子传播率没有关系。结论是关于种子传播低比率和种群育种方法的选择能被用来生产改良的刺果苜蓿和M. murex栽培种凭借对种传AMV好的抗性(Pathipanawat et al., 1997)。

Zodiac X增加物5320的杂交的后代中，调查研究。当植株长到6周大时被嫁接接种以确保成功且统一侵染。在种子传播率中排斥变种应归于病毒分离物或温度，且只有一种AMV分离物是有用的，并且植株被保存在统一的温度条件下。在刺果苜蓿中，重大的不同被发现于AMV通过种子传播到后代树苗的水平中的增加物之间，SA 8250有着种子传播的最高平均水平（52％）而SA 4188最低(3%)。病毒集聚和症状严重度都不影响被公认的种子传播率。然而，发现于这些增加物的种子传播率中的部分变异与它们的开花时期有关，种子传播率随着接种与开花之间的增加的时间间隔而增加。在来自（1）从杂交及相应的杂交的F2产生和（2）回交杂种后代的M. murex的个别嫁接接种植株的种子样本中，AMV通过种子传播到树苗的传播比率范围为0到77％且显示个不断的变异模式。同样，对于低的种子传播率情况是有越亲分离的根据的。这预示着在苜蓿属植物中AMV低种子传播率情况是数量上遗传且在多基因控制下。 对比下，当检查来自杂交及相应杂交的F2后代植株的荚果时，被公认的分离比显示来自亲本增加物5320的光滑的荚果特性是受单个的隐性基因控制的，就这名字sp被提议。基因sp的植株，或来自其它的亲本cv. Zodiac的多刺状的决定荚果的等位基因的存在，与AMV的低种子传播率没有关系。结论是关于种子传播低比率和种群育种方法的选择能被用来生产改良的刺果苜蓿和M. murex栽培种凭借对种传AMV好的抗性(Pathipanawat et al., 1997)。两篇报道指出在1.5% (Laguna et al., 1988)和3% (Iizuka et al., 1988)的大豆种子中AMV的传播。种子健康试验种子中AMV的存在能通过生物学的方法（来自试验下种子的苗木；接种的诊断的寄主如菜豆）(Bailiss and Offei, 1990)，血清学方法（例如，ELISA）(Bailiss and Offei, 1990)，分子方法（反转录/PCR）(Bariana et al., 1994)或斑点杂交法(Pesic and Hiruki, 1988)探测。 Incidence AMV is reported to be seedborne in several host species, including Solanum brevidens and S. tuberosum (Valkonen et al., 1992), Medicago spp. (Jones and Pathipanawat, 1989; Jones and Nicholas, 1992; McKirdy and Jones, 1995), Vicia faba (Fortass and Bos, 1991), lucerne (Walkey et al., 1990), soyabean (Laguna et al., 1988) and Trifolium alexandrinum (Mishra et al., 1980). High incidences of seedborne infection have been recorded, such as 20.2% in S. brevidens (Valkonen et al., 1992), 8-38% in soyabean (Almeida et al., 1982; Laguna et al., 1988) and >60% in Medicago laciniata, murex (Jones and Pathipanawat, 1989; McKirdy and Jones, 1995) and Trifolium alexandrinum (Mishra et al., 1980). Seed infection is usually higher the earlier infection occurs (Nain et al., 1994a). The virus enters the seed both through the ovule and in pollen, with pollen transmission being more frequent than ovule transmission (Frosheiser, 1974; Hemmati and McLean, 1977); however, Bailiss and Offei (1990) suggested that ovule transmission was more frequent than pollen transmission. The amount of infective virus detectable in lucerne seeds decreases rapidly with maturation whereas the amount of antigen decreases at a lower rate (Bailiss and Offei, 1990). AMV infection of medic seed harvested decreased by up to 76% in insecticide sprayed plots (Jones and Ferris, 2000). Effect on Seed Quality AMV infection of parent lucerne plants can result in a 30-50% reduction in seed germination (Hemmati and McLean, 1977). Pathogen Transmission Seed transmission is often regarded as being important in establishing primary infections from which there is secondary transmission by aphid vectors. description:
AMV通过包括Acyrthosiphon pisum 和桃蚜（Myzus persicae）的很多蚜虫种类以口针传播或非持续方式(Swenson, 1952)传播(Edwardson and Christie, 1997)。它越冬于多年生豆科植物且感染种子而且马铃薯块茎提供其它的病毒资源。这病毒的传播范围由Hull (1969)汇报。
AMV已被报道通过苜蓿作物相当快速的传播，且它的发病率五年来说约每年增加1.8倍。然而，从饲料作物的储藏的其它作物的传播，如大豆或豆荚到烟草，并非像预想的那么快(Hull，1969汇报)。
大量的AMV株系或变异体已被描述(Hull, 1969; Jaspars and Bos, 1980)。这些是通过特性如症状学，寄主范围，在烟草细胞里微粒聚集作用的形式，外壳蛋白的化学成分和花粉及种子传播而区别的。显然，AMV的大多数隔离种群各自有着一些不同(Burke, 1963)，因此，这样它不可能鉴别为一种比起它的更重要的株系。 AMV is transmitted in the stylet-borne or non-persistent manner (Swenson, 1952) by many species of aphids including Acyrthosiphon pisum and Myzus persicae (Edwardson and Christie, 1997). It overwinters in perennial legumes and infected seed and potato tubers provide other sources of virus. The field spread of the virus was reviewed by Hull (1969).
AMV has been reported to spread through lucerne crops quite rapidly with its incidence increasing about 1.8 times each year for 5 years. However, the spread from reservoirs of forage legumes into other crops, such as soyabeans or bean to tobacco, is not as rapid as might be expected (reviewed in Hull, 1969)
Numerous strains or variants of AMV have been described (Hull, 1969; Jaspars and Bos, 1980). These are distinguished by characters such as symptomatology, host range, particle aggregation forms in tobacco cells, chemical composition of coat protein and pollen and seed transmission. It appears that most isolates of AMV differ in some way from each other (Burke, 1963) and thus, it is not possible to identify one strain as more important than others.

In Thailand, an outbreak in 1979 covered a total area of 42,200 hectares and resulted in a rice yield loss of up to 70% (Chettanachit et al., 1990); another major outbreak in 1989-90 covered an area of 171,000 hectares (Anon., 1990).^p^pThe most severe losses are caused by infection at the seedling stage; however, it is difficult to separate the losses caused by Nilaparvata lugens feeding from those caused by the virus. author: CPC2006

management_info: The use of rice varieties that are resistant to the RRSV vector, Nilaparvata lugens (brown planthopper) is the most effective method of control. The use of rice varieties that were susceptible to N. lugens led to epidemics of RRSV in Thailand (Chansrisommai and Katanyukul, 1982). A number of brown-planthopper-resistant rice plants have been identified; introducing and maintaining this characteristic is one of the highest priorities in the rice breeding programme at IRRI, to prevent the build-up of the virus vector in rice crops. ^p^pThe use of insecticides, especially at the seedling stage prior to flooding, has also been successful at controlling RRSV (Palmer and Rao, 1981; Disthaporn et al., 1985).^p^pThe eradication of rice (the main food-plant of N. lugens) over large areas for several months by the avoidance of staggered cropping and the cultivation of secondary crops, especially in the dry season, has also been suggested.

The most severe losses are caused by infection at the seedling stage; however, it is difficult to separate the losses caused by Nilaparvata lugens feeding from those caused by the virus. In China, RRSV is currently regarded as either eradicated or present at an undetectable level.

description:
RRSV在它的植物寄主和媒介昆虫中复制。这种病毒褐飞虱、中期稻飞虱传播，没有其它媒介昆虫被认识。当中期稻飞虱取食于水稻植株时，通常在播种期，RRSV被接种入植株。而RRSV植物寄主范围局限在禾本科。
虽然病毒不经过卵期，但褐飞虱的其他所有形态都能当作媒介昆虫。褐飞虱幼虫是比成虫更有效的媒介昆虫。任何个体的带毒飞虱都可以间接传播。褐飞虱可以通过气流作远距离传播，飞虱通过这种方式从中国大陆携带RRSV病毒到日本是有根据的。 RRSV replicates in both its plant host and its insect vector. The virus is transmitted by the brown planthopper Nilaparvata lugens; no other insect vector is known. When N. lugens feeds on rice plants, usually at the seedling stage, RRSV is inoculated into the plants. The plant host range of RRSV is restricted to the Poaceae.
Although the virus is not passed through the egg, all other forms of the brown planthopper can act as vectors. Brown planthopper nymphs are more efficient vectors than adults. Any individual viruliferous planthopper gives intermittent transmission. Brown planthoppers can be carried long distances by jet streams; there is some evidence of RRSV being introduced into Japan by planthoppers that were carried in this way from mainland China.

potential_eco_desc: RBSDV causes yield losses in rice, wheat, barley and maize (Ou, 1985). Rice plants inoculated before the 11-leaf stage produce no grains (Shinkai, 1962). Plants that are infected survive until harvest, although they are severely stunted and produce excessive tillers (Shinkai, 1962; Ling, 1972). Yield loss is related to severity of stunting and gall formation (Choi et al., 1983; Kim et al., 1983). ^p^pSeveral agronomic characteristics, feed value, and mineral uptake of maize hybrids infected by RBSDV are affected (Lee et al., 1988a). For example, as stem length was reduced, the percentage of ear-bearing plants, grain weight, average ear weight and number of grains per ear were greatly reduced in the hybrids tested. Also, the crude protein and fibre in whole plants, as well as N, P, K and Mg in stems and sheaths, increased, but the nitrogen-free extract in the whole plant decreased. Isawa (1983) reported that infection of maize with RBSDV reduced total fresh and grain weights, but had no effect on chemical composition. There was a significant relationship between rice yield and seeding dates in respect of RBSDV infection (Bae and Kim, 1994). Severely infected plants have no panicles; if present, panicles are incompletely emerged. In some instances infected plants with fewer panicles and a lower proportion of ripe grains than uninfected plants can result in 60% yield loss (Young et al., 1987). The grains of the diseased plants are often marked with dark-brown blotches.
author: CPC2006

description: Vector Transmission^p^pRBSDV is transmitted by three species of small brown planthopper: Laodelphax striatellus (Kuribayashi and Shinkai, 1952), Unkanodes sapporonus and Ribautodelphax albifascia [Unkanodes albifascia] (Shinkai, 1966; 1967; Hirao, 1968). U. sapporonus feeds mostly on maize, wheat, barley and rice. Adults and young nymph stages of the insects were caught on diseased and healthy plants while feeding. Furthermore, Dong et al. (1999) has reported Nilaparvata lugens as a vector of RBSDV. These planthoppers vary in their ability to transmit the virus (Shinkai, 1962; 1966; 1967). L. striatellus preferred rice plants to maize for feeding, both in the field and in the cage, but the percentage of infected plants was much higher in maize than in rice (Lee and Kim, 1985). Li et al. (1979) reported that vectors acquired the virus from symptomless Poa annua. The incubation period in the insects is 7-12 days, sometimes up to 35 days (Shinkai, 1967). The maximum infection feeding time is 30 min, while the minimum is 5 min. About half of the individual insects can infect rice plants after feeding for 1-3 h (Shinkai, 1962). Overwintering adults and the first-generation larvae of L. striatellus play an important role in virus infection (Kajino, 1997). L. striatellus multiplies well in Festuca arundinacea, Lolium multiflorum and L. perenne (Choi et al., 1989). The density of overwintering insects in L. multiflorum was higher than that in rice, and the ratio of viruliferous vectors showed the same tendency. Most of the insects remain viruliferous for a long time. The latent period in rice plants is 14-24 days (Shinkai, 1962). The spread of this virus depends on the active, viruliferous insect transmitters among the species of the plant hoppers. ^p^pThe virus is not transmitted by mechanical means or through seed.Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - True Seeds (inc. Grain): borne externally; invisible.Plant parts not known to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bark^p - Bulbs/Tubers/Corms/Rhizomes^p - Fruits (inc. Pods)^p - Growing Medium Accompanying Plants^p - Flowers/Inflorescences/Cones/Calyx^p - Leaves^p - Seedlings/Micropropagated Plants^p - Roots^p - Stems (above Ground)/Shoots/Trunks/Branches^p - Wood.

remark: So far RBSDV is restricted to East Asia (China, Japan and Korea). It is not transmitted through seed or by mechanical means.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pAn overview of the control strategies for RBSDV and other rice viruses is given by Ishii (1973) and Abo and Sy (1998). To date, control of virus diseases has been based largely on the intensification and development of resistant materials through breeding (Shimura, 1977; Thottappilly, 1992). Thus rice varieties resistant to RBSDV are available (Ishii et al., 1966; Morinaka and Sakurai, 1967; 1968; Wang et al., 1999). Interspecific hybrids with resistance to RBSDV developed through embryo rescue are also available (Yang et al., 1991). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pThe use of insecticidal sprays has been practised for control of all the vectors of rice viruses (Abo and Sy, 1998). A great deal of work has been done in Japan on chemical control of plant hoppers (Ou, 1985; Uchida et al., 1985; Lee et al., 1989). The application of granular insecticides in the nursery trays before transplanting is used to control insects in the field (Hirao, 1991; Bae et al., 1992). Imidacloprid and Bichongin [composition unknown, see Wu and Wu, 1999] controlled the population of Laodelphax striatellus, and after 30 days no side effects were detected on the occurrence of natural predatory spiders (Wu and Wu, 1999). Imidacloprid controlled L. striatellus better than carbofuran and carbosulfan (Bae et al., 1992). In Korea, incorporation of carbofuran into the soil before sowing controlled populations of L. striatellus and reduced virus infection (Jin et al., 1988; Kim et al., 1988). ^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pControl of RBSDV also involves a combination of cultural practices, elimination of the virus source, and the exclusion of weeds and crops that increase vector density (Honda and Kameya-Iwaki, 1991). It specifically involves adjusting cropping patterns and suppression of the vector (small brown planthopper) population in the optimal period which should minimize spread of the disease (Zhou et al., 1998; Dong et al., 1999). It also involves early or optimum sowing dates to escape the peak period of insect attack (Lee and Lee, 1987; 1989; Lee et al., 1988c; 1989; Zhou et al., 1998). Plant spacing at 30 x 10 cm per rice plant, compared with a sparse planting of 30 x 15 cm, reduced infection of RBSDV in field tests (Jin and Yung, 1989). ^p^pIn China, Ruan et al. (1981) recommended synchronization of rice planting in large areas, use of resistant varieties, and insecticide application against the vector on barley and wheat at the seedling stage, and on rice at the early paddy stage.

potential_eco_desc: FDV causes a disease of considerable economic importance which has been responsible for major losses of sugarcane in both Fiji and Australia. In Fiji, the first record of the disease was in 1886 and by 1906 it was destroying thousands of acres of sugarcane (Daniels et al., 1971). Further outbreaks occurred in the 1950s after the planting of susceptible varieties, and even by the early 1960s there were fields with 10 per cent infection (Egan et al., 1989). Outbreaks still occur (Tamanikaiyaroi and Johnson, 1996). In Australia, a similar pattern of events has occurred. The disease, present before 1890, caused occasional serious problems, but was reduced to insignificance in the 1950s; however, after the planting of susceptible varieties major epidemics began in the mid-1960s and continued for a number of years, the peak being reached in 1979 when 70 million diseased plants were present in the Bundaburg district of south Queensland (Egan and Fraser, 1977). Overall, losses were estimated at 5-7%, with some farms and localities recording far higher losses (Egan and Ryan, 1986).

In vitro culture is the preferred method and is said to be used routinely (Glazmann et al., 1996). Specific protocols to eradicate FDV from infected germplasm by a combination of heat treatment and tissue culture of axillary buds have been devised (Wagih et al., 1995). However, as this method eradicated FDV from only 28 per cent of the cultures, as determined by DAS-ELISA, it is considered to need refinement, and indexing should be done using the more sensitive RT-PCR before routine application can be recommended (Smith, 1996).^p^pThe technical guidelines (Frison and Putter, 1993) list institutes recovering and maintaining healthy sugarcane germplasm as well as those acting as intermediate quarantine stations.^p^pOn a local level, internal quarantines have been used to limit the spread of FDV around diseased blocks (Turner, 1985).^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pInspection and roguing of diseased plants have been important elements in control in both Fiji and Australia. This method has most potential where disease levels are not excessive, and as long as highly susceptible varieties are not grown (Daniels et al., 1971; Egan, 1982). Roguing has to be done at regular intervals. Where disease incidence continues to increase irrespective of roguing practices, plough-out may be the only feasible method of control (Egan et al., 1989). It can slow the development of an epidemic, but is probably more useful in removing pockets of infection at the end of an epidemic (Ryan, 1988). Legislation has been enacted in Australia to empower authorities to order the mandatory plough-out of diseased cane.^p^pTime of planting has been shown to be important in south Queensland, with plantings in March/April developing more disease than those planted in August/September. This is explained by young plants, which are more susceptible to disease, being in the fields at the time of high leafhoppers numbers (Ryan, 1988).^p^pThe provision of disease-free planting material is also an essential part of FDV control strategies. Plots of clean 'seed' are established in mother blocks at a distance from FDV outbreak areas, with multiplication plots producing propagating stocks for commercial needs (Egan, 1980). ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pPlanting resistant varieties remains the principal method of controlling Fiji disease. Experience in Australia has shown that control of moderate and severe outbreaks can only be obtained by replacing susceptible varieties with those of greater resistance (Egan et al., 1989). The role of tolerant varieties in the resurgence of the disease in epidemics of the 1970s has been detailed by Egan (1976); and Ryan (1988) has commented on the effect of growing  the popular highly susceptible variety Nco310, resulting in higher levels of infection in more resistant varieties and in prolonging the epidemics. Resistance is highly heritable and mostly quantitative in character (Hogarth, 1977; Hogarth et al., 1993). For the most part, conventional techniques have been used to produce varieties with resistance to FDV, although in Fiji tissue culture has been shown to be a useful adjunct, with some somaclones showing greater FDV resistance than parental material (Krishnamurthi and Tlaskal, 1974). However, a poor correlation between the two methods has been noted in Queensland (Reimers et al., 1982), and screening is considered unsuitable for varieties in which resistance to this disease varies with age (Leverington et al., 1977). description:
FDV不是通过机械方法传播的，而是通过叶蝉扁角飞虱（Perkinsiella vastatrix ）(在菲律宾)；甘蔗扁角飞虱（P. saccharicida ）(在澳大利亚)；和P. vitiensis (在斐济)传播的。在巴布亚新几内亚的媒介还未鉴定出，但甘蔗扁角飞虱（P. saccharicida ） 和扁角飞虱（P. vastatrix ）都是存在的，P. lalokinensis被怀疑是媒介(Frison and Putter, 1993)。FDV的获得随着媒介虫龄增加而效率减少。甘蔗扁角飞虱（P. saccharicida ）的成虫可能不能获得病毒。卵巢传播被报道在甘蔗扁角飞虱（P. saccharicida ）中发生(Chang, 1977)，但还未被证实 (Ryan, 1988)。接种获得时间可能由于品种而有所不同，范围为6-24小时。所有的虫龄和成虫都能够传播，潜伏时间为12-24小时。有证据证明FDV在它的媒介当中复制(Francki and Grivell, 1972)。在寄主中的潜伏时期是大约15-28天，这由品种和植物的年龄所决定。在澳大利亚的P. saccharicida的研究已可以断定：昆虫是效率低的的FDV传播媒介，当在生病甘蔗上取食时，少于20％的个体受到感染，在这当中不到一半的个体能传播FDV(Francki et al., 1985)。查阅获毒和传播的研究见Egan et al. (1989)。
Chang and Ota (1978)发现：叶蝉在韧皮部组织取食所花的时间长度与品种对FDV的敏感性有关，非FDV叶蝉大多数在薄壁组织上取食，而以感病甘蔗为食的叶蝉则大多数在韧皮部上取食。
在澳大利亚昆士兰邦德堡地区的二十世纪70和80年代，FDV的病害流行研究给出了足够的信息来预报别的地方发生的病害流行的过程(Egan, 1982; Egan and Hall, 1983; Egan and Ryan, 1986)。甘蔗扁角飞虱（P. saccharicida ）媒介的生物学和种群动态在澳大利亚 (Bull, 1971, 1972, 1977a, 1981) 和斐济 (Husain et al., 1967)的研究已显示：作物的条件和品种影响着叶蝉的发生率。 FDV is not transmitted by mechanical means, but by the leafhoppers Perkinsiella vastatrix (in the Philippines); P. saccharicida (in Australia); and P. vitiensis (in Fiji). Vectors in Papua New Guinea have not been identified, but both P. saccharicida and P. vastatrix are present, and P. lalokinensis is suspected as a vector (Frison and Putter, 1993). Acquisition of FDV occurs with decreasing efficiency as the instars age. Adults of P. saccharicida may not acquire the virus. Transovarial transmission is reported in P. saccharicida (Chang, 1977), but has not been confirmed (Ryan, 1988). Inoculation access times may vary according to species from 6-24 hours. All instars and adults are capable of transmission with latent periods of 12-14 days. There is evidence that FDV multiplies in its vector (Francki and Grivell, 1972). The latent period in the host is about 15-28 days depending on the variety and the age of the plant. Studies in Australia with P. saccharicida have concluded that the insect is an inefficient vector of FDV, with less than 20% of individuals becoming infected when bred on diseased sugarcane and less than half of these transmitting FDV (Francki et al., 1985). For a review of acquisition and transmission studies see Egan et al. (1989). 
Chang and Ota (1978) found that the length of time the leafhoppers spent feeding on phloem tissues was correlated with the susceptibility of the variety to FDV and that non-FDV leafhoppers fed mostly on parenchyma, whereas those bred on diseased cane fed mostly on phloem.
Epidemiological studies of FDV in the Bundaberg districts of Queensland, Australia, in the 1970s and 1980s have given sufficient information to predict the course of epidemics occurring elsewhere (Egan, 1982; Egan and Hall, 1983; Egan and Ryan, 1986). Vector biology and population dynamics investigated for P. saccharicida in Australia (Bull, 1971, 1972, 1977a, 1981) and Fiji (Husain et al., 1967) have shown how the condition of the crop and variety influence the incidence of the leafhopper.

management_info: Introduction^p^pSeveral approaches to control have been investigated. A model has been proposed to forecast MRDV incidence in maize, based on density of viruliferous vectors at the time of sowing (Caciagli, 1986).^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitation Methods^p^pIn Italy, early sowing of maize is associated with increased MRDV incidence (Conti, 1984), possibly due to longer exposure of young maize plants to vectors. ^p^pControl of weeds which grow in late summer and autumn in maize fields should reduce MRDV infection in maize the next growing season (Conti, 1976b). ^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pDifferences in susceptibility to MRDV in different lines and hybrids of maize have long been noted (Grancini, 1962) and more recently experimentally confirmed (Caciagli et al., 1992; Presello, 1993), but commercial resistance or tolerance is still not available.  ^p^p^Chemical Control ^p^pPlanthoppers can be controlled by spraying grasses around fields in spring with insecticide, by seed treatment with imidachloprid, or by application to rows of aldicarb or carbofuran at sowing time (Conti, 1976b; Signoret et al., 2004). The insecticide should act rapidly; formulations with knockdown and repellent effects are more efficient in controlling MRDV incidence in maize (Antignus et al., 1987).

management_info:
越冬媒介和迁飞成虫能通过杀虫剂防治。种植行边缘和沿玉米田边的屏障行的杀虫剂喷雾已被建议使用来防治迁飞的成虫(Conti, 1976b)。迅速、系统的作用并有击倒和驱避作用的杀虫剂在控制MRDV在玉米中的发生率上是更为有效的(Antignus et al., 1987)。系统性杀虫剂(涕灭威,克百威)在播种时的应用在降低MRCV发生率和增加产量上都是有效的(March et al., 1985)。 Overwintering vectors and moving adults can be controlled by insecticides. Insecticide spraying of edge rows and of barrier rows along maize fields has been suggested for controlling moving adults (Conti, 1976b). The insecticide should act rapidly; formulations with knockdown and repellent effects are more efficient in controlling MRDV incidence in maize (Antignus et al., 1987). Treatments with systemic insecticide (aldicarb, carbofuran) applied at sowing have been effective in both reducing MRCV incidence and increasing yield (March et al., 1985). 玉米中不同的系和杂交种对MRDV敏感性的不同已经很早就被记录了(Grancini, 1962)，更最近得到实验性证明(Caciagli et al., 1992; Presello, 1993)，但商业抗性或耐病性仍没被应用。决定MRCV耐病性的基因的作用包括添加性和显性(Eyh閞abide, 1993E, Egidy et al., 1993)。鉴定基因标记与玉米MRCV抗性的连锁的研究正在进行中(Egidy et al., 1993)。 Differences in susceptibility to MRDV in different lines and hybrids of maize have long been noted (Grancini, 1962) and more recently experimentally confirmed (Caciagli et al., 1992; Presello, 1993), but commercial resistance or tolerance is still not available. Genetic effects determining tolerance to MRCV include additivity and dominance (Eyh閞abide, 1993E, Egidy et al., 1993). Studies are in progress to identify genetic markers linked to resistance to MRCV in maize (Egidy et al., 1993). 在意大利，玉米的提早播种与MRDV发生率的增加有关(Conti, 1984)，这可能由于幼嫩的玉米植物对于媒介有较长的曝光时间。在阿根廷，非常早的播种，于是只对媒介暴露较老的植物，这是首先被用作降低MRCV损害的实践方法之一(March, 1990)。
在夏末和秋天生长在玉米田间的野草的防治能减少MRDV在下一个生长季节的侵染(Conti, 1976b)。企图通过用预防性杀草剂防治野草来限制MRCV的发生率的尝试已经在某些情况下导致病害发生率的增加(March, 1990)。 In Italy, early sowing of maize is associated with increased MRDV incidence (Conti, 1984), possibly due to longer exposure of young maize plants to vectors. In Argentina, very early sowing, thus exposing only older plants to the vectors, has been one of the first practices used for reducing MRCV damage (March, 1990).
Control of weeds which grow in late summer and autumn in maize fields should reduce MRDV infection in maize the next growing season (Conti, 1976b). Attempts to limit MRCV incidence by controlling weeds in spring with pre-emergence herbicides have resulted, in some cases, in an increase of incidence of the disease (March, 1990).

potential_eco_desc: MRDV和MRCV只是玉米的重要病原物而已。有时候和在瑞典的有限区域中CTDV在燕麦和其他谷类上是重要的(Lindsten, 1974)。MRDV在意大利北部的侵染发生率每年都有不同（见生态学），范围从<1％到30％，有时还超过60％(Conti, 1983)。类似的情况在伊朗被报道(Conti, 1984)。在阿根廷，MRDV的发生率在1976/1977年和1981/1982年的夏天到达接近80％(March, 1990)。 MRDV and MRCV are significant pathogens of maize only. CTDV is important in oats and other cereals, occasionally and in limited areas of Sweden (Lindsten, 1974). The incidence of MRDV in northern Italy is variable from year to year (see Ecology), ranging from <1 to 30% and occasionally up to 60% (Conti, 1983). A similar situation has been reported in Iran (Conti, 1984). In Argentina, MRCV reached an incidence of nearly 80% in the summer of 1976/77 and 1981/82 (March, 1990). 由MRDV侵染引起的损失不只是受发病率的影响，它还受植物受到侵染时的阶段的影响。发病率和产量之间的负相关被March et al. (1985)所报道。从他们的数据，Lovisolo and Caciagli (1989)估计平均每1％的侵染每公顷损失80kg。在1981/1982年的生长季节中，在阿根廷里奥夸尔托地区，由MRCV侵染引起的生产的总损失被报道是360,000公顷中55,000公顷。 Losses due to MRDV infections vary not only with incidence, but with the stage at which plants become infected. A negative correlation between incidence and yield is reported by March et al. (1985). From their data, Lovisolo and Caciagli (1989) have estimated an average loss of 80 kg of grain per hectare per 1% infection. Total loss of production due to MRCV infections was reported in 55,000 hectares out of 360,000 in the growing season 1981/82 in the district of Rio Cuarto, Argentina (March, 1990).

description:
MRDV由飞虱以持久的方式传播，并能在媒介和寄主植物上复制。复制发生在植物和动物细胞的细胞质中，在一个电子密结构(病毒质)中，病毒粒子从那里传递到细胞质的其他地方(Milne and Lovisolo, 1977)。一个附属RNA的RNA聚合酶活动是病毒mRNA合成的原因，并在纯化的MRDV制剂中被检测出和描述出其特征(Marzach?et al., 1990)。
植物与病毒的关系：
在寄主植物中，MRDV只在韧皮部和贯穿整个植物的维管束系统韧皮部软组织中被发现。未成熟的病毒粒子在在细胞质内产生的病毒质（纤细纤维的密集质量的聚集）中出现，直径大约50nm (Maramorosch et al., 1969; Francki et al., 1985).。RNA合成和病毒粒子的聚集发生在这些结构上(Favali et al., 1974)。全部的直径70nm的病毒粒子之后在病毒质外面出现，或者是分散在巨大的晶体队列上，或者是被附在无支链的管上，直径为100nm(Milne and Lovisolo, 1977)。MRDV引起玉米根、茎、耳穗的鞘和叶片的韧皮部增生(Milne and Lovisolo, 1977)。新生细胞表现细胞壁增生，许多菌液酶液泡(Appiano and Lovisolo, 1979)，和改变的钾、硫、硅、钙的分布，和启发生长调节剂的不正常新陈代谢(Favali et al., 1980)。在受MRCV侵染的玉米的根部和叶片的赤霉素新陈代谢的改变已被报道(Tordable et al., 1993; Poloni et al., 1993)，与在叶片耳突上的吲哚乙酸的水平减少一起发生(Vigliocco et al., 1993)。韧皮部和韧皮部软组织的增生是造成叶脉(耳突)和耳穗的鞘的典型的长出物、以及玉米不定根的纵裂的原因。根部功能中的以及激素新陈代谢的改变可引起感染植物的矮缩和过度分蘖(Tordable et al., 1993)。MRDV侵染似乎能改变一些草，使它们更加适合作为飞虱媒介的寄主(Klein and Harpaz, 1969)。
该病毒不能通过汁液接种传播，虽然一些传播能通过针孔获得(Harpaz, 1972)。没有MADV的种子传播被报道，尽管经过许多尝试(Milne and Lovisolo, 1977)。
飞虱媒介：
灰飞虱（Laodelphax striatellus）在英国是MRDV和CTDV的主要的自然媒介，而Javesella pellucida是一个实验的媒介(Conti, 1984)。Dicranotropis hamata在瑞典是次要的CTDV媒介(Lindsten, 1974)。只有当病毒被注入昆虫体内，黑边黄脊飞虱（Toya propinqua）才能成为MRDV的媒介(Harpaz and Klein, 1969)；它作为MRDV在阿根廷的自然媒介的推断(Nome et al., 1981)是可疑的。Delphacodes kuscheli是MRDV的主要的自然媒介(Nome et al., 1981; March,1990; Ornaghi et al., 1993a)。稗飞虱（Sogatella vibix）在以色列被报道为MRDV的一个实验寄主，但它作为一个媒介的身份不是非常清楚的(Harpaz, 1972)。MRDV的以色列分离种由Ribautodelphax notabilis 传播(Izadpanah et al., 1983)。
媒介与病毒的关系：
在L. striatellus上，MRDV几乎在所有器官上发现，最丰富的是在含菌细胞块和脂肪体上。该病毒侵袭细胞质，首先产生病毒质，之后产生不成熟的颗粒，最后是成熟的病毒粒子和含有病毒的导管病毒质。最小的获毒进入时间是一天，在媒介体内的潜伏期在10到30天内变化，并与获毒时间的长度和温度有关，最小接种进入时间是5个小时(Conti, 1966)，但小于1个小时的有效的接种进入已经被报道(Harpaz, 1972)。在受到感染之后，飞虱保持侵染性整个生命周期(Conti, 1966)，而该病毒保持以一个指数速率繁殖(Caciagli and Casetta, 1986)。L. striatellus在实验条件的传播比率大约是50％。Ornaghi et al. (1993a)报道Delphacodes kuscheli在传播MRCV上的最大比率是8.3％。L. striatellus 中的经卵巢MRDV传播似乎需要再研究，因为有一份肯定（4％）报道(Harpaz and Klein, 1969)和一份由同等数量的昆虫获得的否定报道(Lindsten and Conti, 1977)。MRDV降低后代的发育能力，并可能也降低L. straitellus的生育能力，但不影响寿命(Harpaz, 1972)。 MRDV is transmitted by planthoppers in a persistent manner and replicates in both vector and plant hosts. Replication occurs in the cytoplasm of both plant and animal cells, in an electron-dense structure (viroplasm), from which virus particles pass to other parts of the cytoplasm (Milne and Lovisolo, 1977). An RNA-dependent RNA polymerase activity, which is responsible for the viral mRNA synthesis, has been detected and characterized in purified preparations of MRDV (Marzach?et al., 1990).
Plant-Virus Relationships
In plant hosts, MRDV is only found in the phloem and the phloem parenchyma throughout the vascular system of the plant. The viroplasms (aggregates of dense masses of fine fibrils) develop in the cytoplasm, and within these bodies immature virus particles appear, about 50 nm in diameter (Maramorosch et al., 1969; Francki et al., 1985). RNA synthesis and assembly of virus particles occur in these structures (Favali et al., 1974). Complete virions, 70 nm in diameter, are later found outside the viroplasm, either scattered, in large crystalline arrays, or enclosed in unbranched tubes, 100 nm in diameter (Milne and Lovisolo, 1977). MRDV induces hyperplasia of the phloem in roots, stems, sheaths of the ears, and leaves of maize plants (Milne and Lovisolo, 1977). The neoplastic cells show cell wall proliferation, many lysosomal vacuoles (Appiano and Lovisolo, 1979), and altered distributions of potassium, phosphorus, sulphur, silicon and calcium, suggestive of abnormal metabolism of growth regulators (Favali et al., 1980). Alterations in gibberellin metabolism in roots and leaves of maize infected by MRCV have been reported (Tordable et al., 1993; Poloni et al., 1993), together with decreased levels of indol-acetic acid in leaf enations (Vigliocco et al., 1993). potential_eco_desc: RDV causes considerable yield losses in Japan and China. In southern and central Japan, high local incidences of RDV were recorded from time to time during 1889-1930. After 1955, however, RDV incidence reached epidemic proportions first in southern Japan, then in central Japan (Kiritani, 1983). The incidence was especially high between 1967 and 1978 and declined thereafter. In Chejiang, China, the incidence was high between 1969 and 1973 (Li et al., 1979). ^p^pThe epidemic in Japan that started around 1955 was correlated with an increase in areas planted for early rice. This allowed the first generation of Nephotettix cincticeps to multiply and disperse the virus in rice, and raised vector density and the proportion of vectors that were infected with the virus. The spread of epidemics even farther after 1967 was attributed to several related factors: cropping of winter wheat and barley in paddy fields decreased steadily after 1955, which, in turn increased the number of rice fields left fallow during the winter season and so favoured the overwintering of N. cincticeps on grass weeds. Vector populations also developed pesticide tolerance (Nakasuji and Kiritani, 1977; Kiritani, 1983). The decrease in RDV incidence after 1979 was attributed to the application of insecticide to rice seedlings in nursery boxes for machine transplanters and to the ploughing of fallow rice fields in winter or early spring.^p^pIn rice double-cropping areas in China, the infected second- and third-generation adults of N. cincticeps disperse the virus from the first to the second crop of rice (Li et al., 1979; Cheng et al., 1980; Chinese Collaborative Research Group of Rice Virus Diseases, 1984). The incidence of RDV is generally higher in the second rice crop than in the first rice crop.^p^pPlants infected with RDV at the seedling stages do not produce grains. Plants infected at the vegetatively growing stage have a 50-80% reduction in yield whereas plants infected after heading have <30% reduction in yield (Nakasuji and Nomura, 1968; Ishii et al., 1970). Yield reduction is correlated with the percentage of infected panicles, but not with the percentage of infected hills due to compensation by non-infected plants in the same hills (Ishii and Yamaguchi, 1970). In Japan during 1955-1980, the area infected with RDV was reported to have been 200,000-300,000 ha (Kiritani, 1983). Losses in Japan due to RDV during that time reached 10,000 tons, annually (Iida, 1969).

In these countries, RDV is probably dispersed by Nephotettix nigropictus which occurs locally and rather sporadically.
