management_info: Introduction^p^pEpidemiological models of RDV have been developed in Japan (Muramatsu et al., 1968; Nakasuji and Kiritani, 1972; Nakasuji and Kiritani, 1985; Miyai et al., 1986) and China (Xie and Lin, 1980; Chen et al., 1981). ^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pPloughing of fallow rice fields during the winter reduces vector populations in the following planting season, resulting in a lower incidence of RDV (Kiritani, 1983). Roguing of diseased rice plants early in the growing season slows down dispersal of the disease in fields. A lower level of nitrogen application decreases both the vector population and the susceptibility of rice plants to RDV (Ishii et al., 1970). In Japan, normal or a reduced rate of planting of rice reduces RDV incidence. In China, planting of rice cultivars which have similar growth duration and planting of off-season crops after rice are recommended to control RDV (Cheng et al., 1980).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pThe application of insecticides when the overwintered or first-generation adults move to rice fields effectively reduces RDV incidence. Application of insecticides in the seedbed, in nursery boxes for machine transplanters or in newly transplanted fields is also effective. Applications of insecticides to reduce the vector population give effective control of second-generation leafhoppers when applied 15-30 days after transplanting (Miyahara and Hashizume, 1959). Insecticide applications to control third-generation leafhoppers give effective control in the second crop of rice (Li et al., 1979; Cheng et al., 1980). In Japan, insecticide applications to control RDV are widely practised, especially in areas where the incidence of RDV is high.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pRice cultivars which show resistance to RDV infection were identified in a number of Indica rice cultivars but were rare in Japonica cultivars (Ishii et al., 1969; Koide et al., 1972; Upahyay and Lapis, 1982). Resistance to RDV appeared to be due to resistance to the vector, Nephotettix cincticeps. Resistance from some Indica cultivars has been transferred to Japonica cultivars (Akemiya et al., 1984; Kaneda et al., 1985).

description: Since 2008, a disease showing virus-like symptoms such as dwarfism and leaf crinkling has frequently been observed in fields of Nicotiana tabacum L. in Zhucheng, Rizhao, and Jimo of Shandong Province, China, with a year-to-year incidence varying from 0.5 to 7.1%. To clarify the etiology of the disease, transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and PCR was performed, the results showed the pathogen was Milk vetch dwarf virus (MDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of a nanovirus infecting N. tabacum in natural field conditions and the first report of a nanovirus in Northern China. The nanovirus may pose a potential threat to tobacco cultivation in China.  The disease was transmitted by field-collected Myzus persicae (Sulzer), the transmission efficiency was low.

remark: All reports published so far suggest that FBNYV is not seed transmitted. Accordingly, seed movement between countries does not pose an increased risk of introduction into new locations. However, since the virus is persistently transmitted by aphids, it can be carried in windborne aphids for hundreds of kilometres.

management_info: Introduction^p^pDisease control is based on the results of ecological and epidemiological studies. Control measures may involve one or more of the approaches listed Makkouk et al., 1998b, c.^p^p^Reducing Sources of Infection^p^pA significant decrease in disease incidence can be expected if sources of infection are eliminated from within or near crops. In practice this is not easy, as it is impossible to eliminate all weed hosts of the virus. Prior to advocating such an approach for FBNYV control, more information on the relative importance of wild legumes as sources of FBNYV infection is needed.^p^pAnother measure to decrease disease incidence is to eliminate sources of infection within the crop. Roguing of FBNYV-infected faba bean eliminates or reduces primary infection foci. Reduction in virus incidence was noticed in a number of fields in Egypt when roguing was practised two or three times during the growing season (El-Hadi and Hilmi, personal communication). More experimentation on this aspect is still required to evaluate the economic impact of roguing on crop yield. On the other hand, a scattered distribution of initially infected plants throughout a crop was observed in some faba bean fields in Egypt, suggesting that FBNYV had been introduced from a distant source. This type of spread makes the reduction of infection through management of cropping patterns alone unlikely.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pClassical breeding^p^pIn preliminary screening for FBNYV resistance using 200 pure lines of faba bean, no resistance was found (K. Makkouk, ICARDA, unpublished data). Further work, however, is planned to screen the remaining available faba bean germplasm.^p^pWhen lentil lines were tested for FBNYV resistance under artificial field inoculation by viruliferous aphids, several lines such as ILL 213, 291, 6198, 6193 and 6245 were found to be highly resistant (Mouhanna et al, 1994b). Resistance was expressed by low virus incidence and extremely low (less than 5%) yield loss. These results were obtained in a single environment and require confirmation. Such preliminary data suggest that lentil genotypes vary widely in their reaction to FBNYV infection as compared to faba bean lines.^p^pNovel approaches for virus resistance^p^pFaba bean and FBNYV appear to offer a promising model for assessing the potential of pathogen-derived resistance to a DNA virus in faba bean by using various FBNYV genes. Since four potential Rep genes of FBNYV have been identified, and certain functions (e.g., capsid protein and cell-to-cell spread) have been definitely or tentatively assigned to some of the non-Rep genes of FBNYV Katul et al., 1995, 1997, 1998), several viral genes appear to be suitable candidates to be used for transforming faba bean. However, transformation of faba bean with FBNYV genes depends not only on the availability of FBNYV genes but, more importantly, on an efficient transformation and regeneration protocol for Vicia faba. Since this species is very recalcitrant to tissue-culture techniques, such a protocol has not yet been established. Suitable and highly efficient promoters, supplied either by the FBNYV genome itself or by using well-established promoters, such as the CaMV 35S and the PR1 promoters, are available.^p^pAlthough the molecular details of the replication mechanism of nanaviruses have not yet been elucidated, it appears valid to assume that their overall replication strategy is similar to that of geminiviruses (Lazarowitz, 1992). Several features of the genome structure and the Rep proteins of the nanaviruses (Harding et al., 1993; Boevink et al., 1995;Katul et al., 1995, 1997, 1998; Sano et al., 1998) are very similar to those of the geminiviruses: an inverted repeat sequence with the potential to form a hairpin-like structure; an AT-rich sequence within the loop of the hairpin, very similar to the conserved nonamer sequence that is the origin of geminivirus plus-strand replication; and putative Rep protein

potential_eco_desc: 受FBNYV感染的蚕豆、鹰嘴豆或小扁豆植物产生少量的种子或不产生种子，这是由侵染的时间所决定的。幼嫩植物的侵染导致100％的产量损失，而当较老的植物受到侵染时，重大的产量损失发生。FBNYV的高发病率在埃及、约旦约旦河流域、叙利亚沿海地区河埃塞俄比亚的一些地区的蚕豆上被报道。在1991/92生长季节中在中埃及的蚕豆中，FBNYV的流行导致差不多全部的作物失收(Makkouk et al., 1994)。 FBNYV-infected faba bean, chickpea or lentil plants produce few or no seeds depending on time of infection. Infection of young plants leads to 100% yield loss, whereas when older plants are infected significant yield loss occurs. High incidence of FBNYV has been reported on faba bean in Egypt, in the Jordan Valley of Jordan, in the coastal region of Syria and in some regions of Ethiopia. The FBNYV epidemic on faba bean in Middle Egypt during the growing season 1991/92 led to almost complete crop failure (Makkouk et al., 1994).

management_info:
在1994-1997年间在埃及实行的实验指出：一个或两个选择性杀虫剂（抗蚜威）的叶片喷雾的使用明显地能减少病毒的传播。另外，在ICARDA实行的实验显示：系统性种子处理杀虫剂(吡虫啉)的使用在播种后的两个月能给小扁豆和蚕豆土地对FBNYV侵染一个明显的保护。这些处理在FBNYV侵染可能在季节早期发生的地区中能证明是有用的。 Experiments conducted in Egypt during the period 1994-97 indicated that the use of one or two foliar sprays of a selective insecticide (pirimicarb) reduced virus spread significantly. In addition, experiments conducted at ICARDA showed that the use of a systemic seed treatment insecticide (imidacloprid) gave significant protection of lentil and faba bean plots against FBNYV infection for 2 months after sowing. Such treatment could prove useful in areas where infection with FBNYV is likely to occur early in the season. 传统育种：

当小扁豆品系在通过带病毒蚜虫进行的人造的田间接种下测试FBNYV抗性时，一些品系如ILL 213、291、6198、6193 和6245被发现有高度的抗性(Mouhanna et al, 1994b)。抗性通过低的病毒发生率和非常低（少于5％）的产量损失来表现。这些结果是在一个单一的环境获得并需要得到证实。这些初步的数据说明：与蚕豆品系相比，小扁豆的基因型在它们对FBNYV侵染的反应中有很大的不同。
病毒抗性的新颖方法：
蚕豆和FBNYV似乎呈现一个理想的模式，这模式通过使用不同的FBNYV基因来估定在蚕豆中来自病原物的对一个DNA病毒的抗性。因为FBNYV的四个可能的Rep基因被鉴别出，以及某个功能（如衣壳蛋白和细胞间的传播）已被明确或暂时地被分配到一些FBNYV的非Rep基因中去(Katul et al., 1995, 1997, 1998)，所以一些病毒基因是用作转化蚕豆的适合的候选者。然而，蚕豆FBNYV基因的转化不仅仅取决于FBNYV基因的可用性，而更重要的是取决于对蚕豆有效的转化和再生的方案。因为这些种对组织培养技术非常的抗拒，所以这个方案还未被建立。适当的和非常有效的促进物，通过FBNYV基因自己提供的或通过利用已良好建立的促进物，如CaMV 35S 和 PR1促进物，是可利用的。
虽然nanaviruses的复制机制的分子学细节还未被说明，但是它们全面的复制策略与双生病毒的相类似的假定似乎是正确的(Lazarowitz, 1992)。一些基因结构和nanaviruses的Rep蛋白的特点(Harding et al., 1993; Boevink et al., 1995;Katul et al., 1995, 1997, 1998; Sano et al., 1998)与双生病毒的那些相类似：一个可能形成类似发夹结构的方向重复的序列；一个双生病毒正链复制起源的AT-rich序列；和与双生病毒的Rep蛋白享有共同的基本氨基酸主题的假定的Rep蛋白质。于是，来自病原物的对FBNYV的抗性策略的发展应集中在已在双生病毒上显示成功的策略中(Mettouchi, 1992; Aaziz, 1994; Desbiez et al., 1995)。因此，试管中特别策划的Rep基因似乎是最理想的产生对FBNYV有高水平抗性的转基因蚕豆植物的候选者。这实验方法为产生FBNYV抗性蚕豆品系通过使用一个典型的蒺藜苜蓿（Medicago truncatula）而普遍地被遵循，蒺藜苜蓿（Medicago truncatula）是一个对FBNYV敏感的豆类品种，在这当中有效的转化和再生方案是可利用的。 Classical breeding
In preliminary screening for FBNYV resistance using 200 pure lines of faba bean, no resistance was found (K. Makkouk, ICARDA, unpublished data). Further work, however, is planned to screen the remaining available faba bean germplasm.
When lentil lines were tested for FBNYV resistance under artificial field inoculation by viruliferous aphids, several lines such as ILL 213, 291, 6198, 6193 and 6245 were found to be highly resistant (Mouhanna et al, 1994b). Resistance was expressed by low virus incidence and extremely low (less than 5%) yield loss. These results were obtained in a single environment and require confirmation. Such preliminary data suggest that lentil genotypes vary widely in their reaction to FBNYV infection as compared to faba bean lines.
Novel approaches for virus resistance
Faba bean and FBNYV appear to offer a promising model for assessing the potential of pathogen-derived resistance to a DNA virus in faba bean by using various FBNYV genes. Since four potential Rep genes of FBNYV have been identified, and certain functions (e.g., capsid protein and cell-to-cell spread) have been definitely or tentatively assigned to some of the non-Rep genes of FBNYV (Katul et al., 1995, 1997, 1998), several viral genes appear to be suitable candidates to be used for transforming faba bean. However, transformation of faba bean with FBNYV genes depends not only on the availability of FBNYV genes but, more importantly, on an efficient transformation and regeneration protocol for Vicia faba. Since this species is very recalcitrant to tissue-culture techniques, such a protocol has not yet been established. Suitable and highly efficient promoters, supplied either by the FBNYV genome itself or by using well-established promoters, such as the CaMV 35S and the PR1 promoters, are available.

description: 只有蚜虫品种豌豆蚜（Acyrthosiphon pisum）、苜蓿蚜（Aphis craccivora）和蚕豆蚜（A. fabae）被报道是FBNYV的传播媒介。蚜虫传播的效率被发现在头两个蚜虫品种中是较高的，而蚕豆蚜（A. fabae）的传播效率非常的低(Katul et al., 1993;Franz et al., 1995, 1998)。它的蚜虫传播信息指出：FBNYV是一个典型的持久传播的病毒，它在媒介昆虫内循环但不复制。蚜虫需要长的获毒期和接种取食时期来成为有效的传播媒介，FBNYV几乎终生在蚜虫的体内持续(Franz et al., 1998)。就像所有的限制在韧皮部的病毒一样，FBNYV不是通过种子或机械方式传播的。因为所有的它的寄主都是以真种繁殖的，所以FBNYV唯一的自然传播是通过蚜虫媒介。 Only the aphid species Acyrthosiphon pisum, Aphis craccivora and A. fabae have been reported as FBNYV vectors. The efficiency of transmission by aphids was found to be high for the first two species and very poor for A. fabae (Katul et al., 1993;Franz et al., 1995, 1998). The information on its aphid transmission indicates that FBNYV has features typical of a persistently transmitted virus which circulates but does not multiply in the vector insects. Aphids require long acquisition and inoculation feeding periods to become efficient vectors, and FBNYV persists in the aphids for almost their entire life (Franz et al., 1998). As with all phloem-limited viruses, FBNYV is not known to be transmitted by seed or mechanical means. Since all its hosts are propagated by true seed, the only method of natural spread FBNYV is by aphid vectors.
author: zhangjianjun

host_range: PNYDV has been reported from numerous European countries causing yield loss in peas, faba beans, vetches and lentils.
potential_eco_desc: About 2 to 25% plants were diseased in different regions of Denmark.
description: In July and August 2016, five faba bean (Vicia faba) samples were received from five fields in different regions of Denmark, in which 2 to 25% plants were diseased. Affected plants displayed leaf-rolling, yellowing, and symptoms of severe stunting. The samples reacted positively when analysed with ELISA using antibodies against PNYDV. DNA was extracted and PNYDV infection was confirmed by PCR, and the full genomes of these Danish PNYDV isolates were determined. Molecular diagnostics results confirmed the presence of PNYDV in the samples. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a nanovirus disease in Denmark demonstrating that PNYDV is also widespread throughout Denmark.
reference_name: Molecular characterisation of the first occurrence of Pea necrotic yellow dwarf virus in Denmark
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: PNYDV was first detected in pea crops (Pisum sativum) in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany in 2009. In 2016, PNYDV was detected countrywide in both Germany and Austria not only on pea but also on faba bean (Vicia faba), vetch (V. sativa) and lentil (Lens culinaris).
potential_eco_desc: PNYDV has caused severe yield losses on pea(Pisum sativum), faba bean (Vicia faba), vetch (V. sativa) and lentil (Lens culinaris) in both Germany and Austria.
description: During a routine survey of twelve green pea crops in the Province of Flevoland (The Netherlands), plants with virus-like symptoms were noticed. Symptomatic plant material was pooled from each field and detected for pea viruses. Based on ELISA,  PCR and sequences analysis confirming the presence of Pea necrotic yellow dwarf virus (PNYDV). To our knowledge, this is the first report of PNYDV in The Netherlands. This indicates that nanoviruses are far more spread throughout Europe than previously thought.  PNYDV is aphid-transmitted in a circulative, non-propagative manner, it is expected that more nanovirus diseases will occur in the future as changes in climatic conditions (especially milder winters in Central Europe) favour aphid survival thus facilitating the spread of these viruses.
reference_name: First report of Pea necrotic yellow dwarf virus in The Netherlands
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: After PNYDV infected Pisum sativum in Austria(2010) and Germany(2009), this is the first report of Lens culinaris, Vicia faba and V. sativa as natural hosts of PNYDV in Austria and Germany.
potential_eco_desc: In many faba bean and pea crops infection caused significant yield losses in Austria.
description: A countrywide outbreak of virus-like disease symptoms on faba beans (Vicia faba) was reported in Germany in 2016. In Austria, nanovirus symptoms appeared first in Pea sativum in early June 2016 and shortly after in faba bean. In mid-late June, nearly every V. faba crop showed typical symptoms of nanovirus infection. Lens culinaris, P. sativum, V. faba and V. sativa were tested for nanovirus infection using PCR primers. PNYDV infection was confirmed by PCR and sequencing. This is the first report of L. culinaris, V. faba and V. sativa as natural hosts of PNYDV in Austria and Germany.
reference_name: Vicia faba, V. sativa and Lens culinaris as new hosts for Pea necrotic yellow dwarf virus in Germany and Austria
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

description: In July 2016, heliconia (Heliconia aurantiaca) plants with chlorotic leaves and green flecking of the veins were observed in a community garden in Honolulu, HI (21.2851°N, 157.8280°W). The symptomatic samples were tested for BBTV, it tested positive for BBTV by PCR and ELISA. In addition, some heliconia samples (H. aurantiaca) with similar BBTV-like symptoms were collected from another location in Honolulu (21.2711°N, 157.8215°W) , tested positive for BBTV by ELISA and PCR sequencing. To our knowledge, this is the first report of BBTV infecting Heliconia sp. in Hawaii. Further study is needed to determine whether banana aphids can transmit BBTV from infected heliconia to healthy banana plants.  BBTV is transmitted by banana aphids (Pentalonia spp.), which can also feed on heliconia (Heliconia spp.).
reference_name: First Report of Banana bunchy top virus in Heliconia spp. on Hawaii
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 香蕉Musa spp.
potential_eco_desc: In southern Africa, banana production is threatened by viral diseases including Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV) (family Nanoviridae, genus Babuvirus), cause of the most devastating virus disease of banana.
description: A detection survey for BBTV was done in South Africa in 1996 confirmed the absence of Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV) in the Kiepersol Region of Mpumalanga Province. No other surveys were conducted since then in South Africa. In June 2015, five ‘Williams’ plants, showing symptoms resembling BBTV, including streaks on the pseudostem and upright bunchy appearance, were submitted for identification to the Virology Diagnostic Lab at Agricultural Research Council-Plant Protection Research (ARC-PPR). The plants originated from a farm close to Hibberdene in the KwaZulu Natal South Coast production region (30°30.636’ S; 30°30.653’ E). The samples were collected and identified, based on ELISA test and molecular diagnostics showed that the causal agent was BBTV. This is the first report of BBTV on Musa spp. from South Africa.  The viral diseases of BBTV is spread by the banana aphid Pentalonia nigronervosa Coquerel (Hemiptera: Aphididae) and infected propagation material.
reference_name: First Report of Banana bunchy top virus in Banana (Musa spp.) from South Africa

potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pBBTV is the most serious virus disease of bananas and plantains. Devastating epidemics occurred in Fiji at the turn of the century and in Australia in the 1920s. The economic effect in northern New South Wales was dramatic. Between 1922 and 1926, about 90% of the area under bananas had gone out of production, despite a rapid expansion of the industry to compensate for abandoned farms. In the Currumbin district in southern Queensland, the number of plantations fell from 100 to 4 between 1922 and 1925, and production plummeted by over 95% (Dale, 1987). In recent years, bunchy top disease has been decimating the banana industry in Pakistan. In the early 1990s, statistics revealed that the area under banana cultivation in Sindh province fell by 55% in one year (Jones, 1994). BBTV is a major constraint to production in many areas where it occurs.^p^p^Impact descriptors^p(dayuhao)i>Negative impact on: (dayuhao)/i>crop production; trade / international relations

remark: Great care should be taken to prevent the dissemination of BBTV to areas where it does not occur. The Americas are free of the disease, but the aphid vector, Pentalonia nigronervosa, is present and the disease would be expected to cause very serious problems if it appeared in smallholdings in the Caribbean and Central or South America. No movement should occur other than by tissue culture. However, the transmission of BBTV in micropropagated cultures has been demonstrated (Drew et al., 1989).^p^pInfected plantlets were indistinguishable from uninfected control plantlets in culture (Drew et al., 1992). When plantlets were deflasked after 12 months in culture (as proliferating tissue) and allowed to grow, all plants developed severe symptoms within 1 month and all had died by 4 months. After 16 months in culture, 75% of plantlets showed symptoms, although it took up to 6 months for all plants to develop symptoms. The other 25% grew normally and appeared healthy (Drew et al., 1992). They were later tested for BBTV with negative results.^p^pRecent findings indicate that proliferating tissue cultures initiated from meristems from BBTV-infected plants may eventually 'lose' the virus after many years under slow growth conditions (DR Jones, Montpellier, personal communication, 1995), but it would be advisable to test all germplasm from BBTV-affected areas before meristems are taken to initiate cultures. BBTV has been eliminated from Lakatan (AAA) by heat-treating shoot-tip cultures for extended periods (Ramos and Zamora, 1990). Subsequently, it was reported that the uneven distribution and low concentration of BBTV after exposure of proliferating tissue cultures to heat leads to BBTV-free primordial cells, which in turn develop into healthy plants (Wu and Su, 1991).
author: CPC2006

management_info: Regulatory Control^p^pBBTV has not been eradicated from any country where it occurs, but it is believed to have been eliminated from certain banana-growing districts in Australia. Here, the disease is kept in check by strict State Government legislation which controls the source and movement of planting material, controls the issue of planting permits and requires the destruction of feral plants and all plants with symptoms. Banana inspectors are also employed to police these regulations and locate diseased and feral plants. A new, ambitious programme of eradication is being initiated which is based on replacing plantations where the disease regularly occurs, with BBTV-tested, tissue-cultured, planting material (Thomas et al., 1994).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pLittle testing of germplasm for resistance has been undertaken, but it has been thought that all cultivars are susceptible, although some may take longer to develop symptoms and others may escape infection because of aphid preferences or host morphological factors. However, work in Australia suggests that Musa coccinea, a wild species, and the cultivar Kluai Teparot (ABBB/ABB) may have physiological resistance (J Thomas, QDPI, Indooroopilly, Queensland, Australia, personal communication, 1995).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pBanana bunchy top disease can be effectively controlled by the eradication of diseased plants and the use of virus-tested planting material. Before destruction, diseased plants should first be sprayed with power kerosene or insecticide to kill all viruliferous aphids. The whole stool, including corm and all associated suckers, must then be destroyed by uprooting and chopping into small pieces or by herbicide treatment, as the virus will ultimately spread to all parts of the mat. Control must be practised across the whole production area to avoid the rapid re-infection of virus-tested planting material (Thomas et al., 1994).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pAphicides have been used in some countries to control populations of Pentalonia nigronervosa, the aphid vector of bunchy top, and a decrease in disease incidence has been reported. In Tonga, Aphidius colemani, a parasitic wasp, has been released in an attempt at biological control of the aphid vector, but its effects on disease incidence have been disappointing.
author: CPC2006

potential_eco_desc: BBTV是香蕉和车前草病害最严重的病毒。破坏性的流行病在19世纪末20世纪初发生于斐济而在20世纪20年代发生于澳大利亚。在北新南威尔士中经济影响是显著的。在1922 年和1926年之间，约90％的有香蕉的地区失去生产性，尽管为被抛弃的农场偿还的工业的快速扩充。在南昆士兰可伦宾区中，种植园的数量从100降到4在1922年和1925年之间，且产量垂直落下到超过95％(Dale, 1987)。在最近几年，束顶病害一直大批杀害香蕉产业在巴基斯坦。在20世纪90年代早期，统计资料显示在信德省香蕉耕作的地区降达55％在一年里(Jones, 1994)。BBTV是主要的限制对产品来说在它发生的很多地区中 BBTV is the most serious virus disease of bananas and plantains. Devastating epidemics occurred in Fiji at the turn of the century and in Australia in the 1920s. The economic effect in northern New South Wales was dramatic. Between 1922 and 1926, about 90% of the area under bananas had gone out of production, despite a rapid expansion of the industry to compensate for abandoned farms. In the Currumbin district in southern Queensland, the number of plantations fell from 100 to 4 between 1922 and 1925, and production plummeted by over 95% (Dale, 1987). In recent years, bunchy top disease has been decimating the banana industry in Pakistan. In the early 1990s, statistics revealed that the area under banana cultivation in Sindh province fell by 55% in one year (Jones, 1994). BBTV is a major constraint to production in many areas where it occurs.

description:
通过机械接种传播(Magee, 1927)。
在澳大利亚，香蕉蚜虫(P. nigronervosa)被认为在香蕉束顶(Darnell-Smith, 1924)的病原学中具有角色且最后在1925年被证明为传播媒介(Magee, 1927)。香蕉蚜虫有着广泛的包括焦麻和芭蕉科中其它种类的寄主范围分布。
BBTV的传播是循环的，非增殖型类型。 transmitted by mechanical inoculation (Magee, 1927).
In Australia, the banana aphid (P. nigronervosa) was considered to have a role in the etiology of banana bunchy top (Darnell-Smith, 1924) and in 1925 was conclusively demonstrated to be the vector (Magee, 1927). Banana aphids have a worldwide distribution with a host range that includes M. textilis and other species in the Musaceae. 
Transmission of BBTV is of the circulative, non-propagative type.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info: 香蕉束顶病害能被有效地控制通过根除有病的植株和使用测试病毒的种植材料。在毁灭之前，有病的植株首先应该用动力煤油或杀虫剂喷射以杀死所有携带病毒的蚜虫。包括球茎和所有的联合的吸根的完整的根株，必须通过倒根和砍成小块或除草剂处理而被消灭，因为病毒最后会传播到垫子的所有部位。控制必须被实行在整个生产区以避免测试病毒的种植的材料的快速再侵染(Thomas et al., 1994)。 Banana bunchy top disease can be effectively controlled by the eradication of diseased plants and the use of virus-tested planting material. Before destruction, diseased plants should first be sprayed with power kerosene or insecticide to kill all viruliferous aphids. The whole stool, including corm and all associated suckers, must then be destroyed by uprooting and chopping into small pieces or by herbicide treatment, as the virus will ultimately spread to all parts of the mat. Control must be practised across the whole production area to avoid the rapid re-infection of virus-tested planting material (Thomas et al., 1994). 杀蚜虫剂已被运用于一些国家中以控制香蕉交脉蚜的种群，束顶的蚜虫媒介，及在病害发病率的降低已有被报道。在汤加，蚜茧蜂，一种寄生黄蜂，已被释放于一种尝试在蚜虫媒介的生物控制，但在病害的发病率上它的影响是令人失望的。 Aphicides have been used in some countries to control populations of Pentalonia nigronervosa, the aphid vector of bunchy top, and a decrease in disease incidence has been reported. In Tonga, Aphidius colemani, a parasitic wasp, has been released in an attempt at biological control of the aphid vector, but its effects on disease incidence have been disappointing. 不多的种质抗性试验已被进行，但已被认为所有的植株是易受感染的，虽然有些可能花更长的来发展症状且其它的可能避开侵染由于蚜虫参数选择或寄主形态学因素。然而，作业于澳大利亚显示红蕉，一种野生种类，和栽培种Kluai Teparot (ABBB/ABB)可能有生理学上的抗性(J Thomas, QDPI, Indooroopilly, Queensland, Australia, personal communication, 1995)。 Little testing of germplasm for resistance has been undertaken, but it has been thought that all cultivars are susceptible, although some may take longer to develop symptoms and others may escape infection because of aphid preferences or host morphological factors. However, work in Australia suggests that Musa coccinea, a wild species, and the cultivar Kluai Teparot (ABBB/ABB) may have physiological resistance (J Thomas, QDPI, Indooroopilly, Queensland, Australia, personal communication, 1995). BBTV尚未从它发生的任何国家被根绝，但相信已从澳大利亚若干香蕉种植区消除。在这里，该病害不断的被国家政府立法严格检查，国家政府立法控制来源和种植材料的移动，控制了种植许可证的发行，且要求野生的植株和具症状的所有植株毁灭。香蕉检查员也被雇来管辖这些规章和查找有病的和野生的植株的地点。一种新的，野心勃勃的根除方案正被开始，这是在替代病害有规律地发生的种植园，有BBTV试验的，组织培养的种植材料的基础上(Thomas et al., 1994)。 BBTV has not been eradicated from any country where it occurs, but it is believed to have been eliminated from certain banana-growing districts in Australia. Here, the disease is kept in check by strict State Government legislation which controls the source and movement of planting material, controls the issue of planting permits and requires the destruction of feral plants and all plants with symptoms. Banana inspectors are also employed to police these regulations and locate diseased and feral plants. A new, ambitious programme of eradication is being initiated which is based on replacing plantations where the disease regularly occurs, with BBTV-tested, tissue-cultured, planting material (Thomas et al., 1994).
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc: BBTV是香蕉和车前草病害最严重的病毒。破坏性的流行病在19世纪末20世纪初发生于斐济而在20世纪20年代发生于澳大利亚。在北新南威尔士中经济影响是显著的。在1922 年和1926年之间，约90％的有香蕉的地区失去生产性，尽管为被抛弃的农场偿还的工业的快速扩充。在南昆士兰可伦宾区中，种植园的数量从100降到4在1922年和1925年之间，且产量垂直落下到超过95％(Dale, 1987)。在最近几年，束顶病害一直大批杀害香蕉产业在巴基斯坦。在20世纪90年代早期，统计资料显示在信德省香蕉耕作的地区降达55％在一年里(Jones, 1994)。BBTV是主要的限制对产品来说在它发生的很多地区中。 BBTV is the most serious virus disease of bananas and plantains. Devastating epidemics occurred in Fiji at the turn of the century and in Australia in the 1920s. The economic effect in northern New South Wales was dramatic. Between 1922 and 1926, about 90% of the area under bananas had gone out of production, despite a rapid expansion of the industry to compensate for abandoned farms. In the Currumbin district in southern Queensland, the number of plantations fell from 100 to 4 between 1922 and 1925, and production plummeted by over 95% (Dale, 1987). In recent years, bunchy top disease has been decimating the banana industry in Pakistan. In the early 1990s, statistics revealed that the area under banana cultivation in Sindh province fell by 55% in one year (Jones, 1994). BBTV is a major constraint to production in many areas where it occurs.

The yield loss can therefore be estimated as between 42 and 66%. author: CPC2006

description: No seed or pollen transmission of CFDV has been demonstrated in trials using susceptible cultivars (symptomatic or in remission), or for the tolerant Vanuatu Tall variety. In cultivars in which tree decline occurs sufficiently slowly, inflorescences develop normally, but the number of nuts is reduced. No seed treatments are applicable. Diagnosis of infection is achieved only by molecular methods (see Diagnostic Methods).
author: CPC2006

remark: Due to the lack of genetic tolerance outside Vanuatu, CFDV would be potentially devastating to all other coconut growing areas. CFDV appears to be transmitted specifically in Vanuatu by Myndus taffini (Julia, 1982). Attempted experimental transmission with (i) various jassid and various delphacid leafhoppers, (ii) insect mixtures without any cixiid planhoppers and (iii) insects collected from the understorey grass Digitaria sanguinalis were all negative (Julia, 1982). The vector's breeding host, Hibiscus tiliaceus, is generally widespread in the tropics and would be readily available for the insects. Therefore, the accidental introduction of the vector species to new locations must be regarded as a major quarantine risk. See also Australian Quarantine Service (1987).
author: CPC2006

management_info: CFDV can be controlled by planting the tolerant local cultivar Vanuatu Tall. A programme is being developed for the use of hybrids between Vanuatu Tall and the local dwarf variety Vanuatu Red Dwarf, which show very mild symptoms combined with the advantages of heterosis.^p^pGeneral insect control methods are applicable for vector control, but are not used in Vanuatu.^p^pControl by eradication of Hibiscus tiliaceus, the host plant of the vector, has been suggested, but complete eradication would be extremely difficult due to the wide use of this species as 'living fences', and its general abundance. The effectiveness of this measure has yet to be demonstrated.

description:
叶衰在瓦努阿图引进的椰子树中是致命性的病害。敏感性的不同的水平在不同的品种中被发现，于是从症状首次出现到树木死亡的时间也有所不同。对于最敏感的品种之一的Malayan Red Dwarf (MRD)来说，症状在接种后的7-10个月中出现，在接着的1-2年中植物死亡。病害康复被报道发生在感染的植物当中(Randles et al., 1986)。该病害的传播媒介被证明是Myndus taffini (Julia, 1982)。M. taffini在黄槿（Hibiscus tiliaceus）的根部中繁殖，然而喂食的成虫在椰子的小叶上被发现。病害梯度从含有H. tiliaceus的森林边界中发展(Randles JW, Waite Agricultural Research Institute, Australia, personal communication, 1996)。叶衰被证明有一个通过在病毒和病害之间相符合的联合的病毒的病原。其病原物叫做椰子叶衰病毒(CFDV) (Randles et al., 1986)。它的侵染性目前还未被证明。CFDV有一小的DNA基因组(Randles et al., 1987)，以低数量存在的二十面体粒子可能主要在韧皮部中，并且很难分离(Randles and Hanold, 1989)。核苷序列与已知的DNA植物病毒的比较说明：CEDV是一个新的病毒，它不属于任何正式认可的属，但它的假定的复制酶基因显示与其他类似形态的植物病毒有同种性(Rohde et al., 1990)。
CFDV DNA存在于引进品种的生病棕榈和耐病性品种Vanuatu Tall的叶片、根、树干、坚果果皮、胚胎和韧皮部中(Hanold et al., 1988; Randles et al., 1992)，以及媒介M. taffini 的腹部区域中(Randles et al., 1992)。没有种子传播被证明。目前还不知道该病毒是否是从M. taffini的幼虫或成虫中获得，以及它是否在昆虫体内繁殖或仅仅是积聚。CFDV DNA没有在被M. taffini 侵染的黄槿（H. tiliaceus）或其他任何的棕榈品种或与CFDV侵染的椰子树联合草本单子叶植物的根部发现(Hanold et al., 1988)，或在该媒介分布地区以外的地方发现(Hanold D, University of Adelaide, South Australia, personal communication, 1996)。 Foliar decay is a lethal disease of introduced coconut palm varieties in Vanuatu. Different levels of susceptibility are found in different cultivars, and thus the time from first appearance of symptoms to death of the tree varies. For Malayan Red Dwarf (MRD), one of the most susceptible varieties, symptoms appear 7-10 months after inoculation, and death follows after 1-2 years. Disease remission has been reported to occur in infected plants (Randles et al., 1986). The vector of the disease was shown to be the cixiid bug Myndus taffini (Julia, 1982). M. taffini breeds on the roots of Hibiscus tiliaceus, whereas feeding adults were found on coconut leaflets. Disease gradients develop from forest borders containing H. tiliaceus (Randles JW, Waite Agricultural Research Institute, Australia, personal communication, 1996). Foliar decay was shown to have a viral aetiology by consistent association between virus and disease. The agent was called coconut foliar decay virus (CFDV) (Randles et al., 1986). Its infectivity has yet to be demonstrated. CFDV has a small DNA genome (Randles et al., 1987) and icosahedral particles which are present in low numbers, possibly mainly in the phloem, and are difficult to isolate (Randles and Hanold, 1989). Comparison of nucleotide sequences with known DNA plant viruses suggests that CFDV is a novel virus not belonging to any officially recognised genus, but its presumed replicase gene shows homology with other plant viruses of similar morphology (Rohde et al., 1990).
CFDV DNA is present in leaves, roots, trunk, husk of the nut, embryo and phloem of diseased palms of introduced varieties and tolerant Vanuatu Tall palms (Hanold et al., 1988; Randles et al., 1992), as well as the abdominal region of the vector, M. taffini (Randles et al., 1992). No seed transmission has been demonstrated. It is not yet known whether the virus is acquired by the larvae or adults of M. taffini, and whether it replicates or merely accumulates in the insects. CFDV DNA could not be found in the roots of H. tiliaceus infested with M. taffini or in any other palm species or herbaceous monocotyledons associated with CFDV-infected coconut palms (Hanold et al., 1988), or in locations outside the distribution area of the vector (Hanold D, University of Adelaide, South Australia, personal communication, 1996).

description: 小麦土传花叶病毒通过禾谷多粘菌传播，一种普遍的土居真菌。它能通过土壤移动传播，例如通过农具或气流。小麦作物不在这种真菌能存活在土壤中很多年，因此有潜力传播病害很多年在侵染之后。 Soil-borne wheat mosaic virus is spread by Polymyxa graminis, a common soil-dwelling fungus. It can be spread by soil movement, such as by farm vehicles or wind. The fungus can survive in the soil for many years in the absence of a wheat crop and so has the potential to transmit diseases many years after infection.

potential_eco_desc: In the USA, BSMV has been economically significant only in Montana and North Dakota (Carroll, 1983). Between 1953 and 1970 the total loss in barley caused by this virus was calculated at more than US$ 30 million. In 1964 the virus caused damage estimated at over US$ 3.1 million (Carroll, 1980). description: Incidence^p^pSeed infection of BSMV in barley has been studied extensively. Seed transmissibility (up to 90-100%) depends on the virus strain (Timian, 1974) as well as on the stage of development at which plants become infected, and is influenced by temperature (Singh et al., 1960). The percentage of pollen and ovule transmission varies from 10 to 35% and from 17 to 66%, respectively Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, b. ^p^pElectron microscopy, bioassay and serology have been used to demonstrate the presence of BSMV within all reproductive tissues as well as in all seed tissues (Gold et al., 1954; Crowley, 1959; Inouye, 1962; Hamilton, 1965; Inouye, 1966; Gardner, 1967; Carroll, 1969; Shivanathan, 1970; Carroll, 1972; Carroll, 1974; Mayhew and Carroll, 1974;Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, b; Brlansky et al., 1986). Infection of the seed may occur as a result of prior infection of either male or female reproductive tissues. Presence of the virus in the embryos of infected seed is crucial for virus transmission through the seed to new seedlings (Inouye, 1962; Inouye, 1966; Carroll, 1972).^p^pThe means by which the embryo becomes infected was for long unclear. Much evidence now supports the view that the embryo is infected indirectly through prior infection of immature reproductive cells with subsequent infection of new tissues, including the embryo, as they develop. Other evidence suggests that the embryo may be invaded directly. Evidence of both routes to embryo infection has been obtained by studying the time of parent plant infection in relation to seed transmission. Evidence that some seed transmission could occur even if the mother plant was infected after flowering was obtained by Eslick and Afanasiev (1955), Crowley (1959) and Singh et al. (1960). Evidence that infection of the mother plant must occur prior to fertilization and that BSMV enters the embryo indirectly was obtained by others (Hagborg, 1954; Inouye, 1962; Timian, 1967). Later, a very careful and extensive study by Carroll (1972) confirmed the latter results. Examination of thousands of embryos revealed that none was infected if mother plants were inoculated with BSMV after fertilization.^p	^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pBSMV infection of barley can result in partial sterility of florets, poorly developed heads, fewer and smaller seeds, shrivelled seeds and reduced germination (Hagborg, 1954; Inouye, 1962; Slack et al., 1975; Chiko and Baker, 1978; Mathre, 1982).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pTransmission of BSMV through seed to progeny is well known. Ovule transmission results in a higher percentage of seed transmission than pollen transmission; however, the highest levels of seed transmission result from transmission via both ovule and pollen (Inouye, 1962; Timian, 1967;Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, b). Studies of the ultrastructure of seedlings grown from BSMV-infected barley seed showed that BSMV infection delays or inhibits plastid development and the formation of photosynthetic apparatus (Harsanyi et al., 2002).^p^pHost genotype, virus strain and environmental factors also affect the number of progeny to which the virus is transmitted. In mechanically inoculated barley varieties, percentage seed transmission ranged from zero to 90% (Hagborg, 1954; Inouye, 1962; Timian, 1974). Transmission of BSMV through seed of wheat (Hagborg, 1954; McNeal et al., 1976), oats (McKinney and Greeley, 1965) and wild oats (Chiko, 1975) has also been reported. There is an excellent overview of BSMV transmission via seed by Carroll (1981).^p^pBSMV can spread from plant to plant within a field, but it has no known insect vector. Thus, BSMV may be unique among seed-transmitted viruses in that it appears to depend solely on seed transmission for its natural survival. In fact, its survival appears to be primarily dependent on seed transmission in barley. management_info: Regulatory Control^p^pSince seed transmission is necessary for the survival of BSMV in nature and this virus has no known vectors, a simple and extremely effective means of control involves the sowing of virus-free seed. Barley seed certification schemes in Montana (Carroll, 1983) and North Dakota, USA, have prevented significant yield losses since their inception. There are currently no known losses due to BSMV in the upper midwestern USA.^p^pCertified seed programmes in both Montana and North Dakota involve production of foundation, registered and certified seed. In Montana, field inspections are supplemented with serological assays (Carroll et al., 1979a) on seed samples from foundation seed fields. In North Dakota, no field inspection is done; samples of 1,000 seeds per foundation seed lot are assayed by ELISA. In either programme, only virus-free seed lots are certified.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pResistance to BSMV has been identified in a number of barley cultivars in the USA National Small Grains Germplasm Collection (Timian and Sisler, 1955; Timian, 1975). There appears to be little interest among plant breeders to incorporate resistance into commercial cultivars, probably as a result of the effectiveness of clean seed programmes.^p^pThe inheritance of resistance to BSMV has been investigated in several studies which together identified up to five resistance loci (Timian and Sisler, 1955; Sisler and Timian, 1956; Vazquez et al., 1974; Timian and Franckowiak, 1987). A single gene for resistance was mapped to the centromeric region of the plus arm of barley chromosome 1 and was found to co-segregate with RFLP marker ABC455 (Edwards and Steffenson, 1996). A single recessive gene also conditions resistance to seed transmission of BSMV in Modjo barley (Carroll et al., 1979b).

management_info:
BSMV抗性已在一些大麦品种在USA National Small Grains Germplasm Collection里被鉴定出来 (Timian and Sisler, 1955; Timian, 1975)。植物种植者当中似乎对合并商业品种的抗性有少许兴趣，这可能作为清扫种子程序的效果的结果。　　　　　
BSMV抗性遗传已在一些研究中作调查，这总共识别出超过五种抗性组合(Timian and Sisler, 1955; Sisler and Timian, 1956; Vazquez et al., 1974; Timian and Franckowiak, 1987)。一个单一的抗性基因于大麦染色体1的附加臂的着丝点区域被绘制出来，并且被发现与RFLP标记ABC455共同隔离(Edwards and Steffenson, 1996)。一种单一的隐性基因同样使Modjo barley 对BSMV的种子传播产生抗性。 Resistance to BSMV has been identified in a number of barley cultivars in the USA National Small Grains Germplasm Collection (Timian and Sisler, 1955; Timian, 1975). There appears to be little interest among plant breeders to incorporate resistance into commercial cultivars, probably as a result of the effectiveness of clean seed programmes.
The inheritance of resistance to BSMV has been investigated in several studies which together identified up to five resistance loci (Timian and Sisler, 1955; Sisler and Timian, 1956; Vazquez et al., 1974; Timian and Franckowiak, 1987). A single gene for resistance was mapped to the centromeric region of the plus arm of barley chromosome 1 and was found to co-segregate with RFLP marker ABC455 (Edwards and Steffenson, 1996). A single recessive gene also conditions resistance to seed transmission of BSMV in Modjo barley (Carroll et al., 1979b). 因为种子传播对BSMV在自然界的生存是必要的，并且该病毒没有已知的传播媒介，所以，简单而非常有效的防治方法包括播种无病毒种子。在美国蒙大纳州(Carroll, 1983)和北达科他州的大麦种子鉴定程序，自它们开始以后已防止了重大的产量损失。在美国中西部的上部还普遍存在由于BSMV引起的未知的损失。
在蒙大纳州和北达科他州的鉴定的种子程序包括基础的已登记的和被鉴定的种子的生产。在蒙大纳州，对来自基础种子田地里的种子样本的田间检查补充着血清学化验(Carroll et al., 1979a) 一起进行。在北达科他州，没有进行田间检查；每个基础种子田块的1000个种子样本通过ELISA化验。在每个程序中，只有无病毒种子田块被鉴定。 Since seed transmission is necessary for the survival of BSMV in nature and this virus has no known vectors, a simple and extremely effective means of control involves the sowing of virus-free seed. Barley seed certification schemes in Montana (Carroll, 1983) and North Dakota, USA, have prevented significant yield losses since their inception. There are currently no known losses due to BSMV in the upper midwestern USA.
Certified seed programmes in both Montana and North Dakota involve production of foundation, registered and certified seed. In Montana, field inspections are supplemented with serological assays (Carroll et al., 1979a) on seed samples from foundation seed fields. In North Dakota, no field inspection is done; samples of 1,000 seeds per foundation seed lot are assayed by ELISA. In either programme, only virus-free seed lots are certified.

病毒在所有植物组织内繁殖。它在叶肉和表皮细胞的细胞质中被发现(Shalla, 1966)。此外，有报道说病毒粒子附着在叶绿体表面(Carroll, 1970)或出现在细胞核中(Gardner, 1967)。该病毒存在于种子(McKinney and Greeley, 1965)和花粉(Gold et al., 1954)当中，还在胚珠中被检测出(Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, 1976b)。
种子传播率(超过90-100%)是由病毒的品系(Timian, 1974)，以及植物受感染所处的发展阶段决定，并受温度的影响(e.g., Singh et al., 1960)。花粉传播百分率为10% 到35%，胚珠传播百分率为17%到66% (e.g., Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, 1976b)。 There is no known natural vector of BSMV.
The virus multiplies in all plant tissues. It has been found in the cytoplasm of mesophyll and epidermal cells (Shalla, 1966). Furthermore, it has been reported that virus particles were attached to the surface of chloroplasts (Carroll, 1970) or occurred in nuclei (Gardner, 1967). The virus is 现存 in seed (McKinney and Greeley, 1965) and in pollen (Gold et al., 1954), and has also been detected in ovules (Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, 1976b).
Seed transmissibility (up to 90-100%) depends on the virus strain (Timian, 1974) as well as on the stage of development at which plants become infected, and is influenced by temperature (e.g., Singh et al., 1960). The percentage of pollen and ovule transmission varies from 10 to 35 and from 17 to 66, respectively (e.g., Carroll and Mayhew, 1976a, 1976b).

description: Incidence^p^pToMV can be present in the external mucilage, testa and endosperm, but not the embryo of seeds collected from infected tomato fruits (Taylor et al., 1961; Broadbent, 1965b). The extent of contamination varies greatly in seeds of different fruits; approximately 50% of seed is often contaminated, but this can be up to 94% of seed (Broadbent, 1976). In Iran, serological and test plant studies established that up to 60% of tomato seeds from infected plants were contaminated by the virus (Ahoonmanesh et al., 1992). In a study in Pakistan, ToMV virus was detected in all commercial tomato seed lots tested (Hassan, 1995).^p^pIn an extensive report of the process of infection of tomato seeds with ToMV, Macias (1980) showed that different cultivars varied in rate of transmission of the virus to seeds. Infection of seeds from fruits obtained at various stages of ripeness was similar except in those from overripe fruits. Storage of fruit for 1 week or more caused a reduction of seed infection. Macias (1980) also showed that the attenuated isolate M II-16 of ToMV was seed transmitted much less intensively than virulent ToMV isolates. Highest seed contamination was caused by the green mosaic-producing strain. Infection with potato virus X or Cucumber mosaic virus led to enhanced seed contamination with ToMV.^p^pTomato and bell pepper (Capsicum annuum) were inoculated with ToMV or Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) when they were 35, 50, 90 and 110 days old. Both viruses infected both tomato and bell pepper at all growth stages. The level of virus in the leaf was quantified by local lesion assay and that in the seed by local lesion assay and ELISA. The viruses became established in the seeds, irrespective of growth stage at time of inoculation. However, the concentration of virus was higher in seeds when the plants were inoculated early. Bell pepper and tomato are the preferred hosts for TMV and ToMV, respectively (Chitra et al., 1999).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pUncontaminated tomato seed germinated more quickly than seed infected with ToMV; however, infection was lower in non-germinating seed (Macias, 1980).^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pToMV is transmitted mechanically from contaminated tomato seed if seedlings are handled during transplanting. However, infection rarely occurs if seed is sown and allowed to germinate and grow without being disturbed (van Winckel, 1965; Broadbent, 1976).^p^pThe pathogen is also soilborne. A survey of soils along the coastal region of Lebanon indicated that 18 of 75 soil samples tested were infested with ToMV as determined by serology (Makkouk and Rana, 1979). Lanter et al. (1982) recovered ToMV from debris and soil in a field where infected tomato had been grown the previous year.^p^p^Seed Treatment^p^pToMV can be removed from the external surface of seeds by soaking them for 20 min. in 10% (w/v) tri-sodium phosphate solution (Alexander, 1960; Fry and McCallum, 1960; Broadbent, 1965b). Externally-located virus and that in endosperm is usually eliminated by treating dry seed for 1 day at 80°C or 2-4 days at 70°C (Broadbent, 1965b; Laterrot and Pecaut, 1965).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pSerological^p^pIowa State University Seed Health Testing Laboratory has adapted a diagnostic kit manufactured by Agdia Unc, Elkhart, Indiana, USA, to test for ToMV in seeds. The method is available on the USDA National Seed Health System website at www.seedhealth.org.

management_info: Use of Resistant Cultivars^p^pThree major genes (designated Tm-1, Tm-2 and Tm-22) for resistance have been most used in tomato breeding programmes. The earlier use of cultivars containing genes Tm-1 and/or Tm-2 resulted in the rapid emergence or increased incidence of strains which were able to overcome resistance (see Brunt, 1988). However, gene Tm-22 in homozygous cultivars, or together with genes Tm-1 and/or Tm-2, has been highly effective in controlling ToMV for two decades or so. Although the molecular basis for genetic resistance has yet to be determined, the genes probably inhibit virus multiplication and movement. The origin and exploitation of genes Tm-2 and Tm-22 have been fully reviewed by Hall (1980). Resistance to ToMV has also been reported in Capsicum annuum (Jilaveanu et al., 1984; Patagas et al., 1989).^p^p^Mild Strain Protection^p^pBefore genotypes with effective genetic resistance to ToMV became generally available, virus-induced losses were often reduced by prior infection of seedlings with a mild or attenuated strain of ToMV (Brunt, 1988). This procedure, although once widely used, is now unnecessary where resistant cultivars are grown.^p^p^Seed Treatment^p^pIdeally, seed should only be collected from mother plants shown to be free of virus. Treatment of freshly harvested seed with dilute hydrochloric acid will inactivate virus contaminating seed coats. If the health status of seed is unknown, any virus on seed coats and in endosperm can also be eliminated by dry heating seed at 70°C for 2-4 days (Broadbent, 1965b; Laterrot and Pecaut, 1965). Externally located virus can be eliminated by soaking seed for 20 min in 10% (w/v) tri-sodium phosphate solution (Broadbent, 1976; Hollings and Huttinga, 1976).^p^p^Cultural Practices^p^pThe use of virus-free seed, the cultivation of plants in sterilised compost in plastic bags ('growbags') or hydroponic systems in which the nutrient solution is virus-free and application of strict hygiene can often reduce and sometimes prevent infection occurring (Broadbent, 1976). Tobacco in cigars, cigarettes and pipe tobacco was once thought to be an important source of ToMV. However, it is now recognized that, although tobacco might occasionally be such a source of infection of tobacco mosaic tobamovirus, it is very unlikely to be a source of ToMV (Broadbent, 1976). When infection is detected in a crop, milk sprays can minimise spread by inhibiting mechanical transfer of virus from infected to healthy plants (Crowley, 1958). It is also advisable that all tools be dipped in 3% (w/v) tri-sodium phosphate solution and that nursery workers thoroughly wash hands and any contaminated clothing (Broadbent, 1976).^p^pSpread in crops grown in hydroponic systems can be prevented or minimized by pasteurization of the nutrient solution (Vetten, 1996).^p^p^Transgenic Plants^p^pNon-conventional resistance to ToMV has been conferred on genetically engineered plants containing the virus coat protein gene (Nejidat and Beachy, 1990; Yeh et al., 1996), antisense viral RNA and a ribozyme (Feyter et al., 1996). Such procedures have great potential for future use, but they have not yet been used experimentally.

potential_eco_desc: TMV causes heavy yield losses for tobacco, tomato and pepper worldwide (Piccirillo and Diana, 1991; Gao et al., 1994; Palloix et al., 1994; Xu et al., 1994; Sikora et al., 1998). Lower levels of loss are reported for aubergine.^p^pYield reductions of up to 90% have been estimated on pepper for TMV in association with other viruses (Escudero, 1996). Up to 34% losses have been produced experimentally in tomato (Giri and Mishra, 1991).^p^pEarly infection by TMV may damage young tobacco plants in both nurseries and in the field. A high percentage of plants infected at, or soon after, transplanting can reduce yield by up to 50% (Lucas, 1975). Late field attacks are not infrequent and can injure the middle and apical leaves.^p^p'Flue cured', 'sun cured', Havana and Kentucky tobacco types are most affected, beacuse they lack the N-gene for hypersensitivity reaction. On 'flue cured', yearly losses above US$ 1 million are caused by TMV in the USA (Lucas, 1975) and heavy losses have been reported in China (Gao et al., 1994).^p^pBurley tobacco cultivars mostly have the N-gene, with the hypersensitive reaction functioning as resistance. On sensitive burley cultivars, losses above 50% have been recorded in southern Italy (Piccirillo and Diana, 1991).^p^pTMV infection reduces tobacco quality by modifying ratios of major chemical constituents such as nitrogen, sugar and nicotine (Patel and Patel, 1995). The sugar content of infected leaves is reduced while protein content is increased (Gao et al., 1994).

description: IncidenceAlekseev et al. (1974) reported the incidence of TMV on tomato reaching 100% at the end of the growing period in Russia. Seeds are the main source of infection. Aucuba strains persist in seed material for 3 years. The virus is found on the seed surface, in the coat and in shoots.^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pNo effect on seed quality is known.^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSeed transmission of TMV is unknown for tobacco (Lucas, 1975). Seeds from infected plants give TMV-free plants (Piccirillo, unpublished data, 1992). Primary infection of tomato plantlets in seedbeds is caused by TMV particles on seed. Seed transmission rates of 98, 18 and 7% have been found in tomato, pepper and aubergine, respectively (Cicek and Yorganci, 1991). Seed transmission is frequent in pepper, and field disease outbreaks have been ascribed to the use of contaminated seeds (Fominykh et al., 1996; Beczner et al., 1997).^p^p^Seed Treatment^p^pTrisodium orthophosphate followed by sodium hypochlorite treatment of TMV-infested tomato seed was more effective for inactivation of the virus than either chemical alone. Seeds were soaked in a 1% aqueous solution of trisodium orthophosphate for 15 min and then in a 0.525% sodium hypochloride for 30 min. Treatment did not reduce seed germination (Gooding, 1975).^p^pSeed treatment with 20% hydrochloric acid gave complete control of superficial infection without lowering germination (Alekseev et al., 1975).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pSeedborne TMV can be detected by inoculating a suspension of ground seeds on indicator hosts. ELISA tests have been used to detect tobamoviruses in tomato, aubergine and pepper seeds (Cicek and Yorganci, 1991).

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pTobacco^p^pN-gene hypersensitivity was first recommended as a crop resistance strategy against TMV spread by Holmes (1938), who also bred the Samsun NN cultivar by transferring the N gene from N. glutinosa via the synthetic amphidiploid N. digluta (N. glutinosa (n=24) x N. tabacum (n=12)). The reaction localizes TMV and most tobamoviruses at the infection point. This type of resistance has proved durable (Piccirillo and Piro, 1996; Nielsen, 1997). A reported tobamovirus (OB strain) causing mosaic on NN tobacco has recently been classified as a different virus (Padgett and Beachy, 1993). ^p^pN-gene resistance has proved practically valuable only in Burley type varieties; in other types resistance is correlated with lower quality of the cured leaf (Lucas 1975; Nielsen and Kennedy, 1994; Aycock and McKee, 1995). The introduction via biotechnology of the single N-gene could help overcome the correlated negative traits in the latter types (Whitham et al., 1994; Baker et al., 1996). Genetic engineering is being used extensively to introduce resistance to tobamoviruses in tobacco.^p^pSensitive tobacco plants transformed with a gene expressing the coat protein of TMV acquired considerable resistance to virus replication (Reimann-Philipp and Beachy, 1993). Likewise a mutant gene of TMV coat protein interfered with disassembly in viral replication (Bin-Lu et al., 1998).^p^pInsertion of a TMV-RNA antisense construct in sensitive tobacco inhibits the gene encoding of both 126-183 kDa replicase proteins (Nelson et al., 1993). Transgenic tobacco plants expressing the gene for TMV replicase with an additional insertion in the middle of 183-kDa has been shown to be highly resistant to systemic infection by TMV and other tobamoviruses (Donson et al., 1993). ^p^pPlants transformed with a gene encoding a defective mutant of the TMV movement protein had delayed symptom appearance and reduced systemic spread of infection to upper leaves (Cooper et al., 1995).^p^pA gene for ribosome inactivating protein gives resistance to infection by different viruses (Smirnov et al., 1997).^p^pTomato^p^pThe Tm1, Tm2 and Tm2-2 resistance genes against ToMV have been overcome by the occurrence of the 1, 2, 1-2 and 2-2 virulent pathotypes (Marchoux and Gebre-Selassie, 1989; Betti et al., 1997). Pathotype frequency varies region by region and depends also on the presence of matching resistance genes (Feng et al., 1996).^p^pTransgenic tomato with the N-gene from tobacco shows the hypersensitive type of resistance (Baker et al., 1996).^p^pPepper^p^pThe L1, L2, L3 and L4 genes for resistance to tobamoviruses are matched by pathotypes P0, P1, P1-2, P1-2-3 (Garcia-Luque et al., 1992; Rusko et al., 1995). L1 is wild in Capsicum annuum, L2 in C. frutescens, L3 in C. chinensis and L4 in C. chacoense. The P0 pathotype is considered to belong to tobacco mild green mosaic virus (Green and Wu, 1991), while pathotypes P1-2 and P1-2-3 are considered strains of pepper mild mottle tobamovirus (Garcia et al., 1992).^p^p^Biological Control^p^pIn some cases systemic acquired resistance (SAR), induced by a previous infection with a pathogen or by application of salicylic acid, has been effective against TMV (Ward et al., 1991). Salicylic acid, levels of which increase during the hypersensitivity reaction in tobacco in both inoculated and virus-free leaves, is considered a precursor of SAR (Enyedi et al., 1992; Shulaev et al., 1995). A disease resistant state develops in plants after the hypersensitive reaction.^p^pProteins inactivating the virus in vitro and in vivo have been isolated from numerous vegetable species (Sadasivam et al., 1991) including Phytolacca sp. (Watanabe et al., 1997), Chenopodium murale (Neeta Srivastava and Verma, 1995) and Amaranthus viridis (Kwon et al., 1997). TMV的早期侵染可破坏苗圃和田间幼小的烟草植株。高比例的植株侵染在移植时或移植后能减少50％的产量(Lucas, 1975)。后期的田间侵害是不常发生的，并且能损害中部及顶部叶片。 TMV causes heavy yield losses for tobacco, tomato and pepper worldwide (Piccirillo and Diana, 1991; Gao et al., 1994; Palloix et al., 1994; Xu et al., 1994; Sikora et al., 1998). Lower levels of loss are reported for aubergine.
Early infection by TMV may damage young tobacco plants in both nurseries and in the field. A high percentage of plants infected at, or soon after, transplanting can reduce yield by up to 50% (Lucas, 1975). Late field attacks are not infrequent and can injure the middle and apical leaves.

management_info:
敏感烟草用水杨酸前处理能阻碍TMV复制和降低系统获得抗性(Chivasa et al., 1997)。因为侵染通常由苗床开始，所以用溴甲烷或其它熏蒸剂熏蒸苗圃土壤能有效的防治TMV。 Pre-treatment of sensitive tobacco with salicylic acid interferes with TMV replication and induces systemically acquired resistance (Chivasa et al., 1997). Fumigation of nursery soil with methyl bromide or other fumigants can be an effective means of controlling TMV because infections usually begin in the seedbeds. 在一些情况下，由病原体的前侵染或水杨酸的应用诱导的系统获得性抗性(SAR)，已能有效的对抗TMV (Ward et al., 1991)。在接种和无病毒烟草的过敏性反应时会增加的水杨酸被认为是系统获得性抗性(SAR)的前导(Enyedi et al., 1992; Shulaev et al., 1995)。
接种无毒或致弱株系的TMV病毒进行交互保护可防止敏感的花叶反应被致病性强的TMV株系引起进一步的侵染(Todoroki and Chiba, 1995)。 In some cases systemic acquired resistance (SAR), induced by a previous infection with a pathogen or by application of salicylic acid, has been effective against TMV (Ward et al., 1991). Salicylic acid, levels of which increase during the hypersensitivity reaction in tobacco in both inoculated and virus-free leaves, is considered a precursor of SAR (Enyedi et al., 1992; Shulaev et al., 1995). 
Cross-protection by inoculation with avirulent or attenuated strains of TMV can prevent the sensitive mosaic reaction causing further infection with virulent strains of TMV (Todoroki and Chiba, 1995). 虽然减少氮肥施用量能减低病毒复制，但预防措施的唯一办法是防止病毒在烟草作物侵染和传播。在种植期间每隔一段时间用肥皂或牛奶清洗手和用具，去梢和其它农业栽培措施能降低TMV在作物上的传播。让定位苗床和温室远离烟草储存仓库，以及铲除周围的野草也可帮助减少接种体来源和保护敏感品种免受侵染。
种子卫生在保护番茄和辣椒苗床免受初侵染方面很有效 Prophylactic measures are the only means to prevent virus infection and spread on tobacco crops, though minimizing nitrogen fertilization may reduce viral replication. Hand and tool washing with soap or milk at intervals during planting, topping and other cultural operations reduces the spread of TMV on crops. Locating seedbeds and nurseries far away from tobacco storage warehouses and eradicating weeds around these areas may also help to reduce inoculum sources and save sensitive varieties from infection.
Seed sanitation can be effective in preserving seedbeds of tomato and pepper from primary infection.
author: zhangjianjun

description: 一般来说，TMV不会由昆虫传染，虽然跳甲，烟草跳甲（Epitrix hirtipennis）被报道为TMV的媒介昆虫。蚜虫也被报道说能在田间传播TMV(Xiao et al., 1997)。TMV的侵染速度能通过有翅蚜虫的数量来预测。 Generally, TMV is not transferred by insects, though the flea beetle, Epitrix hirtipennis, has been reported as a vector of TMV. management_info: Prevention and Sanitation^p^pA strict sanitation programme is necessary to prevent inadvertent transmission of the virus from infected to healthy plants. ^p^pCutting tools should be sterilized after cutting each inflorescence. The most effective method is to sterilize tools with heat; reusable razor blades or knives can be heated in a dry oven at 150°C for 1 h. Alternatively, knife blades can be dipped in alcohol and flamed for several seconds (Wisler et al., 1987b). Cutting tools may also be disinfected with liquid inactivating solutions. Fresh bleach (5.25% aqueous sodium hypochlorite solution) or a 1-2% sodium hydroxide solution can also inactivate ORSV effectively (Hu et al., 1994), and a mixture of bleach and 1% sodium hydroxide is also effective (Hu and Ferreira, 1994). A commercial product (Menno Florades) has also been recommended recently as an effective sterilant (Buttner and Bandte, 1999).^p^pBenches previously containing diseased plants should be disinfected, and infected plants removed and burnt (not placed on a compost heap).^p^p^Quarantine^p^pDiseased plants should be isolated from healthy plants.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pOnly a few chemicals have been reported to have antiviral activity; Virazole or ribavirin can inhibit the synthesis of ORSV (Albouy et al., 1988; Loi et al., 1991; Toussiant et al., 1993).^p^p^Production of Virus-Free Plants^p^pThin-section cultures, with or without ribavirin, of infected plantlets and protocorm-like bodies of orchids can produce ORSV-free orchids (Lim et al., 1993; Freitas-Astua and Rezende, 1998).^p^pMeristems of ORSV-infected protocorms treated with ORSV antiserum can regenerate into virus-free plants (Inouye, 1983a).^p^pGamma-ray and thermal-neutron treatment can be used to inactivate ORSV (Mori and Inouye, 1977).

description: In autumn 2018, chlorotic spots and vein chlorosis were observed on several Calibrachoa plants in the greenhouse of a nursery in North-Rhine Westphalia, Germany where only calibrachoa is cultivated. From the first mild symptoms, a severe disease developed with necrosis of leaves and wilting of entire shoots. Almost all plants in the glasshouse (c. 2000 m2) became infected rapidly leading to the total loss of the crop. The result of Bell pepper mottle virus (BPeMV) infecting Calibrachoa was confirmed by RT-PCR. In Europe, its occurrence is documented only once from the Netherlands in 1980 (Tobias et al., 1982). This is the first evidence of the occurrence of BPeMV in Germany, and the first proof that it is infectious in an ornamental plant.  The pathway of introduction of this obviously rarely occurring virus into the vegetatively propagated calibrachoa plants is so far unknown.

Even the mild strain used for cross protection in Italy has some debilitating effect on protected plants (Cartia et al., 1985).^p^pTotal infection can occur in field-grown crops resulting in greatly reduced yields of marketable fruit (Conti and Marte, 1983; Marte and Wetter, 1986)

description: Incidence ^p^pPMMV is seedborne in Capsicum annuum and C. frutescens. Avgelis (1986) reported that 100% of seeds harvested from fruits of pepper plants naturally infected by PPMV, were infected by the virus. Levels of seedborne infections ranging between 0.23 and 100% have also been reported (McKinney, 1952; Tosic et al., 1980; Paludan, 1982; Avgelis, 1986; Tanzi et al., 1990).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pNot reported.^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSeeds extracted from fruits of pepper plants naturally infected by PMMV had transmission rates as high as 36% when planted in steam-sterilized soil (Avgelis, 1986). McKinney (1952), Tosic et al. (1980) and Tanzi et al. (1990) also demonstrated seed transmission of PMMV in grow-out experiments. The level of transmission decreased markedly during seed storage. After storage for 11 months, levels of transmission in cvs Cleopatra No.4 and Yolo Wonder decreased from 36 to 12% and from 32 to 4.5%, respectively (Avgelis, 1986). ^p^pPMMV can also persist in soil in infected debris of previous crops which can be an important primary source of infection (Pares and Gunn, 1989).^p ^p^Seed Treatment^p^pHeating seeds at 80°C for 3 days inactivated PMMV. Germination, however, was significantly reduced (Avgelis, 1986). Treating seeds with trisodium phosphate reduced, but did not eliminate, the virus (Avgelis, 1986).^p^p^Seed Health Tests^p^pIndicator plants (Avgelis, 1986)^pIndividual seeds were triturated and inoculated onto leaves of Nicotiana glutinosa. Each seed was considered infected when it induced at least two lesions/plant. ^p^pGrow-out (Avgelis, 1986)^pSeeds are planted in steam-sterilized soil. Mosiac symptoms of PPMV infection appear within 30 days of emergence. ^p^pDirect immunostaining assay (Takeuchi at al., 1999)^pA new method (direct immunostaining assay, DISA) for the detection of tobamoviruses in C. annuum seeds is reported. The method allows the use of the seeds after testing. Rabbit antisera were raised against purified Tobacco mild green mosaic virus (TMGV) and Pepper mild mottle virus (PMMV). Both antisera reacted with a number of tobamoviruses including Tobacco mosaic virus, PMMV, TMGV and Tomato mosaic virus when tested. Germination of the seeds was not adversely affected by the test and sterilization of the seeds did not affect the staining of the seeds by DISA. When DISA was compared with ELISA, using 33 C. annuum cultivars, there was good agreement between the tests. It is suggested that DISA is a practical technique for the primary screening of tobamoviruses in C. annuum seeds.

remark: RISK CRITERIA 		CATEGORY^pECONOMIC IMPORTANCE	Moderate ^pDISTRIBUTION		Worldwide ^pSEEDBORNE INCIDENCE	High^pSEED TRANSMITTED	Yes^pSEED TREATMENT	Yes^p

management_info: Chemical Control^p^pPMMV can be substantially eliminated from seed coats by soaking seeds in 4.2% sodium hypochlorite for 15 min or in 10% trisodium phosphate for 30 min, or by dry-heating seed for 72 h at 70°C (Demski, 1981; Avgelis, 1986).^p^p^Physical Control^p^pTo minimize secondary spread of infection, plants infected with PMMV should be detected and removed as soon as possible. Milk, the proteins of which act as inhibitors of infection, is usually sprayed on infected and adjacent plants to reduce the possibility of accidental mechanical spread of virus when removing infected plants (Hare and Lucas, 1959; Jaeger, 1966).^p^pEfficient steam sterilization of soil can sometimes reduce the subsequent levels of infection of healthy pepper seedlings. However, it is extremely difficult to sterilize soil to a depth that eliminates virus that may be present in plant debris. Stijger (1993) has also shown that virus in fresh and dried infected pepper leaves and roots cannot be eliminated by exposure to formaldehyde, nitric acid, trisodium phosphate, hydrogen peroxide with activators and an unnamed organic acid; these results confirm the virus is extremely stable.^p^pVirus contamination of glasshouse structures can be substantially reduced by carefully swabbing their surfaces with 3% trisodium phosphate solution; great care, however, is necessary when handling this very corrosive alkali.^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pTo prevent secondary spread of infection, cultural practices should be used that minimize contact with plants by workers and equipment.^p^p^Induced Resistance^p^pAvirulent strains of PMMV, which can mitigate artificially inoculated pepper plants from the severe effects of subsequent natural infection by virulent isolates, have been obtained and used effectively in Japan (Nagai, 1987) and Italy (Tanzi et al., 1986b;Betti et al., 1991, 1992). However, even protective mild strains can have a slightly debilitating effect on artificially-infected pepper seedlings (Cartia et al., 1985).^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pNatural resistance to PMMV, although yet to be exploited commercially in Capsicum annuum, occurs in some C. chilense and C. chacoense accessions, and has been attributed to a gene located at the L locus (van den Berkmortel, 1977; Boukema, 1980; Marte et al., 1992). L3 gene mediated-resistance, the so-called hypersensitive response, is elicited by the coat protein of the virus (Berzal-Herranz et al., 1995). Such resistance is associated with the presence in resistant plants of an inhibitor of virus replication which occurs in other plant species (Gera et al., 1994).^p^pNon-conventional forms of resistance have also been found to confer resistance to PMMV in experimental systems. Thus, Nicotiana benthamiana transgenic plants containing the viral replicase gene sequence were highly resistant to PMMV or showed delayed resistance to the virus Tenllado et al., 1995, 1996). Transgenic tobacco plants expressing the coat protein gene of tobacco mosaic virus showed resistance to PMMV (Nejidat and Beachy, 1990).

description: During the 2014 and 2015 production seasons, hairy roots, root stunting symptoms, and yellowing of leaves, characteristic of Rhizomania disease, were observed on red table beet ‘Red Ace’ in fields on a commercial farm in Bonnievale, Western Cape Province, South Africa. This is the first report of BNYVV in South Africa and is a serious threat to present and future red table beet production, especially when the vector(Polymyxa betae) is present. potential_eco_desc: BNYVV causes severe damage wherever it occurs. Yield losses depend greatly on the inoculum level in the soil, the weather conditions during the season and the timing of infection. Severe infections can cause reduction in yields of 50% or more while sugar contents are reduced from 16-18% to less than 10%. Changes in physiology can lead to difficulties in extracting sugar and reduce beet value as a sugar source. BNYVV can survive in the soil for many years without any decrease in intensity. It is therefore necessary to avoid growing sugarbeet in heavily infested soils.^p^pBNYVV has shown a great capacity for local dispersal from infested fields and for spread to previously uninfested regions. For example, although the exact origin of the epidemic which has arisen since the 1970s is obscure, it is certain that large areas of beet cultivation in Europe, the USA and China were, until recently, free from BNYVV. There has been considerable spread within European countries and also in China and the USA. Its absence from certain countries and regions has been confirmed by intensive surveys. It is thus only in the last 20 years that rhizomania has developed into a serious problem in many sugarbeet-growing regions of the world (Asher, 1983).^p^pBNYVV content and/or symptom intensity have been correlated with sugar yield and polarization, leaf limpness, leaf temperature and leaf calcium content (Ahrens, 1987). Biaggi et al. (1986) reported that in eight sugarbeet genotypes, the content of BNYVV in the main storage roots (assessing glasshouse-grown material) was negatively correlated with sugar content, sucrose yield/ha, juice purity and amino nitrogen content and was positively correlated with sodium content in the same genotypes grown in the field. The disease has also been shown to reduce P and Na contents (Asher, 1993). Significant decreases in the fresh root weight of infected plants have been recorded. Root sugar content is also consistently lower in infected plants than in healthy plants (Henry, 1996).^p^pIn field trials in Yugoslavia in 1989-91, rhizomania reduced sugar and alpha-amino N contents but increased P and Na contents. In the same trials, plant density and N rate had little effect on rhizomania infection (Skrbic, 1995). Nowakowska (1944) reported that in glasshouse experiments, correlations were found between nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium contents, soil acidity and sugarbeet root infection with BNYVV transmitted by Polymyxa betae. Disease resulted in a 68% weight decrease in sugarbeet seedlings.^p^pIn 120 sugarbeet trials carried out in north-central Italy in 1986-90, rhizomania incidence increased with increasing soil pH (Biancardi et al., 1994). Harada et al. (1990) also reported that higher rates of infestation with BNYVV were associated with high soil pH. Uchino and Kanzawa (1995) examined the effect of reducing soil pH on rhizomania over a 6-year period. Soil pH was maintained at pH 6-6.5 in one field and at pH 5-5.5 in another. Rhizomania was not suppressed in the field of soil pH <5.5 in the first 2 years although the number of tap roots in which BNYVV was detected decreased compared with the control field (pH 7.4). After 3 years yellowing, caused by rhizomania, was suppressed in the field of soil pH <6 and sugar yield was higher than in the non-treatment field. After 6 consecutive years of sugarbeet crops, the population of viruliferous P. betae infected with BNYVV was estimated. Inoculum density was lower than in the control when the soil was below pH 5.5. In fields where the soil was above pH 6.5, inoculum density appeared to be intensified by continuous cultivation and higher soil pH.^p^pOther factors have also been reported to influence the spread and severity of BNYVV infection. In Belgium, rhizomania first appeared in 1984. Spread was initially slow, but appeared to accelerate from 1992.
