author: CPC2006

description: Pathogen Transmission^p^pThere is no evidence that BNYVV is seedborne. However, spread of the virus can result from soil contamination of seeds which have been produced in infested areas (Heijbroek, 1988). ^p^pBNYVV is transmitted by the soil-borne fungus Polymyxa betae. When sugarbeet plants are grown in infested fields, zoospores of the fungus are released from cystosori or resting spores and infect root hairs or epidermal cells of the roots (Keskin, 1964; Keskin and Fuchs, 1969; Barr and Asher, 1996). At that time, rootlets become infected with BNYVV carried by viruliferous zoospores. After penetration of the fungus into the root cells, plasmodia develop into zoosporangia, from which new zoospores are released within a few days (Keskin, 1964; Peters and Godfrey-Veltman, 1989).
author: CPC2006

remark: BNYVV is an EPPO A2 quarantine organism (OEPP/EPPO, 1988) but is not of quarantine significance for any other regional plant protection organization. Within the EPPO regions, sugarbeet is grown extensively and represents a major cash crop for agricultural products. Considerable areas are still free from the virus, especially in northern Europe. However, biological and epidemiological studies seem to indicate that the climate zone, where the organism can induce considerable yield losses, is defined by the temperature requirements of the pathogen. If further research in these directions confirms these suggestions, a re-evaluation of the phytosanitary risk of BNYVV would be necessary.
author: CPC2006

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl in diseased fields is unlikely to be successful by adopting cultural or agronomic practice. Some chemicals, especially soil fumigants, have been partially effective in reducing yield losses but are generally not economic. The search for tolerant or resistant cultivars has been actively carried out since 1978: the results obtained have been very encouraging. Forecasting or estimating the level of infestation which corresponds to yield losses would be helpful for selection (adaptation) of resistant varieties and other control measures.^p^p^Phytosanitary Measures^p^pPrecautionary measures should be taken to avoid contamination of healthy areas and to limit the spread of the disease in areas already infested. Areas in which beet seeds and beet stecklings are produced should be kept under constant phytosanitary observation. Any imported seed or stecklings should come from a field (or preferable region) where BNYVV does not occur. Beet seed from infested areas should be kept particularly free from impurities (soil) and should contain not more than 0.5% inert matter (other than pelleting material) in the case of certified seed and 1% in the case of basic seed (OEPP/EPPO, 1990).^p^pCountries where BNYVV does not occur would be well advised to recommend importers of vegetables from infested countries to take special precautions when disposing of waste vegetable matter, soil waste and liquid waste (MAFF, 1985).^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pThe effects of several agronomic factors and cultural practices on disease development and spread have been tested (Schlosser, 1988; Asher, 1993). The former include the soil type and pH, flooding, the level of the ground water table and the influence of ploughed meadows. The latter include crop rotation, the application of organic manure, the depth of ploughing, the date of sowing, herbicide or lime application and sprinkler irrigation. None of these factors had a significant effect, but the disease appeared to be slowed down by early sowing (Blunt et al., 1992), transplanting in paper pots (Richard-Molard, 1985: Abe, 1987) and decreasing soil pH (Abe, 1987).^p^pIn moderately or heavily infested areas, agronomic factors and cultural practices appear to be of minor, if any, importance as far as disease management is concerned. However, in areas where BNYVV is still absent or the inoculum potential is low, measures such as wider crop rotation, controlled irrigation and effective drainage can delay the spread and incidence of the disease.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pA large number of trials of potentially fungitoxic or fungistatic chemicals applied to seed or soil has been carried out in almost all the countries where rhizomania is a problem (Schlosser, 1988; Asher, 1993). Several fungicides have shown an activity against Polymyxa betae in vitro and in glasshouse trials, but none have yet proved sufficiently effective to give yield benefits under field conditions.^p^pIn general, soil fumigants such as dichloropropene, dichloropropene and dichloropropane (D-D), dazomet, metham sodium, chloropicrin and methyl bromide have been effective. For example, dichloropropene is routinely used to reduce damage in California (Martin and Whitney, 1990). Methyl bromide treatment reduced BNYVV in the soil in the first outbreak of the disease in the UK (Henry et al., 1992). In Japan, D-D or dazomet, together with sulfur application to soil to decrease the pH to below 6.0 is recommended for the partial eradication of the disease from discrete patches within infested fields (Abe, 1987). Such treatments of fumigants may be economically worthwhile where the disease is widespread and no other control measures are available. However, they are only partially effective because, although resting spores of the fungus in the upper layers of the soil may be killed, reinfestation from lower layers occurs during the growing season, and treatments must be repeated with every crop cycle.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance

management_info: 一些在病害发展和传播中的农艺因素和栽培操作的影响已被测试(Schlosser, 1988; Asher, 1993)。前者包括土壤类型和PH值、灌溉、土地地下水水位水平以及耕犁草地的影响。后者包括作物轮作、有机肥料的应用、耕作的深度、播种的日期、除草剂和石灰的应用以及晒水灌溉。这些因素当中没有一个有明显的效果，但病害的显示因提早播种 (Blunt et al., 1992)、纸罐中的移植(Richard-Molard, 1985: Abe, 1987)以及降低土壤PH值(Abe, 1987) 而有所减少。 The effects of several agronomic factors and cultural practices on disease development and spread have been tested (Schlosser, 1988; Asher, 1993). The former include the soil type and pH, flooding, the level of the ground water table and the influence of ploughed meadows. The latter include crop rotation, the application of organic manure, the depth of ploughing, the date of sowing, herbicide or lime application and sprinkler irrigation. None of these factors had a significant effect, but the disease appeared to be slowed down by early sowing (Blunt et al., 1992), transplanting in paper pots (Richard-Molard, 1985: Abe, 1987) and decreasing soil pH (Abe, 1987). 通常，土壤熏剂如二氯丙稀、滴－滴混剂（D-D）、棉隆、威百亩、氯化钴和甲基溴化物，是有效的。在病害广泛分布以及没有其他方法可利用的情况下，熏剂的这些处理在经济上是值得的。然而，它们只是部分的有效，因为，虽然在土壤上层的真菌的休眠孢子被杀死了，但来自较低层的再侵染在生长季节期间发生，而处理必须在每一个作物循环中重复。 In general, soil fumigants such as dichloropropene, dichloropropene and dichloropropane (D-D), dazomet, metham sodium, chloropicrin and methyl bromide have been effective. Such treatments of fumigants may be economically worthwhile where the disease is widespread and no other control measures are available. However, they are only partially effective because, although resting spores of the fungus in the upper layers of the soil may be killed, reinfestation from lower layers occurs during the growing season, and treatments must be repeated with every crop cycle. 通常，目前产生的抗性和耐病性品种在正常条件下的产量比标准的品种的产量少大约10％。于是，植物育种者不断的努力应该能确保，通过常规育种或生物工艺学方法，具更高产量和更具抗性的新品种将会在不久的将来产生(Asher, 1993)。一种利用P. betae的游动孢子悬浮液的接种方法适合于BNYVV的高抗性水平的添加物的筛选(Paul et al., 1992, 1993)。 In general, resistant and tolerant cultivars which have so far been developed yield about 10% less than standard cultivars in normal conditions. Therefore, the continuing effort of plant breeders should ensure that new varieties that are higher yielding and more resistant will be developed either by conventional breeding or biotechnological methods in the near future (Asher, 1993). description: Following the recent discovery of the Rice stripe necrosis virus (RSNV) in Burkina Faso and Benin, a targeted rice-associated soil sampling campaign was launched in January 2016 in order to assess the presence of RNSV and its vector in Mali. The samples were collected from rain fed rice (Oryza sativa) from three places around Bamako where RSNV-like symptoms had been reported. Farmers’ reported symptoms were crinkling, distortion, and necrosis of young leaves, and midrib chlorosis, sometimes associated with strong dwarfism. Base on bio-assay, microscope and PCR indicated that the presence of RSNV  with Polymyxa graminis f.sp. colombiana.
reference_name: Detection of the Rice stripe necrosis virus Causing Rice Crinkle Disease and its Vector Polymyxa graminis f. sp. colombiana in Mali
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Oryza sativa
potential_eco_desc: Disease incidence in the field was estimated to be 80 ± 5% on rice plants in an experimental field of INERA at Banfora located in western Burkina Faso.
description: During a survey carried out in April of 2013, severe symptoms characterized by seedling death, severe plant malformation, and foliar striping were observed on rice plants in an experimental field of INERA at Banfora located in western Burkina Faso. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Rice stripe necrosis virus (RSNV). To our knowledge, this is the first confirmed report of RSNV in Burkina Faso.  Rice stripe necrosis virus is a soil-borne virus transmitted by the fungus Polymyxa graminis.
reference_name: First Report of Rice stripe necrosis virus Infecting Rice in Burkina Faso

Red Delicious showing dappling, crinkling and irregular yellow spots on their fruits. The samples were collected from two orchards in the area of Maragheh, northwest Iran. Based on sequences analysis confirming that the pathogen was Apple dimple fruit viroid (ADFVd). To our knowledge, this is the first report of ADFVd in apple trees in Iran.

management_info: 这个病原物以感病动植物的材料的途径传入到新的区域里。因此，一个适当并有效的防治措施需要利用无类病毒的材料。因为通过早期在田间为了降低其种子散步而对感病植株根除的探测，得出ADFVd似乎不是广泛传播的。不受感染的修剪工具的利用避免了类病毒在其已存在的田间上短途传播。 The pathogen is introduced to new areas as infected propagation material. Therefore, an appropriate and effective control method requires the use of viroid-free material. Because ADFVd does not seem to be widespread, early detection in the field followed by eradication of infected plants may delay its dissemination. The use of disinfected pruning tools avoids short distance spread of the viroid in the fields where it is already present.

description:
ADFVd存活在田间感病植物，它重要通过农业耕作传染健康植株上。ADFVd缓慢的散播已经在果树园里发现出来了。与ASSVd相似，它是不通过种子传播或在很低的几率里传播(Hurtt and Podleckis, 1995; Howell et al., 1998; Desvignes et al., 1999)，ADFVd花粉或种子的传播不可能是它的主要散播途径。
受类病毒感染的繁殖材料的销售适合ADFVd的长途扩散，可到达之前该病毒不存在的区域。在田间，没有消毒的修剪工具能够将病毒从一株植物带到另一株植物上。 ADFVd survives in infected plants in the field and is mainly transmitted to healthy plants by agricultural practices. A slow dissemination of ADFVd has been observed in orchards. By analogy with ASSVd, which is not seed transmitted or is transmitted at very low rate (Hurtt and Podleckis, 1995; Howell et al., 1998; Desvignes et al., 1999), it is unlikely that pollen or seed transmission of ADFVd play a major role in its dissemination. 
The distribution of viroid-infected propagation material favours ADFVd dissemination over long distances and into areas where it was previously absent. Pruning tools which have not been disinfected may spread the viroid from plant to plant in the field.
author: zhangjianjun

description: In a recent survey, leaf of Vitis vinifera samples were collected from the three popular grape cultivars (Thompson Seedless, Sharad Seedless, and Flame Seedless) exhibiting yellowing, vein banding, yellow speckle, and downward curling symptoms in the glasshouse at the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) New Delhi. Based on molecular identifications confirmed the presence of Grapevine yellow speckle viroid-2 (GYSVd-2) in the samples. This is the first report of GYSVd-2 in India.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine Yellow Speckle Viroid-2 Infecting Grapevine (Vitis vinifera) in India
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Vitis vinifera cvs. Black Opal seedless, Black Queen and Pok Dum.
potential_eco_desc: Disease incidence in all vineyards is very low (<1%).
description: Grapevine yellow speckle viroid-1 (GYSVd-1) have been reported to infect grapevine in Thailand. From February through March 2014, 22 grapevine leaf samples (Vitis vinifera cvs. Black Opal seedless, Black Queen and Pok Dum) were sampled from eight vineyards in Saraburi (4 samples) and Nakhon Ratchasima (18 samples) provinces, which are the major grapevine plantation regions in Thailand. The test results revealed that 6/22 grapevine leaf samples were infected solely with GYSVd-2. 5/22 samples had mixed GYSVd-1 and GYSVd-2 infections. This is the first report of GYSVd-2 infecting grapevine in Thailand.
reference_name: First report of Grapevine yellow speckle viroid-2 infecting grapevine (Vitis vinifera) in Thailand

management_info:
病原通过健康的繁殖材料的使用（标定指数方案），且若需要，感病的果树的移除而被控制。
受ASSVd侵染的苹果材料的热治疗会有效的只要植株最初发生于休眠期在热治疗和芽尖端的嫁接之前(Howell et al., 1998a)。在梨中，在在玻璃容器中随着顶点的分裂组织培养的热治疗能被用来消除该类病毒(Postman and Hadidi, 1995)。 The causal agent is controlled through the use of healthy propagation materials (indexing programmes) and, if necessary, the removal of diseased trees.
Heat therapy of ASSVd-infected apple materials can be effective as long as plants are first subject to a dormant stage before heat therapy and shoot-tip grafting (Howell et al., 1998a). In pear, in vitro therapy followed by apical meristem culture can be used to eliminate the viroid (Postman and Hadidi, 1995).

potential_eco_desc: 在敏感的栽培种，该类病毒的侵染造成果实大小及质量的大大降低。在ASSVd普遍流行的中国和日本地区中，该类病毒已造成严重的经济损失。通常受ASSVd影响的果树的全部作物是滞销的(Han et al., 2003; Koganezawa et al., 2003)。 In sensitive cultivars, infection with the viroid causes significant reductions in fruit size and quality. In areas of China and Japan where ASSVd is prevalent, the viroid has caused serious economic losses. Usually the entire crop from ASSVd-affected trees is unmarketable (Han et al., 2003; Koganezawa et al., 2003).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
在人类移动的期间，类病毒通过感染植株的发芽和嫁接传播。接种周期为2-3年(N閙eth, 1986 )。当该类病毒已被探测于苹果和梨种子样本中时，它不被显示是种子传播的(Hadidi et al., 1991; Howell et al., 1998b; Koganezawa et al., 2003)。同样地，在东方梨中没有种子传播的证据(Hurtt and Podleckis, 1995)。
没有昆虫传播媒介被知道，但根嫁接可能导致相当缓慢的田间传播(McCrum, 1989)。在希腊的部分该类病毒已被发现于野生的梨中在隔离的地区中，指出那里可能由自然传播的若干方式(Kyriakopoulou et al., 2003)。 In terms of human movement, the viroid spreads through budding and grafting from infected plants. The incubation period is 2-3 years (N閙eth, 1986 ). While the viroid has been detected in apple and pear seed samples, it has not been shown to be seed-transmitted (Hadidi et al., 1991; Howell et al., 1998b; Koganezawa et al., 2003). Similarly, there is no evidence of seed-transmission in oriental pear (Hurtt and Podleckis, 1995).
No insect vector is known, but root grafts may lead to some slow field spread (McCrum, 1989). In parts of Greece the viroid has been found in wild pear in isolated areas, suggesting that there may be some means of natural transmission (Kyriakopoulou et al., 2003).

host_range: In addition to Campbell Early grapevine cultivars and rootstock 188-08, GYSVd1 and HSVd were also found in the newly developed cultivars Jarang and Jungrang. Other than this, Ixeridium dentatum is a natural host for GYSVd1 and HSVd.
description: In June 2016, grapevine leaf samples from two popular cultivars in Korea, Campbell Early and Jaok, and rootstock 188-08 obtained from the Grape Research Institute, Okcheon, Korea, and the Sangju National Agricultural Cooperative Federation, Sangju, Korea, were collected and tested to determine their viroid status. Based on molecular diagnostics confirmed that except Jaok from the Grapevine Research Institute, samples were coinfected by  Grapevine yellow speckle viroid 1 (GYSVd1) and Hop stunt viroid (HSVd). This is the first report of GYSVd1 and HSVd infecting grapevines in Korea.  Ixeridium dentatum is a natural host for the two viroids and that it might be involved in the transmission of the two viroids.

author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

description: Grapevine yellow speckle viroid-1 (GYSVd-1) have been reported to infect grapevine in Thailand. From February through March 2014, 22 grapevine leaf samples (Vitis vinifera cvs. Black Opal seedless, Black Queen and Pok Dum) were sampled from eight vineyards in Saraburi (4 samples) and Nakhon Ratchasima (18 samples) provinces, which are the major grapevine plantation regions in Thailand. The test results revealed that 3/22 grapevine leaf samples were infected with GYSVd-1. Five of the 22 samples had mixed GYSVd-1 and GYSVd-2 infections. All of the GYSVd-1 and GYSVd-2 infections were only found in Nakhon Ratchasima province.

potential_eco_desc: 病株生长受阻，果小而少，或不孕。
我国各地普遍发生，其中尤以河北省的鸭梨、辽宁省的秋白梨产区受害最为严重，在不防治或防治不彻底的情况下常引起严重损失。
description: 孢子借风雨传播。
management_info:
1.清洁果园 秋天树叶落地后清除果园落叶并烧毁或深埋。
2.摘除病梢 发病初期及时摘除基部呈现黑霉的病梢，病梢鳞片不落，正常梢鳞片脱落，很易发现。一般年份，病梢数目并不多，一棵树只有数个或稍多，迅速将之摘除，即在新出现的分生孢子尚未进行重复侵染之前摘除，可以有效减轻以后病害的发生。在辽宁省，摘除病梢的时间约从5月中旬开始；黄河故道地区从4月上中旬起要经常巡视果园，一旦发现，立即摘除。
3.药剂防治。在梨树花前、花后各喷一次1:2:200-240倍式波尔多液、50%多菌灵可湿性粉剂500-800倍液、50%甲基硫菌灵(甲基托布津)可湿性粉剂500-800倍液、50%退菌特可湿性粉剂600-800倍液。配置波尔多液要选用生石灰，最好附加5000倍皮胶或其他粘着剂以增加粘着性能。波尔多液的铜离子对黑星病菌的分生孢子很敏感，波尔多液药效持久，无抗性问题，多为自配自用，为果农乐于使用。北方梨区，一般第一次喷要在5月中下旬(白梨病梢初现期)，第二次在6月中旬，第三次在6月末至7月上旬，第四次在8月上旬。我国南方黑星病发生较早，应在梨树接近开花前和落花70%左右各喷一次药液，以保护花序、嫩梢和新叶。以后根据降雨情况，每隔15-20天喷药一次，先后喷4次。

potential_eco_desc: Chrysanthemum stunt was first recognized in the USA in 1945 (Dimock, 1947), and a disastrous epidemic in cultivated chrysanthemums developed during 1945-1947 (Brierley and Smith, 1949). The disease spread rapidly, first to Canada and in the 1950s to all areas of the world where chrysanthemums are grown, probably through the international transport of cuttings (Lawson, 1987). The induction of early flowering has serious consequences for producers of cut flowers and, to a lesser extent, for growers of pot plants. ^p^pFigures on yield loss are difficult to find; one of the reasons for this may be, that CSVd often occurs together with several chrysanthemum viruses. management_info: Control of the disease is extremely difficult due to its highly contagious nature, the long latent period, the vegetative propagation of chrysanthemum, and the fact that natural resistance or tolerance to CSVd has not been found. Consequently, control measures primarily consist of efforts to prevent transmission by hands, tools and plant-to-plant contact (Lawson, 1987). Most important for nurseries is the prevention of the introduction of CSVd in plant material from elsewhere, for example, for breeding purposes. ^p^pHeat treatment is not effective, as CSVd is very heat-tolerant: it withstands 10 minutes at ca 98°C (Brierley, 1952; Hollings and Stone, 1973). ^p^pSeveral ways to free plants from the viroid have been published, although with low rates of success:^p(a) meristem-tip culture after heat-treatment (Hollings and Stone, 1970);^p(b) meristem-tip culture (Bachelier et al., 1976; Lawson, 1987); ^p(c) cold treatment of plants at 5°C for at least 4 months, followed by meristem culture (Lizarraga et al., 1980; Paludan 1980, 1985; Paduch-Cichal and Kryczynski, 1987). Paludan (1985) stated that he obtained 67% CSVd-free plants by the application of this combined treatment. ^p^pDetection methods for CSVd, however, were not very advanced in 1985. Treatment of Argyranthemum frutescens plants at 4°C for 6 months, followed by meristem culture and repetition of the combined treatment after failure did not lead to viroid-free plants (A van Zaayen, Naktuinbouw, the Netherlands: unpublished results in 2000). ^p^pIn the Netherlands, CSVd-free plants are selected by visual inspection of the flowering crop. The reliability of this visual inspection can reach 90-95%, depending on the expertise of the inspector. Suspect plants are tested by R-PAGE (Roenhorst et al., 2000). The Dutch certification system is described by Van Ruiten (1996).^p^pAccording to the certification schemes presented by EPPO, every plant of the nuclear stock should be tested by grafting or R-PAGE once, and propagation and certified stock are advised to be randomly tested in the same way as nuclear stock (OEPP/EPPO, 1993). ^p^pFor details of phytosanitary measures, see OEPP/EPPO, 1990.

The disease spread rapidly, first to Canada and in the 1950s to all areas of the world where chrysanthemums are grown, probably through the international transport of cuttings (Lawson, 1987). CSVd seriously affects the plants and flowers of several cultivars. In some cultivars the plants are severely stunted, yielding a product that cannot be sold. (1996) 引述了一个在1987年由于CSVd的发生而导致了澳大利亚菊类工业上接近3千万美元的损失。 Figures on yield loss are difficult to find; one of the reasons for this may be, that CSVd often occurs together with several chrysanthemum viruses. author: zhangjianjun

description:
在田间CSVd能够通过叶片接触而传播(Hollings and Stone, 1973)。
没有迹象说明CSVd能够由昆虫介体传播。Brierley 及 Smith (1949)最初报道29%的传播是由蚜虫Rhopalosiphum rufomaculatum传播，但后来更正了这个错误(Brierley and Smith, 1951)。
Keller (1949)报道这是由螨类传播的，但是Hollings 和 Stone (1973)不能证实这个观点。
是否由种媒传播的这个可能性还不清楚：Monsion et al. (1973)报道在菊类上的种子传播上升到11%，而Hollings 和 Stone (1973)发现没有种子传播的迹象。在番茄上，CSVd能通过花粉和种子来传播(Kryczynski et al., 1988)。
CSVd容易地通过汁液传播。在栽培期间，它能够通过在摘芽期间受污染的手及在修剪期间的刀子来传播。它很容易通过嫁接传播(Brierley and Smith, 1949)。将修剪刀具浸在2%的酯胶(TSP)或2%甲醛溶液中2-3秒钟或在修剪	前将手浸入2% TSP中都不能阻止传播(Hollings and Stone, 1973)。
国际间的传播能归因于移植感病的菊类植株和插条。CSVd也能存在于其他种类的植物材料上。 In the field CSVd can be spread by foliar contact (Hollings and Stone, 1973).
There is no evidence that CSVd can be transmitted by insect vectors. Brierley and Smith (1949) first reported transmission of 29% by the aphid Rhopalosiphum rufomaculatum, but later corrected this error (Brierley and Smith, 1951).
Keller (1949) reported transmission by dodder, but this could not be confirmed by Hollings and Stone (1973).
It is not clear whether seedborne spread is possible: Monsion et al. (1973) reported seed transmission in chrysanthemum up to 11%, while Hollings and Stone (1973) found no evidence for seed transmission. In tomato CSVd can be transmitted by pollen and seed (Kryczynski et al., 1988).
CSVd is readily transmitted by sap. During cultivation it can be transmitted on contaminated hands while disbudding and on knives in the course of taking cuttings. It is easily transmitted by grafting (Brierley and Smith, 1949). Dipping cutting knives in a solution of 2% trisodium orthophosphate (TSP) or in 2% formaldehyde for 2-3 sec or dipping hands in 2% TSP before taking cuttings failed to prevent transmission (Hollings and Stone, 1973).
International spread can result from transplanting infected chrysanthemum plants and cuttings. CSVd may also be present in plant material of other species.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
由于它对自然的高度传染性，长时期的潜伏侵染，菊花的生长繁殖，及CSVd的自然抵抗力或忍耐力事实的发现，使得这种病害的防治极端困难。结果，防治估量主要在于防止由手，工具和植物之间的接触传染(Lawson, 1987)。育苗场的重要性是防止其他地方的植物材料上的CSVd引入，例如，繁殖用途的材料。
热处理是没有效果的，这是由于CSVd非常耐热：它能够经受住10分钟的大约98℃的环境(Brierley, 1952; Hollings and Stone, 1973)。
虽然低成功率，但从类病毒上分离植物的几种方法已被公布：
(a)	经过热处理后的分裂组织栽培(Hollings and Stone, 1970)；
(b)	分裂组织栽培(Bachelier et al., 1976; Lawson, 1987)；
(c)	在5℃的环境下冷冻处理植物最少4个月，然后分裂组织栽培(Liz醨raga et al., 1980; Paludan 1980, 1985; Paduch-Cichal and Kryczynski, 1987)。
Paludan (1985)征实他通过这联合处理的应用获得了67% 没有CSVd的植株。
然而，CSVd的探测方法在1985年不是很先进。木茼蒿植株在4℃下处理6个月，然后分裂组织栽培及在没有导致不含类病毒植株的这个失败出现后这联合处理的循环应用(A van Zaayen, Naktuinbouw, the Netherlands: unpublished results in 2000)。
在荷兰，没有CSVd的植株通过开花作物的外形检查而选取出来。依靠检查员的专业技术，使得这外形检查的可靠性能够达到90-95%。通过R-PAGE测试可疑的植物(Roenhorst et al., 2000)。荷兰鉴征系统由Van Ruiten (1996)描述出来。
根据EPPO存在的鉴征方案，每种细胞核树干的植物应该通过嫁接或R-PAGE测试一次，及动植物和已检定的树干建议以细胞核的树干这相同的方法来随便地测试(OEPP/EPPO, 1993)
检疫措施详细资料请参见OEPP/EPPO, 1990。 Control of the disease is extremely difficult due to its highly contagious nature, the long latent period, the vegetative propagation of chrysanthemum, and the fact that natural resistance or tolerance to CSVd has not been found. Consequently, control measures primarily consist of efforts to prevent transmission by hands, tools and plant-to-plant contact (Lawson, 1987). Most important for nurseries is the prevention of the introduction of CSVd in plant material from elsewhere, for example, for breeding purposes. 
Heat treatment is not effective, as CSVd is very heat-tolerant: it withstands 10 minutes at ca 98℃ (Brierley, 1952; Hollings and Stone, 1973). 
Several ways to free plants from the viroid have been published, although with low rates of success:
(a) meristem-tip culture after heat-treatment (Hollings and Stone, 1970);
(b) meristem-tip culture (Bachelier et al., 1976; Lawson, 1987); 
(c) cold treatment of plants at 5℃ for at least 4 months, followed by meristem culture (Liz醨raga et al., 1980; Paludan 1980, 1985; Paduch-Cichal and Kryczynski, 1987). 
Paludan (1985) stated that he obtained 67% CSVd-free plants by the application of this combined treatment. 
Detection methods for CSVd, however, were not very advanced in 1985. Treatment of Argyranthemum frutescens plants at 4℃ for 6 months, followed by meristem culture and repetition of the combined treatment after failure did not lead to viroid-free plants (A van Zaayen, Naktuinbouw, the Netherlands: unpublished results in 2000). 
In the Netherlands, CSVd-free plants are selected by visual inspection of the flowering crop. The reliability of this visual inspection can reach 90-95%, depending on the expertise of the inspector. Suspect plants are tested by R-PAGE (Roenhorst et al., 2000). The Dutch certification system is described by Van Ruiten (1996).
According to the certification schemes presented by EPPO, every plant of the nuclear stock should be tested by grafting or R-PAGE once, and propagation and certified stock are advised to be randomly tested in the same way as nuclear stock (OEPP/EPPO, 1993). 
For details of phytosanitary measures, see OEPP/EPPO, 1990.

description: Pospiviroids, including the quarantine regulated Potato spindle tuber viroid (PSTVd), have recently been shown to cause symptomless infections of various ornamental plant species in Europe. In order to investigate the viroid status of a variety of solanaceous crops, ornamental plants and weed hosts in Australia, a national survey was conducted during 2012, and to our knowledge, this is the first report of pospiviroids infecting ornamental plants in Australia, and the first report of CEVd naturally infecting Petunia spp. Here report survey findings from the state of Queensland, where sampling was conducted between June to September 2012.

potential_eco_desc: Economic damage results when a scion variety infected with CEV is grafted onto susceptible rootstocks.^p^pIn a case study in Belize, CEV-infected budwood was brought into the country and propagated on Carrizo citrange rootstock, which is susceptible to CEV. The management/grove keeping costs were then compared on a block established with the CEV-infected budwood and a grove of the same variety established on Carrizo citrange rootstock under the same owner/management system. Both blocks were planted at 225 trees per hectare. After 8 years, the block established with the CEV-infected budwood had a total loss of US$ 5147 per hectare while the block propagated with viroid-free budwood had a total return of US$ 10,898 per hectare (Roistacher et al., 1995).

potential_eco_desc:
经济损失由于一个嫁接苗受到CEV侵染而变种，并且其被嫁接到易受感染的根茎上。
在伯利兹的一个研究例子中，受到CEV侵染的接芽母树被带到城市里并嫁接到对CEV 易感病的卡里佐枳橙根茎处。这个处理/果园持续损失后来比作的感染CEV接芽母树障碍物和在相同拥有者/处理系统的一个确定相同种类的卡里佐枳橙根茎的果园。相互之间的阻碍物都被种上每公顷225课树。8年后，确定为CEV感染的接芽母树的阻碍物达到了每公顷5147美元的总损失，而阻碍物与没有感病的接芽母树共同繁殖达到了每公顷10,898美元的总收益。 Economic damage results when a scion variety infected with CEV is grafted onto susceptible rootstocks.
In a case study in Belize, CEV-infected budwood was brought into the country and propagated on Carrizo citrange rootstock, which is susceptible to CEV. The management/grove keeping costs were then compared on a block established with the CEV-infected budwood and a grove of the same variety established on Carrizo citrange rootstock under the same owner/management system. Both blocks were planted at 225 trees per hectare. After 8 years, the block established with the CEV-infected budwood had a total loss of US$ 5147 per hectare while the block propagated with viroid-free budwood had a total return of US$ 10,898 per hectare (Roistacher et al., 1995).
author: zhangjianjun

description:
自然散播是通过受类病毒感染的苗圃材料的转移和受病毒污染的刀具，耕作设备及其他修剪工具而扩散。通过受病毒污染的修剪工具的机械传播从一株易受感染的寄主植株到令一株植株上时，如枸橼(Citrus medica)比起从一个甜橙(Citrus sinensis)到另一个的机率更大。
类病毒是热稳定的。在染病的紫鹅绒抽液上的热量失活点是90-100℃10分钟。CEV仍然在受污染的修剪刀具上最少16小时(Garnsey, 1968)，甚至8天的传染性(Allen, 1968)。
CEV还没有被报道为种子传播。
CEV已通过菟丝子(Cuscuta subinclusa)从一株柑橘上传到另一株柑橘上及从柑橘上传到牵牛花上(Weathers, 1965; Weathers et al., 1967
用于生长繁殖的柑橘幼苗材料可能受到CEV的侵染，及应当根据柑橘种质安全贸易的指导方针所建议的手续将其引进到新区域(Frison and Taher, 1991)。 Natural dissemination is by movement of viroid-infected nursery materials and the use of infested knives, pruning equipment and other cutting tools.  Mechanical spread by infested cutting tools is greater when going from one susceptible host to another such at Etrog citron (Citrus medica), than from one sweet orange (Citrus sinensis) to another.
The viroid is heat stable. The thermal inactivation point is 90-100℃ for 10 minutes in infected Gynura aurantiaca sap. CEV remained infective on a contaminated cutting blade for at least 16 hours (Garnsey, 1968) and for up to 8 days (Allen, 1968).
Seed transmission has not been reported for CEV.
CEV has been transmitted from citrus to citrus and citrus to petunia by dodder (Cuscuta subinclusa) (Weathers, 1965; Weathers et al., 1967).
Citrus nursery material used for vegetative propagation of plants may be infected with CEV and should only be imported into new areas following the procedures recommended in the Guidelines for Safe Movement of Citrus Germplasm (Frison and Taher, 1991).
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
管理一定要实行去不使已知的易受CEV污染根茎的抽芽材料传播。
由于CEV容易通过受到污染的刀具和修剪工具的机械传播，管理一定要在整理或修剪另一株植物之前要实行对工具消毒。含钠次氯酸盐或其他杀菌剂已被证实在应该使用的修剪工具上能有效地使类病毒钝化(van der Vyver and van Vuuren, 1999)。 Care must be taken not to propagate budsources known to be contaminated with CEV onto susceptible rootstocks.
As CEV is easily mechanically transmitted on contaminated knives and cutting equipment, care must be taken to sterilize equipment before trimming or cutting another plant. Sodium hypochlorite or another sterilant that has been proven to effectively inactivate viroids on cutting tools should be used (van der Vyver and van Vuuren, 1999). 虽然大多数柑橘类植株容易感染CEV，但只有柑桔属和hybrids containing P. trifoliata，酸橙，柠檬和香橼是显示症状的寄主。在中国，在茶枝柑(C. reticulata)和枳之间的属间混合的细胞体已产生对CEV有忍耐性的三叶样式根茎(Guo et al., 2002)。 Although most Citrus species are susceptible to CEV, only Poncirus trifoliata and hybrids containing P. trifoliata, limes, lemons and citrons are symptomatic hosts. In China, intergeneric somatic hybrids between red tangerine (C. reticulata) and P. trifoliata have been produced to create a trifoliate-type rootstock that has tolerance for CEV (Guo et al., 2002). 清理库存品和包括保证程序有效地防治类病毒如同防治作为嫁接传播的病原物并且使它从母树上灭绝的CEV那么长久。重复的指示一定要实行去保证母树不再受感染。 Clean stock and certification programmes effectively control viroids as long as CEV is included as a target graft transmissible pathogen to eliminate it from mother trees. Repeated indexing must be done to ensure that mother trees don not become reinfected.
author: zhangjianjun

host_range: 番茄（Solanum lycopersicon cv. Juanita）。
description:

description: During a survey conducted in October 2013 in tomato greenhouses in Diano Marina (Imola Province, northwest Italy), in a single greenhouse, unusual disease symptoms were observed in four out 1,400 (~0.3%) of tomato plants cv. Ingrid, grafted on ‘Beaufort’ rootstock. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Tomato apical stunt viroid. host_range: HSVd affects grapevine, peach, sweet cherry, apricot, cucumber, and almond, causing serious diseases. This is the first report of HSVd affecting strawberry plants.
description: In the autumn of 2016 and 2017, severe shrinking and chlorotic and yellowing symptoms resembling viroid infections were observed on strawberry plants in Linyi and Weifang, Shandong Province, China. Samples were collected from exhibiting yellowing plants. The total RNA was extracted from samples. Based on molecular diagnostics, the presence of Hop stunt viroid (HSVd) was confirmed. To our knowledge, this is the first report of HSVd affecting strawberry plants in China.
reference_name: First Report of Hop Stunt Viroid Infecting Strawberry in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: HSVd has been identified in at least 17 plant species, such as citrus, grapevine, apricot, plum, and peach species, from 38 countries.
description: In a survey of viruses and viroids in Japanese apricot (Prunus mume) trees during September 2015, leaf samples from two plants representing two cultivars, Takada and Wallyoung, were collected from an orchard in Korea. Based on the sequencing results from using the PCR amplicon, Hop stunt viroid(HSVd) were identified in two isolates Takada and Wallyoung. To our knowledge, this is the first report of HSVd associated with Japanese apricot.
reference_name: First Report of Hop stunt viroid in Japanese Apricot (Prunus mume) in Korea
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: In addition to Campbell Early grapevine cultivars and rootstock 188-08, GYSVd1 and HSVd were also found in the newly developed cultivars Jarang and Jungrang. Other than this, Ixeridium dentatum is a natural host for GYSVd1 and HSVd.
description: In June 2016, grapevine leaf samples from two popular cultivars in Korea, Campbell Early and Jaok, and rootstock 188-08 obtained from the Grape Research Institute, Okcheon, Korea, and the Sangju National Agricultural Cooperative Federation, Sangju, Korea, were collected and tested to determine their viroid status. Based on molecular diagnostics confirmed that except Jaok from the Grapevine Research Institute, samples were coinfected by  Grapevine yellow speckle viroid 1 (GYSVd1) and Hop stunt viroid (HSVd). This is the first report of GYSVd1 and HSVd infecting grapevines in Korea.  Ixeridium dentatum is a natural host for the two viroids and that it might be involved in the transmission of the two viroids.
reference_name: First Report of Grapevine yellow speckle viroid 1 and Hop stunt viroid Infecting Grapevines (Vitis vinifera) in Korea
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: HSVd has a wide host range that includes hop, cucumber, citrus, grapevine, plum, pear, peach, apricot, and almond， and has also been isolated from sweet and sour cherry trees.
description: In May 2010, sweet cherry trees (Prunus avium  cv. Red-lamp) exhibiting dapple fruit disease were observed in a suburban orchard in Tai’an, Shandong Province, China. Following grafting of scions from the diseased trees onto healthy trees, dapple fruit symptoms developed in fruits of grafted trees 2 to 3 years post grafting. Samples were collected from dapple fruit trees. Based on molecular diagnostics showed the presence of Hop stunt viroid (HSVd). To our knowledge, this is the first report of HSVd-infected sweet cherry trees in China.
reference_name: First Report of Hop stunt viroid From Sweet Cherry With Dapple Fruit Symptoms in China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Trees in the genus Prunus, including apricot, cherry, peach, and plum, are hosts for many different viruses and several viroids, such as Apple scar skin viroid (ASSVd), Hop stunt viroid (HSVd), and Peach latent mosaic viroid (PLMVd). In Korea, PLMVd infections in peach trees have recently been reported; however, HSVd infections in peach trees have not been reported until now, this is the first report of HSVd infection in peach trees in Korea.
description: Recently, we performed RNA-Seq to identify viruses and viroids infecting peach trees. We collected leaf samples from five popular peach cultivars—Mibaek, Janghowon, Cheonjung, Cheonhong, and Baekcheon—grown in three different regions in Korea during May 2013. The BLAST results using amplified PCR products confirmed the HSVd infection. To the best of our knowledge, our study represents the first report of HSVd infection in peach trees in Korea.
reference_name: First Report of Hop stunt viroid in Peach Trees in Korea
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Citrus volkameriana
potential_eco_desc: About 75 percent of the C.volkameriana rootstocks showed gumming and stem pitting symptoms.
description: In 2008, gumming and stem pitting were observed on the trunk of C.volkameriana rootstocks grafted with Valencia sweet orange in citrus orchards in South Sinai, Behera, Monufia and Ismailia governorates. About 75 percent of the rootstocks showed these symptoms. The samples were collected and identified, the pathogen was Hop stunt viroid. This is the first record of Hop stunt viroid associated with gumming and stem pitting on C. volkameriana in Egypt.
reference_name: First record of a Hop stunt viroid variant associated with gumming and stem pitting on Citrus volkameriana trunk rootstock in Egypt

description: In 2017 routine viroid testing at a tissue culture facility in the UK, included four dahlia lines from three cultivars and found Dahlia latent viroid (DLVd) and Potato spindle tuber viroid (PSTVd) in different cultivars using RT-PCR. This report represents the first finding of DLVd in the UK and PSTVd in dahlia in the UK.
reference_name: Dahlia latent viroid and Potato spindle tuber viroid in dahlia plants in the UK
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: Dahlia (Asteraceae).
description: Two viroids belonging to the family Pospiviroidae, Potato pindle tuber viroid (PSTVd) and Dahlia latent viroid (DLVd), were identified separately from dahlia plants in Japan and in the Netherlands, respectively (Tsushima et al., 2011; Verhoeven et al., 2013). The dahlia leaf samples were collected from fields around Japan, irrespective of disease symptoms, and verified by molecular diagnostics assay showed that DLVd is widespread in Japan. To evaluate the pathogenicity of DLVd and PSTVd, these viroids were co-inoculated into dahlia seedlings, the results showed positive for both DLVd and PSTVd and showed mild leaf curling in the early stage of growth. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of DLVd infecting commercial dahlia in Japan and also of the mixed-infection of DLVd and PSTVd in commercial dahlia plants.
reference_name: First report of Dahlia latent viroid and Potato spindle tuber viroid mixed-infection in commercial ornamental dahlia in Japan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

description: Previously, CbVd-1 and CbVd-5 were detected in coleus plants, collected at a local nursery in Fredericton, New Brunswick, Canada. Recently, pooled leaf samples collected at the local nursery in both the summers of 2017 and 2018. Through a series of tests we discover that in addition to CbVd-1 and CbVd-5, next generation sequencing (NGS) detected the presence of CbVd-6 at the nursery in both years of collection. To our knowledge, this is the first detection of CbVd-6 outside of China since its initial description in 2009.
reference_name: Occurrence of Coleus blumei Viroid 6 in Commercial Coleus blumei in Canada: The First Report Outside of China
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 五彩苏Plectranthus scutellarioides  cv. 'Aurora black cherry'
description: Given that numbers of coleus cultivars sold in Japan are increasing, with some of them showing abnormal discoloration or growth retardation, we surveyed coleus cultivars with abnormal growth retardation available in domestic markets for viroid infection. Total RNAs were extracted from symptomatic samples for analysis. A circular RNA band with a size larger than that of CbVd-1 was detected in samples in the cultivar 'Aurora black cherry', a vegetatively propagated clonal coleus. As a result, two specific bands were detected, a major band corresponding to CbVd-1 and a faint band with a size similar to that of CbVd-5. The major sequence variant  was completely matched to CbVd-5 reported in China. This is the first report of CbVd-5 infection in commercial coleus in Japan.  Coleus 'Aurora black cherry' shows poor seed production due to its clonal nature and vegetative propagation is a key factor in the dissemination of CbVd-5 in this situation.
reference_name: First report of Coleus blumei viroid 5 infection in vegetatively propagated clonal coleus cv. 'Aurora black cherry' in Japan
author: cpqis.wangnaiyang

host_range: 锦紫苏 Coleus scutellarioides

host_range: CChMVd has been reported to infect chrysanthemum (Dendranthema x grandiflorum). CChMVd was first reported in 1967 in the cultivar Yellow Delaware in New York State, USA. This is the first molecular evidence for the presence of CChMVd infecting chrysanthemum in Karnataka State, India.
description: During late summer 2010 (May and June), chrysanthemum leaves with yellow-green mottling and chlorotic spots were noted, indicating the possible association with Chrysanthemum chlorotic mottle viroid (CChMVd) in Karnataka. Total RNA was extracted from leaf samples of symptomatic plants, CChMVd was confirmed by molecular detection. This is the first molecular evidence for the presence of CChMVd infecting chrysanthemum in Karnataka State, India. The high degree of sequence diversity reported in the Karnataka isolates of CChMVd will help to clarify the evolution of this viroid and its possible threat to important crops.
reference_name: Molecular Identification of Chrysanthemum chlorotic mottle viroid Infecting Chrysanthemum in Karnataka, India

host_range: Transmission of ASBVd is restricted to species of the Lauraceae under experimental conditions by bark patch grafting (da Graca and van Vuuren, 1980b, 1981b). ASBVd was successfully transmitted to Persea schiedeana, Cinnamomum zeylanicum, Cinnamomum camphora and Ocotea bullata, but not to C. liebertiana, P. indica and the known herbaceous hosts of other viroids (tomatoes and Gynura aurantiaca).
potential_eco_desc: Although it is generally accepted that sunblotch-infected avocado trees are less productive than healthy trees, no extensive evaluations of economic impact have been made. Yield from sunblotch-infected avocado cv. Fuerte was reduced by about 30% with over half of the fruit from infected trees downgraded (da Graca et al., 1983) while the yield of cv. Edranol could reach 82% (da Graca, 1985). Yield reductions of 95% and greater have been suggested for sunblotch symptomless carrier trees of cvs Caliente and Reed (Desjardins, 1987). Fruits from cv Edranol with symptoms of sunblotch, although smaller in size than fruit from non-symptomatic trees, retained a similar oil content (da Graca and van Vuuren, 1977). This impact may be applied to avocado production estimates as summarized by the FAO.
author: CPC2006

description: Graft transmission by human mechanical manipulation remains the primary mode of disease movement. However, natural transmission by root grafts has also been demonstrated (Whitsell, 1952). Mechanical transmission is possible, although highly inefficient, by razor-slash but not by leaf rubbing. Both symptom-expressing and symptomless carrier trees can serve as pollen donors (Desjardins et al., 1984). description: IncidenceThe initial suggestion by Whitsell (1952) for seed transmission of sunblotch was demonstrated by Wallace and Drake (1953) with a level of seed transmission in fruit from sunblotch symptom expressing trees at about 5%. description:
由人工机械操作的嫁接传播依然是病毒转移的主要模式。然而，由根部嫁接的自然传播已得到证明(Whitsell, 1952)。通过高度的无效率剃砍，但不通过汁液摩擦，而使得机械传播是有可能的。这个，就像是病毒传播一样，提出了病原物在接近的脉管组织上是一定会发生的。
当已控制田间的实验记录了一个低水平(1-4%)的蜜蜂(Apis mellifera)花粉传播(Desjardins et al., 1979)，使得令人怀疑的病毒由生物媒介的传播从这是能够证明到的。症状表达和无症状带病的树能起着花粉供给者作用(Desjardins et al., 1984)。然而，这个迁移比被报道的(Wallace and Drake, 1962)在自然显现病态树上的种子传播水平为5%的这个数还要低。
染病的种子被用作来源材料，特别从带病无症状的资源――病毒的种子传播是非常高的(95%)上取得的，这能引起日斑病的爆发。 Graft transmission by human mechanical manipulation remains the primary mode of disease movement.  However, natural transmission by root grafts has also been demonstrated (Whitsell, 1952).  Mechanical transmission is possible, although highly inefficient, by razor-slash but not by leaf rubbing. This, as with virus transmission, suggests that the pathogen must occur in close proximity to vascular tissue.
Suspected spread by a biological vector was demonstrated when controlled field experiments recorded a low level (1-4%) of pollen transmission by bees (Apis mellifera) (Desjardins et al., 1979).  Both symptom-expressing and symptomless carrier trees can serve as pollen donors (Desjardins et al., 1984).  However, this movement is lower than the normal 5% level of transmission reported (Wallace and Drake, 1962) in seed from trees expressing disease.
Contaminated seed to be used as rootstock material especially derived from symptomless carrier sources where seed transmission is very high (95%) can contribute to outbreaks of sunblotch.
author: zhangjianjun

management_info:
移除表现日斑病症状或没表现症状的带病树木对于控制病害的传播是基本的方法。通过用刀刮的机械传播(Desjardins et al., 1980)或使用滤器的含有感病树木汁液的纸张来嫁接接芽(Allen et al., 1981)是有可能传播的，但是效率很低。ASBVd能够通过在20%的次氯酸钠，2%的甲醛和2%的次氯酸钠，或6%的过氧化氢的溶液里浸修剪和繁殖工具可以有效地使其钝化(Desjardins et al., 1987)。
一个对于已登记根茎和接穗材料的标定指数和散播植物卫生方案提供了日斑病最合适的防治方法。ASBVd被报道为在伴随连续暴晒15分钟到56℃时，其在染病组织内就会被钝化(da Graca and van Vuuren, 1980a)。 Removal of sunblotch-expressing or symptomless carrier trees is the primary mode for the control of disease spread.  Mechanical transmission by razor slashing (Desjardins et al., 1980) or graft inoculation with filter paper containing extracts from infected trees (Allen et al., 1981) is possible but of very low efficiency. ASBVd can be effectively inactivated by dipping pruning and propagating tools in solutions of 20% sodium hypochlorite, 2% formaldehyde + 2% sodium hydroxide, or 6% hydrogen peroxide (Desjardins et al., 1987).
A phytosanitation programme for the indexing and dissemination of registered rootstock and scion materials offers the best approach for the control of sunblotch. ASBVd was reported to be inactivated in infected tissue following exposure to 56℃ for 15 minutes (da Graca and van Vuuren, 1980a).
author: zhangjianjun

potential_eco_desc:
虽然，普遍认为日斑病侵染的鳄梨树比健康的树在生产上会减少一些，但没有对存在的经济影响作出的估价。来自受日斑病侵染的鳄梨树的出产减少了30%，这是因为感病树上的果实质量下降了而导致的，然而，cv. Edranol种的出产能到达82% (da Graca, 1985)。出产量95%及更多的降低已表明了其在感染日斑病的无症状携带病毒cvs Caliente 和 Reed (Desjardins, 1987)种的树。有日斑病症状的cv Edranol果实，虽然在大小上比来自无症状树上的果实小，但是保持了一个相似的含油量(da Graca and van Vuuren, 1977)。
这个影响可能归结为对鳄梨产量的估计――由FAO作出总结。 Although it is generally accepted that sunblotch-infected avocado trees are less productive than healthy trees, no extensive evaluations of economic impact have been made. Yield from sunblotch-infected avocado cv. Fuerte was reduced by about 30% with over half of the fruit from infected trees downgraded (da Graca et al., 1983) while the yield of cv. Edranol could reach 82% (da Graca, 1985). Yield reductions of 95% and greater have been suggested for sunblotch symptomless carrier trees of cvs Caliente and Reed (Desjardins, 1987). Fruits from cv Edranol with symptoms of sunblotch, although smaller in size than fruit from non-symptomatic trees, retained a similar oil content (da Graca and van Vuuren, 1977). 
This impact may be applied to avocado production estimates as summarized by the FAO.

description: In May 2015, a virus disease outbreak of cassava with infected plants showing typical symptoms of CMD was observed in the field in Ratanakiri, KaunMoum, Cambodia. The samples were collected and identified, the causal agent was identified as Sri Lankan cassava mosaic virus (SLCMV) by molecular diagnostics. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CMD in Southeast Asia.  Indian cassava mosaic virus and Sri Lankan cassava mosaic virus (SLCMV) were transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae), but the genetic group(s) or cryptic species of the whitefly responsible for the transmission were not determined, as B. tabaci is now known as a complex consisting of >35 morphologically indistinguishable species.

host_range: Solanum pimpinellifolium is considered a host of PYMV (2008). S. americanum has not been found previously to be infected by this begomovirus.
description: In Venezuela, a recent survey showed that PYMV is the most widespread and prevalent begomovirus in tomato fields. However, little is known about natural reservoirs of the virus. In 2007 and 2008 PYMV surveys were performed in several Venezuelan tomato fields and weeds in the genus Solanum showing virus-like symptoms were also collected. The causal agent was confirmed as PYMV in Solanum americanum and S. pimpinellifolium using PCR. This is the first report of PYMV infecting S. americanum in Venezuela.  Begomoviruses are transmitted by Bemisia tabaci which is considered a cryptic species complex. Within this complex, the polyphagous whitefly referred as Middle East Asia-Minor 1 is widespread in Venezuela and its contribution to increasing the number of natural reservoirs may be speculated. Although our results suggest that Solanum americanum might be a natural host for PYMV, more extensive surveys are needed to confirm whether this weed is an important alternative host in the field.
reference_name: First report of Potato yellow mosaic virus infecting Solanum americanum in Venezuela

host_range: 番茄. Solanum lycopersicum.
description: In April 2011 and September 2012, virus-like symptoms were observed in open field- and greenhouse-grown tomato crops (Solanum lycopersicum) in Chiriqui, the western most province of Panama. Samples from symptom bearing plants were collected and tested for the presence of begomoviruses. This analysis revealed Potato yellow mosaic Panama virus (PYMPV) or Tomato leaf curl Sinaloa virus (ToLCSiV) in 44 (90%) or 40 (82%) of the samples, respectively. Differences in symptom expression were in some cases observed between plants infected with both viruses, or with PYMPV or ToLCSiV alone. To our knowledge, this is not only the first detection of ToLCSiV in Panama, but also the first report of PYMPV in Panama's western highlands, and the first ever report of PYMPV/ToLCSiV mixed infection. Additional studies on incidence and distribution of these viruses in Panama are in progress.
reference_name: First report of Tomato leaf curl Sinaloa virus infecting tomato crops in Panama

description: During a survey in 2017 in Madhya Pradesh state, India, greenhouse-cultivated pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo) plants exhibiting leaf symptoms of mosaic and crumpling, typical of begomovirus infection, were observed. Though diseased plants grew to the same size as symptomless plants, there was no flower formation leading to no fruit production, i.e. 100% yield loss. Whiteflies were found associated with the plants. Young diseased leaves were collected to identify the cause of the suspected virus infection. Based on molecular diagnostics confirmed the presence of Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus (MYMIV). This is the first definitive report of MYMIV infection on pumpkin from India and the pathogen may cause severe disease outbreaks in India in the future.  Whiteflies were found associated with the infested plants.
reference_name: First report of Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus infecting pumpkin in India

description: Bean dwarf mosaic disease (BDMD) has emerged as the major economic constraint in French bean-growing areas of India. In 2014 French bean plants were collected from fields in the Gandhinagar District of Gujarat State, India, exhibiting symptoms consisting of severe stunting, leaf distortion, and light-green to yellow mosaic on leaves. The causal agent was isolated from the symptomatic plants and confirmed to be Rhynchosia yellow mosaic virus (RhYMV) and a betasatellite based on molecular diagnostics. These results show that severe BDMD in India is caused by RhYMV and a betasatellite. This is the first report showing the emergence of the weed infecting RhYMV in French bean. The study satisfies Koch’s postulates for the virus, with a beatsatellite, causing BDMD in India. Such tripartite associations (bipartite begomovirus with a betasatellite) are often more pathogenic than the virus alone and pose a serious threat for legume crops in India.

description: To determine the suspected begomoviruses associated with Cassava mosaic disease (CMD) symptoms, leaf samples were collected from five symptomatic cassava plants in Cameroon, and from three symptomatic plants in Togo in August 2014. Total DNA was isolated, the African cassava mosaic virus (ACMV) DNA-A and B components as expected, the DNA-A and B components of Soybean chlorotic blotch virus (SbCBV) (Olufemi et al., 2010) and West African Asystasia virus 1 (WAAV1) (Wyant et al., 2015) were also identified. For SbCBV, sequence identities ranged from 97-99% and 95-96% for the DNA-A and B components, respectively, whereas for WAAV1, sequence identities ranged from 92-95% and 93-96% for the DNA-A and B components, respectively. To confirm the presence of SbCBV and WAAV1 in the cassava samples, PCR was carried out using specific primers designed to the CP and BV1 gene, located on the DNA-A and B components of SbCBV and WAAV1, respectively. The DNA sequence for each cloned amplicon was determined by Sanger sequencing. Amongst the five samples collected from Cameroon, three were infected only with ACMV, one was infected with ACMV and WAAV1, and one was infected with ACMV, SbCBV and WAAV1. The three Togolese samples were all infected with ACMV and one was also infected with SbCMV. BLASTn analysis of the CP and BV1 genes indicated that they shared 99-100% sequence identity with the NGS- determined sequences. To our knowledge, this is the first report that cassava may be infected by SbCBV or WAAV1 in Africa. The isolates shared a close phylogenetic relatedness with previously described SbCBV and WAAV1 isolates, respectively.
reference_name: First report of Soybean chlorotic blotch virus and West African Asystasia virus 1 infecting cassava and a wild cassava relative in Cameroon and Togo

potential_eco_desc: CMD is arguably the most important virus disease of any African food crop (Geddes, 1990), but total losses are extremely difficult to estimate. Yield losses with individual cultivars have been reported from different countries to range from 20 to 95% (Thresh et al., 1994). Losses depend on variety and stage of infection, but are usually substantial. In Cote d'Ivoire, total losses were estimated to be 0.5 million tonnes per year compared with actual production at the time of 0.8 million tonnes (Fargette et al., 1988). This was based on the assumption that all plants were infected and sustained a 37% yield loss average, as estimated experimentally with a moderately susceptible variety. Extended to the whole of Africa, such calculations indicate yield losses of 30 million tonnes per year. In a recent review more realistic assumptions were used to estimate losses in Africa of 15-24%, equivalent to 12-23 million tonnes compared with actual production estimates of 73 million tonnes (Thresh et al., 1997). There have been no comparable estimates of losses in India or Sri Lanka where the overall productivity of cassava is higher than in Africa.^p^pData on the effects of CMD on the yield of cassava have been obtained in many countries including Cameroon, Congo, Cote d'Ivoire, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda and Zanzibar (Thresh et al., 1994). These studies have been made on naturally infected plants in farmers' fields or experimental plantings and also in special plots established with CMG-infected and uninfected cuttings. The losses reported have been very variable and range from insignificant to almost total. Nevertheless, several generalisations are valid:^p^p-Plants grown from infected cuttings sustain a greater yield loss than those of the same variety infected later by whiteflies, and plants infected at a late stage of crop growth are virtually unaffected;^p^p-There are big varietal differences in response to infection (Fargette et al., 1988);^p^p-Infected plants of varieties designated as resistant may sustain substantial yield losses (Seif, 1982);^p^p-There is a positive relationship between the extent and severity of symptoms and yield loss (Cours, 1951; Thresh et al., 1997);^p^p-Competition and compensation effects are likely to be important and infected plants surrounded by uninfected ones are more seriously affected than those in groups (Otim-Nape et al., 1997c);^p^p-Effects on yield are influenced by crop duration;^p^p-From experience with other virus-host combinations, it is likely that soil fertility, seasonal factors, crop spacing and other cropping practices, virus strain, weed control and other pests/diseases influence the effects of CMD on growth and yield, although they have not yet been studied.

description: The virus is not seedborne in cassava. However, the virus is disseminated in the stem cuttings used routinely for propagation.

remark: CMGs seem to have spread rapidly in Africa at the beginning of the century as intensification of cassava production occurred in the continent, despite some unsuccessful attempts to restrict spread through early quarantine controls. One or other of the viruses is now present in all cassava growing regions. Much care is now taken in the transfer of virus-free material from Africa or the Indian sub-continent, in order not to introduce the virus to other regions and to South America in particular, where cassava is extensively grown. CMGs are absent from the neotropics but Bemisia species are present, including B. tabaci on crops other than cassava. Within Africa, different viruses predominate in the East and the West of the continent (Swanson and Harrison, 1994;Harrison et al., 1995, 1997a). Recent epidemics in Uganda are associated with a novel strain that appears to be a recombinant between African cassava mosaic and East African mosaic geminiviruses Harrison et al., 1997a, b. However, it has also been referred to as a distinctive strain of East African cassava mosaic virus (Deng et al., 1997). Care is also required in moving vegetative propagules within Africa, and in vitro cultures only are transferred after testing.

management_info: The two main approaches to controlling CMD are through sanitation and the use of virus-resistant varieties (Thresh and Otim-Nape, 1994; Thresh et al., 1998a). Sanitation has received only limited attention, even though its effectiveness in controlling CMD has been demonstrated convincingly in Uganda (Jameson, 1964). The procedure developed there in the 1950s was to release large quantities of CMG-free cuttings of selected varieties, from official propagation sites at experimental stations, prison farms, farm institutes, training colleges and other establishments. This material was used to displace the heavily infected stocks that were being grown and a systematic campaign was organized so that whole districts were treated before starting on the next. Farmers in treated areas were then subject to local government ordinances to enforce the removal of any remaining infected plants. These measures were successful in Uganda for more than a decade, but then lapsed. They are now being revived in a modified form (Otim-Nape et al., 1997b).^p^pThe use of resistant or tolerant varieties has obvious advantages in seeking to decrease virus-induced losses and some form of resistance to CMD has long been a high priority in cassava breeding programmes in Africa (Jennings, 1994). Initial studies in Tanzania in the 1930s and 1940s were followed by others in Madagascar, Ghana and Nigeria. The main centre of activity since 1971 has been at the International Institute for Tropical Agriculture (IITA, Ibadan), which has greatly influenced national programmes in providing training, support and germplasm for local selection and evaluation (Mahungu et al., 1994).^p^pResistance to CMD is but one of many attributes being sought when developing new cassava varieties and only a few of the improved varieties so far released by IITA or national programmes are highly resistant to CMGs. Others are variously described as 'resistant', 'moderately resistant' or 'moderately susceptible' and their resistance is manifest in different ways. Some improved varieties are more difficult to infect than unimproved ones, but when infected they develop conspicuous symptoms that occur throughout the plant. Others develop relatively inconspicuous symptoms that may be restricted to certain shoots during the later stages of crop growth and plants may eventually become symptomless. A marked feature of some resistant varieties is that they do not seem to be invaded systemically and only some of the cuttings taken from infected plants contain CMGs. An important consequence of this 'reversion' or 'recovery' phenomenon is that stocks of such varieties never become totally infected, even when the same material is grown repeatedly at sites where there is much spread by whiteflies and where susceptible varieties soon succumb (Fargette et al., 1994; Fargette and Vie, 1995).

description: CMGs在来自受感染的植物的插条上散布，它们通过粉虱烟粉虱（Bemisia tabaci）传播(Chant, 1958; Dubern, 1994)。在实验上，它们也能机械地传播岛一些茄属品种中去。通过插条的传播是木薯营养繁殖的不可避免的结果，它反映病毒在植物上的全部分布，包括提供插条的茎。然而，该病毒的分布在木薯上不是完全的系统性的，特别在抗性基因型中，来源于受感染植物的插条的部分必须是无病毒的。这是逆转现象，流行的结果由Fargette et al. (1994) 以及Fargette 和 Vie (1995)所讨论。 CMGs are disseminated in cuttings derived from infected plants and they are transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci (Chant, 1958; Dubern, 1994). Experimentally, they can also be transmitted mechanically to some solanaceous species. Dissemination through cuttings is an inevitable consequence of the vegetative propagation of cassava and reflects the overall distribution of the virus in the plant, including the stems which provide cuttings. However, the distribution of the virus is not fully systemic in cassava, especially in resistant genotypes, and a proportion of cuttings derived from infected plants may be virus-free. This is the phenomenon of reversion and the epidemiological consequences are discussed by Fargette et al. (1994) and Fargette and Vie (1995).

management_info:
防治CMD的两个主要的方法是通过卫生设施和使用病毒抗性品种(Thresh and Otim-Nape, 1994; Thresh et al., 1998a)。卫生设施只得到有限的关注，即使它在防治CMD上的效力在乌干达已被了作出有说服力的证明(Jameson, 1964)。在那里在20世纪50年代的产生的程序，从实验所、监狱农场、农场学会、培训学院和其他商业机构中的官方繁殖的场所中释放出大量的经挑选的品种的无CMG插条。这材料被用来代替正在被种植的严重受侵染的砧木，系统性的活动被组织于是整个区域在下次开始之前就防治。在防治区域的农民之后服从政府法令来强迫移除所有仍然受感染的植物。在乌干达这些方法成功超过了十年，但之后失效。它们现在正在以一个改良的方式来再实施(Otim-Nape et al., 1997b)。
抗性或耐病性品种的使用在寻求降低的由病毒引起的损失上有明显的优势，在非洲对CMD抗性的一些形式已很长时间在木薯的育种程序中处于一个高度优先的位置(Jennings, 1994)。在20世纪30年代的坦桑尼亚进行了最初的研究，之后在20世纪40年代的马达加斯加、加纳和尼日利亚由其他人继续进行。直到1971年活动的主要中西已在热带农业的国际学会(IITA, Ibadan)，它强烈地影响在提供培训、支持以及为局部筛选和评价种质中的国家程序(Mahungu et al., 1994)。
在生产新的木薯品种时CMD抗性是寻求的许多个的品质中的一个，目前只有少许由IITA或国家程序释放的改良过的品种对CMGs有高度的抗性。其他的被不同地被描述成‘抗性’、‘中度抗性’或‘中度敏感’，它们的抗性在不同的方法上是明显的。一些经改良的品种比未经改良的品种更难受侵染，但当受侵染时，它们在整棵植株上产生显著的症状。其他的在作物生长的后期阶段，限制地在某些枝条上产生相对不明显的症状，植物可到最后变成无症的。一些抗性品种的一个明显的特征是，它们似乎不会系统性地受侵染，而且只有一些来自受感染植物的插条会含有CMGs。这‘复原’或‘恢复’现象的一个重要的结果是，这些品种的砧木决不会全部受侵染，即使当同样的材料重复地种植在有很多粉虱的传播的地方和在敏感品种迅速死亡的地方时(Fargette et al., 1994; Fargette and Vi? 1995)。 The two main approaches to controlling CMD are through sanitation and the use of virus-resistant varieties (Thresh and Otim-Nape, 1994; Thresh et al., 1998a). Sanitation has received only limited attention, even though its effectiveness in controlling CMD has been demonstrated convincingly in Uganda (Jameson, 1964). The procedure developed there in the 1950s was to release large quantities of CMG-free cuttings of selected varieties, from official propagation sites at experimental stations, prison farms, farm institutes, training colleges and other establishments. This material was used to displace the heavily infected stocks that were being grown and a systematic campaign was organized so that whole districts were treated before starting on the next. Farmers in treated areas were then subject to local government ordinances to enforce the removal of any remaining infected plants. These measures were successful in Uganda for more than a decade, but then lapsed. They are now being revived in a modified form (Otim-Nape et al., 1997b).
The use of resistant or tolerant varieties has obvious advantages in seeking to decrease virus-induced losses and some form of resistance to CMD has long been a high priority in cassava breeding programmes in Africa (Jennings, 1994). Initial studies in Tanzania in the 1930s and 1940s were followed by others in Madagascar, Ghana and Nigeria. The main centre of activity since 1971 has been at the International Institute for Tropical Agriculture (IITA, Ibadan), which has greatly influenced national programmes in providing training, support and germplasm for local selection and evaluation (Mahungu et al., 1994).
Resistance to CMD is but one of many attributes being sought when developing new cassava varieties and only a few of the improved varieties so far released by IITA or national programmes are highly resistant to CMGs. Others are variously described as‘resistant’, ‘moderately resistant’or ‘moderately susceptible’and their resistance is manifest in different ways. Some improved varieties are more difficult to infect than unimproved ones, but when infected they develop conspicuous symptoms that occur throughout the plant. Others develop relatively inconspicuous symptoms that may be restricted to certain shoots during the later stages of crop growth and plants may eventually become symptomless. A marked feature of some resistant varieties is that they do not seem to be invaded systemically and only some of the cuttings taken from infected plants contain CMGs. An important consequence of this ‘reversion’ or ‘recovery’phenomenon is that stocks of such varieties never become totally infected, even when the same material is grown repeatedly at sites where there is much spread by whiteflies and where susceptible varieties soon succumb (Fargette et al., 1994; Fargette and Vi? 1995).

host_range: This is the first report of Macroptilium yellow spot virus in Desmodium glabrum in Brazil.
potential_eco_desc: Desmodium glabrum is a widely distributed neotropical plant occurring from Mexico to Argentina. In Brazil, D. glabrum can be found as invasive plants in northeastern, central, and southeastern regions in open fields, pasture areas, riparian forests, and also in anthropized and degraded areas. To date, MaYSV has been described only in Brazilian northeastern states; however, pervasive plants such as D. glabrum as well as other reported leguminous noncultivated MaYSV hosts may facilitate the spread of MaYSV to cultivated legume crops such as common bean and soybean in the main cultivated areas.
description: Macroptilium yellow spot virus (MaYSV) is a begomovirus (family Geminiviridae) described infecting common beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) and other leguminous noncultivated hosts in northeastern Brazil. In a recent virus survey in common beans and associated noncultivated plants in the state of Pernambuco, four Desmodium glabrum plants presenting yellow mosaic, leaf curling, rugosity, and leaf deformation symptoms were collected at the periphery of a bean field in Caruaru, in August 2013. Based on molecular diagnostics showed that MaYSV was present in D. glabrum.
reference_name: First Report of Macroptilium yellow spot virus in Desmodium glabrum in Brazil

host_range: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus) crops.
description: In 2012 and 2013, severe symptoms of leaf curling, deformation, and vein thickening, resembling those of okra leaf curl disease(OLCD) were observed on okra in four localities in south-eastern C?te d'Ivoire. Leaf samples with symptoms were collected and tested for the presence of begomoviruses. Based on sequences analysis the results showed the presence of Cotton leaf curl Gezira virus(CLCuGV) and Okra yellow crinkle virus(OYCrV). A maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree, produced from alignments of publicly available begomovirus sequences, confirmed the genetic relationship of Ivorian CLCuGeV and OYCrV isolates with isolates from three neighbouring countries, Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger. To our knowledge, this is the first report of CLCuGeV and OYCrV implicated in OLCD in C?te d’Ivoire. Our results confirm that OLCD is associated with a complex of several strains of CLCuGeV and OYCrV in sub-Saharan Africa and show that Ivorian isolates are genetically closely related to strains described in West Africa.
reference_name: First reports of Cotton leaf curl Gezira virus and Okra yellow crinkle virus associated with okra leaf curl disease in Cote d＇Ivoire

host_range: Ipomoea batatas
description: In October 2016, generalized leaf curl symptoms were observed in a sweet potato field of the local cultivar Baladi in Sharq Al-Nīl, Khartoum State, Sudan. Leaf samples from symptomatic plants were collected and total nucleic acids were extracted. The presence of Sweet potato leaf curl virus (SPLCV) was confirmed by sequences analysis. This is the first report of SPLCV Infecting sweet potato in Sudan, and it is the first confirming the presence of SPLCV in Africa, and the partial sequences reported from Kenya (Miano et al. 2006), suggest that SPLCV could be more widespread than currently recognized in this continent.
reference_name: First Report of Sweet potato leaf curl virus Infecting Sweet Potato in Sudan

host_range: 变色牵牛Ipomoea indica
description: Yellow vein symptoms are frequently observed on these plants. These symptoms are similar to those reported for isolates of Sweet potato leaf curl virus (SPLCV) infecting I. indica in Italy and Spain. SPLCV infects sweet potato (I. batatas) crops around the world. In May 2013, three leaf samples of I. indica showing yellow vein symptoms were collected in Kolymbari (Crete Island), where ~50% of the observed plants were symptomatic, and five asymptomatic leaf samples were collected in Kremasti and Mandriko (Rhodes Island). The test demonstrated that the causal agent was SPLCV. It is worth to note that the infected I. indica plant from Kremasti did not show any conspicuous symptoms, thus highlighting the importance of this species as an alternative host for SPLCV, which could thus affect the sweet potato crop that is grown in Greece in familiar plots. To our knowledge, this is the first report of SPLCV in Greece.
reference_name: First Report of Sweet potato leaf curl virus on Blue Morning Glory in Greece

scientific_name: Sweet potato leaf curl Georgia virus
host_range: 番薯Ipomoea batatas.
description: Leaf curl disease was first reported in Argentina in 2012 associated with an increase of whitefly populations. In September 2014, random samplings of more than 100 plants showing upward leaf curling and mild vein clearing symptoms were conducted in eight sweet potato plots in Colonia Molina, Mendoza Province, Argentina (32.8316311°S, 68.7238142°W). Sweet potato leaf curl Georgia virus (SPLCGV) was present in the samples by molecular diagnostics. This is the first report of SPLCGV in Argentina.  Viruses of the genus Begomovirus (family Geminiviridae) are transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae). In Argentina, leaf curl disease associated with whitefly populations was observe in 2012.
reference_name: First Report of Sweet potato leaf curl Georgia virus in Sweet Potato in Argentina

description: 早在1967年，即在巴基斯坦木尔坦地区发生棉花曲叶病，但首次报道棉花曲叶病是在1985年。1988年，该病害在巴基斯坦木尔坦地区开始流行，其后快速扩散到该国其他棉区。自2O世纪9O年代以来，该病害已成为巴基斯坦棉花生产最主要限制因素。除巴基斯坦外，在印度、苏丹、埃及、尼日利亚、马拉维和南非等国也报道有该病害的发生与严重危害。2006年以来，陆续在广东及广西多个地区的朱槿Hibiscus rosa-sinensis和黄秋葵Abelmoschus esculentus上检测鉴定到CLCuMV，该病毒分别引起朱槿曲叶病、黄秋葵黄脉曲叶病或黄秋葵黄化曲叶病。  由烟粉虱Bemisia tabaci传播。该病毒入侵我国可能通过带毒烟粉虱随东南亚进口的花卉或水果等农产品传人，也可能是随朱槿、黄秋葵等寄主植物直接带毒入侵我国。

host_range: okra
description: Severe leaf curl and small vein thickening symptoms were observed in okra fields in Al-Ain, United Arab Emirates (UAE) during the winter season, 2013. These symptoms were reminiscent of those often associated with begomovirus infection. Based on the symptoms observed in okra plants growing in adjacent fields (20 × 20 m) on two small holding farms, the disease incidence ranged from 90 to 100%. The samples were collected and identified, based on molecular detection showed that the causal agent was was Cotton leaf curl Gezira virus (CLCuGeV).  The okra fields were infested with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci (Genn.), the insect vector of begomoviruses. The recent practice of transporting plants between the Gulf countries represents an important means and route for introducing begomoviruses among neighboring countries, compared to the long-distance aerial dispersal of viruliferous whiteflies, which is less likely because the Arabian desert poses a major barrier to long-distance whitefly flights.
reference_name: Introduction of Cotton leaf curl Gezira virus into the United Arab Emirates

description: To determine the suspected begomoviruses associated with Cassava mosaic disease (CMD) symptoms, leaf samples were collected from five symptomatic cassava plants in Cameroon, and from three symptomatic plants in Togo in August 2014. Total DNA was isolated, the African cassava mosaic virus (ACMV) DNA-A and B components as expected, the DNA-A and B components of Soybean chlorotic blotch virus (SbCBV) (Olufemi et al., 2010) and West African Asystasia virus 1 (WAAV1) (Wyant et al., 2015) were also identified. For SbCBV, sequence identities ranged from 97-99% and 95-96% for the DNA-A and B components, respectively, whereas for WAAV1, sequence identities ranged from 92-95% and 93-96% for the DNA-A and B components, respectively. To confirm the presence of SbCBV and WAAV1 in the cassava samples, PCR was carried out using specific primers designed to the CP and BV1 gene, located on the DNA-A and B components of SbCBV and WAAV1, respectively. The DNA sequence for each cloned amplicon was determined by Sanger sequencing. Amongst the five samples collected from Cameroon, three were infected only with ACMV, one was infected with ACMV and WAAV1, and one was infected with ACMV, SbCBV and WAAV1. The three Togolese samples were all infected with ACMV and one was also infected with SbCMV. BLASTn analysis of the CP and BV1 genes indicated that they shared 99-100% sequence identity with the NGS- determined sequences. To our knowledge, this is the first report that cassava may be infected by SbCBV or WAAV1 in Africa. The isolates shared a close phylogenetic relatedness with previously described SbCBV and WAAV1 isolates, respectively.
reference_name: First report of Soybean chlorotic blotch virus and West African Asystasia virus 1 infecting cassava and a wild cassava relative in Cameroon and Togo

description: In 2014, severe symptoms of leaf curling and yellowing resembling those of tomato yellow leaf curl disease were observed for the first time on tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) plants with whiteflies in greenhouses in Tahiti. Tomato samples with leaf curling and yellowing symptoms, and whiteflies were collected in Tahitian greenhouses from August 2015 to January 2016. Other whiteflies were collected from tomato and melon plants in Huahine and Tubuai islands. The pathogen was identified as Israel strain of Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV-IL) by PCR assays and sequences analysis. The whiteflies was identified as Bemisia tabaci(Middle East- Asia Minor 1, MEAM1) by sequences analysis. To our knowledge, this is the first report of Old World TYLCV-IL implicated in yellow leaf curl disease on tomato in Tahiti. The occurrence of B. tabaci MEAM1 species was reported in 1996-97 in Tahiti, but never on the neighbouring islands of Huahine and Tubuai. This description confirms the invasion and the dissemination of both TYLCV-IL and B. tabaci MEAM1 species in the Asia-Pacific region. description: Over the past two years (2014 to 2016), several farmers’ fields planted with tomato in Trinidad were showing noticeable symptoms. Symptoms were typical of those caused by begomoviruses. TYLCV may have been introduced into Trinidad through imported seed and by the movement of whiteflies and that the virus may have originated from Grenada since both countries are in close proximity. TYLCV has been reported to be spread through whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).

potential_eco_desc: Urtica membranacea is an annual herbaceous plant native to the Mediterranean region. Its natural habitat comprises uncultivated marginal areas close to disturbed areas, as well as moist and nitrogen-rich soils where the plants thrive. Therefore, it is easy to find U. membranacea as a weed of protected crops where fertigation is used routinely.
description: In autumn 2012, unusual symptoms of leaf yellowing and curling were observed on several plants of Urtica membranacea (Poiret) (family Urticaceae) growing along the rows of a greenhouse tomato cultivation in southern Italy (Torre del Greco, Campania Region). Tomato plants (cv. Jama) in the greenhouse were affected by tomato yellow leaf curl disease (TYLCD) and had large population of Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius), mostly likely the Q1 and Q2 variants of the Mediterranean (MED) species. Total nucleic acids were extracted from four different symptomatic U. membranacea plants, based on molecular detection indicated that two plants were infected by Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), one by Tomato yellow leaf curl Sardinia virus (TYLCSV) and one was infected by TYLCV and TYLCSV in mixed infection. This finding suggests that U. membranacea is a newly identified natural host for TYLCV, TYLCSV, and a TYLCV/TYLCSV recombinant. Therefore, it may play a role in the epidemiology of TYLCD, especially in protected crops, acting as a reservoir for geminiviruses responsible for TYLCD. 出现黄曲叶症状的杂草(Urtica membranacea)生长在受感染番茄黄曲叶病(Tomato yellow leaf curl disease)且存在大量烟粉虱(Bemisia tabaci, Q1 and Q2)的番茄作物温室里。

potential_eco_desc: TYLCV-infected weed plants became one of the important factors facilitating its persistence and rapid spread by whiteflies. It is important to manage this weed host in disease control.
description: Viola prionantha is a common weed grown in the field. It has a wide geographic distribution and can be found in courtyards, gardens, and orchards. Twenty-five symptomless samples of V. prionantha were collected near a tomato greenhouse in Haidian District, Beijing, where 70% of tomato plants displayed typical symptoms of TYLCV, and which was heavily infested with Bemisia tabaci. Total DNA was extracted from V. prionantha plants, based on molecular methods showed TYLCV in V. prionantha. Then, TYLCV was inoculated to healthy plants V. prionantha using viruliferous B. tabaci whiteflies with a one-month inoculation access period (IAP). TYLCV was detected in six out of nine V. prionantha plants after a one-month IAP. To our knowledge, this is the first report of V. prionantha naturally infected by TYLCV in China.  Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci, while weed plants act as intermediate hosts and play an important part in the emergence of TYLCV.
