description: 烟草霜霉病于1891年首次在澳大利亚个栽培烟上报道；美国于1921年首次在佛罗里达和佐治亚州发现，1938年在加拿大和巴西，1939年在阿根廷，1953年在智利，1957年在古巴；1960年开始在欧洲大规模流行，1961年向南蔓延至北非、中东和近东，同时也几乎传遍了整个欧洲。1979年至1980年初，随气流侵袭了海地、洪都拉斯和尼加拉瓜，并随风北上沿美国东海岸各州袭击了美国各烟区。  随气流、病残烟组织和种子传播。
management_info:
1．检疫。1966年我国政府公布烟霜霉病为对外检疫对象，1990年又颁布法令，禁止从疫区进口烟叶及种子和有关易感植物，对因科研需要自疫区引进烟属植物幼苗的，应在指定的隔离检疫圃隔离试种，以严防此病传入。
2．灭除病原。任何新区一旦发生烟霜霉病，应立即采取封锁病区、根除发病点的措施，除灭菌处理苗床或病田外，也要消灭病菌的各种越冬场所，包括消灭感病烟株病残体，观赏烟属和野生烟属植物，禁止病区温室栽种试验用的烟属植物。
3．药剂防治。目前，多采用瑞毒霉(Ridomyl或Metalaxyl)结合代森锌、代森锰共同使用，由于瑞毒霉内吸作用，可以延长药效期，取得增效的防治作用。
4．抗病育种。栽培烟草品种间，虽然感病性存在着差异，但迄今未发现稳定的高抗品种，目前采取栽培烟与澳大利亚及南美的当地烟种，如与N. debneyi、N. excelsior等进行种间杂交，获得较好的结果。
5．栽培防治。种子播种前消毒，加强苗木管理，对发病苗木应采用蒸气灭菌，或用2%福尔马林进行土壤薰蒸，或更换新苗床，烧毁病株及残体；清除粉兰烟及野生烟，定期进行田间调查，发现病株及时拔除，消灭带病昆虫，防止人为携带等措施。

host_range: Hosts of blue mould are mostly restricted to the genus Nicotiana. Blue mould was found on N. glauca in 1885, before the first report on cultivated tobacco in Queensland (Australia) in 1891, when the fungus was also found on N. longiflora in Argentina. Blu
potential_eco_desc: Blue mould is currently a very important disease of tobacco worldwide, because of its great capacity to reduce yields. Severe early attacks can completely destroy nurseries and young tobacco crops. Late attacks in July-August are not infrequent and can injure the middle leaves. Stem infection is disastrous.^p^pIn Australia, blue mould is a very destructive disease of tobacco, mainly when stem infections result in the complete loss of entire fields (Lucas, 1975). ^p^pOriginating from Australia, P. hyoscami f.sp. tabacina appeared in America (Georgia, USA) in 1921, where it has recurred sporadically throughout tobacco areas, damaging seedbeds and field crops. In 1951 it caused losses of over US$ 2 million on cigar-type tobacco in Connecticut. Three years later the losses on flue-cured tobacco in North Carolina amounted to US$ 5 million (Lucas, 1975). A severe field outbreak in USA and Canada caused losses in excess of US$ 240 million in 1979 (Lucas, 1980; Gayed, 1982). In Georgia in 1980, the cost of control plus estimated losses by the end of April exceeded US$ 12 million (Csinos and Arnett, 1980). An epidemic destroyed 30% of the flue-cured crop in Ontario (Canada) because of a lack of properly applied and coordinated control measures (McKeen, 1981). Recently blue mould has been described as a menace for the Connecticut (USA) tobacco crop (LaMondia and Aylor, 1997). ^p^pThe fungus was found in Europe in 1958 and soon spread all over the continent. In 1961 in Italy over 65% of the crop was destroyed, even leading to unemployment problems (Marcelli, 1961; Zanardi, 1961; Giammarioli, 1973). Recently in many fields in southern Italy, losses ranged between 50 and 100% (Piccirillo et al., 1995).^p^pBlue mould caused heavy losses in Israel, Iran and North Africa in 1961: yield was reduced to 40 kg/ha in Algeria (Lucas, 1975). management_info: Introduction^p^pBlue mould is difficult and expensive to control, especially when environmental conditions favour disease development. Though resistant cultivars are available for some types of tobacco, disease control relies mainly on fungicides.^p^p^Resistant Cultivars^p^pNicotiana debneyi is the major source of resistance to Peronospora in Australia and Europe. A blue mould resistant version of USA cultivar Hicks (designated Resistant Hicks), with resistance from N. debneyi, was widely used in Europe from 1962 as a germplasm source. From 1965 USDA-bred Bel 61 lines, also with resistance from N. debneyi, were increasingly used as resistance sources in some countries. Resistant Hicks is adapted for growing seasons with few cloudy days, and its high resistance in Australia has been stable for over 40 years. The high resistance to Peronospora in cultivars derived from Bel 61 lines has been stable for more than 20 years in Europe. N. debneyi has resistance to P. hyoscyami on eight chromosomes; there is evidence that both American and Australian resistant cultivars derive some resistance from N. tabacum. Both the cultivar Resistant Hicks and Bel 61 lines possess only part of the full resistance available from N. debneyi; further progress may be possible by hybridizing these lines and incorporating resistance from other resistant Australian species (Lea, 1999). ^p^pResistance to blue mould has been introgressed in tobacco cultivars from Nicotiana debneyi. Only three of several resistance genes distributed among seven to eight chromosomes have been transferred, in order to avoid unfavourable 'debneyi' traits (Clayton, 1968). The resistance from N. debneyi could be reinforced by a factor present in tobacco (Clayton, 1968). According to other workers, resistance in tobacco includes a dominant major gene and additive minor genes (Schiltz et al., 1977; Palakarcheva et al., 1980): the major gene confers resistance to normal strains of P. hyoscami f.sp. tabacina and the minor genes act as supplementary factors that confer resistance to virulent strains only in the presence of the major gene (Palacharkeva, 1981; Vinogradov et al., 1984). Known tobacco lines with debneyi resistance to the PT1 and PT2 pathotypes of blue mould are 'Bel 61-10' and 'Pobeda'. A single dominant factor was introgressed in 'Chemical mutant' (Egerer, 1977; Palakarcheva and Delon, 1986). ^p^pOther sources of resistance have been identified in N. goodspeedii (Gillham et al., 1977), N. megalosiphon, N. rosulata (Konotop et al., 1979), N. maritima (Dorossiev et al., 1978), N. velutina, N. excelsior (Gillham et al., 1977), N. exigua (Manolov, 1980), N. otophora (Gajos, 1979). Sources from exigua (Manolov, 1980) and otophora (Gajos, 1979) have been used in tobacco breeding.^p^pResistance in tobacco increases with plant age, but is not influenced by leaf age (Reuveni et al., 1986). In genotypes resistant to blue mould, increases of lignin and phenolic compounds were elicited after P. tabacina infection (Georgieva et al., 1997) suggesting that the deposition of both compounds may strengthen cell walls and the formation of mechanical barriers against fungus attack. ^p^p^Cultural Methods^p^pControl of the disease is helped by restraining nitrogen fertilization and irrigation. Overhead irrigation favours disease development by lowering the temperature at the bottom of the canopy (Kucharek, 1987). Drip irrigation reduced the level of blue mould by 93% in comparison with overhead irrigation (Kucharek et al., 1996). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pFungicidal control of blue mould is absolutely necessary in temperate and subtropical tobacco areas, particularly in Europe, Australia and recently also in North America (Lucas, 1980). potential_eco_desc:
欧洲烟草霜霉病造成的损失是惨痛的。60年代初的损失，1960年为28.5百万kg，2.5亿美元，1961年为100百万kg，8.8亿美元。这些损失还不包括苏联和罗马尼亚的。70年代，特别是80年代以来，病害的发生为害逐渐趋于平稳发展，没有大的流行。
1979-1980年期间，烟草霜霉病再次在美国、加拿大和古巴流行为害。美国和加拿大因此损失2.5亿美元。古巴1979年有一半烟草被毁，1980年毁掉80％（Lucas,G.B.1980）。
description:
烟草霜霉病原发于澳大利亚（1889），1931年又在美国发生（A.V.Hill,1966），1958年开始在欧洲发生为害，被视为世界烟草生产的一大灾难。
50年代末，烟草霜霉病在欧洲突然出现，迅速蔓延和严重为害，在欧洲烟草史上史无前例（Pierre Schiltz,1983）。（1）中北欧洲∶1958年10月首先在英国温室出现。1959年在北欧的荷兰（Utrecht省）、比利时（西Flanders）和中欧的西德（Tubingen、Oldenburg和Holstein）、东德（Mecklemburg）大田烟草上发生；1960年到达奥地利（Wels和Burgenland）、捷克（南Moravia）、瑞典（Krir stianstad）、匈牙利和波兰。（2）西南欧洲∶1960年出现在瑞士（Thurgovia等地）、法国（Nord）；1961年到达西班牙（Asturias）；1963年到达葡萄牙。1964年到达安道尔。（3）地中海国家∶1960年出现在意大利（Verona）和南斯拉夫（Virovitica）；1961年到达阿尔巴尼亚、希腊（Agrinion）和土耳其（北Thrace和Izmir）；1963年到达保加利亚。罗马尼亚不在Coresta警报系统，故病害传入时间不详。（4）北部非洲∶1961年出现在阿尔及利亚和突尼斯；1962年到达摩洛哥（Duezzane）。（5）中近东地区∶1962年出现在伊朗（Resht）、黎巴嫩（Nabatiya）和叙利亚（Latakia）；1965年到达以色列（Terusalem）；1969年到达伊拉克（Babylone）；1973年到达约旦；1976年到达利比亚（Tripoli）和塞浦路斯（Paphos）。（6）苏联∶1962年克里米亚发生。
1979-1980年期间，烟草霜霉病再次在美国、加拿大和古巴流行为害。美国烟草霜霉病再次流行，说明烟草霜霉病对于烟草作物是个永远的威胁（R.Corbaz 1983）

potential_eco_desc: 甜菜霜霉病是甜菜生产上的危险性病害。  甜菜霜霉病可危害1年生原料及2年生采种株。感病田块产量降低25%～75%，糖度下降1～4度。种子产量减少20%～50%，质量降低，严重发病可造成减产。被侵染的1年生种用植株，生长势弱，块根小，可引起次年采种株发病，影响种子的产量和质量。
description:

病菌的远距离传播主要是通过种子或母根的调运，近距离传播主要是病残体和寄主上产生的孢子囊。
management_info: 发病初期可选用甲霜灵、甲霜灵锰锌、乙磷铝、恶霜菌丹、杀毒矾等药剂喷雾2～3次即可。

The principal control measure advocated is good crop hygiene; separation of seed and root crops, destruction of groundkeepers and prompt clearance of old cleaner-loader sites. Varieties differ in their susceptibility but the limited economic importance of the disease has not favoured attempts to produce resistant varieties. Russell (1969) summarizes breeding work carried out in the UK at the Plant Breeding Institute, Cambridge.^p^p^Chemical ControlKorhon (1996) reported that results obtained in a trial with an intermediately resistant and resistant cultivar indicated that cyproconazole + carbendazim was the most effective treatment against the disease.^p^pAnon. management_info:
1 加强植物检疫
新疆是我国重要的产糖区之一，目前甜菜霜霉病仅局部发生，植物检疫作为防止该病的传播显得尤为重要。禁止从疫区调种，对外来种子应加强检疫与消毒，不得在疫区制种。
2 农业防治
    应用抗病品种，如“苏垦8312”和“HYB—13”；提倡集约化制种，严格控制小规模制种，做到原料田、采种田和夏播母根田相互隔离，轮作倒茬，合理施肥。
3  化学防治
    试验结果表明，应用75％百菌清可湿性粉剂、58％甲霜灵锰锌和40％增效瑞毒霉粉剂，采用叶面喷雾或喷雾与拌种相结合均有较好防
效，能控制霜霉病的危害。

host_range: V. albo-atrum occurs on numerous economically important plant species. The most prominent hosts are lucerne, potato, hop and tomato. ^p^pIn addition to the main economic hosts, V. albo-atrum is an occasional pathogen of other economically important plants
potential_eco_desc: To a very large degree the diseases caused by V. albo-atrum are effectively controlled through the use of healthy planting material, resistant cultivars, pathogen-free growing substrates and good husbandry practices (Pegg, 1984). Nevertheless, because of the greater scope for spread with seed and in the field, V. albo-atrum continues to cause significant losses in North American lucerne crops. For example, results of a 7-year trial in a commercial field naturally infested with V. albo-atrum in Alberta, Canada, showed that the resistant cultivars, Barrier, AC Blue J, Pioneer 5444 and Vertus, had a significantly (P<0.01) lower wilt incidence than the moderately resistant cultivars, Maris Kabul, Admiral and Trumpetor, and the susceptible cultivars, Excalibur, WL-316, Apollo II, Beaver and Pacer (Huang et al., 1994). The total dry forage yields of the resistant cultivars, Pioneer 5444, Barrier and AC Blue J (87143, 86850, and 85398 kg/ha) were significantly (P<0.01) higher than those of the susceptible cultivars, Beaver and Pacer (75420 and 73519 kg/ha). Although the European cultivar Vertus was resistant to Verticillium wilt, its poor winter hardiness resulted in lower forage yield than that of the North American resistant cultivars Pioneer 5444, Barrier and AC Blue J (Huang et al., 1994). In western Canada, the yearly benefits of growing Verticillium-wilt-resistant and adapted lucerne over wilt-susceptible lucerne was $44 (Canadian dollar) per hetare (Smith et al., 1995). A major hazard is the potential for the types of V. albo-atrum to evolve more pathogenic strains which can overcome the resistance in commercial cultivars (as has happened over a number of years in the UK with hop wilt), or strains whose altered physiological characteristics extend their range into areas where crops may be unprotected by resistance. Thus, for lucerne and hops, selection for wilt resistance remains a major criterion in breeding programmes.^p^pIn New Brunswick, Canada, a survey of potato fields in 1991 showed that V. albo-atrum was detected in all 37 potato fields surveyed and the average population was 350 propagules/g dry soil, whereas V. dahliae was detected in 17 fields at very low populations, usually below 1 propagule/g dry soil (Kimpinski et al., 1998).

description: Incidence^p^pV. albo-atrum is seedborne in lucerne (Sheppard and Needham, 1980; Christen, 1983; Huang et al., 1985), both in the debris that is associated with seed (Isaac and Heale, 1961) and within the seed itself (Christen, 1982b). Christen (1983) detected the pathogen in up to 2% of lucerne seed and in 5 of 20 seed lots assayed from the Columbia Basin of Washington, USA in 1979, and in 2 of 20 assayed in 1980. The pathogen was detected both in the seed itself and in external propagules (debris) carried with the seed lot (Isaac, 1957; Christen, 1983).^p^pPlant to seed transfer of the pathogen was demonstrated in a study in which V. albo-atrum was isolated from the seed of stem-inoculated lucerne plants grown under greenhouse conditions. Colony development from surface-sterilized seed indicated that the fungus was present within the seed. SEM revealed that mycelia were located within and between osteosclerid cells of the outer integument of the seed coat. Internal seedborne infection was as high as 25% in the small fraction (0.91-1.6 mg) of seed produced on plants inoculated within 2 weeks following pollination. Infection occurred less frequently in larger seeds (Christen, 1982b). In another study (Huang et al., 1985), infection of lucerne tissue and seed contamination were investigated in a growth room using root-inoculated lucerne plants. The frequency of contamination of seeds by V. albo-atrum ranged from 0 to 5% in Anchor following hand pollination of plants showing disease symptoms. Although the pathogen was present throughout the stems, it occurred only sporadically in peduncles, pedicels, pods and seeds. This sporadic distribution pattern of V. albo-atrum was also observed in infected leaflets of lucerne (Huang, 1989). When the stigmas of healthy Vernal plants were surface inoculated with spores at the time of flower-tripping, infection occurred readily and resulted in a discoloration of the stigma and upper style (Huang et al., 1985). The fungus appeared to be latent in the style during all stages of seed development. It was not detected in seeds from pods with infected styles. However, under humid conditions, the fungus in the remnant style tissue of a mature seed pod was able to colonize the pod and seed coat.^p^pSurvival studies of the pathogen in hard lucerne seeds indicated the complete loss of viability of V. albo-atrum in infected seeds stored at 30°C for 6 months (Huang et al., 1994a).^p^pIn safflower, an incidence of seedborne infection of 9% was detected on seeds from wilted plants (Schuster and Nuland, 1960). Stem injection of lupins with V. albo-atrum produced 2.5-6.8% infected seeds. The pathogen was present internally in infected seeds of Lupinus luteus but in L. albus it was superficial. Histological observations indicated that plugs of amorphous material in infected vessels, and branching of the vessels, may serve as barriers to seed infection. Even the low levels of seed infection observed may have economically significant epidemiological implications (Parnis and Sackston, 1979).^p^pV. albo-atrum has also been reported on other types of seeds, including celery, safflower, sunflower, lettuce, lupins, aubergine and Trifolium, alsike (Trifolium hybridum) (Richardson, 1990) and urd bean (Sharma and Roy, 1991).^p^p^Effect on Seed Quality^p^pThere is no evidence that V. albo-atrum directly affects the quality of the seeds, but plants in which stems had been killed by wilt disease (V. albo-atrum) produced more brown seeds than did healthy ones. Stems which had dried before harvest produced 3.5 times more brown seeds than stems which were still green at harvest. description: Natural Dispersal (non-biotic)^p^pNon-biotic methods of dispersal of V. albo-atrum are air currents (Isaac, 1957; Davies and Isaac, 1958; Jimenez-Diaz and Millar, 1988) and irrigation water (Christen and Peaden, 1982; Palatinus, 1983). Other physical methods of dispersal of V. albo-atrum are contamination of debris of diseased plants and/or particles of infested soil on farm implements such as harvesting machines (Isaac, 1957) and vehicles working in the diseased crop (Heale and Isaac, 1963; Haas and Martin, 1977).^p ^pVector Transmission^p^pInsect pests such as pea aphid (Huang et al., 1983), alfalfa weevil (Huang and Harper, 1985) and grasshoppers (Huang and Harper, 1985) are effective vectors for transmission of verticillium wilt of lucerne caused by V. albo-atrum.  The pollinator, leafcutter bee, is another important vector because the bees are capable of cutting diseased leaf pieces for making cocoon and carrying V. albo-atrum-infected pollen while foraging in the diseased lucerne crop (Huang and Richards, 1983; Huang and Kokko, 1985; Huang et al., 1986a). ^p^pSeedborne Spread^p^pV. albo-atrum is seedborne in lucerne (Sheppard and Needham, 1980; Christen, 1983; Huang et al., 1985) both in the debris that is associated with seed (Isaac and Heale, 1961) and within the seed itself (Christen, 1982b).  The seedborne nature of V. albo-atrum was also reported in other crops such as safflower (Schuster and Nuland, 1960), lupins (Parnis and Sackston, 1979), celery, sunflower, lettuce, aubergine and Trifolium alsike (Trifolium hybridum) (Richardson, 1990) and urd bean (Sharma and Roy, 1991).^p^pAgricultural Practices^p^pV. albo-atrum may be transmitted from field to field if the same harvest equipment is used in a diseased crop and then used again in a healthy crop.^p^pMovement in Trade^p^pVerticillium wilt, caused by V. albo-atrum, is considered a systemic disease.  The pathogen can be isolated from all parts of infected plants, including roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds. The pathogen can be disseminated with infected planting materials such as seeds, tubers (potato) and straw (lucerne hay). Trading of these materials therefore risks the presence of V. albo-atrum in infected seeds, tubers and hay or as surface contaminants on these commodities.Plant parts liable to carry the pest in trade/transport - Bulbs/Tubers/Corms/Rhizomes: Hyphae; borne internally; invisible.^p - Fruits (inc. management_info: Introduction^p^pThere are no prophylactic or therapeutic fungicides that give satisfactory control under field conditions. The diseases caused by V. albo-atrum have been controlled mainly through the use of resistant varieties, by reducing inoculum and by limiting spread.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pHop growing in England, UK, has largely survived by adopting a succession of increasingly wilt-tolerant hop cultivars to outpace increases in pathogenicity in evolving populations of V. albo-atrum. ^p^pIn lucerne, breeding for resistane is the most effective measure for control of Verticillium wilt. In addition to field testing, several indoor methods including the root-trainer method (Huang and Hanna, 1991) and detached leaf method (Plazek, 1996) have been developed for screeing lucerne for resistance to Verticillium wilt. The root-trainer method has been used successfully to identify susceptibility of Chinese lucerne cultivars (Huang et al., 1999) and to develop new lucerne cultivars with resistance to Verticillium wilt in Canadian cultivars including Barrier (Hanna and Huang, 1987), AC Blue J (Acharya et al., 1995) and AC Longview (Acharya and Huang, 2000). Examples of European cultivars with resistance to Verticillum wilt are Vertus (Busch et al., 1985), Szarvasi (Mistinova, 1999), Jitka (Chloupek, 1996a) and Niva (Chloupek, 1996b). In British Columbia, Canada, Stout et al. (1998) reported the possibility of increasing persistence of lucerne stand by sowing mixtures of winter hardy and Verticillium-wilt-resistant cultivars such as Barrier. In the USA, examples of lucerne cultivars with resistance to Verticillium wilt are Parade (Cash et al., 1998a), Tahoe (Cash et al., 1998b) and Multistar (Stratton, 1997).^p^pIn potato, the use of resistant or tolerant cultivars has helped to control wilt in many parts of the world. Goth and Haynes (2000) observed an improvement in yield and quality of potato clones with Verticillium wilt resistance. Jarl et al. (1999) found a wild relative of aubergine, Solanum torvum, which was tolerant to Verticillium wilt and offered potential to transfer this tolerance to aubergine. Lynch et al. (1997) reported that resistance to V. albo-atrum in potato was controlled by a single dominant gene and they concluded that transfer of the Vc gene to tetraploid germplasm could provide effective, economical control of Verticillium wilt. Koike et al. (1996a) observed that callus derived from the cultivar Triumph also showed tolerance to culture filtrates of V. albo-atrum.  The American cultivar St. John is morderately resistant to both V. albo-atrum and V. dahliae (Reeves et al., 1996).^p^pTomato cultivars containing the Ve resistance gene are widely employed to combat the problem of verticillium, although variants of V. albo-atrum able to overcome this gene have appeared recently in the Netherlands (Paternotte and Van Kesteren, 1993). Two tomato cultivars, Hybrid Atina and Hybrid Golden Jubilee, with resistance to V. albo-atrum, were developed for commercial production in Yugoslavia (Markovic et al., 1997). Two American cultivars, Prairie Schooner (Summers, 1966a), Prairie Dawn (Summers, 1966b) and Prairie Pastemaker (Summers, 1966c) are resistant to race 1 of V. albo-atrum.^p^pResistance to V. albo-atrum has also been reported in other crops. Two sweet pepper lines, L 61/3 and L 62/1, with resistance to V. albo-atrum were proposed for cultivar registration in Yugoslavia (Starcevic et al., 1997).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pA chemical, methoxybifurcarenone, isolated from the brown alga Cystoseira tamariscifolia was found to possess antifungal activity against V.albo-atrum (Bennamara et al., 1999).^p^pSeed treatment^p^pSeed treatment and quarantine measures have failed to prevent the introduction of V. albo-atrum into new geographical areas. 黄萎病(Verticillium albo-atrum Reinke&Betthold)是苜蓿的毁灭性病害，在欧洲常于播种当年就有许多植株发病，第二年末或第三年会有大批植株死亡，使苜蓿地失去利用价值。1976年以后，本病在北美流行，并造成巨大经济损失。有效而实际的防治措施是利用抗病品种。中国尚未发现苜蓿黄萎病；但是我国有许多苜蓿种植地区的气候条件与北美的病区近似，病害一旦传人有发展流行的危险。作者于1992年在加拿大Lethbridge农业研究站对5个中国北方广为种植的苜蓿品种和1个野生黄花苜蓿(Medicago falcataL．)做了室内接种鉴定，现将结果简报如下。
  供试菌种是从加拿大Alberta省分离的Verticillium albo-atrum苜蓿菌系。中国苜蓿品种有：公农1号、和田苜蓿、肇东苜蓿、草原1号、草原2号等5个品种和来自内蒙古的野生黄花苜蓿。试验对照用感病品为种植的苜蓿品种公农1号、和田、肇东、种为北美的"Anchor”,抗病品种为欧洲的“Vertus”和加拿大的“Barrier”以及一个新品系"Vw-34-2”苜蓿播种后，在每日16小时光照和8小时黑暗条件下的生长室内生长，有光照时的室温20℃，黑暗时室温15℃。生长12周龄的苜蓿苗，用浸根法接种，以清水浸根为对照。接种后继续在生长室内生长，4周后进行病情调查。病害严重度分为5级。根据平均严重度(发病指数)和抗病植株(1～2级)百分率来评价它们的抗病性。两次鉴定结果看出，抗病品种与感病品种间的差异是明显的，5个中国苜蓿品种和野生黄花苜蓿均属感病类型(见表1)。•在两次鉴定中，同一个品种的病情严重度和抗病植株百分率也会有较大差异，但这是试验本身的误差，抗病品种与感病品种的排列顺序并无太大变化。从两次室内鉴定结果看，中国北方广为种植的苜蓿品种公农1号、和田、肇东、草原1号、草原2号以及内蒙古的野生黄花苜蓿均属感病类型，它们的平均发病指数，接近北美的感病品种"Anchor”。这个结果预示着一旦苜蓿黄萎病传入中国，其扩展速度可能是很快的，造成的损失也将是巨大的。加强对苜蓿黄萎病的检疫防范措施势在必行。
reference_name: 中国苜蓿品种对黄萎病抗病性鉴定

description: 苜蓿黄萎病由黑白轮枝菌Verticillium albo-atrum引起，20世纪20年代首次发现于瑞典，其后在欧洲迅速扩散，并于1926年在加拿大魁北克省罗蔓蒂尔和大不列颠哥伦比亚省温哥华农业研究站实验地发现该病侵害。由于扑灭及时，当时病原未能定殖。1976年美国华盛顿州哥伦比亚河流域突然发现大量苜蓿黄萎病株，标志着该病传入北美并定殖成功，此后该病在北美迅速蔓延，广泛发生。

management_info:
苜蓿黄萎病引起美国和加拿大政府高度重视，通过一系列封锁控制与治理措施，90年代该病得到逐步控制。
1.彻底铲除新发生区的苜蓿黄萎病病原
2.长期实施严格的检疫控制和调查监测
3.广泛开展苜蓿黄萎病发病机理和控制方法研究
4.大力选育并推广抗病品种

management_info: （1）在种植前，对被带病土壤污染的种薯应该进行药剂处理，用液剂处理比粉剂处理效果更好。处理药剂可采用内吸杀菌剂（苯莱特或甲基托布津）或非内吸杀菌剂（代森锰、克菌丹）。（2）有几种线虫能提高轮枝菌萎蔫病的发病率和严重度。因此，采用杀线虫的土壤熏蒸剂也能防治病害。    （1）与禾谷类、其他禾本科和豆科作物轮作，避免与高度感病的茄科植物进行轮作。（2）种植抗病品种。（3）防治感病的杂草。（4）植物检疫，禁止调运和种植马铃薯黄委病产区的马铃薯种薯。能侵染苜蓿的黑白轮枝菌是《中华人民共和国进出境植物检疫危险病、虫、杂草名录》中规定的一类检疫性病原真菌。

management_info:
1. 加强检疫。划定疫区和保护区，封锁疫区，严防从病区引进苗木接穗，防止此病蔓延。
2. 落叶后清扫果园。收集病叶集中烧毁或深埋，清除侵染源。春季在子囊孢子成熟分散前，用10%硫酸铵或5%尿素液地面喷洒，杀死叶中越冬病菌。
3. 喷药保护。根据春季降雨情况和空中子囊孢子预测，从落花后至春稍停止生长期喷洒1：2：200~400式波尔多液、65%代森锌可湿性粉剂600倍液等杀菌剂2~3次，预防侵染。

potential_eco_desc: Losses from scab over a period of years far exceed those from any other disease or pest of apples. The major economic loss to the grower is the reduction in fruit quality of scabbed apples. Severe attack of the leaves will cause mid-season defoliation and a reduction of tree vigour which, in turn may led to failure of fruit bud formation and to stunted and reduced growth. In regions and years with favourable weather conditions for scab infection and with a high PAD, nearly all the fruits may be infected. management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pBreeding programmes are in progress to develop high-quality apple cultivars that are resistant to V. inaequalis (Fischer et al., 1998;Kellerhals et al., 1997, 1998; Goerre et al., 1999; Lateur et al., 1999). In the past, such programmes have mainly been based on the monogenic resistance from Malus floribunda 821 (Vf). In 1988, at Ahrensburg, Germany, small sporulating scab lesions were found on some Vf -hybrid selections. It was later found in other countries that this resistance was not of a durable type. Different races of apple scab are already detected (Kruger et al., 1999). The appearance of race 6, overcoming the resistance of cultivars with the Vf gene and race 7, overcoming the resistance in Malus floribunda (Benaouf and Parisi, 2000) has lead to new breeding programmes with the aim to develop cultivars with a different genetic basis for resistance against scab. Genetically controlled resistance exists for at least five genes (Vf, Vm, Vr, Vb and Vbj) (Hemmat et al., 2000).^p  ^pDARE (Durable Apple Resistance in Europe), set up in 1998 as a joint project between different institutes in Europe was an important initiative to develop durable resistance in new apple varieties to scab and powdery mildew (Lespinasse et al., 2000).     ^p^pInvestigations on the virulence pattern in field isolates of V. inaequalis provided evidence that variation between isolates depends on the biodiversity within the planted cultivars. Orchards with few or only one main cultivar selected a more homogeneous scab population, with all isolates carrying the specific virulence to the dominant cultivar. This offers opportunities to reduce the susceptibility, depending of the planting design of an orchard. In a mixed orchard a large share of the pathogen population will be eliminated from the epidemic process in spring as the ascospores will land on tissue of a non-host (Koch et al., 2000).  ^p^pGenetic studies suggest that in addition to short distance gene flow, dispersal over longer distance by humans also occurs, probably due to transport of infected plant material (Tenzer and Gessler, 1999). ^p^pMolecular biological techniques on varieties and scab strains can improve the search on which varieties should be planted together to enhance the biodiversity in an orchard and to reduce the spread of apple scab in such orchards (MacHardy et al., 2001).^p^pPolygenic resistance and gene transfer technology is the basis for obtaining more tolerant cultivars (Rees et al., 1996; Kellerhals et al., 1997; Lespinasse et al., 1999; Aldwinckle et al., 1999). ^p^pConventional breeding of scab-resistant apple varieties requires at least 15 years. Resistance in these varieties is based on a single gene, which is not very durable, and the quality of most resistant varieties on the market today is below that which would be accepted by the consumer. Multiple resistance genes are desirable but this is very difficult to realize using conventional methods. Researchers around the world are involved in the development and optimisation of protocols for transformation of different apple cultivars of high market value. management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pResistance appears to be due to a significant reduction in the number of appressoria formed by the fungus on resistant species (for example, Gladiolus daleni) compared to the number formed on susceptible cultivars (for example, Goldfield) (Ferreira and Rijkenberg, 1991). An evaluation schedule and a standardized artificial inoculation technique have been developed. All cultivars evaluated were susceptible to U. transversalis; the most resistant species were G. daleni, G. ochroleucus, G. papilio, G. tristis var. concolor and G. tristis var. tristis. Very resistant selections were obtained from the following crosses: G. alatus x G. tristis; Vuurland x G. tristis; Campanella and Nymph x G. angustus; and G. daleni x G. carinatus. The inheritance of resistance from G. daleni and G. tristis has been described.^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pGaribaldi and Aloj (1980) found that systemic fungicides gave better control than preventive chemicals and weekly application of oxycarboxin or benodanil from symptom manifestation till at least appearance of inflorescences gave the best control and are therefore recommended.Aloj and Garibaldi (1980) found that in glasshouse trials with 61 cultivars, Junior Promm, Summer melody and Blondine appeared resistant.Pandolfo and Garibaldi (1986) reported that benodanil, bitertanol, fenpropimorf, myclobutanil, propiconazole, S-3308 [?diniconazole], DPX H-6573 [flusilazole] and penconazole + captan gave excellent control in field trials; no phytotoxicity was noted.Ferreira and Nevill (1989) reported that weekly applications of bitertanol or triadimefon gave significantly better control of U. transversalis than fenarimol and performed better than oxycarboxin, penconazole, EDTA, CuEDTA and DTPA. There was a direct relationship between the number of applications and the incidence of rust. Rolim et al. (1985) found that weekly sprays with bitertanol, mancozeb and chlorothalonil, gave the best control on the basis of results from field trials against natural infection. Results were evaluated by leaf infection and bulb weight.

potential_eco_desc: Onion smut is of sporadic occurrence and generally of minor importance in terms of yields or financial returns (Locke and McBurney, 1995; F Crowe, Central Oregon Agricultural Centre, Madras, USA, personal communication, 1997). At times, however, the disease can affect 70-90% of seedlings and 40% of mature bulbs and reduce yields by 70% (McDonald et al., 1996; McDonald and Janse, 1997). The reasons for site to site variations in smut incidence are not understood. Even minor outbreaks of smut can have far-reaching consequences: following reports of smut in the Marshlands area, onion exports from Canterbury, New Zealand, were suspended, starting again in 1989 (Harrow, 1970a; Grant, 1990; Jermyn et al., 1993). Onion smut does not affect bulbs in store but may increase their susceptibility to other diseases.

description: Incidence^p^pU. cepulae may be found in onion seed lots unattached to the seeds, although this is poorly documented (Mulder and Holliday, 1971). ^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pThere is no evidence for seed transmission of U. cepulae. The pathogen is primarily soilborne (Mulder and Holliday, 1971).^p^p^Seed Treatments^p^pA variety of fungicidal seed treatments reduce smut incidence by controlling soilborne infection. Tebuconazole in combination with soaking in manganese and tebuconazole alone gave total control of smut in pot tests in Egypt and there was no evidence of phytotoxicity (El-Shehaby, 1995). In the same tests, flutriafol was less effective and a prochloraz-carboxin-manganese mixture was phytotoxic. Mancozeb in combination with carboxin and thiram reduced smut incidence by ca 40% when the smut incidence was as high as 70% in untreated plots (McDonald et al., 1996; McDonald and Janse, 1997). ^p^pThiram, quinolate and thiophanate-methyl have also been shown to reduce smut incidence (Cotton, 1919; Macias, 1974a). Certain seed treatments targeted at seedling damping-off or insect attack may also reduce onion smut (Canada Department of Agriculture, 1977). The registration requirements for the use of fungicides should be consulted.

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl measures specifically against smut are practised in areas with a history of the disease but probably not elsewhere.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pField tests in Canada demonstrated considerable variation in response to U. cepulae between 66 Allium cepa cultivars and 255 accessions (Utkhede and Rahe, 1980). A. cepa cv. Hardy White and Wolska, accessions G19685, 164807 and 250660, had high to total resistance to smut (Utkhede and Rahe, 1980). The cultivars Buccaneer, Mustang and Northern Oak (Anon., 1974) and cvs. Giza 6, Giza 20, Shandaweel 1, Red Creole, Hybrids Y 28 and Dessex, cvs Sensuchuko, Yamagochi Kodoka, F1 Fuarni and Sapporiki (Mohamed et al., 1986b) showed some resistance. Allium altaicum, A. obliquum, A. nutans and A. odorum were totally resistant (Semenov, 1977).^p^pIt is not known whether the differences in response of Allium spp. to U. cepulae represent genetic resistance, or some other factor. The predominance of symptoms at the seedling stage suggests that changes in physiology or morphology may be factors involved in the expression of resistance to smut. ^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pShallow sowing depth, moderate temperatures and adequate soil moisture are key factors that favour rapid seedling emergence and hence reduce smut incidence by minimising exposure at the susceptible cotyledon and first leaf stages (Sienstra and Lacy, 1972; Wale and Goats, 1984; Chaput, 1995; LP Moreno, CINVESTAV, Mexico, personal communication 1997). ^p^pThe occurrence of smut in established and intensive onion-growing areas, together with the known role of soilborne infection, suggests that rotation with non-Allium crops is advisable (Croxall and Hickman, 1953). However, onions require high standards of cultivation and their commercial production is limited by the availability of fertile, well-structured soils with adequate water reserves. As a result, rotations may be shorter than is desirable and this may be a factor in the prevalence of smut. The long period of teliospore survival suggest that rotation is the ideal rather than a practical solution. ^p^pAs a result of the brief period of susceptibility of onion at the cotyledon stage, healthy seedlings can be safely transplanted to infested soil (Duran and Fischer, 1959).^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pFoliar fungicide treatment of onions has been reported to increase susceptibility to smut (Mohamed et al., 1986a; El Shehaby and Mohamed, 1987). Various soil fumigants, for example, methyl isothiocyanate, dazomet and formalin, are reported to control soilborne U. cepulae (Harrow, 1970b; Macias, 1974b; Grant, 1990). A variety of fungicidal seed treatments have also been reported to reduce smut incidence (see Seed Treatments in section on Seedborne Aspects of Disease).

potential_eco_desc: Dwarf bunt is a serious disease, particularly of winter wheat at relatively high altitudes. It is very difficult to control because of the resistant resting spores which remain viable in the soil for a number of years and because most seed-applied fungicides are not effective. In Oregon, USA, in 1952-1953, dwarf bunt destroyed 50-90% of the seed in several 1-year-old fields of Elymus hispidus and Arrhenatherum elatius (Hordison, 1963). Disease is occasionally severe in susceptible cultivars of winter wheat in the western USA where wheat is grown under a persistent snow cover. In 1983, Grey et al. (1986) examined 552 samples of wheat being exported from the Pacific Northwestern USA for T. controversa. Of the samples tested, 411 were found to be infected, but none contained levels greater than 1 g of teliospores/kg of seed. Further experiments found that bunted spikes only occurred at levels of infection higher than the samples described and only in disease-conducive conditions (Grey et al., 1986). They then concluded that the risk of transmission of high levels of disease to new areas by such low levels of infestation was minimal. Since February 1974, the export of wheat from Pacific Northwest ports to China has been halted as China has prohibited the introduction of grain carrying dwarf bunt.^p^pThe possibility for establishment of T. controversa in winter wheat regions in China was assessed by simulation models and geographical information system (GIS) by Chen et al (2002). The winter wheat regions were divided into four areas, high, medium, low and basically no risk areas. In the high risk area, T. controversa occurs over nine times every eighteen years; the medium risk area, four to eight times every eighteen years; and the low risk area, one to three times every eighteen years. The percentage of areas with high and medium risk is 19.3% of the whole winter wheat regions of the country.^p^pIn Italy, epidemic outbreaks of dwarf bunt were reported in 1879, 1919, 1929 and 1946; however, in 1956, the disease was reported not to cause great concern. In Bavaria (Germany), up to 30% losses in wheat yield were recorded on crops grown more than once in a rotation of 5-6 years. In the 1970s, the disease was reported to be of great economic importance in the EPPO region in Austria, Poland and the former USSR and of less economic importance in the other countries in which it is established.^p^pWhile the dwarf bunt fungus only affects a small portion of the total wheat production worldwide, presence of this disease has heightened economic importance due to the possibility of spread of the disease to uninfected areas (Mathre, 1996).

The usefulness of the kernels for milling is reduced. Pirson (1978) estimated that 5 mg of bunt balls could contain as many as 1 million spores.^p^p^Pathogen Transmission^p^pSpores adhering to the seed can contaminate uninfested soil and, under suitable conditions, germinate and penetrate the emerging seedling where infection becomes systemic (Neergaard, 1977). Field tests were conducted in five states of the USA over 2 years to determine if seedborne T. controversa teliospores could induce disease. Bunted spikes resulted only when heavily infested seed (>1 g teliospores/kg) was planted in disease-conducive locations (Grey et al., 1986).^p^pThe incidence of T. controversa as a function of inoculum density was studied at three disease-conducive locations in Montana, USA, for three seasons (1993-1996) (Goates and Peterson, 1999). In soil-inoculated plots, a minimum of 16 x 103 teliospores/row was needed to cause trace amounts of disease (0.6% maximum). Only trace amounts or no disease occurred below the 16 x 10(dayuhao)(sup)5> rate. In the seed-inoculated plots, infection was rare and occurred only at inoculation rates of 2 x 10(dayuhao)(sup)5> teliospores/g or higher, with the highest disease incidence being 0.4%.^p^p^Seed Treatment^p^pFungicides^p^pIn a test of 22 formulations of fungicidal seed treatments, thiabendazole provided the highest level of control (Hoffman et al., 1983). Mathre et al. (1990) found that infection of healthy seed was reduced when seeds were treated with formulations containing carboxin or thiabendazole. All teliospores of T. controversa were destroyed when 0.13 M NaOCl was applied at 55°C for 30 seconds (Chastain, 1991). remark: T. solani belongs to the group of South American pests of potato, still confined to that continent, which present a high risk to commercial potato-growing areas around the world. The particular risk factors for T. solani are that it attacks tubers directly (with immediate effect on yield and quality), that no potato disease resembling it occurs elsewhere in the world, and that it can readily contaminate tuber consignments in the form of latent infections or surface contamination by teliospores. Because it is soil-borne, it would be virtually impossible to eradicate once established. On the other hand, its potential economic importance in intensive potato production is not clear, nor is it certain under what climatic conditions it could establish and, therefore, which areas are the most threatened. It has mostly been reported from the Andean region, for example above 3000 m in Venezuela (O'Brien and Thirumulachar, 1974) or from the mountains in Peru (Abbott, 1932). However, the Abbott (1932) also mentions its presence at sea level in Peru. In any case, its establishment (even at non-damaging levels) in countries producing seed potatoes would pose considerable problems for their export certification.^p^pEPPO lists T. solani as an A1 quarantine pest (OEPP/EPPO, 1979) and it is also a quarantine pest for CPPC.
author: CPC2006

management_info: In field trials in Peru, soil applications of methyl bromide and dazomet reduced the total weight of hypertrophied tubers, but did not eliminate T. solani (Torres and Henfling, 1984). Susceptibility of potato cultivars to infection varies and screening for resistance is actively carried out at CIP (International Potato Center) in Peru (Torres and Martin, 1986). General control measures recommended in Hooker (1981) include the use of resistant cultivars, planting of smut-free seed potatoes, long rotations, elimination of the weed Datura stramonium (also reported as a host) and the removal of smutted galls.^p^pAs for other South American pests of potato, the recommended procedure for other parts of the world is post-entry quarantine, together with equivalent checks before export. Only material for scientific purposes should normally be imported from infested countries.^p^pConsignments from areas in which the disease occurs can carry infection at undetectable levels or as spores on the surface of healthy tubers. Inspections cannot be fully reliable and there is no alternative to a quarantine period to ensure freedom from the disease.

description:
Observations of potato plantations undertaken in different agro-ecological zones of Georgia during 2009-2013 showed that potato wart occurred only in the Khulo area, which is the most mountainous region in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, Western Georgia. The region is considered as economically important for potato production. 
PWD symptoms - galls of various colours (from yellow-green to brown) – were observed on the tubers for the first time in Tabakhmela and Didajara villages in June 2009. However, the growers from these villages informed us that disease symptoms had been noted in 2006 and 2007 on potato cv. 'Agria', which is widely grown here for home consumption. According to the survey results from 2010-2012, the disease was also found in other villages of Khulo municipality (Ghorjomi, Tkhilvana, Danisparauli) on varieties Agria, Finka, Picasso and Marfona. The disease symptoms were observed on the tubers, stolons and root neck. In 2013, by the end of potato growing season, the disease was also found in Diakonidzeebi village (Khulo region) and in stored potato in cellars too. The test demonstrated that the pathogen was Synchytrium endobioticum. To our knowledge, this is the first report of potato wart disease caused by Synchytrium endobioticum in Georgia.
remark: The National Agency of Food Safety of Georgia lists Synchytrium endobioticum as an A2 quarantine pest.
reference_name: First report of Synchytrium endobioticum causing potato wart in Georgia

description: 此病1895年最早报道于匈牙利，以后欧洲北部、中部大多数国家相继发生，在英格兰是1896年由Cooke和1902年由Potter记载，在苏格兰和威尔士出现是1902年由Wilson和Bryner Jones报道的，在北美洲，1909年Gussow首次记载此病在加拿大纽芬兰的发生情况，1910年由Gussow提议在加拿大制定了马铃薯癌肿病法规，1912年颁布。美国1918年在西弗吉尼亚和宾夕法尼亚、1926年在马里兰有此病大发生的记录。在南美洲，1928年在秘鲁第一次报道发病情况，亚洲各马铃薯产区也相继通过引种而传入，1953年在西孟加拉大吉岑地区第一次发生此病害。但马铃薯癌肿病起源于何地，至今尚无定论。  被感染的土壤，农事操作时人畜传带，吃了病薯的牲畜粪，雨水和灌溉水等进行近距离传播，食用薯或种薯调运进行远距离传播。
management_info:
1. 划分疫区、封锁疫区、严格检疫外。
2. 建立无病种薯繁育基地，同步推广经过茎尖脱毒、组织繁殖、无土栽培、工厂化生产或家庭网箱生产的脱毒微型种薯和常规抗病品种。种植抗病品种。
3. 合理轮作。可采取与燕麦、玉米、亚麻、向日葵、油菜及豆类等作物长期轮作。
4. 药剂和生物防治。用噻唑钠或生石灰作土壤处理，对癌肿病有防治效果。在病区内使用对癌肿病菌有拮抗作用的放线菌，减少侵染。
remark: 马铃薯癌肿病是世界许多国家马铃薯生产上的严重的危险性病害。现已遍及世界五大洲的50多个国家，并有32个国家将此病列为检疫对象，此病是我国的重要植物检疫对象之一。

potential_eco_desc: S. endobioticum infects epidermal cells of young potato organs, such as eyes, sprouts, young tubers, stolons, stems, leaves, and even flowers, but never roots.
description: In 2008, the Polish Inspectorate of Plant Health and Seed Inspection (PIORiN) collected soil samples from Mazowieckie Region in Central Poland. Microscopic examinations revealed the presence of viable resting spores of S. endobioticum in a soil sample collected from a crop plantation of ornamentals intended for export. One kilogram of soil contained an average of 300 viable spores. A bioassay (pot tests), recommended by the EPPO standard PM 3/59, showed no wart symptoms because of the very low sporangium density of S. endobioticum. However, concentrating S. endobioticum inoculum by centrifugation and using for a bioassay modified Potocek's tube test allowed us to obtain fresh galls with summer sporangia. The first symptoms of PWD were visible on sprouts of extremely susceptible potato genotypes 7 weeks after inoculation. To identify the pathotype of S. endobioticum, 10 differential potato cultivars (Deodara, Tomensa, Eersteling, Producent, Combi, Saphir, Delcora, Miriam, Karolin, and Ulme) were inoculated with fresh galls of S. endobioticum using the Glynne-Lemmerzahl method, according to EPPO standard PM 7/28. Galls were formed on all cultivars except Saphir, Karolin, and Ulme (resistant cultivars). This virulence profile was identical to that of European pathotype 18(T1) of S. endobioticum. This is the first detection in Poland of pathotype 18(T1).  Synchytrium endobioticum (Schilb.) Perc. is a soil-borne biotrophic fungus causing potato wart disease (PWD) of cultivated potato.
remark: S. endobioticum survives in the soil as winter (resting) spores, which germinate, infect the plant, and produce secondary sporangia (summer spores); infection results in galls on the stolons and tubers, in which the pathogen multiplies. Its long persistence in soil and the severe losses it inflicts to potato crops have prompted its inclusion into the A2 quarantine list.
reference_name: First Report of Synchytrium endobioticum (Potato Wart Disease) Pathotype 18(T1) in Poland

potential_eco_desc: Wart disease of potato is so important that quarantine and domestic legislation has been in force globally for more than 65 years to prevent its spread and dissemination. In the 1950s and 1960s numerous EPPO publications were devoted to the disease. Once the pathogen has been introduced to a field of potato cultivation the whole crop may be devastated and unmarketable.  Moreover, introduction into the soil not only renders the crop unusable but the soil itself cannot be used for further crop production due to the longevity of the fungus. Crops other than potato grown in this soil cannot be used for export. EEC Council Directive 69'464/CEE, 1969-12-08, requires the use of officially specified resistant potato cultivars in a protection zone around infested land. These (mainly applied domestically) stringent quarantine and sanitation measures have contained the disease in the EPPO region, and direct losses resulting from the pathogen are minimal. S. endobioticum generally has a much more limited distribution outside of Europe. Indirect losses arising from restrictions on the export of plants from infested areas present a problem to European countries.
author: CPC2006

description: S. endobioticum has a very limited means of spread and dispersal.  Spread in soil by zoospores is limited (50 mm or less) to the infection zones of the plant. Soil water can carry zoospores downstream, although the lifespan of a released zoospore is 1-2 hours. Earthworms can move resting spores short distances. Wind is an active dispersal agent in regions of strong dry summer winds. Local dispersal has been shown in resting spores in soil attached to vehicles and contaminated manure. Long-range dispersal by tuber-movement, especially in international trade, attached soil and plants presents problems of control. Control though statutory methods has been largely successful due to the fungus' self-limited means of dispersal. Though present in many countries, it has a very restricted distribution within them, which justifies its quarantine status. management_info: Phytosanitary Methods^p^pControl of wart disease of potato relies in the main upon statutory measures.  According to OEPP/EPPO (1990) specific quarantine requirement, potatoes should derive from a stock free of S. endobioticum. Potatoes and indeed any kind of plants with roots (including bulbs, corms and tubers) for export, should not be grown in fields where S. endobioticum has occurred or is still present on account of the fungus' longevity factor.^p^pIn practice, this means an extensive system of 'scheduling' 'wart-infested' fields. This system relates back to the early 20th century epidemics. Fields may be 'descheduled' if they can be shown to be pathogen-free. Studies relating to this issue are in progress. The longevity factor of S. endobioticum is still a subject of debate and is the controlling factor in the 'descheduling' process. Those countries in which only pathotype 1 occurs are advised to determine that imported tubers come only from areas where other pathotypes have not been recorded. The common pathotype in Newfoundland, Canada, is pathotype 2; the island portion of the Province was quarantined in 1911, and remains in effect.^p^p^Host-Plant Resistance^p^pWart-resistance remains an important element to be considered in breeding programmes, particularly in Central and Eastern Europe. New screening methods have recently been described.

description:
从在南美洲的马铃薯上所产生的真菌的迹象看，马铃薯癌肿病的原产地可能是南美。报导过这个病的有智利、乌拉圭、玻利维亚、福克兰群岛，尤其是秘鲁。在秘鲁第一次报导癌肿病是在1928年，在豪哈附近喀奇喀奇的一个农场的场主反映，该病已在那里发生许多年了。病害分布很广，都在中部山区，海拔3200至4000米之间，北是卡哈马卡（约南纬7度），最南是普诺（约南纬16度），几乎是秘鲁的整个安第斯山脉（约长1450公里）。鉴于与欧洲相距遥远，并且此病分布的地区都在海拔高处，因此很难相信带病的欧洲薯块曾经被运入这个最先发生癌肿病的很孤立偏避的地方。所以癌肿病可能是秘鲁本地的，而且可能起源于那里。
尼德好塞（Niederhauser）主张，就墨西哥在野生马铃薯上发现这种病的三个地点的其中二处来看，这种病不大可能是从外地传入的。兴提卡（Hintikka）从他的癌肿病在不同国家的气象因子的研究中得出结论，马铃薯癌肿病原产地是欧洲。波伊南斯基（Bojnansky）说英国是这种真菌的原产地。莱皮克（Lepik）认为这种病是从英格兰传到海外国家的，包括秘鲁。奥尔腾（Orton）的判断是该病的原产地在苏联，从那里向西传播的。
文件上说得很清楚，马铃薯是通过西班牙传入欧洲的，而且有证据证明，也大大侧重支持从秘鲁引来的说法。然而，没有资料记载这个病害曾发生在西班牙。伊波南斯基认为西班牙的环境条件是不利于该病发展的，西班牙的环境条件足以使马铃薯在进入欧洲其部分之前已摆脱了马铃薯癌肿病病原菌。在1840-1850年间晚疫病灾难性的暴发之后，许多国家开展了马铃薯育种，许多马铃薯栽培品种和各种茄科属植物多次从南美进入欧洲。马铃薯癌肿病可能就是偶然随着这些进口的马铃薯而传入的。推测此病在英国发生大约是在十九世纪七十年代。
在英格兰，马铃薯癌肿病显然早就有了。顾夫推测它在英国农村菜园里早在1876年就发生了。泰勒（Taylor）引用了一份未说明来源的资料，说在东洛锡安（苏格兰东南部）在马铃薯上发生此病也是在1976年，而结论是从1907年起马铃薯获得经济地位之前许多年，英国已存在这一病害。有些人主张这个病是在1893年随着马铃薯货物从英国进入芬兰的。1909年古绍（Gussow）在访问加拿大纽芬兰时，发现该病分布十分广泛。1910年古绍提议在加拿大制订马铃薯癌肿病的法规，1912年5月和9月加拿大颁布了此项法规。纽芬兰是加拿大有此病扎根的唯一的省。1914年在新斯科舍的哈利法克斯曾有一次小发生，并且很快就消灭掉了。1957年，基乃劳（Genereux）报导，在拉布拉多半岛北岸发生该病。美国关于记录此病大发生的记录是1918年在西弗吉尼亚和宾夕法尼亚，1926年在马里兰。

management_info: Introduction^p^pControl of H. bajulus involves the application of liquid insecticides to the surface of infested wood or the use of fumigants or heat to treat the entire structure. The choice depends on the degree of infestation and whether immediate control is desired Robinson, 1990, 1998). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pSurface treatment is best just before adult emergence to prevent re-infestation by the adult beetle. Most chemicals do not penetrate deep enough into the wood to kill the larval stage nor do larvae feed on treated wood. Localized infestations may be treated with spray or paintbrush applications. The application of borates is environmentally sound, with low mammalian toxicity, and borates are readily absorbed into wood (Petric et al., 2000). Pyrethroids are also very effective (Powell and Robinson, 1992). Licensed pest control operators can drill into infested timbers and introduce insecticides under pressure to force the toxicant throughout the gallery system. It may take a few months to a year to see results, such as a reduction in chewing sounds. More recently, wood destroying borers have been treated with insect growth regulators or their analogues (Cymorek and Pospischil, 1984; Wegen, 1996). These chemicals interfere with the insects' metabolism during their development and cause larval death due to incomplete moulting. Insect growth regulators act very specifically and are applied at very low rates.^p^pWhole-house fumigation is a last resort for infestations that are active and widespread, where damage is significant and an immediate end to the chewing sounds is desired. Fumigation kills all stages of H. bajulus in the wood. In log houses the amount of fumigant used and the amount of time the chemical is held in the structure may have to be increased due to the moisture content of the logs and their greater width compared with a conventional house. Methyl bromide, hydrogen cyanide gas, phosphine, and sulfuryl fluoride have been used satisfactorily (Michelsen, 1964; Rasmussen, 1967c; Unger, 1983; Anon., 1985). Only licensed pest control operators or applicators can apply fumigants. The process requires the structure to be covered with gas-proof tarpaulins for several days. Fumigation will not leave any residual chemical on the wood surface to prevent subsequent re-infestation. Any serious structural defects caused by extensive borer feeding must be replaced or repaired.^p^p^Cultural Control and Sanitary Methods^p^pHeat sterilization of wood to kill H. bajulus is effective only when temperatures of at least 55°C are generated in the centre of the wooden logs for at least 60 minutes (Schmidt and Schneider, 1957; Becker, 1984). For this purpose hot air at temperatures up to 120°C must be transferred into the structure. Like fumigation, hot air treatment will not prevent subsequent re-infestation.^p^pInvestigations into the feasibility of killing H. bajulus with microwaves indicated that a technique based on microwave heating of infested wood can be successfully applied in practice (Andreuccetti, 1994).
remark: H. bajulus is considered a quarantine pest in Australia, New Zealand, USA and Canada.

host_range: To our knowledge, this is the first report of bacterial black spot disease caused by Acidovorax konjaci in cucumber(Cucumis sativus) in Korea. Occurrence of disease caused by A. konjaci has been reported in two vegetables, konjac (Amorphophallus konjac) and Korean radish.

description: In 2013, we detected necrotic, water-soaked leaves and black spots in a commercial cucumber seedling nursery in Yeongam-gun, Jeonnam Province, Korea. Plants exhibiting symptoms were fewer than 5% of the total 5,000 cucumber plants. More than five diseased plants were collected from the field. Severity of symptoms was manifested by black spots on the leaves. Young leaves displayed more severe symptoms than the cotyledons. The causal pathogen was isolated from the black leaf spots. The pathogen was identified as Acidovorax konjaci  by molecular diagnostics and the pathogenicity. To our knowledge, this is the first report of bacterial black spot disease caused by A. konjaci in cucumber in Korea.

potential_eco_desc: In spite of the polyphagous nature of this insect, serious damage is confined mainly to carnation crops in the Mediterranean area, where losses have been reported since the 1920s. In France, around Nice, 25-35% of carnations were affected in 1972-1973, and losses in consignments for export were valued at about 100,000 F. In Morocco, C. pronubana was first found in 1933, on citrus, but it was not until 20 years later that it developed into a widespread pest on this crop, the larvae destroying foliage and damaging fruit. In Algeria, it is found mainly on lemons, but is not considered a serious pest. In Italy (Sicily) surveys reported C. pronubana mainly on olives, weeds and roses but not on lemons (Inserra et al., 1987; Siscaro et al., 1988). In northern countries (for example, Poland), C. pronubana is important in glasshouses.

This means practically that the insect has reached the limits of its natural range. However, C. pronubana is a threat to glasshouse crops, especially carnations and other flowers and ornamental plants. For more information, see Balachowsky (1966).
author: CPC2006

management_info: Control of C. pronubana can be achieved by using pyrethroids such as deltamethrin and fenvalerate (Pandolfo and Zagami, 1983; Inserra et al., 1987). Control of C. pronubana by biological means has not been fully investigated. Monitoring of C. pronubana populations is carried out by sex pheromone traps, but their use as a direct control agent by means of mating disruption is still being questioned (Guda and Capizzi, 1988).^p^pBurgess and Jarret (1978) studied the effect of Bacillus thuringiensis on C. pronubana in glasshouses but found that a higher than normal dose was necessary for effectiveness. Wysoki (1989) tested its effect in Israel where the moth is a pest of avocados. Pheremones have been used extensively for monitoring populations, details are given in Quaglia (1993).^p^pEPPO recommends (OEPP/EPPO, 1990) that, in countries where C. pronubana occurs, nursery inspections should be carried out during the growing season prior to dispatch.Baraldi (1996) stated that experimental research on the use of direct ionizing radiation (radiodisinfestation) to control insect pests on cut flowers has given promising results.

host_range: Colletotrichum kahawae has been reported in Italy on olive. This is, to our knowledge, the first report of C. kahawae on E. sativa in Italy and worldwide. Due to the wide host range of C. kahawae and the economic value of cultivated rocket, this disease could be a threat for this crop in other production areas in Italy.
description: In fall 2014, in a commercial plastic-house in northern Italy, where the crop was grown for 7 years in the same soil, a new leaf spot was observed on rocket plants  (Eruca sativa  ‘Coltivata’) 7 to 35 days after sowing. The incidence ranged from 5 to 15% in the more humid area of the tunnel, with 5 to 75% of the affected leaf area showing white spots. The disease developed at 20 to 28°C and 75 to 90% relative humidity. Fungi were isolated from affected leaf tissues, based on morphological characteristics, molecular diagnostics and the pathogenicity test, the causal agent was identified as Colletotrichum kahawae. This is, to our knowledge, the first report of C. kahawae on E. sativa in Italy and worldwide.
reference_name: First Report of Leaf Spot Caused by Colletotrichum kahawae on Cultivated Rocket (Eruca sativa) in Italy

potential_eco_desc: The disease was first recorded in western Kenya in 1922. McDonald (1926) reports that coffee berry disease then caused losses of up to 75%, causing the abandonment of coffee in several districts of western Kenya. A severe epidemic in central Kenya in 1967 caused the loss of entire crops and overall losses were in excess of 30% (Griffiths, 1969). Efficient chemical control can more than double yields (Griffiths et al., 1971) but the disease still causes appreciable losses which, added to the cost of chemical control, may account for as much as 20% of the value of the crop. Because the disease directly destroys the berries, losses can be dramatic. See also Boisson (1960), Saccas and Charpentier (1969b).^p^pThe occurrence of berry shedding and scab lesions makes accurate disease assessment difficult, as the numbers of diseased berries seen on branches represent a variable proportion of those lost to the disease. Accurate disease/loss assessments can be made by recording the fate of berries on marked branches (Griffiths et al., 1971).

management_info: Chemical Control^p^pThis is essential in most areas affected by coffee berry disease, although resistant varieties exist, and new resistant cultivars have recently been bred and are being grown in some areas. Bordeaux mixture was first used against the disease in Kenya in the 1930s, and copper-based fungicides are still very effective. Resistance to the benzimidazole systemic fungicides soon developed after they were initially successfully used in the early 1970s (Okioga, 1976). Organic protectants such as captafol (now withdrawn; Masaba and Waller, 1992), dithianon and chlorothalonil are effective, as are the modern triazole systemic compounds. Tank mixtures of organic and copper-based protectants are most effective and economic (Okioga, 1978; Masaba et al., 1990). Some newer fungicides are also effective (Masaba et al., 1993). Fungicide suspensions may be applied at 3-4-weekly intervals to protect the developing berries during the rainy season. Earlier spray schedules have been applied to try to reduce the source of bark inoculum but these were shown to exacerbate the disease (Griffiths et al., 1971).^p^p^Resistant Cultivars^p^pMany varieties of Coffea arabica possess appreciable resistance to coffee berry disease but are not widely grown due to problems of quality or yield performance. Many natural C. arabica types in Ethiopia have resistance (Van der Graaff, 1983) and are being selected for wider cultivation. A breeding programme in Kenya during the 1970s produced a new cultivar, Ruiru 11, resistant to both coffee berry disease and leaf rust (Van der Vossen and Walyaro, 1981). A seedling pre-selection test was developed and used for resistance screening; this was based on the susceptibility of young hypocotyls to infection by the pathogen (Van der Vossen et al., 1976). RAPD markers have now been identified which are associated with resistance in coffee to the disease and can be used in marker-assisted breeding (Agwanda et al., 1997). Callus tissue and protoplasts can also be used as a basis for resistance selection Nyange et al., 1995, 1997). There appears to be little genetic variability with in the species (Beynon et al., 1995) and resistance appears to be polygenic and durable (Van der Graaff, 1983).^p^p^Biological Control^p^pThe use of fungicides against coffee berry disease in Kenya has been shown to induce greater levels of disease under some circumstances; some estates which had never used fungicides did not have high levels of coffee berry disease, and when used intermittently fungicides can make the disease worse. The apparently negative affects of fungicides (Griffiths, 1972) were attributed to the removal of micro-organisms antagonistic to the pathogen. This effect was studied in more detail by Masaba (1991) and elements of the microbiota were shown to have a natural biocontrol effect on the disease. This effect is still to be developed and exploited commercially, perhaps in an integrated approach to coffee berry disease control.

host_range: 主要为黄瓜Cucumis sativus，次要寄主为西瓜Citrullus lanatus，香瓜Cucumis melo，南瓜Cucurbita moschata，西葫芦Cucurbita pepo等。
potential_eco_desc: 中国北方保护地及露地栽培黄瓜的常发性病害，一般损失可达10%~20%，严重可达50%以上，甚至绝收。
description: 随种子、繁殖材料传播。
management_info:
1. 带病种子进行消毒，可采用温汤浸种法，即50℃温水浸种30min，或55~60℃恒温浸种15min，取出冷却后催芽播种，亦可用0.4%的50%多菌灵或克菌丹可湿性粉粉剂拌种。
2. 选用抗病品种，如青杂1号、青杂2号，白头霜，吉杂1、吉杂2号、中农11、中农13，津研7号等。
3. 加强栽培管理。覆盖地膜，采用滴灌等节水技术，轮作倒茬，重病棚(田)应与非瓜类作物进行2年以上轮作。施足充分腐熟肥作基肥，适时追肥，避免偏施氮肥，增施磷、钾肥；合理灌水，尤其定植后至结瓜期控制浇水十分重要。保护地黄瓜尽可能采用生态防治，尤其要注意湿度管理，采用放风排湿，控制灌水等措施降低棚内湿度。冬季气温低应加强防寒、保暧措施，使秧苗免受冻害。白天控温28~30℃，夜间15℃，相对湿度低于90%。增强光照，促进黄瓜健壮生长，提高抗病能力。
4. 药剂防治。①药剂浸种：50%多菌灵500倍液浸种20~30min后，冲净再催芽，或用冰醋酸100倍液浸种30min。直播时可用种子重量0.3%~0.4%的50%多菌灵或50%克菌丹拌种，均可取得良好的杀菌效果。②熏蒸消毒：温室、塑料棚定植前10天，每55m3空间用硫磺粉0.13kg，锯末0.25kg混合后分放数处，点燃后密闭大棚，熏1夜。③发病初期及时摘除病瓜，立即喷药防治。用粉尘法或烟雾法于发病初期开始用喷粉器喷撒10%多百粉尘剂，每公顷用药1.5kg；或施用45%百菌清烟剂，每公顷用药1~1.35kg，连续3~4次。④棚室或露地发病初期可喷洒下列杀菌剂：50%多菌灵+70%代森锰锌、50%扑海因、65%甲霉灵、6%乐比耕、40%福星、70%霉奇洁、50%施保功等，隔7~10d 1次，连续3~4次。也可用10%多百粉尘剂，每公顷用药1.5kg，或疫霉净、百菌清、黑星净等烟剂，每公顷熏烟。有研究认为，杜邦福星防治效果明显，优于其他药剂，喷施1~2次就可控制病情的发展。几种药剂交替使用，防治效果更好。

potential_eco_desc: 我国1970年代以前只有零星发生，1980年代随着大棚、温室栽培黄瓜面积扩大，和异地调种频繁等原因，病害蔓延加重。一般因病减产20%~30%，严重时可达80%~100%，而且降低质量和商品价值。

management_info:
1.从无病瓜采种，种子需经消毒。种子用恒温55℃热水浸种15分钟，或用50%多菌灵可湿性粉剂500倍液浸种1小时后水洗再催芽播种。
2.大棚和温室应采用滴灌，加强通风以降低湿度。露地黄瓜应避免连作，远离温室、大棚，雨季要及时排水，必要时打低叶以利通风降湿。
3.发病初期开始喷药，每隔5~7天一次，连喷3~4次，阴雨天多时，要加喷1~2次。常用药有50%多菌灵可湿性粉剂500~1000倍液，50%代森锰锌可湿性粉剂500倍液，70%百菌清可湿性粉剂500~600倍液。

management_info: Host-Plant Resistance^p^pThe use of resistant cultivars is the most acceptable and economic means of disease control in cucumber. A single dominant gene, Ccu, conditions disease resistance in cucumber (Bailey and Burgess, 1935; Andeweg, 1956; Abul-Hayja, 1975). This gene has been widely used since 1955 and continues to be effective (Vakalounakis, 1988). It has been reported that most Dutch-type cucumber hybrids are resistant to scab, having the Ccu gene (Vakalounakis, 1993). The Ccu gene is completely linked to the Foc gene, which confers resistance to Fusarium wilt caused by Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cucumerinum Vakalounakis, 1993, 1995, 1996; Vakalounakis and Smardas, 1995). Although scab resistance or tolerance has been reported in Cucurbita maxima, C. moschata and C. pepo, no resistant cultivars are commercially available (Zitter, 1996). ^p^p^Cultural Control^p^pPlanting disease free seed is important in reducing the incidence of disease initiated from infected seed. Seeds can be surface-disinfected with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite for 10 min (Vakalounakis, 1988). Cultivation of cucurbits in the field during late spring, summer and early autumn reduces disease symptoms, since scab formation is not favoured by these temperatures (Vakalounakis, 1988). Crop rotation with non-host crops, such as maize, is necessary, with two or more years between cucurbit crops, since C. cucumerinum appears to overseason well (Zitter, 1996). Dense planting should be avoided, since it increases the relative humidity, which favours the microclimate for disease development. Care should be taken to avoid the presence of water on the plant surface. If sprays have to be used, these should be applied during the morning. As soon as the first symptoms appear, the structures where the crops grow should be aerated or ventilated to reduce humidity. It is also advisable to raise the temperature, especially during the night. Badly affected plants and fruits should be destroyed. After the crop is harvested, plant debris and especially the fruits should be cleared (Blancard et al., 1991). ^p^p^Chemical Control^p^pIn the absence of host-plant resistance, various fungicides including maneb, mancozeb, chlorothalonil, dichlofluanid, benomyl, fenarimol and triforine may be useful for scab control. Sprays should be applied before disease appearance and continued at regular intervals. However, fungicides are least effective during extended periods of cool and wet weather, because of the short disease cycle. During these periods, sprays should be applied at shorter intervals, depending on the substance. Early applications before fruit formation are necessary. For squashes, fungicides can be applied when plants begin to bloom or, if the weather is favourable, when the first true leaves appear. For pumpkins and melons, fungicides are applied before vines begin to run. ^p^p^Biological Control^p^pInduced resistance against C. cucumerinum has been achieved experimentally by prior inoculation with some pathogens, including Colletotrichum lindemuthianum and Colletotrichum lagenarium (Hammerschmidt et al., 1976; Staub and Kuc, 1980; Vakalounakis and Williams, 1991).

remark: Quarantine regulations were adopted in 1949 to prevent movement of camellia flowers and blooming plants with soil into the southern states of the USA from the states of California, Georgia and Oregon where flower blight was known to occur (Brown, 1954). Concern was so great about flower blight spread that the state of Georgia quarantined an individual homeowner's property (Wilby, 1954). These regulations proved useless as flower blight continued to spread and now occurs throughout the southern states of the USA. ^p^pC. camellia is on the EPPO A1 list of quarantine pests although it is now known to occur in several European countries including the UK (Taylor and Long, 2000). In areas where the fungus does not occur, it was recommended that camellia flowers, plants with open flowers and plants with soil should not be imported from areas or countries where C. camellia does occur (Brooks, 1979).
author: CPC2006

management_info: There is no satisfactory method for controlling camellia flower blight at present. Plant quarantine measures were not successful in preventing its spread in the USA. Cultural methods such as collecting diseased flowers and the use of various mulches are of limited value unless practised on a community-wide basis (Young and Milbrath, 1950; Zummo and Plakidas, 1960; Baxter and Epps, 1981). Host plant resistance has offered little hope as all C. japonica cultivars appear to be susceptible (Baxter and Berly, 1956; Baxter and Epps, 1981; Taylor and Long, 2000). Fungicide soil applications to prevent sclerotial germination may be useful in some situations, such as isolated plantings, but in general must be practised community-wide (Anzalone and Plakidas, 1958; Baxter and Epps, 1981). The use of flower protectant fungicides such as triadimefon can reduce blight by 50%, but the level of control is not great enough to justify their use Holcomb, 1983, 1990, 1991, 1997). There is no indication that a satisfactory control procedure will be developed in the near future.

host_range: Aecia develop on spruce trees, including Picea abies, P. engelmannii, P. glauca, and P. sitchensis. Telia develop on the ericaceous species Arctostaphylos uva-ursi. There is no indication that C. arctostaphyli can perpetuate itself on spruce or Arctostaph
potential_eco_desc: Economic impact^pPicea engelmannii provides timber, wildlife habitat, and scenic and recreational opportunities, and is commonly infected by this rust. In 21 stands of merchantable P. engelmannii in Colorado, USA, an average cull factor of 24% due to broken or dead tops adjacent to dead rust brooms has been reported (Hinds and Hawksworth, 1966; Ziller, 1974). Although shedding dead limbs and spike tops may pose a hazard to people and animals and increase potential fire hazards, there is little documented economic loss.^p^pP. glauca is used for pulpwood and as construction lumber (Nienstaedt and Zasada, 1990). In Canada it is the most important commercial tree and the foremost for pulpwood (Viereck and Little, 1972). It is also used as Christmas tree stock (Hepting, 1971). Economic impacts may result when boles deform the tree or cause needle loss on Christmas tree stock. ^p^pP. mariana is of limited importance for lumber due to its small size (Viereck and Little, 1972). It is a popular Christmas tree, however, and is also used as pulp and fuel wood. Broom rust infections usually remain at low levels but can occasionally become epidemic (Viereck and Johnson, 1990). Economic impacts may result when boles deform the tree or cause needle loss on Christmas tree stock. ^p^pP. pungens is prized for its appearance and used for Christmas trees and ornamental plantings (Fechner, 1990). ^p^pP. sitchensis produces high-grade wood pulp and lumber and is a valuable commercial timber species. Spruce broom rust is of minor importance to P. sitchensis (Viereck and Little, 1972; Harris, 1990).^p^pIn all species, the dead portions of trees infected by spruce broom rust (e.g., tops, large limbs, and large scars) may serve as entrance courts for wood decay fungi. Phellinus pini is an important decay fungus invading dead broom rust sites (Ziller, 1974). Associated wood decay fungi compromise wood structure, which reduces usable wood volume. Also, trees with internal decay are prone to breakage and potentially hazardous if located near homes, or in parks and recreation areas (Hennon and Trummer, 2001).^p^p^Environmental impact^pRust infection sites can be a source for secondary decay fungi.^p^pBrooms appear to serve as important, perhaps critical, winter habitat for birds and mammals (Parks and Bull, 1997; Cotton and Parker, 2000; Hennon and Trummer, 2001)^p^pArctostaphylos alpina and A. rubra, close relatives of A. uva-ursi, may also be susceptible to the fungus, which would extend the range of the disease to spruce growing in northern and western Alaska (Hennon and Trummer, 2001).

remark: Because the alternate host, Arctostaphylos uva-ursi, is commonly associated with Picea in Eurasia, the rust poses a significant potential threat to Picea stands in Europe and Asia (Ziller, 1974). The European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO) lists C. arctostaphyli as an A1 quarantine pest and recommends that all countries prohibit importation of plants and cut branches of Picea from North America. Seeds and tissue cultures are acceptable. It is also of quarantine significance for the InterAfrican Phytosanitary Council (IAPSC) (EPPO, 2002).
author: CPC2006

management_info: No effective chemical control measures are known in combating this disease (Hennon and Trummer, 2001). Control measures are primarily mechanical. In forests managed for wood production, removal of spruce trees with brooms during thinning operations may be the most practical means of control (Hennon and Trummer, 2001). For homeowners and park managers, pruning brooms from branches may be the most effective means of control. However, because many brooms occur on the main bole, the top of the tree may need to be removed (Hennon and Trummer, 2001). ^p^pBecause the only spores of this pathogen that infect spruce occur on Arctostaphylos uva-ursi, removal of A. uva-ursi may help reduce damage on nearby spruce. To effectively protect spruce, all A. uva-ursi within 350 m of the spruce must be removed (Hennon and Trummer, 2001).
